<h1 id="support-api">Support API v2.0.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

Zendesk Support API endpoints

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://example.zendesk.com">https://example.zendesk.com</a>

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Bearer access token authentication.

- oAuth2 authentication. Zendesk OAuth 2.0 access tokens. When an operation lists multiple
scopes, a token needs only one of the scopes to authorize the request.
This behavior differs from the OpenAPI specification, in which all
scopes listed for a security scheme are required.

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [/oauth/authorizations/new](/oauth/authorizations/new)
    - Token URL = [/oauth/tokens](/oauth/tokens)
    - Refresh URL = [/oauth/tokens](/oauth/tokens)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|account_settings:read|View account settings. Includes account configuration, ticket and user fields, and workspaces.|
|account_settings:write|Create, edit, and delete account settings. Includes account configuration, ticket and user fields, and workspaces.|
|accounts:read|Accounts read scope.|
|accounts:write|Accounts write scope.|
|ai_agents:chat|Ai agents chat scope.|
|ai_agents:list|Ai agents list scope.|
|any_channel:write|Push messages from an external channel into Zendesk. Includes creating tickets, comments, and users from an integrated channel. Write only.|
|apps:read|View installed apps and their settings. Includes a list of installed apps and each app's settings.|
|apps:write|Install, configure, and remove apps. Includes installing and uninstalling apps, changing settings, and uploading custom app packages.|
|auditlogs:read|View audit logs, which provide an account-wide record of who changed what and when.|
|automations:read|View automations and their details.|
|automations:write|Create, edit, and delete automations.|
|brands:read|View brands and their agent assignments.|
|brands:write|Create, edit, and delete brands and their agent assignments.|
|custom_objects:read|View custom objects. Includes custom object definitions and record attachments.|
|custom_objects:write|Create, edit, and delete custom objects. Includes definitions and record attachments.|
|deletion_schedules:read|View deletion schedules. Includes data retention policies that automatically delete tickets, users, and other data.|
|deletion_schedules:write|Delete deletion schedules. Includes deleting data retention policies.|
|dynamic_content:read|View dynamic content items and language variants.|
|dynamic_content:write|Create, edit, and delete dynamic content items and language variants.|
|groups:read|View groups and their memberships.|
|groups:write|Create, edit, and delete groups and their memberships.|
|hc:read|View Help Center content. Includes articles, sections, categories, community posts and comments.|
|hc:write|Create, edit, and delete Help Center content. Includes articles, sections, categories, community posts and comments.|
|impersonate|Allows Zendesk Support admins to make requests on behalf of end users. See [Making API requests on behalf of end users](/documentation/ticketing/using-the-zendesk-api/making-api-requests-on-behalf-of-end-users/).|
|macros:read|View macros, their categories, and attachments.|
|macros:write|Create, edit, and delete macros and their attachments.|
|organizations:read|View organizations and their details. Includes memberships, subscriptions, and merge history.|
|organizations:write|Create, edit, and delete organizations and manage their memberships. Includes adding and removing users, managing subscriptions, and merging organizations.|
|read|Read all data. Gives access to GET endpoints, including permission to sideload related resources.|
|requests:read|View support requests and their comments.|
|requests:write|Submit and edit support requests. Includes creating new requests and adding comments to existing ones.|
|satisfaction_ratings:read|View satisfaction ratings, scores, and reasons.|
|satisfaction_ratings:write|Submit satisfaction ratings. Includes rating a ticket as good or bad with an optional reason.|
|security:read|View security and sign-in settings. Includes password policies, session timeouts, IP restrictions, and SSO configuration. Read only.|
|side_conversations:read|Side conversations read scope.|
|side_conversations:write|Side conversations write scope.|
|sla_policies:read|View SLA and group SLA policies.|
|sla_policies:write|Create, edit, delete, and reorder SLA and group SLA policies.|
|targets:read|View targets and their delivery failures.|
|targets:write|Create, edit, and delete targets.|
|themes:read|View Guide themes and their files.|
|themes:write|Create, edit, and delete Guide themes. Includes importing, updating, publishing, exporting, and deleting themes.|
|ticket_attachments:read|View files attached to tickets.|
|ticket_attachments:write|Upload, edit, and delete ticket attachments. Includes uploading files, updating and deleting attachments, and redacting them.|
|ticket_views:read|View ticket views and the tickets they return.|
|ticket_views:write|Create, edit, and delete ticket views.|
|tickets:read|View tickets. Includes ticket contents, comments and conversation history, tags, forms and fields, audits, events, and metrics.|
|tickets:write|Create, edit, and delete tickets. Includes adding comments, tags, merging tickets, marking spam, attachments, forms, and custom statuses.|
|triggers:read|View triggers, trigger categories, and their revision history.|
|triggers:write|Create, edit, delete, and reorder triggers and trigger categories.|
|users:read|View users. Includes identities, active sessions, group, organization, and brand memberships, roles, and settings.|
|users:write|Create, edit, and delete users and manage their access. Includes resetting passwords, ending sessions, adding identities, changing memberships, and managing custom roles.|
|web_widget:write|Edit Web Widget settings and configuration. Write only.|
|webhooks:read|View webhooks and their activity history.|
|webhooks:write|Create, edit, test, and delete webhooks.|
|write|Write all data. Gives access to POST, PUT, and DELETE endpoints.|
|zis:read|View private integrations. Includes configurations, connections, and inbound webhooks.|
|zis:write|Create, edit, and delete private integrations. Includes configurations, connections, and inbound webhooks.|

* API Key (sessionAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **_zendesk_shared_session**, in: cookie. Authenticated browser session. POST requests also require CSRF protection.

<h1 id="support-api-attachments">Attachments</h1>

## Show Attachment

<a id="opIdShowAttachment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/attachments/498483 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/attachments/{attachment_id}`

Shows attachment details. You can get the value of the `attachment_id` parameter by listing the ticket's comments.
See [List Comments](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket_comments/#list-comments). Each comment
in the list has an `attachments` list that specifies an `id` for each attachment.


 #### Allowed for

 * Agents


<h3 id="show-attachment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|attachment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the attachment|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "attachment": {
    "content_type": "application/binary",
    "content_url": "https://company.zendesk.com/attachments/myfile.dat",
    "file_name": "myfile.dat",
    "id": 498483,
    "size": 2532,
    "thumbnails": [],
    "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/attachments/498483"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="show-attachment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success Response|[AttachmentResponse](#schemaattachmentresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Update Attachment for Malware

<a id="opIdUpdateAttachment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/attachments/498483 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "attachment": {
      "malware_access_override": true
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/attachments/{attachment_id}`

Toggles enabling or restricting agent access to attachments with detected malware.

#### Allowed For


|» attachment|body|[AttachmentUpdateInput](#schemaattachmentupdateinput)|false|none|

```json
    "id": 498483,
```

## Redact Comment Attachment

<a id="opIdRedactCommentAttachment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/123456/comments/654321/attachments/498483/redact \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`PUT /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/comments/{comment_id}/attachments/{attachment_id}/redact`

Redaction allows you to permanently remove attachments from an existing comment on a ticket. Once removed from a comment, the attachment is replaced with an empty "redacted.txt" file.

The redaction is permanent. It is not possible to undo redaction or see what was removed. Once a ticket is closed, redacting its attachments is no longer possible.

Also, if you want to redact an inline attachment, you can use the `include_inline_images` parameter in the [List Comments](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket_comments/#list-comments) operation to obtain the inline attachment ID, and use it in the request URL.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents when [deleting tickets is enabled for agents on professional accounts](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408832689818)
* Agents assigned to a custom role with permissions to redact ticket content (Enterprise only)


<h3 id="redact-comment-attachment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|
|comment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the comment|
|attachment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the attachment|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "attachment": {
    "content_type": "application/binary",
    "content_url": "https://company.zendesk.com/attachments/myfile.dat",
    "file_name": "myfile.dat",
    "id": 498483,
    "size": 2532,
    "thumbnails": [],
    "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/attachments/498483"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="redact-comment-attachment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK response|[AttachmentResponse](#schemaattachmentresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Upload Files

<a id="opIdUploadFiles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/uploads?filename=my_document.pdf' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /api/v2/uploads`

Uploads a file that can be attached to a ticket comment. It doesn't attach the file to the comment. For details and examples, see [Attaching ticket comments with the API](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/adding-ticket-attachments-with-the-api/).

The endpoint has a required `filename` query parameter. The parameter specifies what the file will be named when attached to the ticket comment (to give the agent more context about the file). The parameter does not specify the file on the local system to be uploaded. While the two names can be different, their file extensions must be the same. If they don't match, the agent's browser or file reader could give an error when attempting to open the attachment.

The `Content-Type` header must contain a recognized MIME type that correctly describes the type of the uploaded file. Failing to send a recognized, correct type may cause undesired behavior. For example, in-browser audio playback may be interrupted by the browser's security mechanisms for MP3s uploaded with an incorrect type.

Adding multiple files to the same upload is handled by splitting requests and passing the API token received from the first request to each subsequent request. The token is valid for 60 minutes.

**Note**: Even if [private attachments](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/8435939957914) are enabled in the Zendesk Support instance, uploaded files are visible to any authenticated user at the `content_URL` specified in the [JSON response](#json-format) until the upload token is consumed. Once a file is associated with a ticket or post, visibility is restricted to users with access to the ticket or post with the attachment.

#### Allowed For

* End users


<h3 id="upload-files-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filename|query|string|true|The name to assign to the uploaded file|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "upload": {
    "attachment": {
      "content_type": "image/png",
      "content_url": "https://company.zendesk.com/attachments/token/tyBq1ms40dFaHefSIigxZpwGg/?name=crash.png",
      "deleted": false,
      "file_name": "crash.png",
      "height": 62,
      "id": 1503729607981,
      "inline": false,
      "mapped_content_url": "https://company.zendesk.com/attachments/token/tyBq1ms40dFaHefSIigxZpwGg/?name=crash.png",
      "size": 5172,
      "thumbnails": [],
      "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/attachments/1503729607981",
      "width": 80
    },
    "attachments": [
      {
        "content_type": "image/png",
        "content_url": "https://company.zendesk.com/attachments/token/tyBq1ms40dFaHefSIigxZpwGg/?name=crash.png",
        "deleted": false,
        "file_name": "crash.png",
        "height": 62,
        "id": 1503729607981,
        "inline": false,
        "mapped_content_url": "https://company.zendesk.com/attachments/token/tyBq1ms40dFaHefSIigxZpwGg/?name=crash.png",
        "size": 5172,
        "thumbnails": [],
        "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/attachments/1503729607981",
        "width": 80
      }
    ],
    "token": "LXJdriewLBP8JrtzzkN7Ne4k6"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="upload-files-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created response|[AttachmentUploadResponse](#schemaattachmentuploadresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="support-api-sessions">Sessions</h1>

## List Sessions

<a id="opIdListSessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/sessions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/sessions`

If authenticated as an admin, returns all the account's sessions. If authenticated as an agent or end user, returns only the sessions of the user making the request.

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination only

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

#### Allowed For

* Admins, Agents, End users


<h3 id="list-sessions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|object|false|Cursor-based pagination parameters (JSON:API style).<br><br>Supports nested parameters:<br>- `page[size]` - Number of records per page (default varies by endpoint, typically 100)<br>- `page[after]` - Cursor token to fetch records after this position<br>- `page[before]` - Cursor token to fetch records before this position<br><br>Example: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=eyJvIjoiaWQiLCJ2IjoiYVFFPSJ9`<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "sessions": [
    {
      "authenticated_at": "2014-11-18T17:24:29Z",
      "id": 3432,
      "last_seen_at": "2014-11-18T17:30:52Z",
      "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/12345/sessions/3432",
      "user_id": 12345
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-sessions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[SessionsResponse](#schemasessionsresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Delete the Authenticated Session

<a id="opIdDeleteAuthenticatedSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/me/logout \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/users/me/logout`

Deletes the current session. In practice, this only works when using session auth for requests, such as client-side requests
made from a Zendesk app. When using OAuth or basic authentication, you don't have a current session so this endpoint has no effect.

#### Allowed For

* Admins, Agents, End users


<h3 id="delete-the-authenticated-session-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|

</aside>

## Renew the current session

<a id="opIdRenewCurrentSession"></a>

> Code samples

<h1 id="support-api-tags">Tags</h1>

## Search Tags

<a id="opIdAutocompleteTags"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/autocomplete/tags \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/autocomplete/tags`

Returns an array of registered and recent tag names that start with the characters specified in the `name` query parameter. This includes tags where any word within the tag (separated by underscores, hyphens, spaces, or other punctuation) starts with the specified characters. You must specify at least 2 characters.

#### How tag matching works

When tags contain delimiters like underscores, hyphens, or spaces, each word is indexed separately. A tag matches if the tag itself or any word within it starts with your search term.

For example, searching for `trig` will match the tag `set_by_this_trigger` because one of its words ("trigger") starts with "trig". However, searching for `rigger` won't match this tag because neither the full tag nor any of its individual words ("set", "by", "this", "trigger") start with "rigger".

#### Autocomplete limitations

Autocomplete returns up to 15 suggestions from the most commonly used ticket tags in the last 60 days. Tags that match the prefix but aren't in that top set won't appear in the results.

#### Pagination

* Offset pagination only

See [Using Offset Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#using-offset-pagination).


#### Allowed For

* Agents


<h3 id="search-tags-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|string|false|A substring of a tag to search for|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "tags": [
    "attention",
    "attack"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="search-tags-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[TagsByObjectIdResponse](#schematagsbyobjectidresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<a id="opIdAutocompleteTagsPost"></a>

```bash
  -d '{
    "name": "att"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/autocomplete/tags`

Returns an array of registered and recent tag names that start with the characters specified in the `name` parameter. This includes tags where any word within the tag (separated by underscores, hyphens, spaces, or other punctuation) starts with the specified characters. You must specify at least 2 characters.

This endpoint accepts the same parameters as the [GET method](#search-tags) but they are specified in the request body instead of the query string.

#### How tag matching works

When tags contain delimiters like underscores, hyphens, or spaces, each word is indexed separately. A tag matches if the tag itself or any word within it starts with your search term.

For example, searching for `trig` will match the tag `set_by_this_trigger` because one of its words ("trigger") starts with "trig". However, searching for `rigger` won't match this tag because neither the full tag nor any of its individual words ("set", "by", "this", "trigger") start with "rigger".

#### Autocomplete limitations

Autocomplete returns up to 15 suggestions from the most commonly used ticket tags in the last 60 days. Tags that match the prefix but aren't in that top set won't appear in the results.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "att"
}
```

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A substring of a tag to search for|

```json
}
```

<h3 id="add-organization-tags-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of an organization|
|body|body|[TagsAddRequest](#schematagsaddrequest)|false|none|
|» safe_update|body|boolean \| null|false|Write only. When `true`, protects against ticket update collisions. Requires<br>`updated_stamp`; sending `safe_update` without it returns a `409` on every resource.<br>`false` has the same effect as omitting the property or sending `null`: no collision<br>check is performed. Only affects the outcome for tickets. See [Protecting against<br>ticket update collisions](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/tickets/#protecting-against-ticket-update-collisions)<br>|
|» tags|body|[string] \| string|false|The tags to add to the ones already applied. An array of tag strings, or a single<br>string. In either form each value is split on whitespace and on `,` `;` `\|` `(` `)`,<br>then stripped of special characters, downcased and de-duplicated. `null`, an empty array,<br>an empty string and omitting the property are all accepted and leave the existing tags<br>unchanged. Unlike the Set Tags operation, nothing here can clear a tag<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» updated_stamp|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Write only. The resource's last known `updated_at`. The update is applied only if it<br>still matches, otherwise the request returns a `409`. `null` has the same effect as<br>omitting the property: it is ignored unless `safe_update` is set, in which case the<br>request returns a `409`. Only affects the outcome for tickets. See the `safe_update`<br>property<br>|

|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|

## Count Tags

<a id="opIdCountTags"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tags/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/tags/count`

Returns an approximate count of tags. If the count exceeds 100,000, it
is updated every 24 hours.

The `refreshed_at` property of the `count` object is a timestamp that indicates when
the count was last updated.

**Note**: When the count exceeds 100,000, the `refreshed_at` property in the `count` object may
occasionally be null. This indicates that the count is being
updated in the background and the `value` property in the `count` object is limited to
100,000 until the update is complete.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 102
  }
}
```

<h3 id="count-tags-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[TagCountResponse](#schematagcountresponse)|

basicAuth
</aside>

## Add Tags

<a id="opIdPutTagsTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/123456/tags \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "tags": [
      "customer"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/tags`

You can also add tags to multiple tickets with the [Update Many
Tickets](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/tickets/#update-many-tickets) endpoint.

#### Safe Update

If the same ticket is updated by multiple API requests at
the same time, some tags could be lost because of ticket
update collisions. Include `updated_stamp` and `safe_update`
properties in the request body to make a safe update.

For `updated_stamp`, retrieve and specify the ticket's
latest `updated_at` timestamp. The tag update only occurs
if the `updated_stamp` timestamp matches the ticket's
actual `updated_at` timestamp at the time of the request.
If the timestamps don't match (in other words, if the
ticket was updated since you retrieved the ticket's
last `updated_at` timestamp), the request returns a
409 Conflict error.

#### Example

```js
{
  "tags": ["customer"],
  "updated_stamp":"2019-09-12T21:45:16Z",
  "safe_update":"true"
}
```

For details, see [Protecting against ticket update collisions](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/tickets/#protecting-against-ticket-update-collisions).

#### Allowed For

* Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "tags": [
    "customer"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-tags-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|
|body|body|[TagsAddRequest](#schematagsaddrequest)|false|none|
|» safe_update|body|boolean \| null|false|Write only. When `true`, protects against ticket update collisions. Requires<br>`updated_stamp`; sending `safe_update` without it returns a `409` on every resource.<br>`false` has the same effect as omitting the property or sending `null`: no collision<br>check is performed. Only affects the outcome for tickets. See [Protecting against<br>ticket update collisions](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/tickets/#protecting-against-ticket-update-collisions)<br>|
|» tags|body|[string] \| string|false|The tags to add to the ones already applied. An array of tag strings, or a single<br>string. In either form each value is split on whitespace and on `,` `;` `\|` `(` `)`,<br>then stripped of special characters, downcased and de-duplicated. `null`, an empty array,<br>an empty string and omitting the property are all accepted and leave the existing tags<br>unchanged. Unlike the Set Tags operation, nothing here can clear a tag<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» updated_stamp|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Write only. The resource's last known `updated_at`. The update is applied only if it<br>still matches, otherwise the request returns a `409`. `null` has the same effect as<br>omitting the property: it is ignored unless `safe_update` is set, in which case the<br>request returns a `409`. Only affects the outcome for tickets. See the `safe_update`<br>property<br>|
|» via|body|object \| null|false|Write only. `null` is accepted and treated as omitted. Only affects the outcome for tickets|
|» » author_zrn|body|string \| null|false|Write only. The Zendesk Resource Name (ZRN) of the actor on whose behalf the<br>update is made, recorded on the audit. At most 100 characters and must be a<br>valid ZRN. Only affects the outcome for tickets<br>|
|» » channel|body|string \| null|false|The channel to attribute the update to. Defaults to `web_service` when unset,<br>`null` or unrecognized<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "tags": [
    "urgent",
    "printer",
    "fire"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-tags-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[TagsByObjectIdResponse](#schematagsbyobjectidresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="support-api-automations">Automations</h1>

## List Automations

<a id="opIdListAutomations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/automations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/automations`

Lists all automations for the current account.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

#### Available Parameters

You can pass in any combination of the following optional filters:

| Name       | Type    | Comment
| ---------- | ------- | -------
| active     | boolean | Only active automations if true, inactive automations if false
| sort_by    | string  | Possible values are "alphabetical", "created_at", "updated_at", "usage_1h", "usage_24h", or "usage_7d". Defaults to "position"
| sort_order | string  | One of "asc" or "desc". Defaults to "asc" for alphabetical and position sort, "desc" for all others

#### Sideloads

The following sideloads are supported. The usage sideloads are only supported on the Support Professional or Suite Growth plan or above.

| Name             | Will sideload
| ---------------- | -------------
| app_installation | The app installation that requires each automation, if present
| permissions      | The permissions for each automation
| usage_1h         | The number of tickets processed by an automation in the past hour
| usage_24h        | The number of tickets processed by an automation in the past day
| usage_7d         | The number of tickets processed by an automation in the past week
| usage_30d        | The number of tickets processed by an automation in the past thirty days

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination (recommended)
- Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.


<h3 id="list-automations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|active|query|boolean|false|Filter by active automations if true or inactive automations if false|
|include|query|string|false|A sideload to include in the response. See [Sideloads](#sideloads-2)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "automations": [
    {
      "actions": [
        {
          "field": "status",
          "value": "open"
        },
        {
          "field": "assignee_id",
          "value": "296220096"
        }
      ],
      "active": true,
      "conditions": {
        "all": [
          {
            "field": "status",
            "operator": "less_than",
            "value": "solved"
          },
          {
            "field": "assignee_id",
            "operator": "is",
            "value": "296220096"
          }
        ],
        "any": [
          {
            "field": "current_tags",
            "operator": "includes",
            "value": "hello"
          }
        ]
      },
      "id": 25,
      "position": 8,
      "raw_title": "Close and Save",
      "title": "Close and Save"
    },
    {
      "actions": [
        {
          "field": "status",
          "value": "open"
        },
        {
          "field": "assignee_id",
          "value": "296220096"
        }
      ],
      "active": false,
      "conditions": {
        "all": [
          {
            "field": "status",
            "operator": "less_than",
            "value": "solved"
          },
          {
            "field": "assignee_id",
            "operator": "is",
            "value": "296220096"
          }
        ],
        "any": [

    }
  ],
  "count": 2,

  "previous_page": null
}
```

## Create Automation

<a id="opIdCreateAutomation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/automations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "automation": {
      "actions": [
        {
          "field": "priority",
          "value": "high"
        }
      ],
      "all": [
        {
          "field": "status",
          "operator": "is",
          "value": "open"
        },
        {
          "field": "priority",
          "operator": "less_than",
          "value": "high"
        }
      ],
      "title": "Roger Wilco"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/automations`

Creates an automation.

New automations must be unique and have at least one condition that is true only once or an action that nullifies at least one of the conditions. Active automations can have overlapping conditions but can't be identical.

The request must include the following conditions in the `all` array:

- At least one time-based condition
- At least one condition that checks one of the following fields: `status`, `type`, `group_id`, `assignee_id`, or `requester_id`.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "automation": {
    "actions": [
      {
        "field": "priority",
        "value": "high"
      }
    ],
    "all": [
      {
        "field": "status",
        "operator": "is",
        "value": "open"
      },
      {
        "field": "priority",
        "operator": "less_than",
        "value": "high"
      }
    ],
    "title": "Roger Wilco"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-automation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AutomationRequest](#schemaautomationrequest)|true|none|
|» automation|body|[AutomationInput](#schemaautomationinput)|true|The writable attributes accepted when creating an automation|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "automation": {
    "actions": [
      {
        "field": "priority",
        "value": "high"
      }
    ],
    "active": true,
    "conditions": {
      "all": [
        {
          "field": "status",
          "operator": "is",
          "value": "open"
        },
        {
          "field": "priority",
          "operator": "less_than",
          "value": "high"
        }
      ],
      "any": []
    },
    "id": 9873843,
    "position": 8,
    "raw_title": "Roger Wilco",
    "title": "Roger Wilco"
  }
}
```

`PUT /api/v2/automations/{automation_id}`

Updates an automation.

Updated automations must be unique and have at least one condition that is true only once or an action that nullifies at least one of the conditions. Active automations can have overlapping conditions but can't be identical.

The request must include the following conditions in the `all` array:
- At least one time-based condition
- At least one condition that checks one of the following fields: 'status', 'type', 'group_id', 'assignee_id', or 'requester_id'

**Note**: Updating a condition or action updates both the `conditions` and `actions` arrays, clearing all existing values of both arrays. Include all your conditions and actions when updating any condition or action.
**Note**: You might be restricted from updating some default automations.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "automation": {
    "title": "Roger Wilco II"
  }
}
```

|body|body|[AutomationUpdateRequest](#schemaautomationupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» automation|body|[AutomationUpdateInput](#schemaautomationupdateinput)|true|Only the supplied properties are updated. Updating `conditions` or `actions` replaces both arrays in full|

```json
}
```

## Search Automations

<a id="opIdSearchAutomations"></a>

`GET /api/v2/automations/search`

#### Pagination

See [Using Offset Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#using-offset-pagination).

#### Allowed For

#### Sideloads

The following sideloads are supported. For more information, see [Side-loading](/documentation/ticketing/using-the-zendesk-api/side_loading/).

| Name             | Will sideload
| ---------------- | -------------
| app_installation | The app installation that requires each automation, if present
| permissions      | The permissions for each automation
| usage_1h         | The number of tickets processed by an automation in the past hour
| usage_24h        | The number of tickets processed by an automation in the past day
| usage_7d         | The number of tickets processed by an automation in the past week
| usage_30d        | The number of tickets processed by an automation in the past thirty days

<h1 id="support-api-tickets">Tickets</h1>

## List Deleted Tickets

<a id="opIdListDeletedTickets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/deleted_tickets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/deleted_tickets`

Returns a maximum of 100 deleted tickets per page. See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

The results includes all deleted (and not yet archived) tickets that
have not yet been [scrubbed](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408845703194#topic_fv5_w51_sdb) in the past 30 days. Archived tickets are
not included in the results. See [About archived tickets](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408887617050)
in the Support Help Center.

The tickets are ordered chronologically by created date, from oldest to newest.
The first ticket listed may not be the oldest ticket in your
account due to [ticket archiving](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408887617050).

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination (recommended)
- Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

#### Rate Limit

You can make 10 requests every 1 minute using this endpoint.
When making requests beyond page 100, you can make 5 requests every 1 minute. These rate limits apply to both API calls and actions performed in the Admin Center.
The rate limiting mechanism behaves as described in
[Monitoring your request activity](/api-reference/ticketing/account-configuration/usage_limits/#monitoring-your-request-activity) in the API introduction.

<h3 id="list-deleted-tickets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Sort by|
|sort_order|query|string|false|Sort order. Defaults to "asc"|
|support_type_scope|query|string|false|Lists tickets by support type. Possible values are "all", "agent", or "ai_agent". Defaults to "agent"<br>|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_by|id|
|sort_by|subject|
|sort_by|deleted_at|
|sort_by|created_at|
|sort_by|updated_at|
|sort_by|status|
|sort_by|requester|
|sort_by|requester.name|
|sort_by|group|
|sort_by|assignee|
|sort_by|assignee.name|
|sort_order|asc|
|sort_order|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 1,
  "deleted_tickets": [
    {
      "actor": {
        "id": 3946,
        "name": "Taz Wombat"
      },
      "deleted_at": "20140704T15:37:04Z",
      "id": 581,
      "previous_state": "open",
      "subject": "Wombat Party"
    }
  ],
  "next_page": null,
  "previous_page": null
}
```

|200|OK|Successful response|[ListDeletedTicketsResponse](#schemalistdeletedticketsresponse)|

</aside>

## Delete Ticket Permanently

<a id="opIdDeleteTicketPermanently"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/deleted_tickets/123456 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/deleted_tickets/{ticket_id}`

Permanently deletes a soft-deleted ticket. See [Soft delete](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408834005530#topic_zrm_wbj_1db)
in the Zendesk GDPR docs. To soft delete a ticket, use the [Delete Ticket](#delete-ticket) endpoint.

This endpoint enqueues a ticket deletion job and returns a payload with the jobs status.

If the job succeeds, the ticket is permanently deleted. This operation can't be undone.

This endpoint returns a `job_status` [JSON object](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#json-format) and queues a background job to do the work.
Use the [Show Job Status](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#show-job-status) endpoint to check for the job's completion.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

<h3 id="delete-ticket-permanently-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "job_status": {
    "id": "82de0b044094f0c67893ac9fe64f1a99",
    "message": null,
    "progress": null,
    "results": null,
    "status": "queued",
    "total": null,
    "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/job_statuses/82de0b0467893ac9fe64f1a99"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-ticket-permanently-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response|[JobStatusResponse](#schemajobstatusresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Delete Multiple Tickets Permanently

<a id="opIdBulkPermanentlyDeleteTickets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/deleted_tickets/destroy_many?ids=35436%2C35437' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/deleted_tickets/destroy_many`

Permanently deletes up to 100 soft-deleted tickets. See [Soft delete](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408834005530#topic_zrm_wbj_1db)
in the Zendesk GDPR docs. To soft delete tickets, use the [Bulk Delete Tickets](#bulk-delete-tickets) endpoint.

This endpoint accepts a comma-separated list of up to 100 ticket ids. It enqueues
a ticket deletion job and returns a payload with the jobs status.

If one ticket fails to be deleted, the endpoint still attempts to delete the others. If the job succeeds,
the tickets that were successfully deleted are permanently deleted. This operation can't be undone.

This endpoint returns a `job_status` [JSON object](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#json-format) and queues a background job to do the work. Use the [Show Job Status](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#show-job-status) endpoint to check for the job's completion. Only a certain number of jobs can be queued or running at the same time. See [Job limit](/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/#job-limit) for more information.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

<h3 id="delete-multiple-tickets-permanently-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|string|true|Comma-separated list of ticket ids|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "job_status": {
    "id": "82de0b044094f0c67893ac9fe64f1a99",
    "message": null,
    "progress": null,
    "results": null,
    "status": "queued",
    "total": null,
    "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/job_statuses/82de0b0467893ac9fe64f1a99"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-multiple-tickets-permanently-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response|[JobStatusResponse](#schemajobstatusresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Count Organization Tickets

<a id="opIdCountOrganizationTickets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/organizations/16/tickets/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/organizations/{organization_id}/tickets/count`

Returns an approximate count of tickets for a specific organization. If the count exceeds 100,000, it is updated every 24 hours.

The `count[refreshed_at]` property is a timestamp that indicates when the count was last updated.

**Note**: When the count exceeds 100,000, `count[refreshed_at]` may occasionally be null.
This indicates that the count is being updated in the background, and `count[value]` is limited to 100,000 until the update is complete.

#### Allowed For
* Agents


<h3 id="count-organization-tickets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of an organization|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 102
  }
}
```

<h3 id="count-organization-tickets-responses">Responses</h3>

<h3 id="count-organization-tickets-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

## List Ticket Problems

<a id="opIdListTicketProblems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/problems \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/problems`

The response is always ordered by `updated_at` in descending order

#### Allowed For

* Agents

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination (recommended)
* Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

<h3 id="list-ticket-problems-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|include_boundary_indicators|query|boolean|false|When true, includes `has_more` indicator in the cursor pagination response meta.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|include_item_cursors|query|boolean|false|When true, includes cursor values for each item in the cursor pagination response.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "tickets": [
    {
      "custom_status_id": 123,
      "description": "The fire is very colorful.",
      "id": 33,
      "status": "open",
      "subject": "My printer is on fire"
    },
    {
      "custom_status_id": 231,
      "description": "The fire is very colorful as well!",
      "id": 34,
      "status": "pending",
      "subject": "The printer is on fire over here too"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-ticket-problems-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response|[ListTicketProblemsResponse](#schemalistticketproblemsresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Autocomplete Problems

<a id="opIdAutocompleteProblems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/problems/autocomplete \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "text": "fire"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/problems/autocomplete`

Returns tickets whose type is "problem" and whose subject contains the string specified in the `text` parameter.

You can specify the `text` parameter in the request body rather than the query string. Example:

#### Allowed For

```json
}
```

## Delete Ticket

<a id="opIdDeleteTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/123456 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}`

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents with permission to delete tickets

Agent delete permissions are set in Support. See
[Deleting tickets](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408883872538)
in the Support Help Center.

#### Ticket deletion rate limit

You can delete 400 tickets every 1 minute using this endpoint.
The rate limiting mechanism behaves as described in
[Rate limits](/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/) in the API introduction.
Zendesk recommends that you obey the Retry-After header values.
To delete many tickets, you may use [Bulk Delete Tickets](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/tickets/#bulk-delete-tickets).

<h3 id="delete-ticket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|

<h3 id="delete-ticket-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No content|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Merge Tickets into Target Ticket

<a id="opIdMergeTicketsIntoTargetTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/123456/merge \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "ids": [
      123,
      456,
      789
    ],
    "source_comment": "Closing in favor of #111",
    "target_comment": "Combining with #123, #456, #789"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/merge`

Merges one or more tickets into the ticket with the specified id.

See [Merging tickets](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882445594)
in the Support Help Center for ticket merging rules.

Any attachment to the source ticket is copied to the target ticket.

This endpoint returns a `job_status` [JSON object](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#json-format) and queues a background job to do the work. Use the [Show Job Status](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#show-job-status) endpoint to check for the job's completion. Only a certain number of jobs can be queued or running at the same time. See [Job limit](/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/#job-limit) for more information.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

Agents in the Enterprise account must have merge permissions.
See [Creating custom roles and assigning agents](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882) in Zendesk help.

#### Available parameters

The request takes a data object with the following properties:

| Name                     | Type    | Required | Comments                                                |
| ------------------------ | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| ids                      | array   | yes      | Ids of tickets to merge into the target ticket          |
| target_comment           | string  | no       | Private comment to add to the target ticket. This comment is optional but strongly recommended |
| source_comment           | string  | no       | Private comment to add to the source ticket. This comment is optional but strongly recommended |
| target_comment_is_public | boolean | no       | Whether comments in the target ticket are public or private   |
| source_comment_is_public | boolean | no       | Whether comments in the source tickets are public or private |

`target_comment` and `source_comment` can be used to provide a reason for the merge for recordkeeping purposes. If the source ticket has attachments, they are included in `target_comment`.

Comments are private and can't be modified in the following cases:

  * Any of the sources or target tickets are private
  * Any of the sources or target tickets were created through X (formerly Twitter), Facebook or the Channel framework

In any other case, comments default to private but can be modified with the comment privacy parameters.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ids": [
    123,
    456,
    789
  ],
  "source_comment": "Closing in favor of #111",
  "target_comment": "Combining with #123, #456, #789"
}
```

<h3 id="merge-tickets-into-target-ticket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|
|body|body|[TicketMergeInput](#schematicketmergeinput)|false|none|
|» ids|body|[integer]|true|Ids of tickets to merge into the target ticket|
|» source_comment|body|string|false|Private comment to add to the source ticket|
|» source_comment_is_public|body|boolean|false|Whether comment in source tickets are public or private|
|» target_comment|body|string|false|Private comment to add to the target ticket|
|» target_comment_is_public|body|boolean|false|Whether comment in target ticket is public or private|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "job_status": {
    "id": "82de0b044094f0c67893ac9fe64f1a99",
    "message": "Completed at 2018-03-08 10:07:04 +0000",
    "progress": 2,
    "results": [
      {
        "action": "update",
        "id": 244,
        "status": "Updated",
        "success": true
      },
      {
        "action": "update",
        "id": 245,
        "status": "Updated",
        "success": true
      }
    ],
    "status": "completed",
    "total": 2,
    "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/job_statuses/82de0b0467893ac9fe64f1a99"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="merge-tickets-into-target-ticket-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response|[JobStatusResponse](#schemajobstatusresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Count Tickets

<a id="opIdCountTickets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/tickets/count`

Returns an approximate count of tickets in the account. If the count exceeds 100,000, it is updated every 24 hours.

`ccd` lists tickets that the specified user is cc'd on.

The `count[refreshed_at]` property is a timestamp that indicates when the count was last updated.

**Note**: When the count exceeds 100,000, `count[refreshed_at]` may occasionally be null.
This indicates that the count is being updated in the background, and `count[value]` is limited to 100,000 until the update is complete.

#### Allowed For
* Agents

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 102
  }
}
```

<h3 id="count-tickets-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Count of tickets|Inline|

<h3 id="count-tickets-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|object|false|none|none|
|» refreshed_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|» value|integer|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

Only a certain number of jobs can be queued or running at the same time. See [Job limit](/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/#job-limit) for more information.

#### Allowed For

```json
        "body": "The smoke is very colorful."
      },
      "priority": "urgent",
      "subject": "My printer is on fire!"
    },

}
```

`GET /api/v2/tickets/messaging/conversations/{conversation_id}/ticket`

Returns the active ticket associated with the given Sunshine Conversations conversation id.

A ticket is considered active when it's open and the messaging session is still in progress.

## Show Multiple Tickets

<a id="opIdTicketsShowMany"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/show_many?ids=35436%2C35437' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/tickets/show_many`

Accepts a comma-separated list of ticket ids to return.

This endpoint will return up to 100 tickets records.

#### Allowed For
* Agents

<h3 id="show-multiple-tickets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|string|true|Comma-separated list of ticket ids|
|include|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of sideloads to include.<br>|

## Update Many Tickets

<a id="opIdTicketsUpdateMany"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/update_many \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "tickets": [
      {
        "id": 1,
        "priority": "low",
        "status": "solved"
      },
      {
        "assignee_id": 12345,
        "id": 2,
        "status": "pending"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/tickets/update_many`

Accepts an array of up to 100 ticket objects, or a comma-separated list of up to 100 ticket ids.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "tickets": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "priority": "low",
      "status": "solved"
    },
    {
      "assignee_id": 12345,
      "id": 2,
      "status": "pending"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Count User Assigned Tickets

<a id="opIdCountUserAssignedTickets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/35436/tickets/assigned/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/users/{user_id}/tickets/assigned/count`

Returns an approximate count of tickets assigned to the specified user. If the count exceeds 100,000, it is updated every 24 hours.

The `count[refreshed_at]` property is a timestamp that indicates when the count was last updated.

**Note**: When the count exceeds 100,000, `count[refreshed_at]` may occasionally be null.
This indicates that the count is being updated in the background, and `count[value]` is limited to 100,000 until the update is complete.

#### Allowed For
* Agents

<h3 id="count-user-assigned-tickets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the user|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 102
  }
}
```

<h3 id="count-user-assigned-tickets-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Count of tickets|Inline|

<h3 id="count-user-assigned-tickets-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|object|false|none|none|
|» refreshed_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|» value|integer|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="support-api-email-notifications">Email Notifications</h1>

## List Email Notifications

<a id="opIdListEmailNotifications"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/email_notifications?filter%5Bcomment_id%5D=782407' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/email_notifications`

Deleted and archived tickets are not included in the response. See
[About archived tickets](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408887617050) in Zendesk help.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

#### Request parameters

##### Filters

**Important**: You must specify a `filter` query parameter to narrow the scope of the search for this endpoint.

* By notification: `api/v2/email_notifications?filter[notification_id]=7824075373693`
* By comment: `api/v2/email_notifications?filter[comment_id]=782407`
* By ticket: `api/v2/email_notifications?filter[ticket_id]=623`

##### Pagination

By default, a maximum of 100 email notifications are included per page. Use cursor-based pagination parameters (`page[after]` and `page[before]`) to navigate the records (can't be used together in the same request). See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/) for more details.

##### Sorting

By default, email notifications are sorted by creation time (newest first). The query parameter is not supported for this endpoint.


<h3 id="list-email-notifications-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|query|object|true|Filters the email notifications by ticket, comment, or notification id.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of records to return per page|
|sort|query|string|false|The field to sort the list.  Possible values are "created_at", "updated_at" (ascending order) or "-created_at", "-updated_at" (descending order)|

<h1 id="support-api-lookup-relationships">Lookup Relationships</h1>

## Get sources by target

<a id="opIdGetSourcesByTarget"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/zen%3Acustom_object%3Aapartment/1234/relationship_fields/1234/zen%3Acustom_object%3Aapartment \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/{target_type}/{target_id}/relationship_fields/{field_id}/{source_type}`

Returns a list of source objects whose values are populated with the id of a related target object.  For example,
if you have a lookup field called "Success Manager" on a ticket, this endpoint can answer the question,
"What tickets (sources) is this user (found by `target_type` and `target_id`)
assigned as the 'Success Manager' (field referenced by `field_id`)?"

This endpoint also resolves [multi-lookup fields](/api-reference/ticketing/lookup_relationships/lookup_relationships/#about-multi-lookup-relationship-fields).
Pass the multi-lookup field's id as `field_id` and "zen:ticket" as `source_type` to list the tickets that
reference a target record through the field. Multi-lookup reverse lookups are resolved through search, so tickets
the requesting agent can't view are excluded.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination (recommended)
* Offset pagination

For a multi-lookup `field_id`, only cursor pagination applies. Offset pagination parameters are ignored and the
response uses cursor pagination.

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).


<h3 id="get-sources-by-target-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|target_type|path|string|true|The type of object the relationship field is targeting.<br>The options are "zen:user", "zen:ticket", "zen:organization", and "zen:custom_object:CUSTOM_OBJECT_KEY"<br>|
|target_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the object the relationship field is targeting<br>|
|field_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the lookup relationship field<br>|
|source_type|path|string|true|The type of object the relationship field belongs to (example. ticket field belongs to a ticket object).<br>The options are "zen:user", "zen:ticket", "zen:organization", and "zen:custom_object:CUSTOM_OBJECT_KEY"<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "users": [
    {
      "id": 223443,
      "name": "Johnny Agent"
    },
    {
      "id": 8678530,
      "name": "James A. Rosen"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-sources-by-target-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[ReverseLookupResponse](#schemareverselookupresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Filter Definitions

<a id="opIdGetRelationshipFilterDefinitions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/relationships/definitions/zen%3Acustom_object%3Aapartment \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/relationships/definitions/{target_type}`

Returns filter definitions based on the given target type.  Target types
include users (zen:user), tickets (zen:ticket), organizations (zen:organization), or custom objects (zen:custom_object:CUSTOM_OBJECT_KEY).
The returned filter definitions are the options that you can use to build a custom field or ticket field's
`relationship_filter`.


<h3 id="filter-definitions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|target_type|path|string|true|The target type for which you would like to see filter definitions.<br>The options are "zen:user", "zen:ticket", "zen:organization", and "zen:custom_object:CUSTOM_OBJECT_KEY"<br>|
|source_type|query|string|false|The source type for which you would like to see filter definitions.<br>The options are "zen:user", "zen:ticket", and "zen:organization"<br>|

<h1 id="support-api-dynamic-content">Dynamic Content</h1>

## List Items

<a id="opIdListDynamicContents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/dynamic_content/items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/dynamic_content/items`

Returns a list of all dynamic content items for your account if accessed as an admin or agents who have permission to manage dynamic content.

#### Allowed For

* Admins, Agents

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination (recommended)
* Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).


<h3 id="list-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "created_at": "2015-05-13T22:33:12Z",
      "default_locale_id": 1,
      "id": 47,
      "name": "Snowboard Problem",
      "outdated": true,
      "placeholder": "{{dc.snowboard_problem}}",
      "updated_at": "2015-05-13T22:33:12Z",
      "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/dynamic_content/items/47",
      "variants": [
        {
          "active": true,
          "content": "C'est mon contenu dynamique en français",
          "created_at": "2015-05-13T22:33:12Z",
          "default": true,
          "id": 47,
          "locale_id": 1,
          "outdated": false,
          "updated_at": "2015-05-13T22:33:12Z",
          "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/dynamic_content/items/47/variants/47"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-items-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[DynamicContentsResponse](#schemadynamiccontentsresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Create Item

<a id="opIdCreateDynamicContent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/dynamic_content/items \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "item": {
      "default_locale_id": 16,
      "name": "Snowboard Problem",
      "variants": [
        {
          "content": "Voici mon contenu dynamique en français",
          "default": true,
          "locale_id": 16
        },
        {
          "content": "Este es mi contenido dinámico en español",
          "default": false,
          "locale_id": 2
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/dynamic_content/items`

Create a new content item, with one or more variants in the item's `variants` array. See [Specifying item variants](#specifying-item-variants).

The `default_locale_id` and variant `locale_id` values must be one of the locales the account has active. You can get the list with the [List Locales](/api-reference/ticketing/account-configuration/locales/#list-locales) endpoint.

#### Allowed For

* Admins, Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "item": {
    "default_locale_id": 16,
    "name": "Snowboard Problem",
    "variants": [
      {
        "content": "Voici mon contenu dynamique en français",
        "default": true,
        "locale_id": 16
      },
      {
        "content": "Este es mi contenido dinámico en español",
        "default": false,
        "locale_id": 2
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[DynamicContentRequest](#schemadynamiccontentrequest)|true|none|
|» item|body|[DynamicContentInput](#schemadynamiccontentinput)|true|A new dynamic content item. There are two ways to give it a default variant: supply `default_locale_id` and `content` to<br>create a single variant, or supply the `variants` array. `content` must not be combined with `variants`;<br>`default_locale_id` may be sent alongside `variants` but is ignored.<br>|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "item": {
    "created_at": "2015-05-13T22:33:12Z",
    "default_locale_id": 1,
    "id": 47,
    "name": "Snowboard Problem",
    "outdated": false,
    "placeholder": "{{dc.snowboard_problem}}",
    "updated_at": "2015-05-13T22:33:12Z",
    "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/dynamic_content/items/47",
    "variants": [
      {
        "active": true,
        "content": "Voici mon contenu dynamique en français",
        "created_at": "2015-05-13T22:33:12Z",
        "default": true,
        "id": 47,
        "locale_id": 16,
        "outdated": false,
        "updated_at": "2015-05-13T22:33:12Z",
        "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/dynamic_content/items/47/variants/47"
      },
      {
        "active": true,
        "content": "Este es mi contenido dinámico en español",
        "created_at": "2015-05-13T22:33:12Z",
        "default": false,
        "id": 48,
        "locale_id": 2,
        "outdated": false,
        "updated_at": "2015-05-13T22:33:12Z",
        "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/dynamic_content/items/47/variants/48"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-item-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created response|[DynamicContentResponse](#schemadynamiccontentresponse)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

|» item|body|[DynamicContentUpdateInput](#schemadynamiccontentupdateinput)|true|The item attributes to change. The name is the only attribute this endpoint can change; use the<br>[Item Variants API](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content_item_variants/) to add, update or delete<br>variants. ## Update Variant

<a id="opIdUpdateDynamicContentVariant"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/dynamic_content/items/47/variants/23 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "variant": {
      "active": false,
      "content": "C'\''est mon contenu dynamique en français",
      "default": false
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/dynamic_content/items/{dynamic_content_item_id}/variants/{dynamic_content_variant_id}`

Updates the specified variant. You don't need to include all the properties. If you just want to update content, for example, then include just that.

You can't switch the active state of the default variant of an item. Similarly, you can't switch the default to false if the variant is the default. You must make another variant default instead.

#### Allowed For

* Admins, Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "variant": {
    "active": false,
    "content": "C'est mon contenu dynamique en français",
    "default": false
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-variant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dynamic_content_item_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the dynamic content item|
|dynamic_content_variant_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the variant|
|body|body|[DynamicContentVariantUpdateRequest](#schemadynamiccontentvariantupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» variant|body|[DynamicContentVariantUpdateInput](#schemadynamiccontentvariantupdateinput) \| object \| null|true|The attributes to update. `null` is accepted and is a no-op — the variant is returned unchanged with a 200|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[DynamicContentVariantUpdateInput](#schemadynamiccontentvariantupdateinput)|false|The writable attributes accepted when updating a dynamic content item variant. The update is partial — any omitted attribute is left<br>unchanged, and sending no attributes at all is accepted and changes nothing. `locale_id` is not accepted: a variant's locale is fixed at<br>creation, and sending it has no effect<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object \| null|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "variant": {
    "active": false,
    "content": "C'est mon contenu dynamique en français",
    "created_at": "2014-04-09T19:53:23Z",
    "default": false,
    "id": 23,
    "locale_id": 125,
    "outdated": false,
    "updated_at": "2014-04-09T19:53:23Z",
    "url": "https://subdomain.zendesk.com/api/v2/dynamic_content/items/3/variants/23"
  }
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[DynamicContentVariantResponse](#schemadynamiccontentvariantresponse)|

basicAuth

`POST /api/v2/dynamic_content/items/{dynamic_content_item_id}/variants/create_many`

#### Allowed For

* Admins, Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "variants": [
    {
      "active": true,
      "content": "C'est mon contenu dynamique en français",
      "default": false,
      "locale_id": 127
    },
    {
```

|» variants|body|[[DynamicContentVariantInput](#schemadynamiccontentvariantinput)]|true|The variants to create. The request is rejected with a 400 if the array is missing or empty, or if it holds more than 100 variants —<br>the shared bulk-job cap, `BulkJobData::ITEM_COUNT_LIMIT`. Check the returned job<br>status for the per-variant result<br>|
