## Push Content to Support

<a id="opIdPushContentToSupport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/any_channel/push \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /api/v2/any_channel/push`

Pushes Channel framework content to Zendesk.

#### Allowed For

* Admins

#### Request parameters

The POST request takes a JSON object parameter which contains data about all
the resources that the client is pushing.

| Name               | Type      | Required  | Comments
| ------------------ | ----------| --------- | -------------------
| instance_push_id   | string    | yes       | The account ID where data will be pushed. This was passed to the integration service when the administrator set up the account
| request_id         | string    | no        | A unique identifier for the push request
| external_resources | array     | yes       | The [resources](#external_resource-object) to push

#### external_resource object

| Name               | Type                               | Max length | Mandatory | Comments
|------------------- | ---------------------------------- |------------| --------- | ----------
| external_id        | string                             | 255        | yes       | Unique identifier of the external resource. Must be ASCII characters
| internal_note      | boolean                            |            | no        | If true creates a new internal note comment
| message            | string                             | 65535      | yes       | Text to be converted to a ticket or comment
| html_message       | string                             | 65535      | no        | HTML version of message
| parent_id          | string                             | 511        | no        | Unique identifier of the external resource for which this is a response. Used to choose the correct thread. Responses may include `parent_id` or `thread_id`, but not both. See [Conversation threads](/documentation/channel_framework/understanding-the-channel-framework/pull_endpoint/#conversation-threads)
| thread_id          | string                             | 255        | no        | Arbitrary identifier of the thread to which this item should belong. Responses may include `parent_id` or `thread_id`, but not both. See [Conversation threads](/documentation/channel_framework/understanding-the-channel-framework/pull_endpoint/#conversation-threads)
| created_at         | string                             |            | yes       | When the resource was created in the origin system, as an ISO 8601 extended format date-time. Example: '2015-09-08T22:48:09Z'
| author             | object                             |            | yes       | See [author object](#author-object) below
| display_info       | array                              |            | no        | Array of integration-specific data used by apps to modify the agent UI. See [display_info object](#display_info-object) below
| allow_channelback  | boolean                            |            | no        | If false, prevents the agent from making additional comments on the message in the Zendesk interface
| fields             | array                              |            | no        | Array of ticket fields to set in Zendesk and their values. See [fields array](#fields-array)
| file_urls          | array                              | 10         | no        | Array of files to be imported into Zendesk. See [file urls](/documentation/channel_framework/understanding-the-channel-framework/pull_endpoint/#file-urls) in the Channel framework docs

#### author object

| Name        | Type   | Max chars | Mandatory | Comments
|------------ | ------ |---------- |---------- |-----------
| external_id | string | 255       | yes       | Unique identifier of the user in the origin service
| name        | string | 255       | no        | If not supplied, defaults to external id
| image_url   | string | 255       | no        | URL to an image for the user
| locale      | String | 255       | no        | The user's locale. Must be one of the supported [locales](/api-reference/ticketing/account-configuration/locales/#list-available-public-locales) in Zendesk
| fields      | array  |           | no        | Array of items containing user field identifier ('id') and value of field ('value'.)  For system fields ('notes' or 'details'), the identifier is the English name. For custom fields, the identifier may be the ID or the name

#### display_info object

| Name | Type   | Max chars | Mandatory | Comments
|----- | ------ |---------- |---------- |-----------
| type | string | 255       | yes       | Globally unique type identifier defined by the integration origin service. Examples: a GUID or URI
| data | string | 65535     | yes       | JSON data containing display hints

#### fields array

The `fields` array lists ticket fields to set in Zendesk and their values. Each item consists of a field identifier (`id`) and a value (`value`) for the field. For Zendesk system fields such as `subject`, the identifier is the English name. For custom fields, the identifier may be a field ID or a name. See [Ticket Fields](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket_fields/).

The `fields` array can only set ticket values on ticket creation, not on ticket updates.

#### Response format

The response is a JSON object containing a single key:

| Name      | Type     | Comments
| --------- | -------- | -------------------
| results   | array    | An array of [result objects](#result-object)

The `results` array contains an entry for each item in the incoming `external_resources` array, in the
same order.  For example, if you call `push` with 3 external resources, a successful response will include
`results` with three entries, corresponding to your 3 resources.

#### result object

| Name                 | Type                           | Comments
| -------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------
| external_resource_id | string                         | The external ID of the resource, as passed in
| status               | object                         | The status of the import for the indicated resource. See [status object](#status-object)

#### status object

| Name        | Type   | Comments
| ----------- | ------ | -------------------
| code        | string | A code indicating the status of the import of the resource, as described in [status codes](#status-codes)
| description | string | In the case of an exception, a description of the exception. Otherwise, not present.

#### status codes

| Key                                       | Description
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------
| success                                   | The external resource was successfully converted to a ticket or comment
| already_imported                          | Reimport of the external resource was skipped due to a pre-existing ticket or comment for the resource
| could_not_locate_parent_external_resource | The parent resource, as identified by parent_id in the [request](#request-parameters), could not be found. The unrecognized parent ID is returned in the description of the [status](#status-object)
| processing_error                          | An internal exception occurred while processing the resource. See `description` in the [status object](#status-object)
| halted                                    | This resource was not processed because processing of previous resources failed


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "external_resource_id": "234",
      "status": {
        "code": "could_not_locate_parent_external_resource",
        "description": "123"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="push-content-to-support-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[ChannelFrameworkPushResultsResponse](#schemachannelframeworkpushresultsresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="support-api-whatsapp-templates">WhatsApp Templates</h1>

WhatsApp message templates synced from SunCo.

## List WhatsApp Templates

<a id="opIdListWhatsappTemplates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/channels/whatsapp_templates \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/channels/whatsapp_templates`

Returns the WhatsApp message templates synced from SunCo for the account's
WhatsApp integrations. Only templates approved by WhatsApp are synced.

Listing triggers a freshness check per integration. If local data is missing or stale, a
background sync is started and the `syncing` flag is set in the response. The list may be
incomplete while that flag is set, so poll until it clears.

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination (recommended)
* Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

#### Allowed For

* Agents


<h3 id="list-whatsapp-templates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|integration_id|query|string|false|Only return templates active on this SunCo WhatsApp integration.|
|is_active|query|boolean|false|Only return templates with this activation state.|
|category|query|string|false|Only return templates in this WhatsApp category, for example `UTILITY`.|
|language|query|string|false|Only return templates authored in this language, for example `en_US`.|
|name|query|string|false|Only return templates whose name contains this value.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 2,
  "next_page": null,
  "previous_page": null,
  "syncing": false,
  "whatsapp_templates": [
    {
      "category": "UTILITY",
      "components": [
        {
          "text": "Hi {{1}}, your order {{2}} has shipped.",
          "type": "BODY"
        }
      ],
      "created_at": "2026-09-14T14:32:27Z",
      "id": "01JBQ8Z5K7N3M9P2R4T6V8X0YA",
      "integrations": [
        {
          "id": "5f3a1b2c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e",
          "name": "WhatsApp Support"
        }
      ],
      "is_active": true,
      "language": "en_US",
      "name": "order_confirmation",
      "status": "approved",
      "template_id": "1234567890",
      "updated_at": "2026-09-17T17:24:25Z"
    },
    {
      "category": "UTILITY",
      "components": [
        {
          "text": "Reminder: your appointment is on {{1}}.",
          "type": "BODY"
        }
      ],
      "created_at": "2026-09-14T14:32:27Z",
      "id": "01JBQ8Z5K7N3M9P2R4T6V8X0YB",
      "integrations": [],

      "status": "approved",
      "template_id": "1234567891",
      "updated_at": "2026-09-17T17:24:25Z"

`PUT /api/v2/channels/whatsapp_templates/{template_id}/toggle`

`GET /api/v2/organization_merges/{organization_merge_id}`

Retrieves the details of a specific organization merge operation. This endpoint is useful for obtaining the status and outcome of a merge that was previously initiated. It provides information such as the winning and losing organization IDs, the status of the merge, and the associated URLs.

This endpoint can be used to determine if a merge is still in progress, has completed successfully, or has encountered an error.

`GET /api/v2/organizations`

#### Pagination

<h3 id="list-organizations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|

|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|include_boundary_indicators|query|boolean|false|When true, includes `has_more` indicator in the cursor pagination response meta.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|include_item_cursors|query|boolean|false|When true, includes cursor values for each item in the cursor pagination response.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|

## Create Organization

<a id="opIdCreateOrganization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/organizations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "organization": {
      "name": "My Organization"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/organizations`

You must provide a unique `name` for each organization. Normally
the system doesn't allow records to be created with identical names.
However, a race condition can occur if you make two or more identical
POSTs very close to each other, causing the records to have identical
organization names.

**Note**: Leading and trailing whitespace in `name` is automatically trimmed before validation. This means that names differing only by whitespace are treated as duplicates. For example, "API Company" and "API Company " are considered the same name.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents assigned to a custom role with permissions to manage organizations (Enterprise only)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "organization": {
    "name": "My Organization"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateOrganizationRequest](#schemacreateorganizationrequest)|true|none|
|» organization|body|[OrganizationObject](#schemaorganizationobject)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "organization": {
    "created_at": "2020-09-30T01:50:12Z",
    "details": null,
    "domain_names": [],
    "external_id": null,

Every property is optional and omitting one leaves the stored value unchanged, but see the per-property notes: several properties replace the stored value wholesale rather than merging into it. An empty object is accepted and changes nothing.|

## Merge Organization With Another Organization

<a id="opIdCreateOrganizationMerge"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/organizations/16/merge \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "organization_merge": {
      "winner_id": 54321
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/organizations/{organization_id}/merge`

Merges two organizations by moving all users, tickets, and domain names from the organization specified by `{organization_id}` to the organization specified by `winner_id`. After the merge:

- The "losing" organization will be deleted.
- Other organization fields and their values will not be carried over to the "winning" organization.
- The merge operation creates an `Organization Merge` record which contains a status indicating the progress of the merge.

**Note**: This operation is irreversible.

#### Merge Statuses

| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| new | A job has been queued to merge the two organizations. |
| in progress | The job to merge the two organizations has started. |
| error | An error occurred during the merge job. The merge can be retried by repeating the API call. | 
| complete | The merge has been completed successfully. |

#### Allowed For

* Admins


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "organization_merge": {
    "winner_id": 54321
  }
}
```

<h3 id="merge-organization-with-another-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of an organization|
|body|body|[OrganizationMergeRequest](#schemaorganizationmergerequest)|true|none|
|» organization_merge|body|object|false|none|
|» » winner_id|body|integer(int64)|false|The id of the winning organization.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "organization_merge": {
    "id": "01HPZM6206BF4G63783E5349AD",
    "loser_id": 123,
    "status": "new",
    "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/organization_merges/01HPZM6206BF4G63783E5349AD",
    "winner_id": 456
  }
}
```

<h3 id="merge-organization-with-another-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[OrganizationMergeResponse](#schemaorganizationmergeresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## List Organization Merges

<a id="opIdListOrganizationMerges"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/organizations/16/merges \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/organizations/{organization_id}/merges`

Retrieves a list of all organization merge operations associated with a given organization. This endpoint allows you to track the history of merge actions for an organization, including ongoing and completed merges.

Each entry in the list contains details such as the ID of the merge, the winning and losing organization IDs, the current status of the merge, and a URL to access the `Organization Merge` record.

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination is used for this endpoint.
- A maximum of 100 records can be returned per page.

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/) for more details.

#### Allowed For

* Admins


<h3 id="list-organization-merges-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of an organization|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "organization_merges": [
    {
      "id": "01HPZM6206BF4G63783E5349AD",
      "loser_id": 123,
      "status": "complete",
      "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/organization_merges/01HPZM6206BF4G63783E5349AD",
      "winner_id": 456
    }
  ]
}
```

## Count Organizations

<a id="opIdCountOrganizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/organizations/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/organizations/count`

Returns an approximate count of organizations. If the count exceeds
100,000, it is updated every 24 hours.

The `refreshed_at` property of the `count` object is a timestamp that indicates
when the count was last updated.

When the count exceeds 100,000, the `refreshed_at` property may
occasionally be null. This indicates that the count is being
updated in the background and the `value` property of the `count` object is limited to
100,000 until the update is complete.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


<h3 id="count-organizations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include_boundary_indicators|query|boolean|false|When true, includes `has_more` indicator in the cursor pagination response meta.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|include_item_cursors|query|boolean|false|When true, includes cursor values for each item in the cursor pagination response.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 102
  }
}
```

<h3 id="count-organizations-responses">Responses</h3>

## Create Or Update Organization

<a id="opIdCreateOrUpdateOrganization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/organizations/create_or_update \
  -X POST \

      "name": "My Organization"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/organizations/create_or_update`

Creates an organization if it doesn't already exist, or updates
an existing organization. Using this method means one less call
to check if an organization exists before creating it. You need
to specify the id or external id when updating
an organization to avoid a duplicate error response. Name is
not available as a matching criteria.

#### Allowed For

* Agents, with restrictions on certain actions


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "organization": {
    "id": "123",
    "name": "My Organization"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateOrUpdateOrganizationRequest](#schemacreateorupdateorganizationrequest)|true|none|
|» organization|body|[OrganizationCreateOrUpdateInput](#schemaorganizationcreateorupdateinput)|true|Organization attributes to create with, or to apply to the matched organization. Matching is by `id` first and then by `external_id`; when neither matches, a new organization is created from these attributes and `name` becomes mandatory. When an organization is matched, every property is optional and omitting one leaves the stored value unchanged — but see the per-property notes, as several properties replace the stored value wholesale rather than merging into it.|

## Search Organizations

<a id="opIdSearchOrganizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/organizations/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/organizations/search`

Returns an array of organizations matching the criteria. You may search by an organization's `external_id` or `name`, but not both:

#### Searching by `external_id`

If you set the `external_id` value of an organization to associate it to an external record, you can use it to search for the organization.

For an organization to be returned, its `external_id` must exactly match the value provided (case insensitive).

#### Searching by `name`

For an organization to be returned, its `name` must exactly match the value provided (case insensitive).

#### Allowed For:

* Admins
* Agents assigned to a custom role with permissions to add or modify organizations (Enterprise only)

See [Creating custom agent roles](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) in Zendesk help.


<h3 id="search-organizations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|external_id|query|integer|false|The external id of an organization|
|name|query|string|false|The name of an organization|

## Update Many Organizations

<a id="opIdUpdateManyOrganizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/organizations/update_many \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "organizations": [
      {
        "id": "1",
        "notes": "Something interesting"
      },
      {
        "external_id": "2",
        "notes": "Something even more interesting"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/organizations/update_many`

Bulk or batch updates up to 100 organizations.

#### Bulk update

To make the same change to multiple organizations, use the following endpoint and data format:

`https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/organizations/update_many?ids=1,2,3`

```js
{
  "organization": {
    "notes": "Priority"
  }
}
```

#### Batch update

To make different changes to multiple organizations, use the following endpoint and data format:

`https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/organizations/update_many`

```js
{
  "organizations": [
    { "id": 1, "notes": "Priority" },
    { "id": 2, "notes": "Normal" }
  ]
}
```

#### Response

This endpoint returns a `job_status` [JSON object](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#json-format) and queues a background job to do the work. Use the [Show Job Status](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#show-job-status) endpoint to check for the job's completion. Only a certain number of jobs can be queued or running at the same time. See [Job limit](/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/#job-limit) for more information.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents

Agents with no permissions restrictions can only update "notes" on organizations.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "organizations": [
    {
      "id": "1",
      "notes": "Something interesting"
    },
    {
      "external_id": "2",
      "notes": "Something even more interesting"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-many-organizations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|string|false|A list of organization ids|
|external_ids|query|string|false|A list of external ids|
|body|body|[OrganizationBulkUpdateRequest](#schemaorganizationbulkupdaterequest) \| [OrganizationBatchUpdateRequest](#schemaorganizationbatchupdaterequest)|true|One organization object for a bulk update, or an array of organization objects for a batch update|
|» *anyOf*|body|[OrganizationBulkUpdateRequest](#schemaorganizationbulkupdaterequest)|false|Bulk-update mode: the attributes in `organization` are applied to **every** organization named by the `ids` or `external_ids` query parameter. One of those two query parameters is required in this mode — the request returns 400 without one. Both are query parameters, not body properties: a body schema cannot see the query string, so the requirement is stated here rather than encoded. At most 100 organizations can be updated in one request.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[OrganizationBatchUpdateRequest](#schemaorganizationbatchupdaterequest)|false|Batch-update mode: each item in `organizations` names one organization by `id` or `external_id` and carries the attributes to apply to it, so a single request can make different changes to up to 100 organizations. An empty array, an explicit null and a missing wrapper are all rejected with 400.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "job_status": {
    "id": "8b726e606741012ffc2d782bcb7848fe",
    "message": "Completed at Fri Apr 13 02:51:53 +0000 2012",
    "progress": 2,
    "results": [
      {
        "action": "update",
        "id": 380,
        "status": "Updated",
        "success": true
      }
    ],
    "status": "completed",
    "total": 2,
    "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/job_statuses/8b726e606741012ffc2d782bcb7848fe"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-many-organizations-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[JobStatusResponse](#schemajobstatusresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

`GET /api/v2/users/{user_id}/organizations`

Returns a list of organizations associated with the specified user.

#### Pagination

* Offset pagination

If the agent has a custom agent role that restricts their access to only users in their own organization, a 403 Forbidden error is returned. See [Creating custom agent roles](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) in Zendesk help.


<h3 id="list-user-organizations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|include_boundary_indicators|query|boolean|false|When true, includes `has_more` indicator in the cursor pagination response meta.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|include_item_cursors|query|boolean|false|When true, includes cursor values for each item in the cursor pagination response.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|user_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the user|

## Count User's Organizations

<a id="opIdCountUserOrganizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/35436/organizations/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/users/{user_id}/organizations/count`

Returns an approximate count of organizations for a specific user. If the count exceeds
100,000, it is updated every 24 hours.

The `refreshed_at` property of the `count` object is a timestamp that indicates
when the count was last updated.

When the count exceeds 100,000, the `refreshed_at` property may
occasionally be null. This indicates that the count is being
updated in the background and the `value` property of the `count` object is limited to
100,000 until the update is complete.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


<h3 id="count-users-organizations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the user|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 102
  }
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[CountOrganizationResponse](#schemacountorganizationresponse)|

## List Ticket Triggers

<a id="opIdListTriggers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/triggers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/triggers`

Lists all ticket triggers for the current account.

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination (recommended)
- Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

#### Sideloads

The following sideloads are supported. The usage sideloads are only supported on the Support Professional or Suite Growth plan or above.

| Name             | Will sideload
| ---------------- | -------------
| app_installation | The app installation that requires each trigger, if present
| permissions      | The permissions for each trigger
| usage_1h         | The number of times each trigger has been used in the past hour
| usage_24h        | The number of times each trigger has been used in the past day
| usage_7d         | The number of times each trigger has been used in the past week
| usage_30d        | The number of times each trigger has been used in the past thirty days


<h3 id="list-ticket-triggers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|query|boolean|false|Filter by active triggers if true or inactive triggers if false|
|sort|query|string|false|Cursor-based pagination only. Possible values are "alphabetical", "created_at", "updated_at", or "position".|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Offset pagination only. Possible values are "alphabetical", "created_at", "updated_at", "usage_1h", "usage_24h", or "usage_7d". Defaults to "position"|
|sort_order|query|string|false|One of "asc" or "desc". Defaults to "asc" for alphabetical and position sort, "desc" for all others|
|category_id|query|string|false|Filter triggers by category ID|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|include|query|string|false|A sideload to include in the response. See [Sideloads](#sideloads-2)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 2,
  "next_page": null,
  "previous_page": null,
  "triggers": [
    {
      "actions": [],
      "active": true,
      "conditions": {},
      "created_at": "2012-09-25T22:50:26Z",
      "description": "Close and save a ticket",
      "id": 25,
      "position": 8,
      "raw_title": "Close and Save",
      "title": "Close and Save",
      "updated_at": "2012-09-25T22:50:26Z",
      "url": "http://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/triggers/25"
    },
    {
      "actions": [],
      "active": false,
      "conditions": {
        "all": [
          {
            "field": "status",
            "operator": "less_than",
            "value": "solved"
          },
          {
            "field": "assignee_id",
            "operator": "is",
            "value": "296220096"
          }
        ],
        "any": [
          {
            "field": "status",
            "operator": "less_than",
            "value": "solved"
          },

            "field": "custom_status_id",
            "operator": "includes",
            "value": [
              "1",

            ]

## List Ticket Trigger Revisions

<a id="opIdListTriggerRevisions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/triggers/198/revisions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/triggers/{trigger_id}/revisions`

List the revisions associated with a ticket trigger. Ticket trigger revision history is only available on Enterprise plans.

#### Allowed For

 * Agents

#### Sideloads

The following sideloads are supported:

| Name  | Will sideload
| ----- | -------------
| users | The user that authored each revision

#### Pagination

This endpoint uses cursor-based pagination. The records are ordered in
descending order by the `created_at` timestamp, then by `id` on duplicate
`created_at` values.

The `cursor` parameter is a non-human-readable argument you can use to move
forward or backward in time.

Each JSON response will contain the following attributes to help you get
more results:

- `after_url` requests more recent results
- `before_url` requests older results
- `after_cursor` is the cursor to build the request yourself
- `before_cursor` is the cursor to build the request yourself

The properties are null if no more records are available.

You can request a maximum of 1000 records using the `limit` parameter. If
no `limit` parameter is supplied, it will default to 1,000.


<h3 id="list-ticket-trigger-revisions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of revisions to return per page. You can request a maximum of 1000<br>records. If no limit is supplied, it defaults to 1000.<br>|
|cursor|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination)<br>obtained from the `after_cursor` or `before_cursor` value of a previous response.<br>|
|order|query|string|false|The sort order of the revisions. Only the lowercase values `asc` and `desc`<br>are accepted. If no order is supplied, it defaults to `desc`.<br>|
|include|query|string|false|Accepts "users". Use this parameter to side-load the user that authored each revision. Example: `?include=users`|
|trigger_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the trigger|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|asc|
|order|desc|

## List Active Ticket Triggers

`GET /api/v2/triggers/active`

Lists all active ticket triggers.

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination (recommended)
- Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.
#### Allowed For

* Agents

#### Sideloads

The following sideloads are supported:

| Name             | Will sideload
| ---------------- | -------------
| app_installation | The app installation that requires each ticket trigger, if present
| permissions      | The permissions for each trigger
| usage_1h         | The number of times each ticket trigger has been used in the past hour
| usage_24h        | The number of times each ticket trigger has been used in the past day
| usage_7d         | The number of times each ticket trigger has been used in the past week
| usage_30d        | The number of times each ticket trigger has been used in the past thirty days


<h3 id="list-active-ticket-triggers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sort|query|string|false|Cursor-based pagination only. Possible values are "alphabetical", "created_at", "updated_at", or "position".|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Offset pagination only. Possible values are "alphabetical", "created_at", "updated_at", "usage_1h", "usage_24h", or "usage_7d". Defaults to "position"|
|sort_order|query|string|false|One of "asc" or "desc". Defaults to "asc" for alphabetical and position sort, "desc" for all others|
|category_id|query|string|false|Filter triggers by category ID|

## Reorder Ticket Triggers

<a id="opIdReorderTriggers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/triggers/reorder \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "trigger_ids": [
      324376,
      564937,
      164318
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/triggers/reorder`

Alters the firing order of ticket triggers in the account. See
[Reordering and sorting triggers](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/10356973691546)
in the Zendesk Help Center. The firing order is set in a `trigger_ids` array in the request body.

You must include the id of every **active** ticket trigger in the account to reorder the ticket triggers — inactive triggers are excluded by the endpoint and must not be sent. If not, the endpoint will return a `400 Bad Request` (`Invalid attribute`) error and nothing is reordered.

Reordering ticket triggers via the API is not permitted if you have more than one ticket trigger category. If there is more than one
ticket trigger category, the endpoint will return a `LimitOneCategory` error.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "trigger_ids": [
    324376,
    564937,
    164318
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="reorder-ticket-triggers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TriggerReorderRequest](#schematriggerreorderrequest)|true|none|
|» trigger_ids|body|[integer(int64)]|true|The complete set of active ticket trigger ids in the account, in the firing order to apply. Each id's new position is its 1-based index in this array. The array must contain exactly the ids of every **active** ticket trigger in the account — no more, no fewer. A partial or padded list is rejected with a `400 Bad Request` ("Invalid attribute: all triggers are not provided") and nothing is reordered, so a generated call must first read the account's active ticket triggers and send all of them. Inactive triggers are not reordered and must not be included. An empty array is only accepted on an account that has no active ticket triggers; otherwise it is the same `400`. Omitting the property is not supported.|

<h3 id="reorder-ticket-triggers-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response (empty body)|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Search Ticket Triggers

<a id="opIdSearchTriggers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/triggers/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/triggers/search`

#### Pagination

* Offset pagination only

See [Using Offset Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#using-offset-pagination).

#### Allowed For

* Agents

#### Sideloads

The following sideloads are supported. For more information, see [Side-loading](/documentation/ticketing/using-the-zendesk-api/side_loading/).

| Name             | Will sideload
| ---------------- | -------------
| app_installation | The app installation that requires each ticket trigger, if present
| permissions      | The permissions for each ticket trigger
| usage_1h         | The number of times each ticket trigger has been used in the past hour
| usage_24h        | The number of times each ticket trigger has been used in the past day
| usage_7d         | The number of times each ticket trigger has been used in the past week
| usage_30d        | The number of times each ticket trigger has been used in the past thirty days

#### Filter

Use the `filter` query parameter to filter a ticket trigger search by one or more attributes. For example, the following `filter` argument filters ticket triggers by the `description` attribute:

```json
{
  "json": {
    "description": "Close a ticket"
  }
}
```


<h3 id="search-ticket-triggers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|Query string used to find all triggers with matching title|
|filter|query|string|false|JSON-encoded trigger attribute filters for the search. See [Filter](#filter).<br><br>Example: `{"json":{"description":"Close a ticket"}}`<br>|
|active|query|boolean|false|Filter by active triggers if true or inactive triggers if false|
|sort|query|string|false|Cursor-based pagination only. Possible values are "alphabetical", "created_at", "updated_at", or "position".|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Offset pagination only. Possible values are "alphabetical", "created_at", "updated_at", "usage_1h", "usage_24h", or "usage_7d". Defaults to "position"|
|sort_order|query|string|false|One of "asc" or "desc". Defaults to "asc" for alphabetical and position sort, "desc" for all others|
|include|query|string|false|A sideload to include in the response. See [Sideloads](#sideloads-2)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 2,
  "next_page": null,
  "previous_page": null,
  "triggers": [
    {
      "actions": [],
      "active": true,
      "conditions": {
        "all": [
          {
            "field": "status",
            "operator": "less_than",
            "value": "solved"
          },
          {
            "field": "assignee_id",
            "operator": "is",
            "value": "296220096"
          }
        ],
        "any": [
          {
            "field": "status",
            "operator": "less_than",
            "value": "solved"
          }
        ]
      },
      "created_at": "2012-09-25T22:50:26Z",
      "description": "Close and save a ticket",
      "id": 25,
      "position": 9,
      "raw_title": "Close and Save",
      "title": "Close and Save",
      "updated_at": "2012-09-25T22:50:26Z"
    },
    {
      "actions": [],
      "active": true,
      "conditions": {},
      "created_at": "2012-09-25T22:50:26Z",
      "id": 28,
      "position": 9,
      "raw_title": "{{dc.close_and_redirect}}",
      "title": "Close and redirect to topics",
      "updated_at": "2012-09-25T22:50:26Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Update Many Ticket Triggers

<a id="opIdUpdateManyTriggers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/triggers/update_many \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "triggers": [
      {
        "id": 25,
        "position": 5
      },
      {
        "active": false,
        "id": 26
      },
      {
        "category_id": "10027",
        "id": 27
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/triggers/update_many`

Updates the position or the active status of multiple ticket triggers. Any additional properties are ignored.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

#### Request Parameters

The PUT request expects a `triggers` object that lists the ticket triggers to update.

A maximum of 100 ticket triggers can be updated per request.

Each ticket trigger may have the following properties:

| Name        | Mandatory | Description
| --------    | --------- | -----------
| id          | yes       | The ID of the ticket trigger to update
| position    | no        | The new position of the ticket trigger
| active      | no        | The active status of the ticket trigger (true or false)
| category_id | no        | The ID of the new category the ticket trigger is to be moved to

#### Example Request

```js
{
  "triggers": [
    {"id": 25, "position": 3},
    {"id": 23, "position": 5},
    {"id": 27, "position": 9},
    {"id": 22, "position": 7}
  ]
}
```


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "triggers": [
    {
      "id": 25,
      "position": 5
    },
    {
      "active": false,
      "id": 26
    },
    {
      "category_id": "10027",
      "id": 27
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-many-ticket-triggers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TriggerBulkUpdateRequest](#schematriggerbulkupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» triggers|body|[[TriggerBulkUpdateItem](#schematriggerbulkupdateitem)]|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

{
  "count": 2,
  "next_page": null,
  "previous_page": null,

    {
      "actions": [],
      "active": true,
      "conditions": {},
      "created_at": "2012-09-25T22:50:26Z",
      "description": "Close and save a ticket",
      "id": 25,
      "position": 8,
      "raw_title": "Close and Save",
      "title": "Close and Save",
      "updated_at": "2012-09-25T22:50:26Z",
      "url": "http://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/triggers/25"
    },
    {
      "actions": [],
      "active": false,
      "conditions": {
        "all": [
          {
            "field": "status",
            "operator": "less_than",
            "value": "solved"
          },
          {
            "field": "assignee_id",
            "operator": "is",
            "value": "296220096"
          }
        ],
        "any": [
          {
            "field": "status",

          },

## Validate Ticket Trigger

<a id="opIdValidateTrigger"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/triggers/validate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "trigger": {
      "actions": [
        {
          "field": "group_id",
          "value": "20455932"
        }
      ],
      "conditions": {
        "all": [
          {
            "field": "status",
            "operator": "is",
            "value": "open"
          }
        ]
      },
      "title": "Roger Wilco"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/triggers/validate`

Validates a ticket trigger definition without creating or updating a trigger record. Useful for checking whether trigger conditions and actions are valid before submitting a create or update request.

This endpoint applies create-time validation, so the body must include the required fields (`title` and `actions`); partial update bodies (which omit them) are not accepted here even though `UpdateTrigger` accepts them.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "trigger": {
    "actions": [
      {
        "field": "group_id",
        "value": "20455932"
      }
    ],
    "conditions": {
      "all": [
        {
          "field": "status",
          "operator": "is",
          "value": "open"
        }
      ]
    },
    "title": "Roger Wilco"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="validate-ticket-trigger-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» fail_on_validate|body|boolean|false|Accepted for parity with the create and update trigger endpoints. Does not currently affect the response of this endpoint.|
|» trigger|body|[TriggerObject](#schematriggerobject)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "valid": true
}
```

<h3 id="validate-ticket-trigger-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Validation result|[TriggerValidationResponse](#schematriggervalidationresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

|sort_order|query|string|false|One of "asc" or "desc". Defaults to "asc" for alphabetical and position sort, "desc" for all others|

## Delete Many Object Triggers

<a id="opIdDeleteManyObjectTriggers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/triggers/destroy_many?ids=131%2C178%2C938' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/triggers/destroy_many`

Deletes the object triggers corresponding to the provided comma-separated list of ids. 

**Note**: You can only bulk-delete triggers associated with one object at a time, specified by the `custom_object_key` in the request.

#### Allowed For

* Administrators
* Agents in custom roles with the `manage_triggers` permission (Enterprise only)

#### Request Parameters

The DELETE request takes an `ids` object that lists the
object triggers to delete. All of the specified object trigger `ids` must be associated with a single object.

| Name | Description
| ---- | -----------
| ids  | The ids of the triggers to delete

#### Example request

```js
{
  "ids": "25,23,27,22"
}
```


<h3 id="delete-many-object-triggers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|ids|query|string|true|A comma separated list of trigger IDs|

<h3 id="delete-many-object-triggers-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No content response|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Search Object Triggers

<a id="opIdSearchObjectTriggers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/triggers/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/triggers/search`

Returns a list of object triggers that meet your filter or search criteria.

#### Pagination

* Offset pagination only

See [Using Offset Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#using-offset-pagination).

#### Allowed For

* Agents

#### Filter

Use the `filter` query parameter to filter an object trigger search by one or more attributes. For example, the following `filter` argument filters object triggers by the `title` attribute:

```json
{
  "json": {
    "title": "test"
  }
}
```


<h3 id="search-object-triggers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|query|query|string|false|Query string used to find all triggers with matching title|
|filter|query|string|false|JSON-encoded trigger attribute filters for the search. See [Filter](#filter).<br><br>Example: `{"json":{"description":"Close a ticket"}}`<br>|
|active|query|boolean|false|Filter by active triggers if true or inactive triggers if false|
|sort|query|string|false|Cursor-based pagination only. Possible values are "alphabetical", "created_at", "updated_at", or "position".|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Offset pagination only. Possible values are "alphabetical", "created_at", "updated_at", "usage_1h", "usage_24h", or "usage_7d". Defaults to "position"|
|sort_order|query|string|false|One of "asc" or "desc". Defaults to "asc" for alphabetical and position sort, "desc" for all others|
|include|query|string|false|A sideload to include in the response. See [Sideloads](#sideloads-2)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 1,
  "next_page": null,
  "previous_page": null,
  "triggers": [
    {
      "actions": [
        {
          "field": "custom_object.order.custom_fields.miles",
          "value": "100"
        }
      ],
      "active": true,
      "conditions": {
        "all": [
          {
            "field": "custom_object.order.custom_fields.heat",
            "operator": "is",
            "value": "1"
          }
        ],
        "any": []
      },
      "created_at": "2024-07-09T21:29:59Z",
      "description": "",
      "id": 28,
      "position": 1,
      "raw_title": "Testing CO trigger with tagger field condition",
      "title": "Testing CO trigger with tagger field condition",
      "updated_at": "2024-07-09T21:29:59Z",
      "url": "http://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/order/triggers/28"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="search-object-triggers-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[ObjectTriggersResponse](#schemaobjecttriggersresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Update Many Object Triggers

<a id="opIdUpdateManyObjectTriggers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/triggers/update_many \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "triggers": [
      {
        "id": 25,
        "position": 1
      },
      {
        "active": false,
        "id": 26
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/triggers/update_many`

Updates the position or the active status of multiple object triggers. Any additional properties are ignored.

**Note**: You can only bulk-update triggers associated with one object at a time, specified by the `custom_object_key` in the request.

#### Allowed For

* Administrators
* Agents in custom roles with the `manage_triggers` permission (Enterprise only)

#### Request Parameters

The PUT request expects a `triggers` object that lists the object triggers to update. All of the specified object trigger `ids` must be associated with a single object.

You can specify the following properties for each object trigger you're updating:

| Name        | Mandatory | Description
| --------    | --------- | -----------
| id          | yes       | The ID of the object trigger to update
| position    | no        | The new position of the object trigger
| active      | no        | The active status of the object trigger (true or false)

#### Example Request

```js
{
  "triggers": [
    {"id": 25, "position": 3},
    {"id": 23, "active": true},
    {"id": 27, "position": 9, "active": false},
    {"id": 22, "position": 7}
  ]
}
```


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "triggers": [
    {
      "id": 25,
      "position": 1
    },
    {
      "active": false,
      "id": 26
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-many-object-triggers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|body|body|[ObjectTriggerBulkUpdateRequest](#schemaobjecttriggerbulkupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» triggers|body|[[ObjectTriggerBulkUpdateItem](#schemaobjecttriggerbulkupdateitem)]|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 2,
  "next_page": null,
  "previous_page": null,
  "triggers": [
    {
      "actions": [],
      "active": true,
      "conditions": {},
      "created_at": "2024-06-27T16:51:54Z",
      "description": "A trigger for custom object of type = order",
      "id": 25,
      "position": 1,
      "raw_title": "Order object trigger",
      "title": "Order object trigger",
      "updated_at": "2024-06-27T16:51:54Z",
      "url": "http://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/order/triggers/25"
    },
    {
      "actions": [],
      "active": false,
      "conditions": {
        "all": [
          {
            "field": "custom_object.order.custom_fields.heat",
            "operator": "not_present"
          }
        ],
        "any": []
      },
      "created_at": "2024-07-08T20:44:32Z",
      "description": "Check order's heat and set field as needed",
      "id": 26,
      "position": 2,
      "raw_title": "Set order miles when heat not present",
      "title": "Set order miles when heat not present",
      "updated_at": "2024-07-08T20:44:32Z",
      "url": "http://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/order/triggers/26"
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[ObjectTriggersResponse](#schemaobjecttriggersresponse)|

<h1 id="support-api-incremental-export">Incremental Export</h1>

## Incremental Sample Export

<a id="opIdIncrementalSampleExport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/tickets/sample?start_time=1332034771' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/incremental/{incremental_resource}/sample`

Use this endpoint to test the incremental export format. It's more strict in terms of rate limiting,
at 10 requests per 20 minutes instead of 10 requests per minute. It also returns only up to 50
results per request. Otherwise, it's identical to the above APIs.

Use the `incremental_resource` parameter to specify the resource. Possible values are "tickets", "ticket_events", "users", or "organizations".

#### Allowed For

* Admins


<h3 id="incremental-sample-export-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_time|query|integer|true|The time to start the incremental export from. Must be at least one minute in the past. Data isn't provided for the most recent minute|
|incremental_resource|path|string|true|The resource requested for incremental sample export|

## Incremental Ticket Event Export

<a id="opIdIncrementalTicketEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/ticket_events?start_time=1332034771' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/incremental/ticket_events`

Returns a stream of changes that occurred on tickets, excluding events occuring within one minute of the request. Each event is tied
to an update on a ticket and contains all the fields that were updated in that
change. For more information, see:

- [Exporting ticket events](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api#exporting-ticket-events) in [Using the Incremental Exports API](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api)
- [Time-based incremental exports](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api#time-based-incremental-exports) in [Using the Incremental Exports API](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api)

You can include comments in the event stream by using the `comment_events`
sideload. See Sideloading below. If you don't specify the sideload, any comment
present in the ticket update is described only by Boolean `comment_present`
and `comment_public` object properties in the event's `child_events` array.
The comment itself is not included.

The `child_events` within a parent `ticket_event` are ordered by `id` by default, 
which reflects the order the changes were actually applied. For example, when 
several "Change" events touch the same field in one update, the child event with 
the highest id is the final value of that field.

#### Allowed For

 * Admins

#### Sideloading

The endpoint supports the `comment_events` sideload. Any comment present in the ticket
update is listed as an object in the event's `child_events` array. Example:

```js
"child_events": [
  {
    "id": 91048994488,
    "via": {
      "channel": "api",
      "source": {"from":{},"to":{},"rel":null}},
    "via_reference_id":null,
    "type": "Comment",
    "author_id": 5031726587,
    "body": "This is a comment",
    "html_body": "&lt;div class="zd-comment"&gt;&lt;p dir="auto"&gt;This is a comment&lt;/p&gt;",
    "public": true,
    "attachments": [],
    "audit_id": 91048994468,
    "created_at": "2009-06-25T10:15:18Z",
    "event_type": "Comment"
  },
  ...
],
...
```


<h3 id="incremental-ticket-event-export-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include|query|string|false|Sideloads to include in the response. Accepts a comma-separated list of values.<br>Supports `comment_events` to include full comment data in the response.<br>|
|start_time|query|integer|true|The time to start the incremental export from. Must be at least one minute in the past. Data isn't provided for the most recent minute|
|support_type_scope|query|string|false|Lists tickets by support type. Possible values are "all", "agent", or "ai_agent". Defaults to "agent"<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 1,
  "end_of_stream": true,
  "end_time": 1601357503,
  "next_page": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/ticket_events?start_time=1601357503",
  "ticket_events": [
    {
      "id": 926256957613,
      "instance_id": 1,
      "metric": "agent_work_time",
      "ticket_id": 155,
      "time": "2020-10-26T12:53:12Z",
      "type": "measure"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="incremental-ticket-event-export-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[ExportIncrementalTicketEventsResponse](#schemaexportincrementalticketeventsresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Incremental Ticket Export, Time Based

<a id="opIdIncrementalTicketExportTime"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/tickets?start_time=1332034771' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/incremental/tickets`

Returns the tickets that changed since the start time. For more information,
see [Exporting tickets](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api#exporting-tickets) in [Using the Incremental Exports API](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api).

This endpoint supports time-based incremental exports.
For more information, see [Time-based incremental exports](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api#time-based-incremental-exports) in [Using the Incremental Exports API](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api). You can also return tickets using cursor-based pagination. See [Incremental Ticket Export, Cursor Based](#incremental-ticket-export-cursor-based).

The results include tickets that were updated by the system. See
[Excluding system-updated tickets](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api#excluding-system-updated-tickets-time-based-exports) in [Using the Incremental Exports API](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api).

The endpoint can return tickets with an `updated_at` time that's earlier than the
`start_time` time. The reason is that the API compares the `start_time` with the ticket's
`generated_timestamp` value, not its `updated_at` value. The `updated_at` value is
updated only if the update generates a [ticket event](#incremental-ticket-event-export).
The `generated_timestamp` value is updated for all ticket updates, including system
updates. If a system update occurs after a ticket event, the unchanged
`updated_at` time will become earlier relative to the updated `generated_timestamp`
time.

#### Allowed For

 * Admins

#### Sideloading

See [Tickets sideloads](/documentation/ticketing/using-the-zendesk-api/side_loading/#supported-endpoints). For performance reasons,
`last_audits` sideloads aren't supported.


<h3 id="incremental-ticket-export-time-based-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_time|query|integer|true|The time to start the incremental export from. Must be at least one minute in the past. Data isn't provided for the most recent minute|

## Incremental Ticket Export, Cursor Based

<a id="opIdIncrementalTicketExportCursor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor`

Returns the tickets that changed since the start time. For more information,
see [Exporting tickets](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api#exporting-tickets) in [Using the Incremental Exports API](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api).

This endpoint supports cursor-based incremental exports.
Cursor-based exports are highly encouraged because they provide more consistent performance and
response body sizes. For more information, see [Cursor-based incremental exports](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api#cursor-based-incremental-exports) in [Using the Incremental Exports API](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api).



#### Allowed For

 * Admins

#### Sideloading

See [Tickets sideloads](/documentation/ticketing/using-the-zendesk-api/side_loading/#supported-endpoints). For performance reasons,
`last_audits` sideloads aren't supported.


<h3 id="incremental-ticket-export-cursor-based-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_time|query|integer|false|The time to start the incremental export from. Must be at least one minute in the past. Data isn't provided for the most recent minute. Required on the initial export request; not required on subsequent cursor-based pagination requests|
|cursor|query|string|false|The cursor pointer to work with for all subsequent exports after the initial request|
|support_type_scope|query|string|false|Lists tickets by support type. Possible values are "all", "agent", or "ai_agent". Defaults to "agent"<br>|

## Update Account Settings

<a id="opIdUpdateAccountSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/account/settings \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "settings": {
      "active_features": {
        "customer_satisfaction": false
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/account/settings`

Updates settings for the account. See [JSON Format](#json-format) above for the settings you can update.

#### Allowed For

* Admins


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "settings": {
    "active_features": {
      "customer_satisfaction": false
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-account-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AccountSettingsUpdateRequest](#schemaaccountsettingsupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» settings|body|object|true|none|
|» » active_features|body|object|false|none|
|» » » access_logs_enabled|body|boolean|false|Only takes effect for accounts with at least one Advanced Data Protection<br>SKU product; otherwise silently dropped before the setting is saved<br>(`settings_controller_support.rb`, `products.none?(&:advanced_data_protection_sku?)`).<br>|
|» » » agent_task_lists|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » allow_ccs|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » approvals_activated|body|boolean|false|Rejected with a 422 ("Approvals cannot be activated for this account") unless<br>the account has `has_activate_approvals?` (`validate_approvals_settings`,<br>`settings_controller.rb`). Setting it to `true` also activates approval-related<br>views and object triggers as a side effect.<br>|
|» » » approvers_as_end_users|body|boolean|false|Rejected with a 422 unless the account has `has_activate_approvals?`<br>(`validate_end_user_approvers`, `settings_controller.rb`).<br>|
|» » » audit_logs_gdpr|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » automatic_answers|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » business_hours|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » custom_objects_activated|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » customer_satisfaction|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » release_control_enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » ticket_tagging|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » user_tagging|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » agents|body|object|false|See the authorization note on the parent object: a non-admin agent may<br>only send this key when every property in it is one of<br>`spell_checker_enabled`, `ai_async_comment_translations_eap_enabled` or<br>`ai_translation_disclosure_enabled`.<br>|
|» » » agent_dashboard_enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » agent_home|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » agent_workspace|body|boolean|false|May be silently dropped without effect in either direction<br>(`validate_agent_workspace_update`, `settings_controller_support.rb`):<br>turning it on is dropped unless the account is `agent_workspace_compatible?`<br>and has `aw_self_serve_migration_enabled`, and (if Groups & Departments<br>aren't migrated) dropped outright when the account has a Chat product,<br>otherwise `groups.check_group_name_uniqueness` is forced to `true` as a side<br>effect; turning it off is dropped if the account has native messaging or<br>`aw_prevent_opt_out` without the auto-activation override. Setting it to<br>`false` also forces `routing.enabled` to `false`<br>(`settings_controller_support.rb:481-483`).<br>|
|» » » ai_async_comment_translations_eap_enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » ai_translation_disclosure_enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » dark_mode_agent_workspace|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » dark_mode_terms_and_conditions_accepted|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » explore_zra_monitoring_assistant_enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » focus_mode|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » idle_timeout_enabled|body|boolean|false|Deprecated: silently dropped without effect for accounts with the<br>`deprecate_idle_timeout_from_settings_api` Arturo<br>(`has_deprecate_idle_timeout_from_settings_api?`,<br>`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|» » » show_user_profile_page_toggle|body|boolean|false|Silently dropped without effect unless the account has<br>`has_ocp_customer_profile?` (`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|

<h1 id="support-api-ticket-metrics">Ticket Metrics</h1>

## List Ticket Metrics

<a id="opIdListTicketMetrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/ticket_metrics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/ticket_metrics`

Returns a list of tickets with their metrics.

Tickets are ordered chronologically by created date, from newest to oldest.
The last ticket listed may not be the absolute oldest ticket in your account
due to ticket archiving.

Archived tickets are not included in the response. See
[About archived tickets](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408887617050) in
Zendesk help.

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination (recommended)
- Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.


#### Allowed For

* Agents


<h3 id="list-ticket-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|object|false|Cursor-based pagination parameters (JSON:API style).<br><br>Supports nested parameters:<br>- `page[size]` - Number of records per page (default varies by endpoint, typically 100)<br>- `page[after]` - Cursor token to fetch records after this position<br>- `page[before]` - Cursor token to fetch records before this position<br><br>Example: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=eyJvIjoiaWQiLCJ2IjoiYVFFPSJ9`<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|

<h1 id="support-api-groups">Groups</h1>

## List Groups

<a id="opIdListGroups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/groups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/groups`

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination (recommended)
* Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents


<h3 id="list-groups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|exclude_deleted|query|boolean|false|Whether to exclude deleted entities|
|include|query|string|false|Sideloads to include in the response. Accepts a comma-separated list of values.<br>|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|include_boundary_indicators|query|boolean|false|When true, includes `has_more` indicator in the cursor pagination response meta.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|include_item_cursors|query|boolean|false|When true, includes cursor values for each item in the cursor pagination response.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "groups": [
    {
      "created_at": "2009-05-13T00:07:08Z",
      "id": 211,
      "is_public": true,
      "name": "DJs",
      "updated_at": "2011-07-22T00:11:12Z"
    },
    {
      "created_at": "2009-08-26T00:07:08Z",
      "id": 122,
      "is_public": true,
      "name": "MCs",
      "updated_at": "2010-05-13T00:07:08Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|include_boundary_indicators|query|boolean|false|When true, includes `has_more` indicator in the cursor pagination response meta.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|include_item_cursors|query|boolean|false|When true, includes cursor values for each item in the cursor pagination response.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|

## Count Groups

<a id="opIdCountGroups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/groups/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/groups/count`

Returns an approximate count of groups. If the count exceeds 100,000, it is updated every 24 hours.

The `refreshed_at` property of the `count` object is a timestamp that indicates when the count was last updated.

**Note**: When the count exceeds 100,000, `refreshed_at` may occasionally be null. This indicates that the count is being updated in the background, and the `value` property of the `count` object is limited to 100,000 until the update is complete.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 102
  }
}
```

<h3 id="count-groups-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[GroupsCountObject](#schemagroupscountobject)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Bulk Create Memberships

<a id="opIdGroupMembershipBulkCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/group_memberships/create_many \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{

      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/group_memberships/create_many`

Assigns up to 100 agents to given groups.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents assigned to a custom role with permissions to manage group memberships (Enterprise only)

#### Response

This endpoint returns a `job_status` [JSON object](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#json-format) and queues a background job to do the work. Use the [Show Job Status](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#show-job-status) endpoint to check for the job's completion.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "group_memberships": [
    {
      "group_id": 88,
      "user_id": 72
    },
    {
      "group_id": 88,
      "user_id": 73
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-create-memberships-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BulkCreateGroupMembershipsRequest](#schemabulkcreategroupmembershipsrequest)|true|none|
|» group_memberships|body|[object]|true|An array of group membership objects to create. Maximum 100 items|
|» » default|body|boolean|false|If true, tickets assigned directly to the agent will assume this membership's group|
