```bash
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/organization_memberships`

Returns a list of organization memberships for the account, user or organization in question.

**Note**: When returning organization memberships for a user, organization memberships are sorted with the default organization first, and then by organization name.

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination (recommended)
* Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

#### Allowed For

- Agents
- End users


<h3 id="list-memberships-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|include|query|string|false|Sideloads to include in the response. Accepts a comma-separated list of values.<br>Valid values: `users`, `organizations`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "organization_memberships": [
    {
      "created_at": "2009-05-13T00:07:08Z",
      "default": true,
      "id": 4,
      "organization_id": 12,
      "organization_name": "first organization",
      "updated_at": "2011-07-22T00:11:12Z",
      "user_id": 29,
      "view_tickets": true
    },
    {
      "created_at": "2012-03-13T22:01:32Z",
      "default": null,
      "id": 49,
      "organization_id": 3,
      "organization_name": "second organization",
      "updated_at": "2012-03-13T22:01:32Z",
      "user_id": 155,
      "view_tickets": true
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="opIdCreateOrganizationMembership"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/organization_memberships \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

    "organization_membership": {

    }
```

`POST /api/v2/organization_memberships`

Assigns a user to a given organization. Returns an error with status 422 if the user is already assigned to the organization.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents when creating a new organization membership for an end user


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "organization_membership": {
    "organization_id": 88,
    "user_id": 72
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-membership-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[OrganizationMembershipRequest](#schemaorganizationmembershiprequest)|true|none|
|» organization_id|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the organization to assign the user to, supplied at the root of the request instead of<br>inside `organization_membership`. It is only consulted when no `user_id` is given at the root or in<br>the query string; when it is consulted, `organization_membership.organization_id` is ignored.<br><br>This may equivalently be sent as an `organization_id` **query parameter**, which takes precedence<br>over the root of the body.<br><br>An organization must likewise be identified in **at least one of** three places — this property, the<br>`organization_id` query parameter, or `organization_membership.organization_id` — and a request that<br>names none of them is a 422. As with `user_id`, that rule is stated rather than encoded, because the<br>query location is not visible to a request-body schema.<br>|
|» organization_membership|body|[OrganizationMembershipInput](#schemaorganizationmembershipinput)|true|none|
|» user_id|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the user to assign to the organization, supplied at the root of the request instead of<br>inside `organization_membership`. When present it selects the user the membership is created for,<br>and `organization_membership.user_id` is ignored.<br><br>This may equivalently be sent as a `user_id` **query parameter**, which takes precedence over the<br>root of the body.<br><br>A user must be identified in **at least one of** three places — this property, the `user_id` query<br>parameter, or `organization_membership.user_id` — and a request that names none of them is a 422.<br><br>That rule is stated here rather than encoded as a schema constraint, deliberately: one of the three<br>legal locations is the **query string**, which lies outside the request body a body schema can see.<br>Any structural encoding of "at least one of" would therefore have to reject a body that names the<br>user nowhere — even though such a body is a legal `201` whenever the `user_id` query parameter<br>supplies it. Being unenforced is the lesser fault: over-strictness here would forbid calls the API<br>accepts.<br>|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "organization_membership": {
    "created_at": "2012-04-03T12:34:01Z",
    "default": true,
    "id": 461,
    "organization_id": 88,
    "updated_at": "2012-04-03T12:34:01Z",
    "user_id": 72
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-membership-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created response|[OrganizationMembershipResponse](#schemaorganizationmembershipresponse)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth

## Create Many Memberships

<a id="opIdCreateManyOrganizationMemberships"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/organization_memberships/create_many \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "organization_memberships": [
      {
        "organization_id": 88,
        "user_id": 72
      },
      {
        "organization_id": 88,
        "user_id": 27
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/organization_memberships/create_many`

Accepts an array of up to 100 organization membership objects.

This endpoint returns a `job_status` [JSON object](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#json-format) and queues a background job to do the work. Use the [Show Job Status](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#show-job-status) endpoint to check for the job's completion. Only a certain number of jobs can be queued or running at the same time. See [Job limit](/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/#job-limit) for more information.

#### Allowed For
* Admins
* Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "organization_memberships": [
    {
      "organization_id": 88,
      "user_id": 72
    },
    {
      "organization_id": 88,
      "user_id": 27
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-many-memberships-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[OrganizationMembershipCreateManyRequest](#schemaorganizationmembershipcreatemanyrequest)|true|none|
|» organization_memberships|body|[[OrganizationMembershipCreateManyItemInput](#schemaorganizationmembershipcreatemanyiteminput)]|true|The memberships to create. An empty array, an explicit `null` and a missing wrapper are all rejected with 400, and more than 100 items is rejected with 400.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "job_status": {
    "id": "8b726e606741012ffc2d782bcb7848fe",
    "message": "Completed at Fri Apr 13 02:51:53 +0000 2012",
    "progress": 2,
    "results": [
      {
        "action": "create",
        "id": 380,
        "status": "Created",
        "success": true
      }
    ],
    "status": "completed",
    "total": 2,
    "url": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/job_statuses/8b726e606741012ffc2d782bcb7848fe"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-many-memberships-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[JobStatusResponse](#schemajobstatusresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="support-api-search">Search</h1>

## List Search Results

<a id="opIdListSearchResults"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/search?query=https%3A%2F%2Fsubdomain.zendesk.com%2Fapi%2Fv2%2Fsearch%3Fquery%3Dtype%3Aticket%20status%3Aclosed%26sort_by%3Dstatus%26sort_order%3Ddesc' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/search`

Returns the search results. See [Query syntax](#query-syntax) for details on the `query` parameter.

Use the ampersand character (&) to append the `sort_by` or `sort_order` parameters to the URL.

For examples, see [Searching with Zendesk API](/documentation/ticketing/using-the-zendesk-api/searching-with-the-zendesk-api).

This endpoint has its own rate limit. The rate limit counts towards the global API rate limit. See [Limits](#limits).

#### Allowed For

* Agents

#### Pagination

* Offset pagination only

Offset pagination may result in duplicate results when paging. You can also use the
[Export Search Results](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/search/#export-search-results) endpoint, which
uses cursor-based pagination and doesn't return duplicate results. See
[Using cursor pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#using-cursor-pagination) for more information.


#### Errors JSON Format

Errors are represented as JSON objects which have the following keys:

| Name                  | Type                 | Comment
| --------------------- | ---------------------| --------------------
| error                 | string               | The type of error. Examples: "unavailable", "invalid"
| description           | string               |

##### Example Error
```js
{
  "error": "unavailable",
  "description": "Sorry, we could not complete your search query. Please try again in a moment."
}
```


<h3 id="list-search-results-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|true|The search query. See [Query basics](#query-basics) above. For details on the query syntax, see the [Zendesk Support search reference](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408886879258)|
|sort_by|query|string|false|One of `updated_at`, `created_at`, `priority`, `status`, or `ticket_type`. Defaults to sorting by relevance|
|sort_order|query|string|false|One of `asc` or `desc`.  Defaults to `desc`|
|brand_id|query|string \| integer(int64)|false|When brand separation is enabled, scopes user results to the specified brand.<br>This parameter applies only when the account has brand separation enabled<br>(`brand_user_separation_eap`). Non-user document types are unaffected.<br><br>Accepted values:<br><br>* "all" — apply no brand scoping.<br>* 0 — return only account-scoped (brand-less) end users; all agents and admins remain visible.<br>* A numeric brand id — if the brand has user separation enabled, return that<br>  brand's end users plus the agents with membership in that brand and all admins.<br>  If the brand does not have user separation enabled, the request falls back to<br>  account scope (0). A brand id that does not exist on the account matches no users.<br><br>Any other value returns 400 Bad Request, whether or not brand separation is enabled.<br><br>The query keyword form (`query=type:user brand_id:{brand_id}`) continues to work. It<br>matches the brand id as indexed on every document type, so admins match only through<br>their brand memberships, and it does not apply the account-scope fallback for brands<br>without user separation.<br>|
|include|query|string|false|Sideloads to include in the response. Accepts a comma-separated list of values.<br>The available sideloads depend on the search result types.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 1234,
  "facets": null,
  "next_page": "https://foo.zendesk.com/api/v2/search?query=\"type:Group hello\"&sort_by=created_at&sort_order=desc&page=2",
  "previous_page": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "created_at": "2009-05-13T00:07:08Z",
      "id": 211,
      "name": "Hello DJs",
      "result_type": "group",
      "updated_at": "2011-07-22T00:11:12Z",
      "url": "https://foo.zendesk.com/api/v2/groups/211"
    },
    {
      "created_at": "2009-08-26T00:07:08Z",
      "id": 122,
      "name": "Hello MCs",
      "result_type": "group",
      "updated_at": "2010-05-13T00:07:08Z",
      "url": "https://foo.zendesk.com/api/v2/groups/122"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-search-results-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[SearchResponse](#schemasearchresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Export Search Results

<a id="opIdExportSearchResults"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/search/export?query=https%3A%2F%2Fsubdomain.zendesk.com%2Fapi%2Fv2%2Fsearch%3Fquery%3Dtype%3Aticket%20status%3Aclosed%26sort_by%3Dstatus%26sort_order%3Ddesc&filter%5Btype%5D=ticket' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/search/export`

Exports a set of results. See [Query syntax](#query-syntax) for the syntax of the `query` parameter.

Use this endpoint for search queries that will return more than 1000 results. The result set is ordered only by the `created_at` attribute.

The search only returns results of a single object type. The following object types are supported: ticket, organization, user, or group.

You must specify the type in the `filter[type]` parameter. Searches with type in the query string will result in an error.

#### Allowed For

- Agents

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 1000 records per page. The number of results shown in a page is determined by the `page[size]` parameter.

**Note**: You may experience a speed reduction or a timeout if you request 1000 results per page and you have many archived tickets in the results. Try reducing the number of results per page. We recommend 100 results per page.

The cursor specified by the `after_cursor` property in a response expires after one hour.

For more information on cursor-based pagination, see the following articles:

- [Comparing cursor pagination and offset pagination](/documentation/developer-tools/pagination/comparing-cursor-pagination-and-offset-pagination)
- [Paginating through lists using cursor pagination](/documentation/developer-tools/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination)

#### Export Search Results Limits

This API endpoint is rate-limited to 100 requests per minute per account. The limit also counts towards the global API rate limit.

#### Response Format

| Name                  | Type                 | Comment
| --------------------- | ---------------------| --------------------
| links[next]           | string               | URL to the next page of results
| meta[has_more]        | string               | Boolean indicating if there are more results
| meta[after_cursor]    | string               | Cursor object returned from the Search Service
| results               | array                | May consist of tickets, users, groups, or organizations, as specified by the `filter[type]` parameter

The response is similar to the response of `GET /api/v2/search?`, with a few changes:

* `links` - Has the following nested properties: `prev` and `next`. These replace the `next_page` and `prev_page` links. The `prev` property is always null because backward pagination is not supported. The `next` property may include an auto-generated link to the next page of results.
* `meta` - Has the following nested properties: `has_more` and `after_cursor`. The `has_more` property indicates whether the next page has more results. The `after_cursor` property is the cursor used to paginate to the next page. It expires after one hour.

There's no `count` property.


<h3 id="export-search-results-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|true|The search query. See [Query basics](#query-basics) above. For details on the query syntax, see the [Zendesk Support search reference](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408886879258)|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|The number of results shown in a page.|
|page[after]|query|string|false|The cursor token for fetching the next page of results.|
|filter[type]|query|string|true|The object type returned by the export query. Can be `ticket`, `organization`, `user`, or `group`.|
|include|query|string|false|Sideloads to include in the response. Accepts a comma-separated list of values.<br>The available sideloads depend on the search result types.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "facets": null,
  "links": {
    "next": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/search/export?filter%5Btype%5D=ticket&page%5Bafter%%3D%3D&page%5Bsize%5D=100&query=hello%26page%5Bsize%5D%3D100%26filter%5Btype%5D%3Dticket",
    "prev": null
  },
  "meta": {
    "after_cursor": "",
    "before_cursor": null,
    "has_more": true
  },
  "results": []
}
```

<h3 id="export-search-results-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[SearchExportResponse](#schemasearchexportresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

`GET /api/v2/routing/agents/instance_values`

Accepts a comma-separated list of up to 100 agent ids and returns attribute values for each agent in the list.

|page[before]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.before_cursor` value from a previous request.<br>|
|page[after]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.after_cursor` value from a previous request.<br>|
|page[size]|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to return per page|

## Bulk Set Agent Attribute Values Jobs

<a id="opIdBulkSetAgentAttributeValuesJob"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/routing/agents/instance_values/jobs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "job": {
      "action": "upsert",
      "attributes": {
        "attribute_values": [
          {
            "agent_skill_priority": "NORMAL",
            "id": "b376b35a-e38b-11e8-a292-e3b6377c5575"
          }
        ]
      },
      "items": [
        224,
        225
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/routing/agents/instance_values/jobs`

Adds, replaces or removes multiple attributes for up to 100 agents.

#### Allowed For
* Admins
* [Agents in custom role with permission to manage skills](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882)

#### Available Parameters

The request takes a data object with the following properties:
| Name       | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| action     | string | true     | The action to perform on the attribute values. One of the following: "upsert", "update", "delete"                                                                                                                                                 |
| attributes | object | true     | The attribute values to update. See [Attribute Values](#attribute-values). `agent_skill_priority` is optional. If not provided, it keeps the current priority or defaults to `NORMAL` when adding new attribute values.                           |
| items      | array  | true     | The list of agent ids                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

Action can be one of the following:
  * upsert: Adds new attribute values to the agents
  * update: Replaces all the current attribute values of the agents with the new values
  * delete: Removes specified attribute values from the agents

This endpoint returns a `job_status` [JSON object](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#json-format) and queues a background job to do the work. Use the [Show Job Status](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#show-job-status) endpoint to check for the job's completion.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "job": {
    "action": "upsert",
    "attributes": {
      "attribute_values": [
        {
          "agent_skill_priority": "NORMAL",
          "id": "b376b35a-e38b-11e8-a292-e3b6377c5575"
        }
      ]
    },
    "items": [
      224,
      225
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-set-agent-attribute-values-jobs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BulkSkillBasedRoutingAttributeValuesRequest](#schemabulkskillbasedroutingattributevaluesrequest)|true|none|
|» job|body|[BulkSkillBasedRoutingAttributeValueJob](#schemabulkskillbasedroutingattributevaluejob)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "job_status": {
    "id": "V3-25da3dc252ff0f7b63f65d9a8c3ead61",
    "job_type": "Bulk upsert/update/delete agent instance values",
    "message": null,
    "progress": null,
    "results": null,
    "status": "queued",
    "total": 2,
    "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/job_statuses/82de0b0467893ac9fe64f1a99"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "You passed an invalid value for the job.items attribute. Invalid parameter: job.items must be an integer from api/v2/routing/instance_values/update_many_agent_instance_values",
    "title": "Invalid attribute"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-set-agent-attribute-values-jobs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[JobStatusResponse](#schemajobstatusresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[SkillBasedRoutingAttributeValuesError](#schemaskillbasedroutingattributevalueserror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="support-api-macros">Macros</h1>

## List Macros

<a id="opIdListMacros"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/macros \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/macros`

Lists all shared and personal macros available to the current user. For admins, the API returns all macros for the account, including the personal macros of agents and other admins.

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination (recommended)
- Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

#### Allowed For
* Agents


<h3 id="list-macros-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include|query|string|false|A sideload to include in the response. See [Sideloads](#sideloads-2)|
|access|query|string|false|Filter macros by access. Possible values are "personal", "agents", "shared", or "account". The "agents" value returns all personal macros for the account's agents and is only available to admins.|
|active|query|boolean|false|Filter by active macros if true or inactive macros if false|
|category|query|integer|false|Filter macros by category|
|group_id|query|integer(int64)|false|Filter macros by group|
|only_viewable|query|boolean|false|If true, returns only macros that can be applied to tickets. If false, returns all macros the current user can manage. Default is false|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Possible values are "alphabetical", "created_at", "updated_at", "usage_1h", "usage_24h", "usage_7d", or "usage_30d". Defaults to alphabetical|
|sort_order|query|string|false|One of "asc" or "desc". Defaults to "asc" for alphabetical and position sort, "desc" for all others|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort order for cursor pagination. Possible values are "alphabetical", "position", "created_at", or "updated_at".<br>Prefix with a dash (`-`) for descending order. Example: "-updated_at".<br>Usage-based sorts (`sort_by=usage_*`) are not supported with cursor pagination.<br>|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 2,
  "macros": [
    {
      "actions": [],
      "active": true,
      "description": "Sets the ticket status to `solved`",
      "id": 25,
      "position": 42,
      "restriction": {},
      "title": "Close and Save"
    },
    {
      "actions": [],
      "active": false,
      "description": "Adds a `priority` tag to the ticket",
      "id": 26,
      "restriction": {},
      "title": "Assign priority tag"
    }
  ],
  "next_page": null,
  "previous_page": null
}
```

<h3 id="list-macros-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success Response|[MacrosResponse](#schemamacrosresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Show Changes to Ticket

<a id="opIdShowChangesToTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/macros/25/apply \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/macros/{macro_id}/apply`

Returns the changes the macro would make to a ticket. It doesn't actually
change a ticket. You can use the response data in a subsequent API call
to the [Tickets](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/tickets/) endpoint to update the ticket.

The response includes only the ticket fields that would be changed by the
macro. To get the full ticket object after the macro is applied,
see [Show Ticket After Changes](#show-ticket-after-changes).

#### Allowed For
* Agents


<h3 id="show-changes-to-ticket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|macro_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the macro|
|normalize_comment|query|boolean|false|If true, normalizes the newline formatting of the macro's comment to more closely match the formatting produced by the ticket comment editor|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "ticket": {
      "assignee_id": 235323,
      "comment": {
        "body": "Assigned to Agent Uno.",
        "public": false,
        "scoped_body": [
          [
            "channel:all",
            "Assigned to Agent Uno."
          ]
        ]
      },
      "fields": [
        {
          "id": 27642,
          "value": "745"
        },
        {
          "id": 27648,
          "value": false
        },
        {
          "id": 27650,
          "value": null
        }
      ],
      "group_id": 98738
    }
  }
}
```

</aside>


`GET /api/v2/macros/active`

Lists all active shared and personal macros available to the current user.

#### Allowed For
* Agents


<h3 id="list-active-macros-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include|query|string|false|A sideload to include in the response. See [Sideloads](#sideloads-2)|
|access|query|string|false|Filter macros by access. Possible values are "personal", "agents", "shared", or "account". The "agents" value returns all personal macros for the account's agents and is only available to admins.|
|category|query|integer|false|Filter macros by category|
|group_id|query|integer(int64)|false|Filter macros by group|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Possible values are "alphabetical", "created_at", "updated_at", "usage_1h", "usage_24h", "usage_7d", or "usage_30d". Defaults to alphabetical|
|sort_order|query|string|false|One of "asc" or "desc". Defaults to "asc" for alphabetical and position sort, "desc" for all others|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort order for cursor pagination. Possible values are "alphabetical", "position", "created_at", or "updated_at".<br>Prefix with a dash (`-`) for descending order. Example: "-updated_at".<br>|

```json
  "next_page": null,
```

## Create Support Address

<a id="opIdCreateSupportAddress"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/recipient_addresses \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /api/v2/recipient_addresses`

Adds a Zendesk or external support address to your account.

To add a Zendesk address, use the following syntax: `{local-part}@{accountname}.zendesk.com`.
Example: 'sales-team@example.zendesk.com'. The [local-part](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Email_address#Local-part) can be anything you like.

To add an external email address such as help@omniwearshop.com, the email must already exist and you must set up forwarding on your email server. The exact steps depend on your mail server. See [Forwarding incoming email to Zendesk Support](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408836514202). After setting up forwarding, run the [Verify Support Address Forwarding](#verify-support-address-forwarding) endpoint. The address won't work in Zendesk Support until it's been verified.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents with permission to manage channels and extensions. See the system permissions in [Creating custom agent roles](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) in Zendesk help


> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "recipient_address": {
    "brand_id": 123,
    "cname_status": "verified",
    "created_at": "2017-04-02T22:55:29Z",
    "default": false,
    "email": "help@example.zendesk.com",
    "forwarding_status": "waiting",
    "id": 33,
    "name": "Sales",
    "spf_status": "verified",
    "updated_at": "2017-04-02T22:55:29Z"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-support-address-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created response|[SupportAddressResponse](#schemasupportaddressresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Verify Support Address Forwarding

<a id="opIdVerifySupportAddressForwarding"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/recipient_addresses/33/verify \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`PUT /api/v2/recipient_addresses/{support_address_id}/verify`

Sends a test email to the specified support address to verify that email forwarding for the address works. An external support address won't work in Zendesk Support until it's verified.

**Note**: You don't need to verify Zendesk system support addresses.

The endpoint takes the following body: `{"type": "forwarding"}`. The value of the `type` property defaults to "forwarding" if none is specified, but the values "spf" and "dns" are also accepted.

Use this endpoint after [adding](#create-support-address) an external support address to Zendesk Support and setting up forwarding on your email server. See [Forwarding incoming email to Zendesk Support](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408836514202).

The endpoint doesn't return the results of the test. Instead, use the [Show Support Address](#show-support-address) endpoint to check that the `forwarding_status` property is "verified".

Other verification checks can also be performed using this API. These include SPF checks and DNS checks.

When calling the endpoint with `type` set to "spf", it will queries the DNS records to check that the SPF records for Zendesk are present for outbound emails.

When calling the endpoint with `type` set to "dns", it runs checks on your CNAME records to make sure they are set up properly in your DNS.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents with permission to manage channels and extensions. See the system permissions in [Creating custom agent roles](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) in Zendesk help


<h3 id="verify-support-address-forwarding-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|support_address_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the support address|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
""
```

<h3 id="verify-support-address-forwarding-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|include_boundary_indicators|query|boolean|false|When true, includes `has_more` indicator in the cursor pagination response meta.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|include_item_cursors|query|boolean|false|When true, includes cursor values for each item in the cursor pagination response.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|user_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the user|

## Create Identity

<a id="opIdCreateUserIdentity"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/35436/identities \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "identity": {
      "type": "email",
      "value": "foo@bar.com"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/users/{user_id}/identities`

Adds an identity to a user's profile. An agent can add an identity to any user profile.

Supported identity types:

| Type             | Example |
| ---------------- | ------- |
| email            | `{ "type" : "email", "value" : "someone@example.com" }` |
| twitter          | `{ "type" : "twitter", "value" : "screen_name" }` |
| facebook         | `{ "type" : "facebook", "value" : "855769377321" }` |
| google           | `{ "type" : "google", "value" : "example@gmail.com" }` |
| agent_forwarding | `{ "type" : "agent_forwarding", "value" : "+1 555-123-4567" }` |
| phone_number     | `{ "type" : "phone_number", "value" : "+1 555-123-4567" }` |

To create an identity without sending out a verification email, include a `"skip_verify_email": true` property. The `"skip_verify_email": true` property does not apply when updating your own agent profile. A welcome or verification email will be sent regardless of this setting.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "identity": {
    "type": "email",
    "value": "foo@bar.com"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-identity-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brand_id|query|integer(int64)|false|When the account has multiple active brands, sets the active brand context<br>for the created identity. Used to scope verification emails to the correct brand.<br>|
|user_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the user|
|body|body|[UserIdentityCreateRequest](#schemauseridentitycreaterequest)|true|none|
|» identity|body|[UserIdentityCreateInput](#schemauseridentitycreateinput)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "identity": {
    "created_at": "2012-02-12T14:25:21Z",
    "id": 77938,
    "primary": false,
    "type": "twitter",
    "updated_at": "2012-02-12T14:25:21Z",
    "user_id": 13531,
    "value": "cabanaboy",
    "verification_method": "none",
    "verified": false
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-identity-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created response|[UserIdentityResponse](#schemauseridentityresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Update Identity

<a id="opIdUpdateUserIdentity"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/35436/identities/77938 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "identity": {
      "value": "foo@bar.com"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/users/{user_id}/identities/{user_identity_id}`

This endpoint allows you to:

* Set the specified identity as verified (by setting `verified` to "true" or `verification_method` to "low")
* Unverify a verified identity (by setting `verified` to "false" or `verification_method` to "none")
* Update the `value` property of the specified identity

You can't change an identity's `primary` attribute with this endpoint. You must use the [Make Identity Primary](#make-identity-primary) endpoint instead.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "identity": {
    "value": "foo@bar.com"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-identity-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the user|
|user_identity_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the user identity|
|body|body|[UserIdentityUpdateRequest](#schemauseridentityupdaterequest)|false|none|
|» identity|body|[UserIdentityUpdateInput](#schemauseridentityupdateinput) \| null|false|The attributes to change. An explicit null is accepted and is a complete no-op: the whole update<br>branch is skipped, so unlike `{}` it does not unverify and re-mail a non-primary email identity of<br>the account owner.<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[UserIdentityUpdateInput](#schemauseridentityupdateinput)|false|A partial update. Only the properties listed here can be changed on an existing identity - `type` and<br>`primary` cannot, and are ignored if sent. Omitting a property leaves it unchanged.<br><br>One exception to "leaves it unchanged": if the identity is a non-primary email identity of the account<br>owner, sending an `identity` object unverifies the identity and sends a verification email. The<br>trigger is the presence of the object - its contents make no difference, and `verified: true` or<br>`verification_method: low` does not prevent it. Sending `"identity": null` instead of an object is the<br>one way to avoid it, because the whole update branch is then skipped. The account owner's primary<br>email identity cannot be updated at all.<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|null|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "identity": {
    "created_at": "2011-07-20T22:55:29Z",
    "deliverable_state": "deliverable",
    "id": 35436,
    "primary": true,
    "type": "email",
    "updated_at": "2011-07-20T22:55:29Z",
    "user_id": 135,
    "value": "someone@example.com",
    "verification_method": "low",
    "verified": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-identity-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[UserIdentityResponse](#schemauseridentityresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

`DELETE /api/v2/users/{user_id}/identities/{user_identity_id}`

Deletes the identity for a given user.
In certain cases, a phone number associated with an identity is still visible on the user profile after the identity has been deleted via API. You can remove the phone number from the user profile by updating the `phone` attribute of the user to an empty string. See [Update User via API](/api-reference/ticketing/users/users/#update-user) for details and examples.

Deleting identities with type `messaging` could break messaging functionality. For example, an agent may stop being able to send messages via the messaging channel.

## Verify Identity

<a id="opIdVerifyUserIdentity"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/35436/identities/77938/verify \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`PUT /api/v2/users/{user_id}/identities/{user_identity_id}/verify`

Sets the specified identity as verified.

For security reasons, you can't use this endpoint to update the email identity of the account owner. To verify the person's identity, send a verification email. See [Verifying the account owner's email address](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408828975130) in Zendesk help.

If [automatic mapping of users to organizations using the email domain](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882246298-Creating-organizations#topic_nxl_vdt_bc) is enabled and the user is not already a member of an organization, they will be automatically added to the organization associated with the email domain once the email identity is verified.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


<h3 id="verify-identity-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the user|
|user_identity_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the user identity|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "identity": {
    "created_at": "2012-02-12T14:25:21Z",
    "id": 77938,
    "primary": false,
    "type": "twitter",
    "updated_at": "2012-02-12T14:25:21Z",
    "user_id": 13531,
    "value": "cabanaboy",
    "verified": false
  }
}
```

<h3 id="verify-identity-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[UserIdentityResponse](#schemauseridentityresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="support-api-activity-stream">Activity Stream</h1>

## List Activities

<a id="opIdListActivities"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/activities \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/activities`

Lists ticket activities in the last 30 days affecting the agent making the request.
Also sideloads the following arrays of user records:

- actors - All actors involved in the listed activities
- users - All users involved in the listed activities

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination (recommended)
- Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


<h3 id="list-activities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|since|query|string|false|A UTC time in ISO 8601 format to return ticket activities since said date.|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|include|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of sideloads to include. Supported values: `fields_metadata`.<br>|

## Count Activities

<a id="opIdCountActivities"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/activities/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/activities/count`

Returns an approximate count of ticket activities in the last 30 days affecting the agent making the request. If the count exceeds 100,000, the count will return a cached result. This cached result will update every 24 hours.

The `count[refreshed_at]` property is a timestamp that indicates when the count was last updated.

**Note**: When the count exceeds 100,000, `count[refreshed_at]` may occasionally be null.
This indicates that the count is being updated in the background, and `count[value]` is limited to 100,000 until the update is complete.

#### Allowed For
* Agents

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 102
  }
}
```

<h3 id="count-activities-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Count of ticket activities|[ActivitiesCountResponse](#schemaactivitiescountresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

`GET /api/v2/group_slas/policies`

#### Availability

* Accounts on the Professional and Enterprise plans

#### Allowed For

* Admins

```json
{
  "count": 1,

    {
      "description": "For low priority tickets, the Tier 1 group will solve or reassign the ticket in one hour.",
      "filter": {
        "all": [

      ],
      "position": 3,
      "title": "Incidents",

  "previous_page": null
```

|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - the account does not have the operational level agreements feature, which requires both a Service Level Agreements subscription and the group SLAs subscription feature, or the requester is not an admin|Inline|

## Create Group SLA Policy

<a id="opIdCreateGroupSLAPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/group_slas/policies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "group_sla_policy": {
      "description": "Tier 1 Group SLA",
      "filter": {
        "all": [
          {
            "field": "group_id",
            "operator": "includes",
            "value": [
              6
            ]
          }
        ]
      },
      "policy_metrics": [
        {
          "business_hours": true,
          "metric": "group_ownership_time",
          "priority": "normal",
          "target": 1800
        },
        {
          "business_hours": false,
          "metric": "group_ownership_time",
          "priority": "urgent",
          "target": 600
        }
      ],
      "position": 3,
      "title": "Tier 1 Group SLA"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/group_slas/policies`

#### Allowed For

* Admins

```json
    "description": "Tier 1 Group SLA",
```

`PUT /api/v2/group_slas/policies/{group_sla_policy_id}`

#### Allowed For

<h3 id="update-group-sla-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|group_sla_policy_id|path|string|true|The id of the Group SLA policy|
|body|body|[GroupSLAPolicyUpdateRequest](#schemagroupslapolicyupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» group_sla_policy|body|[GroupSLAPolicyUpdateInput](#schemagroupslapolicyupdateinput)|true|Only the supplied properties are updated. Each property is applied only when its value is present, so a<br>blank or null value leaves the current value in place rather than clearing it, and an empty object is<br>rejected. `filter` and `policy_metrics` are the exceptions: when either is supplied it **replaces** what<br>the policy already has, so a partial value destroys the conditions or targets it leaves out<br>|

```json
    "filter": {
      "all": [
        {

          "operator": "includes",
          "value": [
            6,
            7
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "id": "01H078CBDY28BZG7P6BONY09DN",
    "policy_metrics": [
      {
        "business_hours": false,
        "metric": "group_ownership_time",
        "priority": "normal",
        "target": 1800
      }
    ],
    "position": 3,
    "title": "Urgent Incidents",
    "url": "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/group_slas/policies/01H078CBDY28BZG7P6BONY09DN"
  }
}
```

|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - the request was made without valid credentials|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - the account does not have the operational level agreements feature, which requires both a Service Level Agreements subscription and the group SLAs subscription feature, or the requester is not an admin|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable Entity - the reorder arguments are invalid. The `error` value is the message of the raised error|Inline|

## List All Ticket Audits

<a id="opIdListTicketAudits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/ticket_audits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/ticket_audits`

Returns ticket audits. Archived tickets are not included in the response. Use the [List Audits for a Ticket](#list-audits-for-a-ticket) endpoint to
retrieve audit records for an archived ticket. To learn more about archived tickets, see [About archived tickets](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408887617050).

This endpoint should not be used for capturing change data. When continually chasing the tail of a cursor, some records will be skipped. For this use case, use the [Incremental Ticket Event Export API](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/incremental_exports/#incremental-ticket-event-export).

#### Allowed For

* Admins


<h3 id="list-all-ticket-audits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[before]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.before_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.<br>|
|page[after]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.after_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.<br>|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Specifies how many records to be returned in the response. You can specify up to 100 records per page.|

> Example responses

## List Audits for a Ticket

<a id="opIdListAuditsForTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/123456/audits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/audits`

Lists the audits for a specified ticket.

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination (recommended)
- Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

**Note**: Audits for [Archived Tickets](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408887617050) do not support pagination for this endpoint.

#### Allowed for

* Agents


<h3 id="list-audits-for-a-ticket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|include|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of sideloads to include in the response.<br>|
|include_boundary_indicators|query|boolean|false|When true, includes `has_more` indicator in the cursor pagination response meta.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|include_item_cursors|query|boolean|false|When true, includes cursor values for each item in the cursor pagination response.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|filter_events|query|[string]|false|Filter audit events by type. Use the format `filter_events[]=Type1&filter_events[]=Type2`.|
|sort_order|query|string|false|Sort order. Defaults to "asc"|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_order|asc|
|sort_order|desc|

> 200 Response

## Count Audits for a Ticket

<a id="opIdCountAuditsForTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/123456/audits/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/audits/count`

Returns an approximate count of audits for a specified ticket. If the count exceeds 100,000, the count will return a cached result.  This cached result will update every 24 hours.

The `count[refreshed_at]` property is a timestamp that indicates when the count was last updated.

**Note**: If the total number of audits for a ticket exceeds 100,000, this endpoint returns a count of 100,000 with a `count[refreshed_at]` value of null. This value is cached for 24 hours, during which any requests returns the same count and timestamp. After 24 hours, the endpoint temporarily shows the same count again before providing an updated total.

#### Allowed for

* Agents


<h3 id="count-audits-for-a-ticket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 18
  }
}
```

<h3 id="count-audits-for-a-ticket-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Count of audits on a ticket|[TicketAuditsCountResponse](#schematicketauditscountresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="support-api-ticket-metric-events">Ticket Metric Events</h1>

## List Ticket Metric Events

<a id="opIdListTicketMetricEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/ticket_metric_events?start_time=1332034771' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/incremental/ticket_metric_events`

Returns ticket metric events that occurred on or after the start time.

Cursor pagination returns a maximum of 100 records per page. Events are listed in chronological order.

If the results are not paginated, events will be returned as a time-based incremental export.

See [Time-based incremental exports](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api#time-based-incremental-exports).

#### Pagination
* Cursor pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

#### Allowed For

* Admins

<h3 id="list-ticket-metric-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_time|query|integer|true|The Unix UTC epoch time of the oldest event you're interested in. Example: 1332034771.|
|include_changes|query|boolean|false|This optional parameter enhances incremental data retrieval, delivering a consistent and accurate representation of data changes.|
|exclude_deleted|query|boolean|false|When true, excludes ticket metric events for deleted tickets. Use this to avoid<br>receiving events for tickets that are deleted.|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 3,
  "end_time": 1603716792,
  "next_page": "https://company.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/ticket_metric_events?start_time=1603716792",
  "ticket_metric_events": [
    {
      "id": 926232157301,
      "instance_id": 0,
      "metric": "agent_work_time",
      "ticket_id": 155,
      "time": "2020-10-26T12:53:12Z",
      "type": "measure"
    },
    {
      "id": 926232757371,
      "instance_id": 1,
      "metric": "agent_work_time",
      "ticket_id": 155,
      "time": "2020-10-26T12:53:12Z",
      "type": "activate"
    },
    {
      "id": 926232927415,
      "instance_id": 0,
      "metric": "pausable_update_time",
      "ticket_id": 155,
      "time": "2020-10-26T12:53:12Z",
      "type": "measure"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "You do not have access to this page. Please contact the account owner of this help desk for further help.",
    "title": "Forbidden"
  }
}
```

<h1 id="support-api-brands">Brands</h1>

## List Brands

<a id="opIdListBrands"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/brands \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/brands`

Returns a list of all brands for your account sorted by name.

#### Allowed for

* Admins
* Agents with the `assign_tickets_to_any_brand` permission can list all brands for the account
* Agents without the `assign_tickets_to_any_brand` permission can only list brands they are members of

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

<h3 id="list-brands-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Cursor pagination parameters using deepObject format.<br><br>Use `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` to paginate through results.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br><br>(Marked internal-only because only used with traditional offset pagination,<br>which is only supported for internal/bime requests)<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|assignable_from|query|integer(int64)|false|Filters brands to only those assignable from the specified brand ID. A brand-separated brand is only assignable to itself, while account-separated brands are assignable to all other account-separated brands.|
|include_deleted|query|boolean|false|When true, includes soft-deleted brands in the response.|
|include|query|string|false|Use `permissions` to include a top-level array of per-brand permissions with `brand_id`, `can_update`, and `can_delete`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|include|permissions|

## List Brand Agent Memberships

<a id="opIdListBrandAgents"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/brand_agents \

```

`GET /api/v2/brand_agents`

Returns a list of all brand agent memberships for your account.


#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination (recommended)
* Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

#### Allowed For:

* Admins


<h3 id="list-brand-agent-memberships-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "brand_agents": [
    {
      "brand_id": 12,
      "created_at": "2009-05-13T00:07:08Z",
      "id": "4",
      "updated_at": "2011-07-22T00:11:12Z",
      "user_id": 29
    },
    {
      "brand_id": 3,
      "created_at": "2012-03-13T22:01:32Z",
      "id": "49",
      "updated_at": "2012-03-13T22:01:32Z",
      "user_id": 155
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-brand-agent-memberships-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response|[BrandAgentsResponse](#schemabrandagentsresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Create Brand Agent Membership

<a id="opIdCreateBrandAgent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/brand_agents \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "brand_agent": {
      "brand_id": 88,
      "user_id": 72
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/brand_agents`

Creates a brand agent membership, granting the agent access to the brand.


Returns `422` if the user is not an agent, the brand does not belong to the
account, or a membership for the same user and brand already exists.

#### Allowed For:

* Admins


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "brand_agent": {
    "brand_id": 88,
    "user_id": 72
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-brand-agent-membership-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BrandAgentCreateRequest](#schemabrandagentcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» brand_agent|body|object|true|none|
|» » brand_id|body|integer(int64)|true|The id of a brand|
|» » user_id|body|integer(int64)|true|The id of an agent|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "brand_agent": {
    "brand_id": 88,
    "created_at": "2012-04-03T12:34:01Z",
    "id": "461",
    "updated_at": "2012-04-03T12:34:01Z",
    "user_id": 72
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-brand-agent-membership-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created response|[BrandAgentResponse](#schemabrandagentresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## List Brand User Migrations

<a id="opIdListBrandUserMigrations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/brands/360002783572/user_migrations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/brands/{brand_id}/user_migrations`

Returns a list of brand user migrations for a specific brand, sorted by
creation date in descending order.

The response is not paginated; all migrations for the brand are returned.

#### Allowed For

* Admins

#### Availability

Available on accounts with Department Spaces.


<h3 id="list-brand-user-migrations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brand_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the brand|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "user_migrations": [
    {
      "account_id": 1234567,
      "active": true,
      "brand_id": 360002783572,
      "completed_at": null,
      "direction": {
        "from": {
          "scope": "account"
        },
        "to": {
          "scope": "brand"
```

## Create Brand User Migration

<a id="opIdCreateBrandUserMigration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/brands/360002783572/user_migrations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "user_migration": {
      "direction": {
        "from": {
          "scope": "account"
        },
        "to": {
          "scope": "brand"
        }
      },
      "mode": "manual"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/brands/{brand_id}/user_migrations`

Creates a brand user migration for the specified brand. Only one active
migration may exist per account at a time.

The `direction.from.scope` must match the brand's current user separation
setting, and the from/to scopes must differ.

#### Allowed For

* Admins

#### Availability

Available on accounts with Department Spaces.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_migration": {
    "direction": {
      "from": {
        "scope": "account"
      },
      "to": {
        "scope": "brand"
      }
    },
    "mode": "manual"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-brand-user-migration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brand_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the brand|
|body|body|[BrandUserMigrationCreateRequest](#schemabrandusermigrationcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» user_migration|body|object|true|none|
|» » direction|body|[BrandUserMigrationDirection](#schemabrandusermigrationdirection)|true|none|
|» » mode|body|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » mode|manual|
|» » mode|auto|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "user_migration": {
    "account_id": 1234567,
    "active": true,
    "brand_id": 360002783572,
    "completed_at": null,
    "direction": {
      "from": {
        "scope": "account"
      },
      "to": {
        "scope": "brand"
      }
    },
    "id": "01J8X4Q3Z9K7M2N5P8R6T0V1WY",
    "jobs": [
      {
        "id": "V3-validation",
        "type": "validation"
      }
    ],
    "mode": "manual",
    "status": "in_progress",
    "updated_at": "2025-09-15T10:30:00Z",
    "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/brands/360002783572/user_migrations/01J8X4Q3Z9K7M2N5P8R6T0V1WY"
  }
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "description": "an active migration already exists for this account",
  "error": "Active migration"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "details": {
    "property1": [
      {
        "description": "string"
      }
    ],
    "property2": [
      {
        "description": "string"
      }
    ]
  },
  "error": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-brand-user-migration-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Migration created|[BrandUserMigrationResponse](#schemabrandusermigrationresponse)|
|409|Conflict|Concurrent requests for migration creation were received. An active<br>migration already exists for the account; retrying after the existing<br>migration completes or is aborted should succeed. The normal failure<br>for an existing active migration is 422.<br>|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed. Returned when the account has an active migration<br>that cannot be superseded, when `direction.from.scope` does not match<br>the brand's current user separation setting, or when the from/to<br>scopes do not differ.<br><br>A reversal is supported without error: creating a migration in the<br>exact opposite direction of an active `in_progress` migration aborts<br>that migration and creates the new one.<br>|Inline|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|error|string|false|none|none|

|details|object|false|none|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|[object]|false|none|none|
|» » description|string|false|none|none|

## List Deleted Users

<a id="opIdListDeletedUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/deleted_users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/deleted_users`

Returns deleted users, including permanently deleted users.

If the results contains permanently deleted users, the users' properties
that normally contain personal data, such as `email` and `phone`,
are null. The `name` property is "Permanently Deleted User".

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination (recommended)
* Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


<h3 id="list-deleted-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|limit|query|integer|false|Legacy cursor pagination page size. Defaults to the maximum of 100|
|order|query|string|false|Legacy cursor pagination sort order. One of `asc` or `desc` (case-insensitive)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|asc|
|order|desc|
|order|ASC|
|order|DESC|

> Example responses

## Permanently Delete User

<a id="opIdPermanentlyDeleteUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/deleted_users/35436 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/deleted_users/{deleted_user_id}`

Before permanently deleting a user, you must delete the user first. See [Delete User](/api-reference/ticketing/users/users/#delete-user).

WARNING: Permanently deleting a user deletes all of their information. This information is not recoverable.

#### Permanent user deletion rate limit

You can permanently delete 700 users every 10 minutes.
The rate limiting mechanism behaves as described in
[Rates Limits](/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/#monitoring-your-request-activity) in the API introduction.
Zendesk recommends that you obey the Retry-After header values.

#### Allowed For

* Admins and [agents in custom roles with permission](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) to manage end users or team members


<h3 id="permanently-delete-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|deleted_user_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the deleted user|

```json
  "deleted_user": {
    "active": false,
    "created_at": "2019-08-26T02:10:24Z",
    "email": "david@email.com",

    "locale": "en-US",
    "locale_id": 1,
    "name": "David",
    "organization_id": 360000000008,
    "phone": null,
    "photo": null,
    "role": "end-user",
    "separation": {
      "brand_id": 123,
      "scope": "brand"
    },

}
```

## Count Deleted Users

<a id="opIdCountDeletedUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/deleted_users/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/deleted_users/count`

Returns an approximate count of deleted users, including permanently deleted users. If the count exceeds 100,000, it is updated every 24 hours.

The response includes a `refreshed_at` property in a `count` object that contains a timestamp indicating when the count was last updated.

**Note**: When the count exceeds 100,000, `count[refreshed_at]` may occasionally be null.
This indicates that the count is being updated in the background, and `count[value]` is limited to 100,000 until the update is complete.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 13
  }
}
```

<h3 id="count-deleted-users-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[CountResponse](#schemacountresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Count Organization Users

<a id="opIdCountOrganizationUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/organizations/16/users/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/organizations/{organization_id}/users/count`

Returns an approximate count of users for a specific organization. If the count exceeds 100,000, it is updated every 24 hours.

The response includes a `refreshed_at` property in a `count` object that contains a timestamp indicating when the count was last updated.

**Note**: When the count exceeds 100,000, the `refreshed_at` property may occasionally be null.
This indicates that the count is being updated in the background. The `count` object's `value` property is limited to 100,000 until the update is complete.

#### Allowed For

* Admins, Agents and Light Agents


<h3 id="count-organization-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role|query|string|false|Filters the results by role. Possible values are "end-user", "agent", "admin", or a custom role name<br>|
|role[]|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by more than one role using the format `role[]={role}&role[]={role}`<br>|
|permission_set|query|integer(int64)|false|For custom roles which is available on the Enterprise plan and above. You can only filter by one role ID per request|
|organization_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of an organization|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 102
  }
}
```

<h3 id="count-organization-users-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[CountResponse](#schemacountresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h3 id="list-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role|query|string|false|Filters the results by role. Possible values are "end-user", "agent", "admin", or a custom role name<br>|
|role[]|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by more than one role using the format `role[]={role}&role[]={role}`<br>|
|permission_set|query|integer(int64)|false|For custom roles which is available on the Enterprise plan and above. You can only filter by one role ID per request|
|external_id|query|string|false|List users by external id. External id has to be unique for each user under the same account.|
|include|query|string|false|Sideloads to include in the response. Accepts a comma-separated list of values.<br>See [Sideloading](/documentation/api-basics/working-with-data/side_loading/#supported-endpoints).<br>|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|include_boundary_indicators|query|boolean|false|When true, includes `has_more` indicator in the cursor pagination response meta.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|include_item_cursors|query|boolean|false|When true, includes cursor values for each item in the cursor pagination response.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|brand_id|query|string \| integer(int64)|false|When brand separation is enabled, scopes the listing to users belonging to<br>the specified brand. Only applicable when the account has brand separation enabled.<br><br>Accepted values:<br><br>* "all" — return all users across all brands (no brand filtering applied).<br>* 0 — return only account-scoped (brand-less) end users plus all agents and admins.<br>* A numeric brand id — if the brand has user separation enabled, return<br>  end users belonging to that brand plus the agents with membership in<br>  that brand and all admins. If the brand does not have user separation<br>  enabled, the request falls back to account scope (0).<br><br>If `brand_id` is omitted, the account's `brand_user_separation_scope_query_default`<br>[brand setting](/api-reference/ticketing/account-configuration/account_settings/#brands)<br>decides the scope. If it's set to `"error"`, the request is rejected with `400 Bad Request`.<br>Agent Workspace, other signed-in Zendesk sessions and internal Zendesk requests always use `all`. The resolved<br>scope is returned in the `X-Zendesk-Brand-Id-Scope-Resolved` response header.<br>|
