## Delete User

<a id="opIdDeleteUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/35436 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/users/{user_id}`

Deletes the user and associated records from the account.

**Warning**:

* Deleted users are not recoverable.
* Both agents and administrators can soft delete users in the agent interface in Zendesk Support. Agents with permission can delete end users, while administrators can delete all users except the account owner.

To comply with GDPR, a further step is needed. See [Permanently Delete User](/api-reference/ticketing/users/users/#permanently-delete-user).

#### Allowed For

* Admins and [agents in custom roles with permission](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) to manage end users or team members


<h3 id="delete-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the user|

```json
  "user": {
    "active": false,
    "id": 9873843,
    "name": "Roger Wilco II",
    "separation": {
      "brand_id": 123,
      "scope": "brand"
    }
  }
}
```

## Merge End Users

<a id="opIdMergeEndUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/35436/merge \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "user": {
      "id": 35436
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/users/{user_id}/merge`

Merges the end user specified in the path parameter into the existing end user specified in the request body.

Any two end users can be merged with the exception of end users created by sharing agreements.

To be eligible for merging, the user in the path parameter must be a requester on 10,000 or fewer tickets. Otherwise, the merge will be blocked.

Agents, admins, and users with more than 10,000 requested tickets cannot be merged.

For more information about how user data is merged, see [Merging a user's duplicate account](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408887695898) in Zendesk help.

#### Allowed For

* Admins or agents with permission to edit end users


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user": {
    "id": 35436
  }
}
```

|user_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the user|
|body|body|[UserRequest](#schemauserrequest)|true|none|
|» user|body|[UserInput](#schemauserinput)|true|none|

```json
    "id": 35436,
    "name": "Johnny Agent",
    "separation": {

    }
  }
}
```

## Update a User's Suspension

<a id="opIdUpdateUserSuspension"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/35436/suspension \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "suspension": {
      "additional_comments": "Updated comments",
      "reason": "impersonating_others",
      "suspended_channels": [
        "all"
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/users/{user_id}/suspension`

Updates the suspension details for a user. `suspended_channels` can be updated when [the messaging channel suspension feature](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/10575252020250-Announcing-user-suspension-from-messaging-channels-only) is enabled on the account.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* [Agents in custom roles with permission](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) to manage end users or team members

#### OAuth Scopes

Requires one of the following OAuth scopes: `users:write` or `write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "suspension": {
    "additional_comments": "Updated comments",
    "reason": "impersonating_others",
    "suspended_channels": [
      "all"
    ]
  }
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the user|
|body|body|[SuspensionUpdateRequest](#schemasuspensionupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» suspension|body|object|true|none|
|» » additional_comments|body|string|false|none|
|» » reason|body|string|false|none|
|» » suspended_channels|body|[string]|false|Only accepted when the account has the messaging channel suspension feature enabled. See [Announcing user suspension from messaging channels only](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/10575252020250-Announcing-user-suspension-from-messaging-channels-only).|

|» » reason|impersonating_others|
|» » reason|extended_leave|
|» » reason|parental_time_off|
|» » reason|sabbatical|
|» » reason|other_reason|
|» » suspended_channels|all|
|» » suspended_channels|messaging|

`POST /api/v2/users/{user_id}/suspension`

Creates a suspension record for a user. A user can be suspended on specific channels via `suspended_channels`, when [the messaging channel suspension feature](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/10575252020250-Announcing-user-suspension-from-messaging-channels-only) is enabled on the account.

#### Allowed For

* [Agents in custom roles with permission](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) to manage end users or team members

#### OAuth Scopes

Requires one of the following OAuth scopes: `users:write` or `write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "suspension": {

    "reason": "impersonating_others"
```

|body|body|[SuspensionCreateRequest](#schemasuspensioncreaterequest)|true|none|
|» suspension|body|object|true|none|
|» » additional_comments|body|string|false|none|
|» » reason|body|string|false|none|

|» » suspended_channels|body|[string]|false|Only accepted when the account has the messaging channel suspension feature enabled. See [Announcing user suspension from messaging channels only](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/10575252020250-Announcing-user-suspension-from-messaging-channels-only).|

## Autocomplete Users

<a id="opIdAutocompleteUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/autocomplete \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/users/autocomplete`

Returns an array of users whose name starts with the value specified in the `name` parameter.
It only returns users with no foreign identities.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


<h3 id="autocomplete-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|string|false|The name to search for the user. You must specify either `name` or `phone`.<br>|
|phone|query|string|false|The phone number to search for the user. You must specify either `name` or `phone`.<br>|
|filter|query|string|false|Filter to apply to autocomplete results.<br>|
|field_id|query|string|false|The id of a lookup relationship field.  The type of field is determined<br>by the `source` param<br>|
|source|query|string|false|If a `field_id` is provided, this specifies the type of the field.<br>For example, if the field is on a "zen:user", it references a field on a user<br>|
|include|query|string|false|Sideloads to include in the response. Accepts a comma-separated list of values.<br>See [Sideloading](/documentation/api-basics/working-with-data/side_loading/#supported-endpoints).<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of results to return.|
|brand_id|query|string \| integer(int64)|false|When brand separation is enabled, scopes the autocomplete results to users<br>belonging to the specified brand. Only applicable when the account has brand separation enabled.<br><br>Accepted values:<br><br>* "all" — search all users across all brands (no brand filtering applied).<br>* 0 — restrict the autocomplete results to account-scoped (brand-less) users only.<br>* A numeric brand id — if the brand has user separation enabled, autocomplete<br>  returns only end users belonging to that brand. Agents and admins are not included<br>  in the results when filtering by a specific brand. If the brand does not have user<br>  separation enabled, the request falls back to account scope (0).<br><br>If `brand_id` is omitted, the account's `brand_user_separation_scope_query_default`<br>[brand setting](/api-reference/ticketing/account-configuration/account_settings/#brands)<br>decides the scope. If it's set to `"error"`, the request is rejected with `400 Bad Request`.<br>Agent Workspace, other signed-in Zendesk sessions and internal Zendesk requests always use `all`. The resolved<br>scope is returned in the `X-Zendesk-Brand-Id-Scope-Resolved` response header.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter|assignable|
|filter|requester|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "users": [
    {
      "id": 35436,
      "name": "Robert Jones",
      "notes": "sigil issue",
      "separation": {
        "brand_id": 123,
        "scope": "brand"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": 9873843,
      "name": "Terry Gilliam",
      "separation": {
        "brand_id": 123,
        "scope": "brand"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Invalid brand_id parameter: 999999999"
}
```

## Count Users

<a id="opIdCountUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/users/count`

Returns an approximate count of users. If the count exceeds 100,000, it is updated every 24 hours.

The response includes a `refreshed_at` property in a `count` object that contains a timestamp indicating when the count was last updated.

**Note**: When the count exceeds 100,000, the `refreshed_at` property may occasionally be null.
This indicates that the count is being updated in the background. The `count` object's `value` property is limited to 100,000 until the update is complete.

#### Allowed For

* Admins, Agents and Light Agents


<h3 id="count-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role|query|string|false|Filters the results by role. Possible values are "end-user", "agent", "admin", or a custom role name<br>|
|role[]|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by more than one role using the format `role[]={role}&role[]={role}`<br>|
|permission_set|query|integer(int64)|false|For custom roles which is available on the Enterprise plan and above. You can only filter by one role ID per request|
|brand_id|query|string \| integer(int64)|false|When brand separation is enabled, scopes the count to users belonging to<br>the specified brand. Only applicable when the account has brand separation enabled.<br><br>Accepted values:<br><br>* "all" — count all users across all brands (no brand filtering applied).<br>* 0 — count only account-scoped (brand-less) end users plus all agents and admins.<br>* A numeric brand id — if the brand has user separation enabled, count<br>  end users belonging to that brand plus the agents with membership in<br>  that brand and all admins. If the brand does not have user separation<br>  enabled, the request falls back to account scope (0).<br><br>If `brand_id` is omitted, the account's `brand_user_separation_scope_query_default`<br>[brand setting](/api-reference/ticketing/account-configuration/account_settings/#brands)<br>decides the scope. If it's set to `"error"`, the request is rejected with `400 Bad Request`.<br>Agent Workspace, other signed-in Zendesk sessions and internal Zendesk requests always use `all`. The resolved<br>scope is returned in the `X-Zendesk-Brand-Id-Scope-Resolved` response header.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 102
  }
}
```

<h3 id="count-users-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[CountResponse](#schemacountresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Create Many Users

<a id="opIdCreateManyUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/create_many \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "users": [
      {
        "agent_brand_ids": [
          8119246973690,
          8119246973691,
          8119246973692
        ],
        "email": "roge@example.org",

        "name": "Woger Rilco",
        "role": "admin"
      }
    ]
```

`POST /api/v2/users/create_many`

Accepts an array of up to 100 user objects.

**Note**: To protect the data in your Zendesk account, bulk user imports are not enabled by default in Zendesk accounts. The account owner or an admin must contact [Zendesk Customer Support](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408843597850) to enable the imports. A 403 Forbidden
error is returned if data imports are not enabled.

#### Allowed For

* Admins and [agents in custom roles with permission](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) to manage end users or team members

#### Specifying an organization

You can assign a user to an existing organization by setting an
`organization_id` property in the user object.

#### Response

Only a certain number of jobs can be queued or running at the same time. See [Job limit](/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/#job-limit) for more information.

## Create Or Update User

<a id="opIdCreateOrUpdateUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/create_or_update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "user": {
      "agent_brand_ids": [
        8119246973690,
        8119246973691,
        8119246973692
      ],
      "custom_role_id": 123456,
      "email": "roge@example.org",
      "identities": [
        {
          "type": "email",
          "value": "test@user.com"
        },
        {
          "type": "twitter",
          "value": "tester84"
        }
      ],
      "name": "Roger Wilco",
      "organization": {
        "name": "VIP Customers"
      },
      "role": "agent"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/users/create_or_update`

Creates a user if the user does not already exist, or updates an existing user
identified by e-mail address or external ID.

If you don't specify a role parameter, the new user is assigned the role of end user.

If you need to create users without sending out a verification email, include a `"skip_verify_email": true` property in the body.

#### External ID Case Sensitivity

When providing an external id to identify an existing user to update, the search for the user record is not case sensitive.

However, if an existing user is found, the system will update the user's external id to match the case of the external id used to find the user.

#### Response Status Code

- If the user already exists in Zendesk, a successful request returns a 200 OK status code.
- If the user does not exist in Zendesk and is created, the request returns a 201 Created status code.
- In both cases, the API responds with a JSON body containing the full user object, which includes the user's id and the fully-resolved URL to the user resource.

Example response:
```json
{
  "user": {
    "id": 8929981612030,
    "url": "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/8929981612030",
  ...
  }
}
```

#### Allowed For

* Admins and [agents in custom roles with permission](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) to manage end users or team members


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user": {
    "agent_brand_ids": [
      8119246973690,
      8119246973691,
      8119246973692
    ],
    "custom_role_id": 123456,
    "email": "roge@example.org",
    "identities": [
      {
        "type": "email",
        "value": "test@user.com"
      },
      {
        "type": "twitter",
        "value": "tester84"
      }
    ],
    "name": "Roger Wilco",
    "organization": {
      "name": "VIP Customers"
    },
    "role": "agent"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[UserRequest](#schemauserrequest)|true|none|
|» user|body|[UserInput](#schemauserinput)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "user": {
    "custom_role_id": 123456,
    "email": "roge@example.org",
    "id": 9873843,
    "name": "Roger Wilco",
    "organization_id": 57542,
    "role": "agent",
    "role_type": 0,
    "separation": {
      "brand_id": 123,
      "scope": "brand"
    }
  }
}
```

> 201 Response

```json
  "user": {
    "custom_role_id": 123456,
    "email": "roge@example.org",
    "id": 9873843,

    "organization_id": 57542,

}
```

`POST /api/v2/users/create_or_update_many`

Accepts an array of up to 100 user objects. For each user, the user is created if it does not
already exist, or the existing user is updated.

**Note**: To protect the data in your Zendesk account, bulk user imports are not enabled by default in Zendesk accounts. The account owner or an admin must contact [Zendesk Customer Support](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408843597850) to enable the imports. A 403 Forbidden
error is returned if data imports are not enabled.

Each individual user object can identify an existing user by `email` or by `external_id`.

This endpoint returns a `job_status` [JSON object](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#json-format) and queues a background job to do the work. ## Bulk Delete Users

<a id="opIdDestroyManyUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/destroy_many \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/users/destroy_many`

Accepts a comma-separated list of up to 100 user ids.

The request takes an `ids` or an `external_ids` query parameter.

#### Allowed for

* Admins

#### Response

This endpoint returns a `job_status` [JSON object](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#json-format) and queues a background job to do the work. Use the [Show Job Status](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#show-job-status) endpoint to check for the job's completion. Only a certain number of jobs can be queued or running at the same time. See [Job limit](/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/#job-limit) for more information.


<h3 id="bulk-delete-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|string|false|Id of the users to delete. Comma separated|
|external_ids|query|string|false|External Id of the users to delete. Comma separated|
|brand_id|query|string \| integer(int64)|false|Scopes the deletion of users matched by `external_ids` to a specific brand<br>or to account-scoped (brand-less) users. Only applicable when the account<br>has brand separation enabled (`brand_user_separation_eap`); ignored<br>otherwise so existing numeric callers continue to behave as before.<br><br>Accepted values:<br><br>* `0` — restrict the lookup to account-scoped (brand-less) users only.<br>* A numeric brand id — restrict to that brand. Brands without<br>  `user_separation` enabled collapse to account scope (`0`).<br><br>Rejected with `400 Bad Request`:<br><br>* `all` — cross-brand deletion is not supported on this endpoint.<br>* Any other non-numeric string.<br>* A numeric brand id that does not exist on the account.<br>* Combining `brand_id` with `ids` (use `external_ids` instead — `ids` are<br>  globally unique so brand scoping is meaningless).<br><br>When `external_ids` is provided without `brand_id`, the request defaults<br>to account scope (`0`).<br><br>When forwarded to the bulk-delete background job, the resolved brand id<br>is always passed as an Integer (`0` for account scope; the brand id<br>otherwise) for backward compatibility with existing job consumers.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "job_status": {
    "id": "82de0b044094f0c67893ac9fe64f1a99",
    "message": "Completed at 2018-03-08 10:07:04 +0000",
    "progress": 2,
    "results": [
      {
        "action": "delete",
        "id": 244,
        "status": "Deleted",
        "success": true
      },
      {
        "action": "delete",
        "id": 245,
        "status": "Deleted",
        "success": true
      }
    ],
    "status": "completed",
    "total": 2,
    "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/job_statuses/82de0b0467893ac9fe64f1a99"
  }
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[JobStatusResponse](#schemajobstatusresponse)|

The endpoint returns [user information](/api-reference/ticketing/users/users/) and an `authenticity_token`.

Zendesk API calls made by end users from a Zendesk help center must include `authenticity_token` in the `X-CSRF-Token` HTTP header. This helps prevent [cross-site request forgery (CSRF)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-site_request_forgery) attacks.

## Update Current User Settings

<a id="opIdUpdateCurrentUserSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/me/settings \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "settings": {
      "admin_center": {
        "has_admin_center_side_nav_open": true
      },
      "lotus": {
        "agent_workspace_theme_preference": "1",
        "keyboard_shortcuts_enabled": true,
        "show_onboarding_tooltips": false
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/users/me/settings`

Updates the settings for the currently authenticated user. This includes UI preferences for onboarding, tooltips, keyboard shortcuts, theme preferences, and other feature toggles.

Settings are grouped into:
- **Support**: Support UI preferences (onboarding, tooltips, shortcuts, theme)
- **admin_center**: Admin Center UI preferences (navigation, onboarding)
- **shared_views_order**: Optional array of view IDs for custom ordering
- **agent_home_pinned_views**: Optional ordered array of view IDs pinned in the Agent Home sidebar (max 8)

Only the specified settings will be updated. Other settings will remain unchanged.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "settings": {
    "admin_center": {
      "has_admin_center_side_nav_open": true
    },
    "lotus": {
      "agent_workspace_theme_preference": "1",
      "keyboard_shortcuts_enabled": true,
      "show_onboarding_tooltips": false
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-current-user-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[UserSettingsUpdateRequest](#schemausersettingsupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» settings|body|object|true|User settings to update|
|» » admin_center|body|object|false|Admin Center UI settings for onboarding and preferences|
|» » » has_admin_center_side_nav_open|body|boolean|false|Whether the Admin Center side navigation is open|
|» » agent_home_pinned_views|body|[integer]|false|Ordered list of view IDs pinned in the Agent Home sidebar (max 8)|
|» » lotus|body|object|false|Lotus UI settings for onboarding, tooltips, and feature preferences|
|» » » agent_workspace_theme_preference|body|string|false|Agent workspace theme preference (0=light, 1=dark, 2=system)|
|» » » agent_workspace_theme_preference_for_conversation_panel|body|string|false|Theme preference for conversation panel (0=light, 1=dark, 2=system)|
|» » » keyboard_shortcuts_enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable keyboard shortcuts in Lotus|
|» » » macro_shortcuts_enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable macro shortcuts in Lotus|
|» » » show_onboarding_tooltips|body|boolean|false|Show tooltips for first-time user|
|» » shared_views_order|body|[integer]|false|Order of shared views (array of view IDs)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » » agent_workspace_theme_preference|0|
|» » » agent_workspace_theme_preference|1|
|» » » agent_workspace_theme_preference|2|
|» » » agent_workspace_theme_preference_for_conversation_panel|0|
|» » » agent_workspace_theme_preference_for_conversation_panel|1|
|» » » agent_workspace_theme_preference_for_conversation_panel|2|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "settings": {
    "admin_center": {
      "has_admin_center_side_nav_open": true
    },
    "lotus": {
      "agent_workspace_theme_preference": "0",
      "agent_workspace_theme_preference_for_conversation_panel": "0",
      "keyboard_shortcuts_enabled": false,
      "macro_shortcuts_enabled": false,
      "show_onboarding_tooltips": true,

      "show_welcome_dialog": true,

    }
  }
}
```

## Search Users

<a id="opIdSearchUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/users/search`

Returns an array of users who meet the search criteria.

Returns up to 100 records per page to a maximum of 10,000 records per query. See [Using offset pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#using-offset-pagination).

#### Pagination

* Offset pagination only

See [Using Offset Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#using-offset-pagination).

#### Allowed For

* Agents


<h3 id="search-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number for offset-based pagination (non-negative integer).|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|query|query|string|false|The `query` parameter supports the Zendesk search syntax for more advanced<br>user searches. It can specify a partial or full value of any<br>user property, including name, email address, notes, or phone. Example:<br>`query="jdoe"`.<br>See the [Search API](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/search/).<br>|
|external_id|query|string|false|The `external_id` parameter does not support the search syntax. It only accepts ids.<br>|
|brand_id|query|string \| integer(int64)|false|When brand separation is enabled, scopes the search to users belonging to<br>the specified brand. Only applicable when the account has brand separation enabled.<br><br>Accepted values:<br><br>* "all" — search all users across all brands (no brand filtering applied).<br>* 0 — restrict the search to account-scoped (brand-less) users only.<br>* A numeric brand id — if the brand has user separation enabled, search<br>  returns end users belonging to that brand plus the agents with membership<br>  in that brand and all admins. If the brand does not have user separation<br>  enabled, the request falls back to account scope (0).<br><br>If `brand_id` is omitted, the account's `brand_user_separation_scope_query_default`<br>[brand setting](/api-reference/ticketing/account-configuration/account_settings/#brands)<br>decides the scope. If it's set to `"error"`, the request is rejected with `400 Bad Request`.<br>Agent Workspace, other signed-in Zendesk sessions and internal Zendesk requests always use `all`. The resolved<br>scope is returned in the `X-Zendesk-Brand-Id-Scope-Resolved` response header.<br>|
|include|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of sideloads to include in the response.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "users": [
    {
      "id": 35436,
      "name": "Robert Jones",
      "notes": "sigil issue",
      "separation": {
        "brand_id": 123,
        "scope": "brand"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": 9873843,
      "name": "Terry Gilliam",
      "separation": {
        "brand_id": 123,
        "scope": "brand"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="search-users-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[UsersResponse](#schemausersresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Show Many Users

<a id="opIdShowManyUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/show_many \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/users/show_many`

Accepts a comma-separated list of up to 100 user ids or external ids.

#### Allowed For:

* Agents


<h3 id="show-many-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|string|false|Accepts a comma-separated list of up to 100 user ids.<br>|
|external_ids|query|string|false|Accepts a comma-separated list of up to 100 external ids.<br>|
|include_deleted|query|boolean|false|If true, returns inactive or deleted users.<br>|
|brand_id|query|integer(int64)|false|When brand separation is enabled and `external_ids` is provided, scopes the lookup to<br>users belonging to the specified brand. Only applicable when the account<br>has brand separation enabled. Omitting `brand_id` always uses account<br>scope (0), regardless of account or Agent Workspace defaults.<br><br>Accepted values when used with `external_ids`:<br><br>* 0 — restrict the lookup to account-scoped (brand-less) users only.<br>* A numeric brand id — if the brand has user separation enabled, return<br>  only users belonging to that brand; account-scoped agents and admins<br>  are excluded. If the brand does not have user separation enabled, the<br>  request resolves to account scope (0), including account-scoped agents<br>  and end users.<br>* "all" — invalid for `show_many` lookups.<br><br>When `ids` is provided instead of `external_ids`, numeric brand scopes<br>are accepted but filtering is not applied because user IDs are globally<br>unique. `brand_id=all` is rejected consistently with the other many-user<br>endpoints.<br>|
|include|query|string|false|Sideloads to include in the response. Accepts a comma-separated list of values.<br>See [Sideloading](/documentation/api-basics/working-with-data/side_loading/#supported-endpoints).<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "users": [
    {
      "id": 345678,
      "name": "Johnny Appleseed",
      "separation": {
        "brand_id": 123,
        "scope": "brand"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": 901234,
      "name": "Rupert Root",
      "separation": {
        "brand_id": 123,
        "scope": "brand"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Invalid brand_id parameter: all"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[UsersResponse](#schemausersresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - `brand_id=all` is invalid|Inline|

<h3 id="show-many-users-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|string|false|none|none|

## Update Many Users

<a id="opIdUpdateManyUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/update_many \
```

`PUT /api/v2/users/update_many`

```json
  "user": {
    "organization_id": 1
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-many-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|string|false|Id of the users to update. Comma separated|
|external_ids|query|string|false|External Id of the users to update. Comma separated|
|brand_id|query|integer(int64)|false|Scopes the bulk update of users matched by `external_ids` to a specific brand<br>or to account-scoped (brand-less) users. Only applicable when the account<br>has brand separation enabled (`brand_user_separation_eap`). Ignored<br>otherwise so existing numeric callers continue to behave as before.<br><br>Accepted values:<br><br>* 0 — restrict the lookup to account-scoped (brand-less) users only.<br>* A numeric brand id — restrict to that brand. Brands without<br>  `user_separation` enabled collapse to account scope (0).<br><br>Rejected with "400 Bad Request":<br><br>* "all" — cross-brand bulk update is not supported on this endpoint.<br>* Any other non-numeric string.<br>* A numeric brand id that does not exist on the account.<br>* Combining `brand_id` with `ids` (use `external_ids` instead — `ids` are<br>  globally unique so brand scoping is meaningless).<br><br>When `external_ids` is provided without `brand_id`, the request defaults<br>to account scope (0).<br>|
|body|body|[UserUpdateRequest](#schemauserupdaterequest) \| [UsersRequest](#schemausersrequest)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[UserUpdateRequest](#schemauserupdaterequest)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[UsersRequest](#schemausersrequest)|false|none|

<h1 id="support-api-ticket-forms">Ticket Forms</h1>

## List Ticket Forms

<a id="opIdListTicketForms"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/ticket_forms \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/ticket_forms`

Returns a list of all ticket forms for your account if accessed as an admin or agent. End users only see ticket forms that have `end_user_visible` set to true.

#### Allowed For

* Anyone


<h3 id="list-ticket-forms-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|query|boolean|false|true returns active ticket forms; false returns inactive ticket forms. If not present, returns both|
|end_user_visible|query|boolean|false|true returns ticket forms where `end_user_visible`; false returns ticket forms that are not end-user visible. If not present, returns both|
|fallback_to_default|query|boolean|false|true returns the default ticket form when the criteria defined by the parameters results in a set without active and end-user visible ticket forms|
|form_type|query|string|false|Filter ticket forms by type. Use 'standard' for regular ticket forms, 'service_catalog' for service catalog forms, or 'all' to return all form types|
|associated_to_brand|query|boolean|false|true returns the ticket forms of the brand specified by the url's subdomain|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|include_boundary_indicators|query|boolean|false|When true, includes `has_more` indicator in the cursor pagination response meta.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|include_item_cursors|query|boolean|false|When true, includes cursor values for each item in the cursor pagination response.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|locale|query|string|false|Locale to use for the ticket form names. If not specified, the default locale is used.|

## Show Many Ticket Forms

<a id="opIdShowManyTicketForms"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/ticket_forms/show_many?ids=1%2C2%2C3' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/ticket_forms/show_many`

Takes an `ids` query parameter that accepts a comma-separated list of up to 100 ticket form ids. This endpoint is used primarily by the [mobile SDK](/documentation/classic-web-widget-sdks/) and the [Web Widget](/api-reference/widget/introduction/).

#### Allowed For

* Anyone


<h3 id="show-many-ticket-forms-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|string|true|IDs of the ticket forms to be shown|
|include_boundary_indicators|query|boolean|false|When true, includes `has_more` indicator in the cursor pagination response meta.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|include_item_cursors|query|boolean|false|When true, includes cursor values for each item in the cursor pagination response.<br><br>Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).<br>|
|active|query|boolean|false|true returns active ticket forms; false returns inactive ticket forms. If not present, returns both|
|end_user_visible|query|boolean|false|true returns ticket forms where `end_user_visible`; false returns ticket forms that are not end-user visible. If not present, returns both|
|fallback_to_default|query|boolean|false|true returns the default ticket form when the criteria defined by the parameters results in a set without active and end-user visible ticket forms|
|associated_to_brand|query|boolean|false|true returns the ticket forms of the brand specified by the url's subdomain|

<h1 id="support-api-suspended-tickets">Suspended Tickets</h1>

## List Suspended Tickets

<a id="opIdListSuspendedTickets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/suspended_tickets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/suspended_tickets`

#### Allowed For

* Admins and [agents in custom roles with permission](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) to manage suspended tickets on Enterprise plans
* Unrestricted agents on all other plans

#### Sorting

You can sort the tickets with the `sort_by` and `sort_order` query string parameters.

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).


<h3 id="list-suspended-tickets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort_by|query|string|false|The field to sort the suspended tickets by. One of "author_email", "cause", "created_at", or "subject"|
|sort_order|query|string|false|The order in which to sort the suspended tickets.  This can take value `asc` or `desc`.|

## Recover Suspended Ticket

<a id="opIdRecoverSuspendedTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/suspended_tickets/35436/recover \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`PUT /api/v2/suspended_tickets/{id}/recover`

**Note**: During recovery, the API sets the requester to the authenticated agent who called the API, not the original requester. This prevents the ticket from being re-suspended after recovery. To preserve the original requester, use the [Recover Multiple Suspended Tickets](#recover-multiple-suspended-tickets) endpoint with the single ticket.

This endpoint does not queue an asynchronous job that can be tracked from [Job Statuses](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/). Instead, it processes the request with a synchronous response.
   - If the recovery is successful, it returns a 200 with the restored ticket as a `ticket` object in the response.
   - If the recovery fails, it returns a 422 with no response body.

#### Allowed For

* Admins and [agents in custom roles with permission](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) to manage suspended tickets on Enterprise plans
* Unrestricted agents on all other plans


<h3 id="recover-suspended-ticket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|id of the suspended ticket|

## Bulk Recover Suspended Tickets

<a id="opIdBulkRecoverSuspendedTickets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/suspended_tickets/bulk_recover?ids=1%2C2%2C3' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "author": {
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "id": 12345
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/suspended_tickets/bulk_recover`

Enqueues a bulk job to recover multiple suspended tickets. Returns a job status that can be tracked via the Job Statuses API.

Unlike the [Recover Multiple Suspended Tickets](#recover-multiple-suspended-tickets) endpoint which processes tickets synchronously, this endpoint queues an asynchronous job for processing large batches.

#### Allowed For

* Admins and [agents in custom roles with permission](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) to manage suspended tickets on Enterprise plans
* Unrestricted agents on all other plans


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "author": {
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "id": 12345
  }
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-recover-suspended-tickets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|string|true|Comma-separated list of suspended ticket IDs to recover|
|body|body|object|false|Optional author information for recovered tickets|
|» author|body|object|false|none|
|» » email|body|string(email)|false|Email address to identify the author|
|» » id|body|integer(int64)|false|User ID to set as the author of recovered tickets|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "job_status": {
    "id": "8b726e606741012ffc2d782bcb7848fe",
    "message": null,
    "progress": 0,
    "results": null,
    "status": "queued",
    "total": 3,
    "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/job_statuses/8b726e606741012ffc2d782bcb7848fe.json"
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Invalid parameters"
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-recover-suspended-tickets-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Job successfully enqueued|[JobStatusResponse](#schemajobstatusresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid request - missing or malformed parameters|Inline|

<h3 id="bulk-recover-suspended-tickets-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **422**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Export Suspended Tickets

<a id="opIdExportSuspendedTickets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/suspended_tickets/export \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /api/v2/suspended_tickets/export`

Exports a list of suspended tickets for the Zendesk Support instance. To export the list, the endpoint enqueues a job to create a CSV file with the data. When done, Zendesk sends the requester an email containing a link to the CSV file. In the CSV, tickets are sorted by the update timestamp in ascending order.

 #### Allowed For

 * Admins and [agents in custom roles with permission](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882#topic_cxn_hig_bd) to manage suspended tickets on Enterprise plans
 * Unrestricted agents on all other plans

 #### Rate limits

 Limited to one request per minute and up to one million records in return. The rate-limiting mechanism behaves identically to the one described in [Usage limits](/api-reference/ticketing/account-configuration/usage_limits/#monitoring-your-request-activity).
 We recommend using the `Retry-After` header value as described in [Catching errors caused by rate limiting](/documentation/ticketing/using-the-zendesk-api/best-practices-for-avoiding-rate-limiting#catch).


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "export": {
    "status": "enqueued",
    "view_id": "suspended"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="export-suspended-tickets-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Ok|[SuspendedTicketsExportResponse](#schemasuspendedticketsexportresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="support-api-satisfaction-ratings">Satisfaction Ratings</h1>

## List Satisfaction Ratings

<a id="opIdListSatisfactionRatings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/satisfaction_ratings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/satisfaction_ratings`

#### Allowed For
* Admins

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination (recommended)
* Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

#### Filters

| Parameter  | Value
| ---------- | -----
| score      | offered, unoffered, received, received\_with\_comment, received\_without\_comment,<br/>good, good\_with\_comment, good\_without\_comment,<br/>bad, bad\_with\_comment, bad\_without\_comment
| start_time | Time of the oldest satisfaction rating, as a [Unix epoch time](https://www.epochconverter.com/)
| end_time   | Time of the most recent satisfaction rating, as a [Unix epoch time](https://www.epochconverter.com/)

If you specify an unqualified score such as `good`, the results include all the records with and without comments.

Examples:

* `/api/v2/satisfaction_ratings?score=bad`
* `/api/v2/satisfaction_ratings?score=bad&start_time=1498151194`
* `/api/v2/satisfaction_ratings?start_time=1340384793&end_time=1371920793`


<h3 id="list-satisfaction-ratings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "satisfaction_ratings": [
    {
      "assignee_id": 135,
      "comment": "Awesome support!",
      "created_at": "2011-07-20T22:55:29Z",
      "group_id": 44,
      "id": 35436,
      "requester_id": 7881,
      "score": "good",
      "ticket_id": 208,
      "updated_at": "2011-07-20T22:55:29Z",
      "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/satisfaction_ratings/35436"
    },
    {
      "assignee_id": 136,
      "comment": "Awesome support!",
      "created_at": "2012-02-01T04:31:29Z",
      "group_id": 44,
      "id": 120447,
      "requester_id": 7881,
      "score": "good",
      "ticket_id": 209,
      "updated_at": "2012-02-02T10:32:59Z",
      "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/satisfaction_ratings/120447"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Count Satisfaction Ratings

<a id="opIdCountSatisfactionRatings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/satisfaction_ratings/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/satisfaction_ratings/count`

Returns an approximate count of satisfaction ratings in the account. If the count exceeds 100,000, the count will return a cached result. This cached result will update every 24 hours.

The `count[refreshed_at]` property is a timestamp that indicates when the count was last updated.

**Note**: When the count exceeds 100,000, `count[refreshed_at]` may occasionally be null.
This indicates that the count is being updated in the background, and `count[value]` is limited to 100,000 until the update is complete.

#### Allowed For
* Admins

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 102
  }
}
```

<h3 id="count-satisfaction-ratings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Count of satisfaction ratings|[SatisfactionRatingsCountResponse](#schemasatisfactionratingscountresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/35436/satisfaction_rating \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "satisfaction_rating": {
      "comment": "Awesome support.",
      "score": "good"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/satisfaction_rating`

Creates a CSAT rating for a solved ticket, or for a ticket that was previously
solved and then reopened.

Only the end user listed as the ticket requester can create a satisfaction rating for the ticket.

Only "good" and "bad" are valid values for the score when creating a rating. Other states, like "offered", are not valid and will result in a 422 error.

#### Allowed For

* End user who requested the ticket

The end user must be a verified user.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "satisfaction_rating": {
    "comment": "Awesome support.",
    "score": "good"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-satisfaction-rating-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the ticket|
|body|body|[SatisfactionRatingRequest](#schemasatisfactionratingrequest)|true|none|
|» satisfaction_rating|body|[SatisfactionRatingInput](#schemasatisfactionratinginput)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "satisfaction_rating": [
    {
      "assignee_id": 135,
      "comment": "Awesome support!",
      "created_at": "2011-07-20T22:55:29Z",
      "group_id": 44,
      "id": 35436,
      "requester_id": 7881,
      "score": "good",
      "ticket_id": 208,
      "updated_at": "2011-07-20T22:55:29Z",
      "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/satisfaction_ratings/35436"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Redact Chat Comment Attachment

<a id="opIdRedactChatCommentAttachment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/chat_file_redactions/123456 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "chat_id": "2109.10502823.Sjuj2YrBpXwei",
    "chat_indexes": [
      0,
      1
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/chat_file_redactions/{ticket_id}`

Permanently removes one or more chat attachments from a chat ticket.

**Note**: This does not work on active chats. For chat tickets that predate March 2020, consider using [Redact Ticket Comment In Agent Workspace](#redact-ticket-comment-in-agent-workspace).

#### Allowed For

- Agents

[Agent Workspace](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408821259930) must enabled for the account. Deleting tickets must be enabled for agents.

#### Request Body Properties

| Name         | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------ | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| chat_id      | string  | true     | The `chat_id` in the `ChatStartedEvent` event in the ticket audit. See [Ticket Audits](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket_audits)                                                                                                                 |
| chat_indexes | array   | false    | The array of `chat_index` in the `ChatFileAttachment` event in the ticket audit. See [Ticket Audits](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket_audits). Mandatory if `message_ids` is not used                                                           |
| message_ids  | array   | false    | The array of `message_id` in the `ChatFileAttachment` event in the ticket audit that is part of a `ChatStartedEvent` history. Used when redacting a ChatFileAttachment that is part of a conversation history. Mandatory if `chat_indexes` is not used |

To get the required body properties, make a request to the [Ticket Audits](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket_audits) endpoint. Example response:

```http
Status 200 OK
{
  "audits": [
    "events": [
      {
        "id": 1932802680168,
        "type": "ChatStartedEvent",
        "value": {
          "visitor_id": "10502823-16EkM3T6VNq7KMd",
          "chat_id": "2109.10502823.Sjuj2YrBpXwei",
          "history": [
            {
              "chat_index": 0,
              "type": "ChatFileAttachment",
              "filename": "image1.jpg"
            },
            {
              "chat_index": 1,
              "type": "ChatFileAttachment",
              "filename": "image2.jpg"
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  ]
}
```


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "chat_id": "2109.10502823.Sjuj2YrBpXwei",
  "chat_indexes": [
    0,
    1
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="redact-chat-comment-attachment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chat_id|body|string|true|The `chat_id` in the `ChatStartedEvent` event in the ticket audit.|
|» chat_indexes|body|[integer]|false|The array of `chat_index` in the `ChatFileAttachment` event in the ticket audit. Mandatory if `message_ids` is not used.|
|» message_ids|body|[string]|false|The array of `message_id` in the `ChatFileAttachment` event in the ticket audit that is part of a `ChatStartedEvent` history. Used when redacting a ChatFileAttachment that is part of a conversation history. Mandatory if `chat_indexes` is not used.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "chat_event": {
    "id": 1932802680168,
    "type": "ChatStartedEvent",
    "value": {
      "chat_id": "2109.10502823.Sjuj2YrBpXwei",
      "history": [
        {
          "chat_index": 0,
          "filename": "redacted.txt",
          "type": "ChatFileAttachment"
        },
        {
          "chat_index": 1,
          "filename": "redacted.txt",
          "type": "ChatFileAttachment"
        }
      ],
      "visitor_id": "10502823-16EkM3T6VNq7KMd"
    }
  }
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|200|OK|Success response|[TicketChatCommentRedactionResponse](#schematicketchatcommentredactionresponse)|

## Redact Chat Comment

<a id="opIdRedactChatComment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/chat_redactions/123456 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "chat_id": "2109.10502823.Sjuj2YrBpXwei",
    "chat_index": 0,
    "text": "My ID number is <redact>847564</redact>!"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/chat_redactions/{ticket_id}`

Permanently removes words or strings from a chat ticket's comment. 

Wrap `<redact>` tags around the content in the chat comment you want redacted. Example: 

```json
{
  "text": "My ID number is <redact>847564</redact>!"
}
```

The characters contained in the tag will be replaced by the ▇ symbol.

**Note**: This does not work on active chats. For chat tickets that predate March 2020, consider using [Redact Ticket Comment In Agent Workspace](#redact-ticket-comment-in-agent-workspace).

**Limitations**:

- Redaction is a synchronous process. For archived tickets, only one redaction request can be processed at a time per ticket. Concurrent redaction requests on the same archived ticket will receive a 409 Conflict response with a `Retry-After` header indicating how many seconds to wait before retrying (up to 30 seconds). The lock is released immediately when the redaction completes. This limit does not apply to requests from the Zendesk UI.

#### Allowed For

- Agents

[Agent Workspace](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408821259930) must enabled for the account. Deleting tickets must be enabled for agents.

#### Request Body Properties

| Name                     | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------ | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| chat_id                  | string  | true     | The `chat_id` in the `ChatStartedEvent` event in the ticket audit. See [Ticket Audits](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket_audits)                                                                                                            |
| chat_index               | integer | false    | The `chat_index` in the `ChatMessage` event in the ticket audit. See [Ticket Audits](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket_audits). Mandatory if `message_id` is not used                                                                       |
| message_id               | string  | false    | The `message_id` of the `ChatMessage` event in the ticket audit that is part of a `ChatStartedEvent` history. Used when redacting a ChatMessage that is part of a conversation history. Mandatory if `chat_index` is not used                     |
| text                     | string  | true     | The `message` in the `ChatMessage` event in the ticket audit. See [Ticket Audits](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket_audits).  Wrap `message` with `<redact>` tags                                                                           |

To get the required body properties, make a request to the [Ticket Audit](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket_audits) endpoint. Example response:

```http
Status 200 OK
{
  "audits": [
    "events": [
      {
        "id": 1932802680168,
        "type": "ChatStartedEvent",
        "value": {
          "visitor_id": "10502823-16EkM3T6VNq7KMd",
          "chat_id": "2109.10502823.Sjuj2YrBpXwei",
          "history": [
            {
              "chat_index": 0,
              "type": "ChatMessage",
              "message": "My ID number is 847564!"
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  ]
}
```


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "chat_id": "2109.10502823.Sjuj2YrBpXwei",
  "chat_index": 0,
  "text": "My ID number is <redact>847564</redact>!"
}
```

<h3 id="redact-chat-comment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chat_id|body|string|true|The `chat_id` in the `ChatStartedEvent` event in the ticket audit.|
|» chat_index|body|integer|false|The `chat_index` in the `ChatMessage` event in the ticket audit. Mandatory if `message_id` is not used.|
|» message_id|body|string|false|The `message_id` of the `ChatMessage` event in the ticket audit that is part of a `ChatStartedEvent` history. Used when redacting a ChatMessage that is part of a conversation history. Mandatory if `chat_index` is not used.|
|» text|body|string|true|The `message` in the `ChatMessage` event in the ticket audit. Wrap `message` with `<redact>` tags.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "chat_event": {
    "id": 1932802680168,
    "type": "ChatStartedEvent",
    "value": {
      "chat_id": "2109.10502823.Sjuj2YrBpXwei",
      "history": [
        {
          "chat_index": 0,
          "message": "My ID number is ▇▇▇▇!",
          "type": "ChatMessage"
        }
      ],
      "visitor_id": "10502823-16EkM3T6VNq7KMd"
    }
  }
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "description": "A redaction is already in progress for this ticket. Please retry in 15 seconds.",
  "error": "ConflictError"
}
```

<h3 id="redact-chat-comment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[TicketChatCommentRedactionResponse](#schematicketchatcommentredactionresponse)|
|409|Conflict|Conflict - A redaction is already in progress for this archived ticket|[TicketRedactionConflictError](#schematicketredactionconflicterror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|409|Retry-After|integer||Number of seconds to wait before retrying the request|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## Redact Ticket Comment In Agent Workspace

<a id="opIdRedactTicketCommentInAgentWorkspace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/comment_redactions/35436 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "html_body": "<div class=\"zd-comment\" dir=\"auto\">My ID number is <redact>847564</redact>!</div>",
    "ticket_id": 100
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/comment_redactions/{ticket_comment_id}`

Redaction allows you to permanently remove words, strings, or attachments from a ticket comment.

In the `html_body` of the comment, wrap the content you want redacted in `<redact>` tags. Example:

```json
{
  "html_body": "<div class=\"zd-comment\" dir=\"auto\">My ID number is <redact>847564</redact>!</div>",
  "ticket_id":100
}
```

The characters in the redact tag will be replaced by the ▇ symbol.

To redact HTML elements such inline images, anchor tags, and links, add the `redact` tag attribute to the element as well as the `<redact>` tag to inner text, if any. Example: 

`<a href="http://example.com" redact><redact>some link</redact></a>`

The `redact` attribute only redacts the tag. Any inner text will be left behind if not enclosed in a `<redact>` tag.

Redaction is permanent and can not be undone. Data is permanently deleted from Zendesk servers with no way to recover it.

This endpoint provides all the same functionality that the [Redact String in Comment](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket_comments/#redact-string-in-comment) endpoint provides, plus:

- Redaction of comments in closed tickets

- Redaction of comments in archived tickets

- Redaction of formatted text (bold, italics, hyperlinks)

**Limitations**:

- When content is redacted from an email comment, the content is also redacted from the original email through a background job. It may take a while for the changes to be completed.

- Redaction is a synchronous process. For archived tickets, only one redaction request can be processed at a time per ticket. Concurrent redaction requests on the same archived ticket will receive a 409 Conflict response with a `Retry-After` header indicating how many seconds to wait before retrying (up to 30 seconds). The lock is released immediately when the redaction completes. This limit does not apply to requests from the Zendesk UI.

**Note**: We recommend using this endpoint instead of the [Redact String in Comment](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket_comments/#redact-string-in-comment) endpoint, which will eventually be deprecated.

#### Allowed For

- Agents

[Agent Workspace](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408821259930) must be enabled on the account. For professional accounts, deleting tickets must be enabled for agents. On Enterprise accounts, you can assign agents to a custom role with permissions to redact ticket content.

#### Rate limits

When enabled, this endpoint has a rate limit shared by all agents and tickets in an account. The burst allowance holds up to 400 requests and replenishes at 9 requests per second, up to that capacity. Requests from the Zendesk UI are exempt from this endpoint-specific limit.

Applicable account API limits also apply and can reduce throughput. Account API rate-limit headers do not report this endpoint-specific allowance.

Requests that exceed this limit receive a 429 Too Many Requests response. Wait for the number of seconds specified in the returned `Retry-After` header before retrying. A retry can still be rate limited.

#### Request Body Properties

| Name                     | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------| ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| ticket_id                | integer | true     | The ID of the ticket                                                                                                                             |
| html_body                | string  | false    | The `html_body` of the comment containing `<redact>` tags or `redact` attributes                                           |
| external_attachment_urls | array   | false    | Array of attachment URLs belonging to the comment to be redacted. See [`content_url` property of Attachment](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket-attachments/) |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "html_body": "<div class=\"zd-comment\" dir=\"auto\">My ID number is <redact>847564</redact>!</div>",
  "ticket_id": 100
}
```

<h3 id="redact-ticket-comment-in-agent-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_comment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket comment|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» external_attachment_urls|body|[string]|false|Array of attachment URLs belonging to the comment to be redacted.|
|» html_body|body|string|false|The `html_body` of the comment containing `<redact>` tags or `redact` attributes.|
|» ticket_id|body|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "comment": {
    "attachments": [],
    "author_id": 123,
    "id": 100,
    "plain_body": "My ID number is ▇▇▇▇!",
    "public": true,
    "type": "Comment"
  }
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "description": "A redaction is already in progress for this ticket. Please retry in 15 seconds.",
  "error": "ConflictError"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "description": "Comment redaction rate limit exceeded. Please retry later.",
  "error": "TooManyRequests"
}
```

<h3 id="redact-ticket-comment-in-agent-workspace-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[TicketCommentResponse](#schematicketcommentresponse)|
|409|Conflict|Conflict - A redaction is already in progress for this archived ticket|[TicketRedactionConflictError](#schematicketredactionconflicterror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too Many Requests - Comment redaction rate limit exceeded|Inline|

<h3 id="redact-ticket-comment-in-agent-workspace-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **429**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|error|string|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|409|Retry-After|integer||Number of seconds to wait before retrying the request|
|429|Retry-After|integer||Number of seconds to wait before retrying the request|

## List Comments

<a id="opIdListTicketComments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/123456/comments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/comments`

Returns the comments added to the ticket.

Each comment may include a `content_url` for an attachment or a `recording_url` for a voice comment that points to a file that may be hosted externally. For security reasons, take care not to inadvertently send Zendesk authentication credentials to third parties when attempting to access these files. See [Working with url properties](/documentation/api-basics/best-practices/working-with-url-properties/).

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination (recommended)
- Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

#### Sorting

By default, comments are sorted by creation date in ascending order.

When using cursor pagination, use the following parameter to change the sort order:

| Name   | Type   | Required | Comments
| ------ | ------ | -------- | --------
| `sort` | string | no       | Possible values are "created_at" (ascending order) or "-created_at" (descending order)

When using offset pagination, use the following parameters to change the sort order:

| Name         | Type   | Required | Comments
| ------------ | ------ | -------- | --------
| `sort_order` | string | no       | One of `asc`, `desc`. Defaults to `asc`

#### Allowed For

* Agents


<h3 id="list-comments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include_inline_images|query|boolean|false|Default is false. When true, inline images are also listed as attachments in the response|
|include|query|string|false|Accepts "users". Use this parameter to list email CCs by side-loading users. Example: `?include=users`. **Note**: If the comment source is email, a deleted user will be represented as the CCd email address. If the comment source is anything else, a deleted user will be represented as the user name.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|
|sort_order|query|string|false|Sort order. Defaults to "asc"|
|sort|query|string|false|Cursor pagination sort value. Use `created_at` for ascending order or `-created_at` for descending order|
|page|query|object|false|Cursor-based pagination parameters (JSON:API style).<br><br>Supports nested parameters:<br>- `page[size]` - Number of records per page (default varies by endpoint, typically 100)<br>- `page[after]` - Cursor token to fetch records after this position<br>- `page[before]` - Cursor token to fetch records before this position<br><br>Example: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=eyJvIjoiaWQiLCJ2IjoiYVFFPSJ9`<br>|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_order|asc|
|sort_order|desc|
|sort|created_at|
|sort|-created_at|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "comments": [
    {
      "attachments": [
        {
          "content_type": "text/plain",
          "content_url": "https://company.zendesk.com/attachments/crash.log",
          "file_name": "crash.log",
          "id": 498483,
          "size": 2532,
```

## Redact String in Comment

<a id="opIdRedactStringInComment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/123456/comments/35436/redact \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "text": "987-65-4320"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/comments/{ticket_comment_id}/redact`

Permanently removes words or strings from a ticket comment. Specify the string to redact in an object with a `text` property. Example: `'{"text": "987-65-4320"}'`. The characters of the word or string are replaced by the ▇ symbol.

If the comment was made by email, the endpoint also attempts to redact the string from the original email retained by Zendesk for audit purposes.

**Note**: If you use the rich text editor, support for redacting formatted text (bold, italics, hyperlinks) is limited.

Redaction is permanent. You can't undo the redaction or see *what* was removed. Once a ticket is closed, you can no longer redact strings from its comments.

To use this endpoint, the "Agents can delete tickets" option must be enabled in the Zendesk Support admin interface at **Admin** > **Settings** > **Agents**.

#### Allowed For

* Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "text": "987-65-4320"
}
```

<h3 id="redact-string-in-comment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|
|ticket_comment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket comment|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» text|body|string|true|The word or string to permanently redact from the comment|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "comment": {
    "author_id": 1,
    "id": 35436,
    "plain_body": "My social security number is ▇▇▇▇!",
    "type": "Comment"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="redact-string-in-comment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[TicketCommentResponse](#schematicketcommentresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Count Ticket Comments

<a id="opIdCountTicketComments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/123456/comments/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/comments/count`

Returns an approximate count of the comments added to the ticket. If the count exceeds 100,000, the count will return a cached result.  This cached result will update every 24 hours.

The `count[refreshed_at]` property is a timestamp that indicates when the count was last updated.

**Note**: When the count exceeds 100,000, `count[refreshed_at]` may occasionally be null.
This indicates that the count is being updated in the background, and `count[value]` is limited to 100,000 until the update is complete.

#### Allowed For
* Agents

<h3 id="count-ticket-comments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": {
    "refreshed_at": "2020-04-06T02:18:17Z",
    "value": 12
  }
}
```

<h3 id="count-ticket-comments-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Count of ticket comments|[TicketCommentsCountResponse](#schematicketcommentscountresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## List Requests

<a id="opIdListRequests"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/requests \
```

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination (recommended)
* Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

#### High volume requests

Requesting a large number of tickets may return intermittent "503 Service Unavailable" errors. Workarounds:

- Use cursor pagination with a smaller page size. Example: GET /api/v2/requests?page[size]=100. If you continue to see timeouts, try a smaller value, such as 50 or 25. 
- Use [Search Requests](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket-requests/#search-requests) instead.  


<h3 id="list-requests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Possible values are "updated_at", "created_at"|
|sort_order|query|string|false|One of "asc", "desc". Defaults to "asc"|
|status|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of request statuses to filter by. Example `status=hold,open`|
|page|query|integer \| object|false|Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:<br><br>- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)<br>- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)<br><br>These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.<br>|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page.<br><br>Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific<br>documentation for limits.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "requests": [
    {
      "custom_status_id": 123,
      "description": "My printer is on fire!",
      "id": 33,
      "status": "open",
      "subject": "Help!"
    },
    {
      "custom_status_id": 234,
      "description": "I can't find my keys",
      "id": 34,
      "status": "closed",
      "subject": "Help!"
    }
  ]
}
```
