
`POST /api/v2/accounts`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account": {
    "help_desk_size": "Large group",
    "name": "Sample Partner Account",
    "remote_authentication": {
      "fingerprint": "0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF00000000",
      "remote_login_url": "https://saml.example.com/login",
      "remote_logout_url": "https://saml.example.com/logout",
      "type": "saml"
    },
    "subdomain": "partner12345"
  },
  "address": {
    "phone": "123-456-7890"
  },
  "owner": {
    "email": "bob@example.com",
    "name": "Bob Owner"
  },
  "partner": {
    "name": "BCSG",
    "url": "https://partner.example.com"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-trial-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TrialAccountRequest](#schematrialaccountrequest)|true|none|
|» account|body|object|true|Attributes of the account to provision.|
|» » _zd_choose_shard_udupi|body|integer \| null|false|Preferred database shard for the new account. Formerly read by `Zendesk::Accounts::Initializer` on the Classic creation path, which PLATOPS-1372 removed; the value is now accepted and forwarded verbatim, and whether the account service honours it is outside this repository.|
|» » currency|body|string \| null|false|Currency code for the account.|
|» » employee_service_suite_trial|body|boolean \| null \| string \| integer|false|Provisions an Employee Service Suite trial (a professional-plan `employee_service_suite` SKU expiring in 14 days) with `account.account_type` set to `pre_spp`. Enabled by any value the parameter gate coerces to true (`1`, `"1"`, `true`, `"true"`, `"on"`). Takes effect only when `zendesk_suite_trial` is not set, which is evaluated first.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » google_apps_domain|body|string \| null|false|Google Workspace domain to associate with the account. Must not already be routed to another account and must not be `gmail.com`; either returns `409 Conflict`.|
|» » help_desk_size|body|string \| null|false|Free-form description of the expected number of agents, for example `Small Team`, `1-9` or `Large group`. Surfaced verbatim as `company_size` in the signup tracking properties (`Account::Tracking`); any categorisation happens downstream of this repository. Not enforced by this controller's own gates; `Account` validates its presence on create, but the record is created by the account service, out of process. `null` and omission are indistinguishable here.|
|» » language|body|string \| null|false|Locale for the new account, for example `ja`. Copied to `account.locale` before the payload is forwarded.|
|» » multiproduct|body|boolean \| null \| string \| integer|false|Legacy switch for the account's product configuration. PLATOPS-1372 removed the multiproduct branch and the legacy Classic fallback from `create`, so this controller no longer reads the value and it has no effect on which service handles the request. It is still accepted by the parameter gate and forwarded verbatim to the account service like every other permitted property; whether it affects provisioning is decided by the account service, outside this repository. The value the account service returns is echoed back as `account.multiproduct` in the response body.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the account. Not enforced by this controller's own gates; accepted and forwarded to the account service, which decides whether it is required. `null` and omission are indistinguishable here.|
|» » remote_authentication|body|[TrialAccountRemoteAuthenticationInput](#schematrialaccountremoteauthenticationinput) \| object \| null|false|Single sign-on configuration for the new account. Accepted and forwarded to the account service verbatim; this controller does not read it.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|[TrialAccountRemoteAuthenticationInput](#schematrialaccountremoteauthenticationinput)|false|Single sign-on configuration for the new account. Corresponds to the `remote_authentication` member of `Api::V2::AccountsController::ACCOUNT_PARAMETER`.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» » remote_login_url|body|string \| null|false|Remote login URL for the account. Distinct from `remote_authentication.remote_login_url`; both are accepted and forwarded.|
|» » source|body|string \| null|false|Provisioning channel this signup came from. Also copied into `trial_extras.source` when present.|
|» » subdomain|body|string|true|The subdomain to provision, and the only place this controller looks for it. Must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,}[a-z0-9]$` (`SUBDOMAIN_PATTERN`, lib/vars.rb), must not start with `xn--`, and must be neither taken nor reserved; the value is trimmed of surrounding whitespace before those checks run. A missing, blank, invalid, reserved or taken subdomain returns `409 Conflict` with a `success: false` body rather than a validation error. Note that a successful request locks the subdomain in the shared cache for 60 seconds *before* the account is created, so retrying a request that failed with a `422` returns a `409` until the lock expires.|
|» » suite_trial|body|boolean \| null \| string \| integer|false|Provisions a `suite` trial SKU instead of the default `support` SKU. Also copied into `trial_extras.suite_trial` when present. Declared as a boolean in the parameter gate, which also accepts and coerces the string and integer spellings `"true"`, `"1"`, `"on"`, `1`, `"false"`, `"0"` and `0`.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » utc_offset|body|integer \| null \| string|false|Time zone for the new account, given either as a UTC offset (for example `7` or `"7"`) or as an ActiveSupport time zone name. Resolved by `Account::Localization.utc_to_tz` into `account.time_zone`; an unrecognised, empty or `null` value falls back to `Eastern Time (US & Canada)`.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » zendesk_suite_trial|body|boolean \| null \| string \| integer|false|Provisions a Zendesk Suite trial (a professional-plan `zendesk_suite` SKU expiring in 14 days) rather than the default SKU. Enabled by any value the parameter gate coerces to true (`1`, `"1"`, `true`, `"true"`, `"on"`); every other value is ignored. Evaluated before `employee_service_suite_trial`.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» address|body|object|true|Contact address of the account. Only `phone` is required.|
|» » city|body|string \| null|false|City.|
|» » phone|body|string \| integer|true|Contact phone number. A missing or blank value returns `422 Unprocessable Entity` with "Address phone can't be blank" (`Zendesk::Accounts::CreationParamsValidator`). No format is enforced.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » province|body|string \| null|false|State, province or region.|
|» » street|body|string \| null|false|Street address.|
|» » zip|body|string \| null|false|Postal code.|
|» agents|body|[[TrialAccountAgentInput](#schematrialaccountagentinput)]|false|Additional agents to invite into the new account. Forwarded to the account creator; this controller does not read the value.|
|» force_pod_id|body|string \| null|false|Pins the new account to a specific pod. When present it is forwarded as `pod_id` to the account creator.|
|» owner|body|object|true|Attributes of the account owner to create.|
|» » email|body|string|true|The owner's email address. A malformed address returns `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`Zendesk::Accounts::CreationParamsValidator#valid_owner_email`).|
|» » is_verified|body|string \| null \| boolean \| integer|false|Marks the owner's email as already verified. Only the values `1` and `true` (in their string, boolean or integer spellings) count as verified; the controller normalises whatever is supplied to a boolean before forwarding it, so any other value, `null`, and omitting the property, mean unverified.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|true|The owner's full name. A missing or blank value returns `422 Unprocessable Entity` with "Owner name can't be blank" (`Zendesk::Accounts::CreationParamsValidator`).|
|» » password|body|string \| null|false|Initial password for the owner. When omitted the owner is created without one and is expected to set it through the owner verification link returned in the response.|
|» partner|body|[TrialAccountPartnerInput](#schematrialaccountpartnerinput) \| object \| null|false|Reseller/partner attribution for the account. Accepted and forwarded to the account service verbatim; this controller does not read it. The `partner_name`/`partner_url` account settings these historically became were written on the Classic creation path, removed by PLATOPS-1372.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[TrialAccountPartnerInput](#schematrialaccountpartnerinput)|false|Reseller/partner attribution for the new account. Corresponds to `Api::V2::AccountsController::PARTNER_PARAMETER`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» trial_extras|body|object \| null|false|Free-form bag of trial metadata. Every value is coerced to a string, and the controller then injects `confirm_origin`, `creation_channel`, `original_remote_ip`, `region`, and copies `account.source` and `account.suite_trial` into it (`AccountsController#account_creation_params_trial_extras`). Declared as `Parameters.anything`, so a non-object value passes the parameter gate but then fails when the controller iterates it.|

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/channels/voice/agents/385473779372/tickets/123456/display \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /api/v2/channels/voice/agents/{agent_id}/tickets/{ticket_id}/display`

Allows you to instruct an agent's browser to open a ticket.

When the message is successfully delivered to an agent's browser:

```http
Status: 200 OK
```

When `agent_id` or `ticket_id` is invalid:

```http
Status: 404 Not Found
```

#### Allowed For
* Agents

|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of an agent|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
""
```

> 404 Response

```json
""
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response|Inline|
|404|Not Found|When the `agent_id` or `ticket_id` is invalid|Inline|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth

## Create Ticket or Voicemail Ticket

<a id="opIdCreateTicketOrVoicemailTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/channels/voice/tickets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "display_to_agent": 1234,
    "ticket": {
      "comment": {
        "body": "My printer is on fire!"
      },
      "priority": "urgent",
      "via_id": 46,
      "voice_comment": {
        "answered_by_id": 28,
        "call_duration": 40,
        "from": "+16617480240",
        "location": "Dublin, Ireland",
        "recording_type": "call",
        "recording_url": "http://yourdomain.com/recordings/1.mp3",
        "started_at": "2019-04-16T09:14:57Z",
        "to": "+16617480123",
        "transcription_text": "The transcription of the call"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/channels/voice/tickets`

#### Allowed For
* Agents

### Creating tickets

#### Introduction

Creating tickets using Talk Partner Edition follows the same conventions as the Create Ticket endpoint. See [Create Ticket](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/tickets/#create-ticket).

#### Request parameters

The POST request takes a mandatory `ticket` object that lists the values to set when the ticket is created.
You may also include an optional `display_to_agent` value such as the ID of the agent that will see the newly created ticket.
The `display_to_agent` is validated before creating the ticket, returning a 422 error if it is invalid.

Tickets created using this endpoint must have a `via_id` parameter. See the following
section for possible values.

#### Zendesk Talk Integration Via IDs

Tickets created using this endpoint must have one of the following `via_id` parameters:

| ID       | Description
| ---------| -------------
| 44       | Voicemail
| 45       | Phone call (inbound)
| 46       | Phone call (outbound)

### Creating voicemail tickets
#### Request parameters

The POST request takes a mandatory `ticket` object that lists the values to set when the ticket is created.
The ticket must have a `voice_comment` with the following values:

| Name               | Type                  | Comment
| ------------------ | ----------------------| -------
| from               | string                | Incoming phone number
| to                 | string                | Dialed phone number
| recording_url      | string                | URL of the recording
| recording_type     | string                | Type of recording (call, voicemail, or ai)
| started_at         | date                  | [ISO 8601](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) timestamp of the call starting time
| call_duration      | integer               | Duration in seconds of the call
| answered_by_id     | integer               | The agent who answered the call
| transcription_text | string                | Transcription of the call (optional)
| location           | string                | Location of the caller (optional)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "display_to_agent": 1234,
  "ticket": {
    "comment": {
      "body": "My printer is on fire!"
    },
    "priority": "urgent",
    "via_id": 46,
    "voice_comment": {
      "answered_by_id": 28,
      "call_duration": 40,
      "from": "+16617480240",
      "location": "Dublin, Ireland",
      "recording_type": "call",
      "recording_url": "http://yourdomain.com/recordings/1.mp3",
      "started_at": "2019-04-16T09:14:57Z",
      "to": "+16617480123",
      "transcription_text": "The transcription of the call"
    }
  }
}
```


To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## List Custom Ticket Statuses

<a id="opIdListCustomStatuses"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_statuses \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/custom_statuses`

Lists all undeleted custom ticket statuses for the account. No pagination is provided.

#### Allowed For

* End Users


<h3 id="list-custom-ticket-statuses-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status_categories|query|string|false|Filter the list of custom ticket statuses by a comma-separated list of status categories|
|active|query|boolean|false|If true, show only active custom ticket statuses. If false, show only inactive custom ticket statuses. If the filter is not used, show all custom ticket statuses|
|default|query|boolean|false|If true, show only default custom ticket statuses. If false, show only non-default custom ticket statuses. If the filter is not used, show all custom ticket statuses|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "custom_statuses": [
    {
      "active": true,
      "agent_label": "Responding quickly",
      "created_at": "2021-07-20T22:55:29Z",
      "default": false,
      "description": "Customer needs a response quickly",
      "end_user_description": "Your ticket is being responded to",
      "end_user_label": "Urgent processing",
      "id": 35436,
      "raw_agent_label": "Responding quickly",
      "raw_description": "Customer needs a response quickly",
      "raw_end_user_description": "Your ticket is being responded to",
      "raw_end_user_label": "Urgent processing",
      "status_category": "open",
      "updated_at": "2021-07-20T22:55:29Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-custom-ticket-statuses-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|List custom ticket statuses|[CustomStatusesResponse](#schemacustomstatusesresponse)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth

`PATCH /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}`

Updates an individual custom object. The updating rules are as follows:
* Takes a `custom_object` object that specifies the properties to update
* The `key` property cannot be updated
#### Allowed For
* Admins

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_object": {
    "title": "Electric Car",
    "title_pluralized": "Electric Cars"
  }
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|body|body|[CustomObjectsUpdateRequest](#schemacustomobjectsupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» custom_object|body|[CustomObjectUpdateInput](#schemacustomobjectupdateinput)|false|The writable attributes accepted when updating a custom object. Every property is optional: the request hash is mass-assigned to the<br>object, so an omitted property is left unchanged. `key` is accepted by the parameter filter on create only and cannot be updated<br>|

```json
    "url": "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/01GC0617DV48CAXK6WA4DW51HD"
```

`POST /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/access_rules`

Creates a new access rule for a custom object.
Access rules define conditions that restrict which records a role can access based on field values or relationships.
#### Allowed For
* Admins


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_rule": {
    "conditions": {
      "all": [
        {
          "field": "created_by_user",
          "operator": "matches",
          "value": "current_user"
        }
      ],
      "any": [
        {
          "field": "custom_object.order.custom_fields.status",
          "operator": "is",
          "value": "pending"
        }
      ]
    },
    "description": "Access rule that limits access to orders created by the current user",
    "title": "Orders Created by Current User"
  }
}
```

|» access_rule|body|object|false|none|
|» » conditions|body|object|false|The conditions that define when this rule applies|

|» » » any|body|[[AccessRuleCondition](#schemaaccessrulecondition)]|false|Any condition can be true (OR logic)|

## Create Custom Object Field

<a id="opIdCreateCustomObjectField"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/fields \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "custom_object_field": {
      "key": "color",
      "title": "Color",
      "type": "text"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/fields`

Creates any of the following custom field types:

* text (default when no "type" is specified)
* textarea
* checkbox
* currency
* date
* integer
* decimal
* regexp
* dropdown
* lookup
* multiselect
* parent

Additionally, you can create a roll-up summary field by specifying an existing type (`integer`, `decimal`, or `date`) with roll-up configuration in the `properties` object. See [About roll-up summary fields](/api-reference/custom-data/custom-objects/custom_object_fields/#about-roll-up-summary-fields).

To make a text, integer, regexp, or lookup field require unique values, set `is_unique` to true in the `properties` object. See [About unique fields](/api-reference/custom-data/custom-objects/custom_object_fields/#about-unique-fields).

See [About custom field types](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408838961562) in Zendesk help.

#### Allowed For

* Admins


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_object_field": {
    "key": "color",
    "title": "Color",
    "type": "text"
  }
}
```

|» custom_object_field|body|[CustomObjectField](#schemacustomobjectfield)|false|none|

## Update Custom Object Field

<a id="opIdUpdateCustomObjectField"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/fields/make \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "custom_object_field": {
      "title": "Primary Color"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/fields/{custom_object_field_key_or_id}`

Updates individual custom object fields. The updating rules are as follows:
* Takes a `custom_object_field` object that specifies the properties to update.
* The `key` property cannot be updated.
* If updating a standard field, only the `title`, `description`, and `properties` attributes can be updated.
* Standard name field is always required. Therefore, the `required` property for standard name field isn't editable.
* The `properties` parameter is comprised of four parts and can't be changed if any records exist for the object.
    * `autoincrement_enabled`: A Boolean that enables and disables autonumbering. Must be false if is_unique is true.
    * `autoincrement_prefix`: A string value that is used as a prefix to the autogenerated numbers. It can't exceed 30 characters.
    * `autoincrement_padding`: An integer specifying the starting number of digits in the autogenerated numbers. This value may be between 0-9. However, if you create records in excess of of these digits, additional digits are added as necessary.
    * `autoincrement_next_sequence`: An integer that will be used as the next number in the autonumbering sequence. It can't be negative or less than the current autonumbering value.
    * `is_unique`: A Boolean that enforces uniqueness for manually entered record names. When true, custom object record names must be unique. Must be false if autoincrement_enabled is true.
* For text, integer, regexp, and lookup fields, `properties` can include `is_unique`, a Boolean that requires each record to have a different value in the field. Unlike the name field's properties, it can be changed when records exist: it can be turned on only if no record has a value for the field, and it can always be turned off. See [About unique fields](#about-unique-fields).

#### Updating drop-down field options

You can also use the update endpoint to add, update, or remove options in a drop-down custom field. Updating field options for multi-select fields works exactly the same as drop-down field options.

**Important**: Unless you want to remove some options, you must specify all existing options in any update request. Omitting an option removes it from the drop-down field, which removes its values from any tickets or macros.

Use the `custom_field_options` attribute to update the options. The attribute consists of an array of option objects, with each object consisting of an `id`, `name`, and `value` property. The name and value properties correspond to the "Title" and "Tag" text boxes in the admin interface respectively. For new drop-down options, specify `"id":"null"`. Example request body:

```json
{"custom_object_field": {
    "custom_field_options": [
      {"id": "null", "name": "Apple Pie", "value": "apple"},
      {"id": "null", "name": "Pecan Pie", "value": "pecan"}
    ]
  }
}
```

#### Example Request

```bash
curl https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/fields/{custom_object_field_key_or_id}
  -d '{"ticket_field": {"custom_field_options": [{"name": "Apple Pie", "value": "apple"}, {"name": "Pecan Pie", "value": "pecan"}]}}' \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X PUT \
  -v -H "Authorization: Bearer {access_token}"
```
#### Allowed For
* Admins

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_object_field": {
    "title": "Primary Color"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-custom-object-field-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|custom_object_field_key_or_id|path|string|true|The key or id of a custom object field|
|body|body|[CustomObjectFieldsUpdateRequest](#schemacustomobjectfieldsupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» custom_object_field|body|[CustomObjectFieldUpdateInput](#schemacustomobjectfieldupdateinput)|false|The writable attributes accepted when updating a custom object field. Every property is optional and an omitted property is left unchanged,<br>with one exception: see the deletion warning on `custom_field_options`. `key` and `type` cannot be changed — `type` is filtered out of the<br>request and a changed `key` is rejected with a validation error. On a standard field (`standard::name`, `standard::external_id`) only<br>the title, description and properties may change (`raw_title` and `raw_description` are alternate routes to the title and description);<br>anything else fails validation<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "custom_object_field": {
    "active": true,
    "created_at": "2022-09-07T23:21:59Z",
    "description": "Make",
    "id": 4398096842879,
    "key": "make",
    "position": 0,
    "raw_description": "Make",
    "raw_title": "Make",
```

## Custom Object Record Bulk Jobs

<a id="opIdCustomObjectRecordBulkJobs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/jobs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "job": {
      "action": "create",
      "items": [
        {
          "custom_object_fields": {
            "color": "Red",
            "year": 2020
          },
          "name": "2020 Tesla"
        },
        {
          "custom_object_fields": {
            "color": "Blue",
            "external_id": "ddd444",
            "year": 2012
          },
          "name": "2012 Toyota"
        },
        {
          "custom_object_fields": {
            "color": "Silver",
            "external_id": "ddd445",
            "year": 2017
          },
          "name": "2017 Ford"
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/jobs`

Queues a background job to perform bulk actions on up to 100 custom object records per single request.
Takes a `job` object with the following nested fields:
* `action`, one of:
    * `"create"`
    * `"delete"`
    * `"delete_by_external_id"`
    * `"delete_by_unique_field"`
    * `"create_or_update_by_external_id"`
    * `"create_or_update_by_name"`
    * `"create_or_update_by_unique_field"`
    * `"update"`
* `items`
    * For a `"create"` action, an array of JSON objects representing the custom object records being created
    * For a `"delete"` action, an array of strings representing Zendesk record ids
    * For a `"delete_by_external_id"` action, an array of strings representing external ids
    * For a `"delete_by_unique_field"` action, an array of strings representing values of the unique field named in `unique_field_key`
    * For a `"create_or_update_by_external_id"` action, an array of JSON objects representing the custom object records being created or updated by external id
    * For a `"create_or_update_by_name"` action, an array of JSON objects representing the custom object records being created or updated by name. The `is_unique` property on the custom object's name field must be enabled.
    * For a `"create_or_update_by_unique_field"` action, an array of JSON objects representing the custom object records being created or updated by the unique field named in `unique_field_key`. Each object must include that field's value in `custom_object_fields`.
    * For an `"update"` action, an array of JSON objects representing the custom object records being updated
* `unique_field_key`, required for the `"create_or_update_by_unique_field"` and `"delete_by_unique_field"` actions: the key of the custom object field that identifies the records. The field's `is_unique` property must be enabled. Use the `*_by_name` actions to identify records by name.

Note: If autonumbering is selected for the custom object's name field, record names aren't allowed in the request body because they are generated automatically. If uniqueness is enabled, the record names must be unique.

#### Identifying records by a unique field
Returns a `400 Bad Request` with the error `InvalidUniqueFieldKey` if `unique_field_key` is missing or isn't the key of a unique field on the custom object.

In the job status `results`, each item of a `"delete_by_unique_field"` job reports the `unique_field_key` and `value` from the request, along with its `index` and `status` (for example, `"Deleted"`). An item that matches no record fails with "Record not found". Each item in a `"create_or_update_by_unique_field"` job reports the record's `id`, its `index` and `status`. An item without a value for the unique field fails with "Unique field value cannot be blank". If the field's uniqueness is turned off before the job runs, its items fail with "Uniqueness must be enabled on the field to identify records by it".

#### Allowed For
* Agents

#### Response ###
This endpoint returns a `job_status` [JSON object](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#json-format) and queues a background job to do the work. Use the [Show Job Status](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#show-job-status) endpoint to check for the job's completion. Only a certain number of jobs can be queued or running at the same time. See [Job limit](/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/#job-limit) for more information.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "job": {
    "action": "create",
    "items": [
      {
        "custom_object_fields": {
          "color": "Red",
          "year": 2020
        },
        "name": "2020 Tesla"
      },
      {
        "custom_object_fields": {
          "color": "Blue",
          "external_id": "ddd444",
          "year": 2012
        },
        "name": "2012 Toyota"
      },
      {
        "custom_object_fields": {
          "color": "Silver",
          "external_id": "ddd445",
          "year": 2017
        },
        "name": "2017 Ford"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="custom-object-record-bulk-jobs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|body|body|[CustomObjectRecordsBulkCreateRequest](#schemacustomobjectrecordsbulkcreaterequest)|false|none|
|» job|body|object|false|none|
|» » action|body|string|false|none|
|» » items|body|[[CustomObjectRecord](#schemacustomobjectrecord) \| string]|false|An array of record objects for job actions that create, update, or set. An array of strings for job actions that delete.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[CustomObjectRecord](#schemacustomobjectrecord)|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » unique_field_key|body|string|false|The key of the unique field that identifies the records. Required for the `create_or_update_by_unique_field` and `delete_by_unique_field` actions.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "job_status": {
    "id": "V3-291e720c98aef4d953563ab090486213",
    "message": null,
    "progress": null,
    "results": null,
    "status": "queued",
    "total": 2,
    "url": "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/job_statuses/V3-291e720c98aef4d953563ab090486213"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "description": "job.unique_field_key must be the key of a unique field on the car custom object",
  "error": "InvalidUniqueFieldKey"
}
```

<h3 id="custom-object-record-bulk-jobs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|[CustomObjectRecordsJobsResponse](#schemacustomobjectrecordsjobsresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request - `unique_field_key` is missing or isn't the key of a unique field on the custom object|Inline|

<h3 id="custom-object-record-bulk-jobs-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|error|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

`GET /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records`

Lists all undeleted custom object records for the specified object.

If the object has a parent field with `cascade_permissions_enabled`, non-admin agents receive a `403 Forbidden` response. Use the [Filtered Search endpoint](#filtered-search-of-custom-object-records) with a filter on the parent field instead.

 #### Pagination

* [Cursor pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#cursor-pagination) only.
#### Allowed For
* Agents

<h3 id="list-custom-object-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|filter[ids]|query|string|false|Optional comma-separated list of ids to filter records by. If one or more ids are specified, only matching records are returned. The ids must be unique and are case sensitive.|
|filter[external_ids]|query|string|false|Optional comma-separated list of external ids to filter records by. If one or more ids are specified, only matching records are returned. The ids must be unique and are case sensitive.|
|sort|query|string|false|One of `id`, `updated_at`, `-id`, or `-updated_at`. The `-` denotes the sort will be descending.<br>|
|page[before]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.before_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.<br>|
|page[after]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.after_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.<br>|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Specifies how many records should be returned in the response. You can specify up to 100 records per page.<br>|

## Create Custom Object Record

<a id="opIdCreateCustomObjectRecord"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/records \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

        "model": "Y"
      },
      "name": "My car 1"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records`

Creates a custom object record according to all the properties described by a custom object definition. If `autoincrement_enabled` is true, record names aren't allowed in the request body because they are generated automatically. If `is_unique` is true, record names must be unique.

If the custom object has a parent relationship field, the parent field is required and must reference a valid parent record. Set the value in `custom_object_fields` using the parent record's id, external id (`"external_id:value"`), or name (`"name:value"`).
#### Allowed For
* Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_object_record": {
    "custom_object_fields": {
      "make": "Tesla",
      "model": "Y"
    },
    "name": "My car 1"
  }
}
```

|body|body|[CustomObjectRecordsCreateRequest](#schemacustomobjectrecordscreaterequest)|false|none|
|» custom_object_record|body|[CustomObjectRecord](#schemacustomobjectrecord)|false|none|

## Delete Custom Object Record by External Id Or Name

<a id="opIdDeleteCustomObjectRecordByExternalIdOrName"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/records \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records`

Deletes a record with the specified external id, name, or unique field value. Specify only one identifier per request.

* The `is_unique` property on the custom object's name field must be enabled in order to delete by name.
* To delete by a unique field, send the field's key as the query parameter, for example `?vin=1HGCM82633A004352`. The field's `is_unique` property must be enabled.

If the record is a parent in a parent-child relationship, all associated child records are also deleted asynchronously via a background job.
#### Allowed For
* Agents


<h3 id="delete-custom-object-record-by-external-id-or-name-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|external_id|query|string|false|The external id of a custom object record|
|name|query|string|false|The name of a custom object record|
|unique_field_value|query|object|false|A value of one of the custom object's unique fields, sent as `{unique_field_key}={value}`. For example, `vin=1HGCM82633A004352` identifies the record whose unique field with the key "vin" holds that value. The field's `is_unique` property must be enabled.<br>|

<h3 id="delete-custom-object-record-by-external-id-or-name-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No content response|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Create or Update Custom Object Record

<a id="opIdUpsertCustomObjectRecordByExternalIdOrName"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/records \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "custom_object_record": {
      "custom_object_fields": {
        "make": "Oldsmobile",
        "model": "Cutlass Supreme"
      },
      "name": "1997 Cutlass Supreme"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records`

Creates or updates a custom object record based on the provided external id, name, or unique field value. If a record exists for the given identifier, the endpoint updates it. Only the specified attributes are updated. Otherwise, the endpoint creates a new record with the provided identifier and other attributes. Specify only one identifier per request.

* The `is_unique` property on the custom object's name field must be enabled in order to update or create by name.
* To update or create by a unique field, send the field's key as the query parameter, for example `?vin=1HGCM82633A004352`. The field's `is_unique` property must be enabled. A new record is created with that value in the field.
#### Allowed For
* Agents


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_object_record": {
    "custom_object_fields": {
      "make": "Oldsmobile",
      "model": "Cutlass Supreme"
    },
    "name": "1997 Cutlass Supreme"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-custom-object-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|external_id|query|string|false|The external id of a custom object record|
|name|query|string|false|The name of a custom object record|
|unique_field_value|query|object|false|A value of one of the custom object's unique fields, sent as `{unique_field_key}={value}`. For example, `vin=1HGCM82633A004352` identifies the record whose unique field with the key "vin" holds that value. The field's `is_unique` property must be enabled.<br>|
|body|body|[CustomObjectRecordsUpsertRequest](#schemacustomobjectrecordsupsertrequest)|false|none|
|» custom_object_record|body|[CustomObjectRecord](#schemacustomobjectrecord)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "custom_object_record": {
    "created_at": "2023-09-26T22:25:10Z",
    "created_by_user_id": "10001",
    "custom_object_fields": {
      "make": "Oldsmobile",
      "model": "Cutlass Supreme"
    },
    "custom_object_key": "car",
    "external_id": "X90001",
    "id": "01GDXYEY1FQYN066VHF49YHJ21",
    "name": "1997 Cutlass Supreme",
    "updated_at": "2023-09-26T22:25:10Z",
    "updated_by_user_id": "10001",
    "url": "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/records/01GDXYEY1FQYN066VHF49YHJ21"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-custom-object-record-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[CustomObjectRecordResponse](#schemacustomobjectrecordresponse)|

## Delete Custom Object Record

<a id="opIdDeleteCustomObjectRecord"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/records/01GCSJW391QVSC80GYDH7E93Q6 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records/{custom_object_record_id}`

Deletes a record with the specified id.

If the record is a parent in a parent-child relationship, all associated child records are also deleted asynchronously via a background job. Child records are soft-deleted first and then permanently deleted after a 30-day retention period. The delete request returns immediately; the cascade deletion happens in the background.

#### Allowed For
* Agents

<h3 id="delete-custom-object-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|custom_object_record_id|path|string|true|The id of a custom object record|

<h3 id="delete-custom-object-record-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No content response|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Update Custom Object Record

<a id="opIdUpdateCustomObjectRecord"></a>

```bash
      }
    }
```

`PATCH /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records/{custom_object_record_id}`

Updates an individual custom object record. The updating rules are as follows:
* Takes a `custom_object_record` object that specifies the properties to update
* The custom object fields should be nested inside a `custom_object_fields` object
#### Allowed For
* Agents

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_object_record": {
    "custom_object_fields": {
      "model": "Civic",
      "year": 2002
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-custom-object-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|custom_object_record_id|path|string|true|The id of a custom object record|
|body|body|[CustomObjectRecordsUpdateRequest](#schemacustomobjectrecordsupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» custom_object_record|body|[CustomObjectRecordUpdateInput](#schemacustomobjectrecordupdateinput) \| object \| null|false|The record attributes to update. `null` is accepted and is a no-op — the record is returned unchanged with a 200|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[CustomObjectRecordUpdateInput](#schemacustomobjectrecordupdateinput)|false|The writable attributes accepted when updating a custom object record. Every property is optional and an omitted property is left<br>unchanged. `name` and `external_id` fall back to the record's current value, so they cannot be cleared by sending null — send a new<br>value instead<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object \| null|false|none|

`GET /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records/autocomplete`

Retrieves an array of custom object records that have a field value that matches the value specified in the `name` parameter.

If the object has a parent field with `cascade_permissions_enabled`, the request must be made in the context of a cascade parent field using the `field_id` and `source` parameters.

#### Pagination

* [Cursor pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#cursor-pagination) only.
* Returns the first 10,000 records sorted by relevancy with page limits.
#### Allowed For

|page[before]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.before_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.<br>|

It should be a `meta.after_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.<br>|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|The number of records to return in the response. You can specify up to 100 records per page.<br>|

|source|query|string|false|One of "zen:user", "zen:ticket", "zen:organization", or "zen:custom_object:CUSTOM_OBJECT_KEY". Represents the object `field_id` belongs to. Must be used with field_id param.<br>|

## Search Custom Object Records

<a id="opIdSearchCustomObjectRecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/records/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records/search`

Returns an array of custom object records where the search query matches the values in Text Fields, Multi Line Text fields, and RegExp fields. To find records in other fields, use the [Filtered Search API](/api-reference/custom-data/custom-objects/custom_object_records/#filtered-search-of-custom-object-records) endpoint.

If the object has a parent field with `cascade_permissions_enabled`, non-admin agents receive a `403 Forbidden` response. Use the [Filtered Search endpoint](/api-reference/custom-data/custom-objects/custom_object_records/#filtered-search-of-custom-object-records) with a filter on the parent field instead.

#### Pagination

* [Cursor pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#cursor-pagination) only.
* Returns the records sorted by relevancy with page limits. Without a `sort` parameter, only the first 10,000 records are returned. With a `sort` parameter, all records are returned.
#### Allowed For
* Agents

<h3 id="search-custom-object-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|query|query|string|false|The query parameter is used to search text-based fields for records that match specific query terms.<br>The query can be multiple words or numbers. Every record that matches the beginning of any word or number in the query string is returned.<br/><br/><br><br>Fuzzy search is supported for the following text-based field types: Text fields, Multi Line Text fields, and RegExp fields.<br/><br/><br><br>For example, you might want to search for records related to Tesla vehicles: `query=Tesla`. In this example the API would return every record for the given custom object where any of the supported text fields contain the word 'Tesla'.<br/><br/><br><br>You can include multiple words or numbers in your search. For example: `query=Tesla Honda 2020`. This search phrase would be URL encoded as `query=Tesla%20Honda%202020` and return every record for the custom object for which any of the supported text fields contained 'Tesla', 'Honda', or '2020'.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|One of `name`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `-name`, `-created_at`, or `-updated_at`. The `-` denotes the sort will be descending. Defaults to sorting by relevance.<br>|
|page[before]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.before_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.<br>|
|page[after]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.after_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.<br>|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Specifies how many records should be returned in the response. You can specify up to 100 records per page.<br>|

## Filtered Search of Custom Object Records

<a id="opIdFilteredSearchCustomObjectRecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/records/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "filter": {
      "$and": [
        {
          "custom_object_fields.key_one": {
            "$eq": "foo"
          }
        },
        {
          "custom_object_fields.key_two": {
            "$eq": "bar"
          }
        }
      ],
      "$or": [
        {
          "custom_object_fields.key_three": {
            "$eq": "foo"
          }
        },
        {
          "custom_object_fields.key_four": {
            "$eq": "bar"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records/search`

Returns an array of custom object records that meet the search and filter criteria. For simple searches limited to only text fields and no complex logic, use the [Search Custom Object Records API](/api-reference/custom-data/custom-objects/custom_object_records/#search-custom-object-records) endpoint.

If the object has a parent field with `cascade_permissions_enabled`, non-admin agents must include a filter on the parent field (for example, `"custom_object_fields.parent_field_key": { "$eq": "parent_record_id" }`). Requests without a parent filter return `403 Forbidden`.

Filters can contain either an individual [comparison object](#comparison-object) or an array of filter expressions within logical namespaces. Filter expressions can themselves be either comparison objects or `$and` / `$or` groups, so logical operators can be nested to build complex Boolean queries.

A filter is a JSON object that has the following properties:

| Name      | Type   | Required | Description
| --------- | ------ | -------- | -----------
| ATTRIBUTE | object | no       | A [comparison object](#comparison-object) specifying an attribute value condition to be met for records to match.<br/><br/>Examples are marked below.
| $and      | array  | no       | Array of filter expressions combined with logical AND. Each element may be a comparison object or a nested `$and` / `$or` group.
| $or       | array  | no       | Array of filter expressions combined with logical OR. Each element may be a comparison object or a nested `$and` / `$or` group.

Limits for nested `$and` / `$or` groups:

* Maximum nesting depth: `5` (outermost `$and` / `$or` counts as level 1). Exceeding it returns `422 Invalid Condition`.
* Attribute keys cannot share a level with `$and` / `$or` once the payload contains any `$and` / `$or` nested inside another `$and` / `$or`. The request returns `422 Invalid Condition`; wrap the attribute inside the group instead.

##### Examples

```js
{
  "filter": {
    "custom_object_fields.field_key": { "$eq": "value" } // ATTRIBUTE
  }
}
```

```js
{
  "filter": {
    "$or": [
      { "custom_object_fields.field_key": { "$eq": "value" } }, // ATTRIBUTE
      { "external_id": { "$eq": "Record123" } } // ATTRIBUTE
    ]
  }
}
```

```js
// Nested $and / $or
{
  "filter": {
    "$and": [
      { "custom_object_fields.contract_term_months": { "$gt": 5 } },
      {
        "$or": [
          { "custom_object_fields.status": { "$eq": "active" } },
          { "custom_object_fields.status": { "$eq": "pending" } }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

#### Comparison Object

A comparison object defines a condition a record must meet to be considered a match. The condition is based on an attribute value or object type.

A comparison object is a JSON object that has the following properties:

| Name      | Type          | Required | Description
| --------- | ------------- | -------- | -----------
| FIELD_KEY | string        | yes      | When filtering on a custom field, they must be namedspaced with `custom_object_fields.`. ex. `custom_object_fields.field_key`<br/><br/>When filtering on a standard field, no namespace is required. The following fields are considered standard: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by_user`, `updated_by_user`, `name`, `external_id`
| OPERATOR  | string        | yes      | [Supported operators](/documentation/custom-data/v2/searching-custom-object-records/) vary by the value's data type
| VALUE     | string, array | yes      | The value you're filtering for

* Date values should be in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.

#### Pagination

* [Cursor pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#cursor-pagination) only.
* Returns the records sorted by relevancy with page limits. Without a `sort` parameter, only the first 10,000 records are returned. With a `sort` parameter, all records are returned.

#### Allowed For

* Agents
* End users (when an admin [configures](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/6034260247066) the custom object to be accessible to end users)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filter": {
    "$and": [
      {
        "custom_object_fields.key_one": {
          "$eq": "foo"
        }
      },
      {
        "custom_object_fields.key_two": {
          "$eq": "bar"
        }
      }
    ],
    "$or": [
      {
        "custom_object_fields.key_three": {
          "$eq": "foo"
        }
      },
      {
        "custom_object_fields.key_four": {
          "$eq": "bar"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="filtered-search-of-custom-object-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|query|query|string|false|The query parameter is used to search text-based fields for records that match specific query terms.<br>The query can be multiple words or numbers. Every record that matches the beginning of any word or number in the query string is returned.<br/><br/><br><br>Fuzzy search is supported for the following text-based field types: Text fields, Multi Line Text fields, and RegExp fields.<br/><br/><br><br>For example, you might want to search for records related to Tesla vehicles: `query=Tesla`. In this example the API would return every record for the given custom object where any of the supported text fields contain the word 'Tesla'.<br/><br/><br><br>You can include multiple words or numbers in your search. For example: `query=Tesla Honda 2020`. This search phrase would be URL encoded as `query=Tesla%20Honda%202020` and return every record for the custom object for which any of the supported text fields contained 'Tesla', 'Honda', or '2020'.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|One of "name", "created_at", "updated_at", "-name", "-created_at", or "-updated_at". The "-" denotes the sort will be descending. Defaults to sorting by relevance.<br>|
|page[before]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.before_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.<br>|
|page[after]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.after_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.<br>|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Specifies how many records should be returned in the response. You can specify up to 100 records per page.<br>|

## Show Custom Object Record by Unique Identifier

<a id="opIdShowCustomObjectRecordByUniqueIdentifier"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/records/show_by_unique_identifier \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records/show_by_unique_identifier`

Returns a custom object record identified by its external id, its name, or the value of one of the custom object's unique fields. Send exactly one identifier per request.

* To identify the record by name, the `is_unique` property on the custom object's name field must be enabled.
* To identify the record by a unique field, send the field's key as the query parameter, for example `?vin=1HGCM82633A004352`. The field's `is_unique` property must be enabled. For a unique lookup field, the value is the id of the record the field references.

Returns a `400 Bad Request` if more than one identifier is sent, if `name` is sent and the name field isn't unique, or if no identifier is sent. A parameter that isn't the key of a unique field doesn't count as an identifier. Returns a `404 Not Found` if no record matches.
#### Allowed For
* Agents


<h3 id="show-custom-object-record-by-unique-identifier-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|external_id|query|string|false|The external id of a custom object record|
|name|query|string|false|The name of a custom object record|
|unique_field_value|query|object|false|A value of one of the custom object's unique fields, sent as `{unique_field_key}={value}`. For example, `vin=1HGCM82633A004352` identifies the record whose unique field with the key "vin" holds that value. The field's `is_unique` property must be enabled.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "custom_object_record": {
    "created_at": "2022-09-26T22:25:10Z",
    "created_by_user_id": "10001",

      "model": "Y"
    },

    "id": "01GDXYEY1FQYN066VHF49YHJ21",
    "name": "My Tesla",
    "photo": {

      "id": 928374,

      "size": 166144
    },
    "updated_at": "2022-09-26T22:25:10Z",
    "updated_by_user_id": "10001",
    "url": "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/records/01GDXYEY1FQYN066VHF49YHJ21"
  }
}
```

## Update Custom Object Record by Unique Identifier

<a id="opIdUpdateCustomObjectRecordByUniqueIdentifier"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/records/update_by_unique_identifier \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "custom_object_record": {
      "custom_object_fields": {
        "make": "Oldsmobile",
        "model": "Cutlass Supreme"
      },
      "name": "1997 Cutlass Supreme"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records/update_by_unique_identifier`

Updates a custom object record identified by its external id, its name, or the value of one of the custom object's unique fields. Unlike [Create or Update Custom Object Record](#create-or-update-custom-object-record), it never creates a record. Send exactly one identifier per request.

* To identify the record by name, the `is_unique` property on the custom object's name field must be enabled.
* To identify the record by a unique field, send the field's key as the query parameter, for example `?vin=1HGCM82633A004352`. The field's `is_unique` property must be enabled. For a unique lookup field, the value is the id of the record the field references.

The update rules are the same as for [Update Custom Object Record](#update-custom-object-record):
* Send a `custom_object_record` object that specifies the properties to update
* Nest the custom object fields inside a `custom_object_fields` object

Returns a `400 Bad Request` if more than one identifier is sent, if `name` is sent and the name field isn't unique, or if no identifier is sent. A parameter that isn't the key of a unique field doesn't count as an identifier. Returns a `404 Not Found` if no record matches.
#### Allowed For
* Agents

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_object_record": {
    "custom_object_fields": {
      "make": "Oldsmobile",
      "model": "Cutlass Supreme"
    },
    "name": "1997 Cutlass Supreme"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-custom-object-record-by-unique-identifier-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|external_id|query|string|false|The external id of a custom object record|
|name|query|string|false|The name of a custom object record|
|unique_field_value|query|object|false|A value of one of the custom object's unique fields, sent as `{unique_field_key}={value}`. For example, `vin=1HGCM82633A004352` identifies the record whose unique field with the key "vin" holds that value. The field's `is_unique` property must be enabled.<br>|
|body|body|[CustomObjectRecordsUpsertRequest](#schemacustomobjectrecordsupsertrequest)|false|none|
|» custom_object_record|body|[CustomObjectRecord](#schemacustomobjectrecord)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "custom_object_record": {
    "created_at": "2022-09-26T22:25:10Z",
    "created_by_user_id": "10001",
    "custom_object_fields": {
      "color": "white",
      "make": "Tesla",
      "model": "Y"
    },
    "custom_object_key": "car",
    "external_id": null,
    "id": "01GDXYEY1FQYN066VHF49YHJ21",
    "name": "My Tesla",
    "photo": {
      "content_type": "image/png",
      "content_url": "https://company.zendesk.com/record_photos/my_funny_pic.png",
      "id": 928374,
      "name": "my_funny_pic.png",
      "size": 166144
    },
    "updated_at": "2022-09-26T22:25:10Z",
    "updated_by_user_id": "10001",
    "url": "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/records/01GDXYEY1FQYN066VHF49YHJ21"
  }
}
```

## Incremental Custom Object Record Export, Cursor Based

<a id="opIdIncrementalCustomObjectRecordExportCursor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/custom_objects/apartment/cursor \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/incremental/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/cursor`

Returns the custom object records that changed since the start time. This endpoint supports 
cursor-based incremental exports for custom object records.

This endpoint only supports cursor-based pagination and does not support offset-based pagination.
Cursor-based exports provide more consistent performance and response body sizes. For more information, 
see [Cursor-based incremental exports](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api#cursor-based-incremental-exports) in [Using the Incremental Exports API](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/using-the-incremental-export-api).

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents with custom object read permissions

#### Rate Limiting

You can make up to 10 requests per minute to this endpoint.

#### Notes

- `start_time` is only required for the initial request for the pages in the record set, then `cursor` is required for all subsequent requests
- The `start_time` must be more than 60 seconds ago
- Deleted records will have their field values replaced with "[DELETED]" unless excluded via filter
- Photo fields are excluded from incremental export responses


<h3 id="incremental-custom-object-record-export-cursor-based-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_time|query|integer|false|The time to start the incremental export from. Must be at least one minute in the past. Data isn't provided for the most recent minute. Required on the initial export request; not required on subsequent cursor-based pagination requests|
|cursor|query|string|false|The cursor pointer to work with for all subsequent exports after the initial request|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key identifier for the custom object|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records to return per page (default 1000, maximum 1000)|
|filter[exclude_deleted]|query|boolean|false|If true, exclude deleted records from the export|

> Example responses

> 200 Response


## Update Custom Object Record Attachment for Malware

<a id="opIdUpdateCustomObjectRecordAttachment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/custom_objects/car/records/01GCSJW391QVSC80GYDH7E93Q6/attachments/01HQ2Z3X4Y5T6R7S8P9Q0W1E2 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "custom_object_record_attachment": {
      "malware_access_override": true
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records/{record_id}/attachments/{id}`

Updates malware access settings for the specified attachment. This is typically used to allow access to attachments that were flagged as containing malware.

#### Allowed For
* Admins


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_object_record_attachment": {
    "malware_access_override": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-custom-object-record-attachment-for-malware-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_key|path|string|true|The key of a custom object|
|record_id|path|string|true|The id of a custom object record|
|id|path|string|true|The id of a custom object record attachment|
|body|body|[CustomObjectRecordAttachmentUpdateRequest](#schemacustomobjectrecordattachmentupdaterequest)|false|none|
|» custom_object_record_attachment|body|object|true|none|
|» » malware_access_override|body|boolean|true|If true, allows access to an attachment flagged as malware. If false, blocks access to such an attachment.|

> Example responses

```json

  "custom_object_record_attachment": {
```

|id|path|string|true|The id of a custom object record attachment|
|inline|query|boolean|false|If true, the attachment content is displayed inline in the browser. If false or omitted, the attachment is downloaded as a file.<br>|

<a id="opIdReorderQueues"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/queues/order \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "queue_ids": [
      "01HE5HE5RCZMCEVAVV60VTHA2G",
      "01HE5HHPM1RETPV4N0H3178P0N"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/queues/order`

Alters the evaluation order of OCR queues in the account.
The evaluation order is set in a `queue_ids` array in the request body.

You must include every queue id in your account to reorder the OCR queues. If not, the endpoint will return 400 Bad Request.

#### Allowed For

* Admins


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "queue_ids": [
    "01HE5HE5RCZMCEVAVV60VTHA2G",
    "01HE5HHPM1RETPV4N0H3178P0N"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="reorder-queues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[QueuesReorderRequest](#schemaqueuesreorderrequest)|true|none|
|» queue_ids|body|[string]|true|Every queue id in the account, in the evaluation order you want. Duplicates are collapsed and the request succeeds. Only missing or<br>invalid ids cause a 400 response.<br>|

<h3 id="reorder-queues-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="support-api-oauth-clients">OAuth Clients</h1>

`GET /api/v2/oauth/clients`

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination (recommended)
* Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

#### Allowed For

* Admins


<h3 id="list-clients-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|object|false|Cursor-based pagination parameters (JSON:API style).<br><br>Supports nested parameters:<br>- `page[size]` - Number of records per page (default varies by endpoint, typically 100)<br>- `page[after]` - Cursor token to fetch records after this position<br>- `page[before]` - Cursor token to fetch records before this position<br><br>Example: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=eyJvIjoiaWQiLCJ2IjoiYVFFPSJ9`<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|

```json
      "created_at": "2009-05-13T00:07:08Z",

      "id": 8678530,

}
```

## Create Client

<a id="opIdCreateOAuthClient"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/oauth/clients \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /api/v2/oauth/clients`

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents with the [Manage APIs](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882) permission

#### Allowed scopes

You can optionally set a `scope` property on the client to restrict which scopes it is
permitted to request during the OAuth authorization flow. The value is a space-separated
string of scope values. When set, any token request using this client must only include
scopes from this list. If a client requests a scope not included in its allowed scopes,
the request fails with a `400 Bad Request` response and an `invalid_scope` error. If
`scope` is omitted, no scope restrictions are applied to the client.

For the full list of valid scope values, see [Scopes](/api-reference/ticketing/oauth/grant_type_tokens/#scope).


> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "client": {
    "company": "Zendesk",
    "created_at": "2009-05-13T00:07:08Z",
    "description": "Zendesk Test Client",
    "id": 223443,
    "identifier": "test_client",
    "name": "Test Client",
    "redirect_uri": [
      "https://example.com/callback"
    ],
    "secret": "af3t24tfj34h43s...",
    "updated_at": "2011-07-22T00:11:12Z",
    "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/clients/223443",
    "user_id": 29
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-client-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created response|[OauthClientResponse](#schemaoauthclientresponse)|

<aside class="warning">

basicAuth
</aside>

|200|OK|Success response|[OAuthClientsResponse](#schemaoauthclientsresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="support-api-oauth-tokens">OAuth Tokens</h1>

OAuth tokens are credentials used to authenticate API requests on behalf of users or applications.

**Note**: The Create Token (POST /api/v2/oauth/tokens) endpoint is no longer available. To create OAuth access tokens, use [Create Token for Grant Type](/api-reference/ticketing/oauth/grant_type_tokens/#create-token-for-grant-type) instead. This endpoint supports OAuth grant types including authorization code, refresh token, and client credentials.


## List Tokens

<a id="opIdListOAuthTokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/oauth/tokens \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/oauth/tokens`

Returns the properties of the tokens for the current user. Admins can view OAuth token properties for all users using the [all](/api-reference/ticketing/oauth/oauth_tokens/#parameters) parameter. To filter the list by OAuth client, use the [client_id](/api-reference/ticketing/oauth/oauth_tokens/#parameters) parameter for a local OAuth client ID, or the [global_client_id](/api-reference/ticketing/oauth/oauth_tokens/#parameters) parameter for a global OAuth client ID. For security reasons, only the first 10 characters of each access token are included.

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination (recommended)
* Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

#### Allowed For

* Admins


<h3 id="list-tokens-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|object|false|Cursor-based pagination parameters (JSON:API style).<br><br>Supports nested parameters:<br>- `page[size]` - Number of records per page (default varies by endpoint, typically 100)<br>- `page[after]` - Cursor token to fetch records after this position<br>- `page[before]` - Cursor token to fetch records before this position<br><br>Example: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=eyJvIjoiaWQiLCJ2IjoiYVFFPSJ9`<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|
|client_id|query|integer(int64)|false|The id of the OAuth client|
|global_client_id|query|integer(int64)|false|The id of the global OAuth client|
|all|query|boolean|false|A boolean that returns all OAuth tokens in the account. Requires admin role|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "tokens": [
    {
      "client_id": 41,
      "created_at": "2009-05-13T00:07:08Z",
      "expires_at": "2011-07-22T00:11:12Z",
      "id": 223443,
      "refresh_token": "af3t24tfj34h43s...",
      "scopes": [
        "read"
      ],
      "token": "af3345kdj3",
      "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tokens/223443",
      "used_at": "2010-01-22T00:11:12Z",
      "user_id": 29
    },
    {
      "client_id": 41,
      "created_at": "2009-05-13T00:07:08Z",
      "expires_at": "2011-07-22T00:11:12Z",
      "id": 8678530,
      "refresh_token": "af3t24tfj34h43s...",
      "scopes": [
        "read"
      ],
      "token": "34hjgkjas4",
      "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tokens/8678530",
      "used_at": "2010-01-22T00:11:12Z",
      "user_id": 29
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-tokens-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[OAuthTokensResponse](#schemaoauthtokensresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Show Token

<a id="opIdShowToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/oauth/tokens/223443 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/oauth/tokens/{oauth_token_id}`

Returns the properties of the specified token. For security reasons, only the first 10 characters of the access token are included.

In the first endpoint, `id` is a token id, not the full token.

In the second endpoint, include an `Authorization: Bearer` header with the full token to get its associated properties. Example:

```sh
curl https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/oauth/tokens/current \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${authToken}'
```

#### Allowed for

* Admins, Agents, End Users

```json
  "token": {
    "client_id": 1234,
    "created_at": "2009-05-13T00:07:08Z",
    "expires_at": "2011-07-22T00:11:12Z",
    "id": 223443,
    "refresh_token": "af3t24tfj34h43s...",
    "scopes": [
      "read",
      "write"
    ],
    "token": "af3345kdj3",
    "url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tokens/223443",
    "used_at": "2010-01-22T00:11:12Z",
    "user_id": 29
  }
}
```

<h3 id="show-token-responses">Responses</h3>
