<h1 id="support-api-api-tokens">API Tokens</h1>

API tokens are a deprecated credential used to authenticate API requests. They are
created, viewed, updated, and revoked from the account's Admin Center.

API tokens are scheduled for removal as a supported authentication method on
April 30, 2027.


## List API Tokens

<a id="opIdListApiTokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/api_tokens \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/api_tokens`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Lists the API tokens for the account. Token values are truncated in the response — see the
`visible_token` property.

**Deprecated.** API tokens are being removed as a supported authentication method for API
requests. This endpoint is scheduled for removal on April 30, 2027.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents with the [Manage APIs](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882) permission


<h3 id="list-api-tokens-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include_users|query|boolean|false|When set to true, includes the `user_id`, `user_name`, and `user_email` of the agent<br>who created each token in the response.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "api_tokens": [
    {
      "active": true,
      "created_at": "2009-05-13T00:07:08Z",
      "description": "token 1",
      "id": 1,
      "last_used": "2021-05-13T00:07:08Z",
      "updated_at": "2011-07-22T00:11:12Z",
      "visible_token": "gKGF9GQu"
    },
    {
      "active": false,
      "created_at": "2009-08-26T00:07:08Z",
      "description": "token 2",
      "id": 2,
      "last_used": null,
      "updated_at": "2010-05-13T00:07:08Z",
      "visible_token": "Jl9Sr28H"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "You do not have access to this page. Please contact the account owner of this help desk for further help.",
    "title": "Forbidden"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="list-api-tokens-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[ApiTokensResponse](#schemaapitokensresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden. Returned when the authenticated user does not have required permissions.<br>|[ApiTokenErrorResponse](#schemaapitokenerrorresponse)|
|404|Not Found|Returned when API token access has been disabled for the account. No response body is<br>returned in this case.<br>|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Create API Token

<a id="opIdCreateApiToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/api_tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "api_token": {
      "description": "token 1"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/api_tokens`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Creates a new API token for the account. The response includes the full, unencrypted token
value in the `token` property. This is the only time the full value is returned — store it
securely, as it can't be retrieved again. On every subsequent request, the token is
represented by its truncated `visible_token` value instead.

**Deprecated.** API tokens are being removed as a supported authentication method for API
requests. This endpoint is scheduled for removal on April 30, 2027.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents with the [Manage APIs](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882) permission


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "api_token": {
    "description": "token 1"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-api-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateApiTokenRequest](#schemacreateapitokenrequest)|false|none|
|» api_token|body|object|false|none|
|» » description|body|string|false|The description of the token that displays in Admin Center|
|» » user_id|body|integer(int64)|false|Assigns the token to the specified agent or admin. If omitted, the token is not<br>associated with a specific user.<br>|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "api_token": {
    "active": true,
    "created_at": "2021-07-22T00:11:12Z",
    "description": "token 1",
    "id": 3,
    "last_used": null,
    "token": "gKGF9GQu7dfX93JD09n3ue5PIjlK",
    "updated_at": "2021-07-22T00:11:12Z"
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "You do not have access to this page. Please contact the account owner of this help desk for further help.",
    "title": "Forbidden"
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "description": "Record validation errors",
  "details": {
    "base": [
      {
        "description": "Maximum number of API tokens reached"
      }
    ]
  },
  "error": "RecordInvalid"
}
```

<h3 id="create-api-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created response|[ApiTokenResponse](#schemaapitokenresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden. Returned when the authenticated user is not an admin and does not have <br>required permissions.<br>|[ApiTokenErrorResponse](#schemaapitokenerrorresponse)|
|404|Not Found|Returned when API token access has been disabled for the account. No response body is<br>returned in this case.<br>|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed, for example because the account has reached its maximum number of<br>API tokens.<br>|[ApiTokenValidationErrorResponse](#schemaapitokenvalidationerrorresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Update API Token

<a id="opIdUpdateApiToken"></a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \

    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/api_tokens/{id}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Updates the description of an API token, or activates or deactivates it. Setting `active` to

requests without deleting it.

**Deprecated.** API tokens are being removed as a supported authentication method for API
requests. This endpoint is scheduled for removal on April 30, 2027.

#### Allowed For

* Admins

```json
    "active": false,

    "description": "token 2",
    "id": 1,
    "last_used": "2021-05-13T00:07:08Z",
    "updated_at": "2021-07-22T00:11:12Z",
    "visible_token": "gKGF9GQu"
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "You do not have access to this page. Please contact the account owner of this help desk for further help.",
    "title": "Forbidden"

}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "You've reached this page because what you were looking for does not exist or there's been an error.",

```

> 422 Response

```json
  "description": "Record validation errors",
  "details": {
    "base": [
      {
        "description": "is invalid"
      }
    ]
  },
  "error": "RecordInvalid"
}
```

<h3 id="update-api-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[ApiTokenResponse](#schemaapitokenresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden. Returned when the authenticated user does not have required permissions.<br>|[ApiTokenErrorResponse](#schemaapitokenerrorresponse)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found. Returned either when no API token exists with the given id, or when API token<br>access has been disabled for the account (in the latter case, no response body is<br>returned).<br>|[ApiTokenErrorResponse](#schemaapitokenerrorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed for one or more of the supplied attributes.|[ApiTokenValidationErrorResponse](#schemaapitokenvalidationerrorresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="support-api-grant-type-tokens">Grant Type Tokens</h1>

## Create Token for Grant Type

<a id="opIdCreateTokenForGrantType"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/oauth/tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /oauth/tokens`

Returns an OAuth access token in exchange for one of the following:

- an [authorization code](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408845965210#topic_pvr_ncl_1l)
- a [refresh token](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408845965210#topic_p1c_xjf_52c)
- a [client secret](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408845965210#topic_s21_lfs_qk)

**Note**: The password grant type flow, which used a Zendesk username and password to get an access token, has been deprecated and is highly discouraged.

To revoke an access token, see [Revoke Token](/api-reference/ticketing/oauth/oauth_tokens/#revoke-token).

#### Request parameters

The POST request takes the following parameters, which must be formatted as JSON:

| Name                     | Description
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------
| grant_type               | "authorization_code", "refresh_token", or "client_credentials"
| code                     | Authorization grant flow only. The authorization code you received from Zendesk after the user granted access. The code is valid for only 120 seconds. See [Handle the user's authorization decision](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408845965210#topic_ykc_dcm_dcc) in Zendesk help
| client_id                | The **Identifier** value specified in an OAuth client in the Zendesk Admin Center (**Apps and integrations** > **APIs** > **OAuth clients**). See [Registering your application with Zendesk](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408845965210#topic_s21_lfs_qk)
| client_secret            | The **Secret** value specified in an OAuth client in the Admin Center (**Apps and integrations** > **APIs** > **OAuth clients**). See [Registering your application with Zendesk](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408845965210#topic_s21_lfs_qk)
| redirect_uri             | Authorization grant flow only. The redirect URL you specified when you sent the user to the Zendesk authorization page. For ID purposes only. See [Send the user to the Zendesk authorization page](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408845965210#topic_mkc_dcm_dcc)
| scope                    | Valid scope for this token. A space-separated string of scope values. Must be within the client's configured allowed scopes, if set. See [Scope](#scope) below
| expires_in               | Number of seconds the access token is valid. Must be greater than or equal to 300 seconds (5 minutes) and less than or equal to 172,800 seconds (2 days), or less than `refresh_token_expires_in`, whichever is the shorter. Defaults to null
| refresh_token_expires_in | Number of seconds the refresh token is valid. Must be greater than or equal to 604,800 seconds (7 days) or `expires_in` (if given), and less than or equal to 7,776,000 seconds (90 days). Defaults to 2,592,000 seconds (30 days)
| refresh_token            | A valid refresh token. See [Replacing expired access tokens](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408845965210#topic_p1c_xjf_52c)

**Authorization code example**

```javascript
const tokenResponse = await axios.post(
  "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/oauth/tokens",
  {
    grant_type: "authorization_code",
    code: AUTHORIZATION_CODE,
    client_id: ZENDESK_CLIENT_ID,
    redirect_uri: REDIRECT_URI_PKCE,
    scope: "tickets:read users:read",
    code_verifier: CODE_VERIFIER,
    expires_in: 86400,
    refresh_token_expires_in: 604800,
  },
  { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } }
);
```

**Refresh token example**

```javascript
const tokenResponse = await axios.post(
  "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/oauth/tokens",
  {
    grant_type: "refresh_token",
    refresh_token: REFRESH_TOKEN,
    client_id: ZENDESK_CLIENT_ID,
    client_secret: ZENDESK_CLIENT_SECRET,
    scope: "tickets:write",
    expires_in: 86400,
    refresh_token_expires_in: 604800,
  },
  { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } }
);
```

**Client credentials example**

```javascript
const tokenResponse = await axios.post(
  "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/oauth/tokens",
  {
    grant_type: "client_credentials",
    client_id: ZENDESK_CLIENT_ID,
    client_secret: ZENDESK_CLIENT_SECRET,
    scope: "tickets:write",
    expires_in: 86400
  },
  { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } }
);
```

#### Scope

You must specify a scope to control the app's access to Zendesk resources. The "read" scope gives access to GET endpoints and includes permission to sideload related resources. The "write" scope gives access to POST, PUT, and DELETE endpoints for creating, updating, and deleting resources.

**Note**: Don't confuse the **scope** parameter (singular) with the **scopes** parameter (plural) for non-grant-type tokens described in [OAuth Tokens](/api-reference/ticketing/oauth/oauth_tokens).

The "impersonate" scope allows a Zendesk admin to make requests on behalf of end users. See [Making API requests on behalf of end users](/documentation/ticketing/using-the-zendesk-api/making-api-requests-on-behalf-of-end-users/).

**Broad scopes**

The following parameter gives read access to all resources:

`"scope": "read"`

The following parameter gives read and write access to all resources:

`"scope": "read write"`

**Resource-specific scopes**

You can fine-tune access using resource-specific scopes. The syntax is as follows:

`"scope": "resource:action"`

For example, the following parameter restricts the scope to only reading tickets:

`"scope": "tickets:read"`

To give read and write access to a resource, specify both scopes:

`"scope": "users:read users:write"`

To give write access only to one resource, such as organizations, and read access to everything else:

`"scope": "organizations:write read"`

**Scope errors**

There are two distinct scope-related error cases to be aware of:

- **Unrecognized scope string**: If you specify a scope value that doesn't exist (for example, a typo such as `"scope": ["read", "write"]` using an array instead of a string), the endpoint still creates an access token. However, any API request made with that token will return a `403 Forbidden` error.
- **Scope outside client's allowed scopes**: If the OAuth client has [allowed scopes](/api-reference/ticketing/oauth/oauth_clients/#create-client) configured and you request a scope not included in that list, the endpoint returns `400 Bad Request` with an `invalid_scope` error and no token is created.

**Available scopes**

| Scope | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `read` | Read all data. Gives access to GET endpoints, including permission to sideload related resources. |
| `write` | Write all data. Gives access to POST, PUT, and DELETE endpoints. |
| `impersonate` | Allows Zendesk Support admins to make requests on behalf of end users. See [Making API requests on behalf of end users](/documentation/ticketing/using-the-zendesk-api/making-api-requests-on-behalf-of-end-users/). |
| `account_settings:read` | View account settings. Includes account configuration, ticket and user fields, and workspaces. |
| `account_settings:write` | Create, edit, and delete account settings. Includes account configuration, ticket and user fields, and workspaces. |
| `ai_agents:chat` | Chat with AI agents. Includes sending messages and receiving responses via the Zendesk Developers API. |
| `ai_agents:list` | List AI agents. Includes listing the AI agents configured on the account via the Zendesk Developers API. |
| `apps:read` | View installed apps and their settings. Includes which apps are installed and each app's settings. |
| `apps:write` | Install, configure, and remove apps. Includes installing and uninstalling apps, changing settings, and uploading custom app packages. |
| `auditlogs:read` | View audit logs. Includes the account-wide record of changes: who changed what and when. Read only. |
| `automations:read` | View automations and their details. |
| `automations:write` | Create, edit, and delete automations. |
| `brands:read` | View brands and their agent assignments. |
| `brands:write` | Create, edit, and delete brands and their agent assignments. |
| `custom_objects:read` | View custom objects. Includes custom object definitions and record attachments. |
| `custom_objects:write` | Create, edit, and delete custom objects. Includes definitions and record attachments. |
| `deletion_schedules:read` | View deletion schedules. Includes data retention policies that automatically delete tickets, users, and other data. |
| `deletion_schedules:write` | Delete deletion schedules. Includes deleting data retention policies. |
| `dynamic_content:read` | View dynamic content items and language variants. |
| `dynamic_content:write` | Create, edit, and delete dynamic content items and language variants. |
| `groups:read` | View groups and their memberships. |
| `groups:write` | Create, edit, and delete groups and their memberships. |
| `hc:read` | View Help Center content. Includes articles, sections, categories, community posts and comments. |
| `hc:write` | Create, edit, and delete Help Center content. Includes articles, sections, categories, community posts and comments. |
| `macros:read` | View macros, their categories, and attachments. |
| `macros:write` | Create, edit, and delete macros and their attachments. |
| `organizations:read` | View organizations and their details. Includes memberships, subscriptions, and merge history. |
| `organizations:write` | Create, edit, and delete organizations and manage their memberships. Includes adding and removing users, managing subscriptions, and merging organizations. |
| `requests:read` | View support requests and their comments. |
| `requests:write` | Submit and edit support requests. Includes creating new requests and adding to existing ones. |
| `satisfaction_ratings:read` | View satisfaction ratings, scores, and reasons. |
| `satisfaction_ratings:write` | Submit satisfaction ratings. Includes rating a ticket good or bad with an optional reason. |
| `security:read` | View security and sign-in settings. Includes password policy, session timeouts, IP restrictions, and SSO configuration. Read only. |
| `side_conversations:read` | View side conversations. Includes the side conversations on a ticket, their messages and events, and their participants. |
| `side_conversations:write` | Create, update, and reply to side conversations. Includes starting side conversations with people outside the ticket by email, Slack, or Microsoft Teams, creating child tickets, sending replies and files, and importing conversations from other systems. |
| `sla_policies:read` | View SLA and group SLA policies. |
| `sla_policies:write` | Create, edit, delete, and reorder SLA and group SLA policies. |
| `targets:read` | View targets and their delivery failures. |
| `targets:write` | Create, edit, and delete targets. |
| `themes:read` | View Guide themes and their files. |
| `themes:write` | Create, edit, and delete Guide themes. Includes importing, updating, publishing, exporting, and deleting themes. |
| `ticket_attachments:read` | View files attached to tickets. |
| `ticket_attachments:write` | Upload, edit, and delete ticket attachments. Includes uploading files, updating and deleting attachments, and redacting them. |
| `ticket_views:read` | View ticket views and the tickets they return. |
| `ticket_views:write` | Create, edit, and delete ticket views. |
| `tickets:read` | View tickets. Includes ticket contents, comments and conversation history, tags, forms and fields, audits, events, and metrics. |
| `tickets:write` | Create, edit, and delete tickets. Includes adding comments, tags, merging tickets, marking spam, attachments, forms, and custom statuses. |
| `triggers:read` | View triggers, trigger categories, and their revision history. |
| `triggers:write` | Create, edit, delete, and reorder triggers and trigger categories. |
| `users:read` | View users. Includes identities, active sessions, group, organization, and brand memberships, roles, and settings. |
| `users:write` | Create, edit, and delete users and manage their access. Includes resetting passwords, ending sessions, adding identities, changing memberships, and managing custom roles. |
| `webhooks:read` | View webhooks and their activity history. |
| `webhooks:write` | Create, edit, test, and delete webhooks. |
| `any_channel:write` | Push messages from an external channel into Zendesk. Includes creating tickets, comments, and users from an integrated channel. Write only. |
| `web_widget:write` | Edit Web Widget settings and configuration. Write only. |
| `zis:read` | View private integrations. Includes configurations, connections, and inbound webhooks. |
| `zis:write` | Create, edit, and delete private integrations. Includes configurations, connections, and inbound webhooks. |


> Example responses

```json
  "scope": "organizations:write read",
  "token_type": "bearer"
}
```

<a id="opIdListGlobalOAuthClients"></a>

> Code samples


`GET /api/v2/oauth/global_clients`

Returns all the global OAuth clients that users on your account have authorized.

#### Pagination

* Cursor pagination (recommended)
* Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents with the [Manage APIs](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408882153882) permission


<h3 id="list-global-oauth-clients-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|page|query|object|false|Cursor-based pagination parameters (JSON:API style).<br><br>Supports nested parameters:<br>- `page[size]` - Number of records per page (default varies by endpoint, typically 100)<br>- `page[after]` - Cursor token to fetch records after this position<br>- `page[before]` - Cursor token to fetch records before this position<br><br>Example: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=eyJvIjoiaWQiLCJ2IjoiYVFFPSJ9`<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.<br><br>When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.<br><br>Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`<br>|

<h1 id="support-api-approval-requests">Approval Requests</h1>

## Create Approval Clarification Flow Message

<a id="opIdCreateApprovalClarificationFlowMessage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/approval_clarification_flow_messages \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "approval_request_id": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
    "message": "Can you clarify the budget line?"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/approval_clarification_flow_messages`

Adds a message to the clarification flow thread for an approval request and returns the
full, updated thread.

#### Allowed For

* The approval request's assignee or creator, the ticket assignee, or a member of the
  assigned group
* Any user who can view the ticket when the `approvals_allow_comments_from_ticket_viewers`
  feature is enabled


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "approval_request_id": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
  "message": "Can you clarify the budget line?"
}
```

<h3 id="create-approval-clarification-flow-message-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» approval_request_id|body|string|true|The id of the approval request to add the message to|
|» message|body|string|true|The content of the message|
|» raw|body|object \| null|false|Slack rich-text blocks for the message. Only used when `via` is `SLACK`|
|» via|body|string \| null|false|The channel the message is sent through. Defaults to `SUPPORT` when omitted or blank|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» via|SUPPORT|
|» via|SLACK|
|» via|""|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "approval_request_id": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
  "clarification_flow_messages": [
    {
      "author": {
        "avatar": "https://company.zendesk.com/system/photos/12345/avatar.png",
        "id": 12345,
        "name": "Jane Doe",
        "role": "end_user"
      },
      "created_at": "2026-09-29T14:32:00Z",
      "id": "msg_123",
      "message": "Can you clarify the budget line?",
      "via": "SUPPORT"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "You passed an invalid value for the via attribute.",
    "title": "Invalid attribute"
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": "Access denied"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "You've reached this page because what you were looking for does not exist or there's been an error.",
    "title": "Not Found"
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "error": "CommentLimitExceeded",
  "errors": "Comment limit reached, approvers can still approve or deny."
}
```

<h3 id="create-approval-clarification-flow-message-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|[ApprovalClarificationFlowMessagesShowResponse](#schemaapprovalclarificationflowmessagesshowresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request - the via parameter is invalid|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|The current user is not permitted to comment on this approval request, SLACK commenting is not enabled for the account, or the clarification flow feature is not enabled|Inline|
|404|Not Found|The approval request could not be found|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The message could not be added. The `errors` field is an array of validation messages<br>when the approval request is no longer active, or a single string paired with an<br>`error` code when the comment limit has been reached.<br>|Inline|

<h3 id="create-approval-clarification-flow-message-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|object|false|none|none|
|» message|string|false|none|none|
|» title|string|false|none|none|

Status Code **403**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|string|false|none|none|

Status Code **404**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|object|false|none|none|
|» message|string|false|none|none|
|» title|string|false|none|none|

Status Code **422**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|string|false|none|Present only when the comment limit has been reached. Value is always `CommentLimitExceeded`|
|errors|object|false|none|Validation errors (array), or the comment-limit message (string)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## List Approval Requests

<a id="opIdListApprovalRequests"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/approval_requests \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/approval_requests`

Lists all approval requests for the current account with optional filtering by status and assignee.

#### Allowed For

* Admins

#### Query Parameters

| Name                      | Type   | Description
|---------------------------|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
| filter[status]            | string | Filter by a comma-separated list of one or more approval statuses. Values: active, approved, rejected, withdrawn
| filter[assignee_user_id]  | string | Filter by a comma-separated list of assigned user ids. Maximum 100 ids
| filter[assignee_group_id] | string | Filter by a comma-separated list of assigned group ids. Maximum 100 ids
| include                   | string | Comma-separated list of extra fields to sideload. Supports `deeplinks` — adds a `deeplink` field to each approval request, resolving to that request's agent-facing or Help Center decision page. Omitting `include` leaves the response unchanged.

`include=deeplinks` requires the `approvals_api_parity` feature to be enabled for the account. When it isn't, `include=deeplinks` is silently ignored: no `deeplink` field is added, and the rest of the response is unaffected.

#### Filtering Logic

- When multiple values are provided for a filter, `or` logic is used. For example, `filter[status]=active,approved` is evaluated as `status=active OR status=approved`.
- If multiple filters are applied to a single request, `AND` logic is used. For example, `filter[status]=active AND filter[assignee_user_id]=123`.
- Each filter parameter supports a maximum 100 values.
- Numeric ids must be valid integers.

#### Pagination

This endpoint supports cursor-based pagination. Use `after_cursor` and `before_cursor` parameters to navigate through results.


<h3 id="list-approval-requests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[status]|query|string|false|Filter by a comma-separated list of one or more approval statuses. Allowed values are active, approved, rejected, withdrawn. Maximum 100 values.|
|filter[assignee_user_id]|query|string|false|Filter by a comma-separated list of assigned user ids. Maximum 100 ids.|
|filter[assignee_group_id]|query|string|false|Filter by a comma-separated list of assigned group ids. Maximum 100 ids.|
|before_cursor|query|string|false|Cursor for pagination. Fetch records before this cursor|
|after_cursor|query|string|false|Cursor for pagination. Fetch records after this cursor|
|include|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of extra fields to sideload. Supports `deeplinks` — adds a<br>`deeplink` field to each approval request. Requires the `approvals_api_parity`<br>feature; silently ignored when the account doesn't have it enabled.<br>|

## Create Approval Request

<a id="opIdCreateApprovalRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/approval_requests \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "assignee_group_id": 789,
    "message": "Please approve this request for new office equipment for the support team",
    "subject": "Office Equipment Approval",
    "ticket_id": 123
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/approval_requests`

Creates one or more approval requests for a ticket.

When manual approval requests are turned off for the account, approval requests can still be created through this API. Approval requests created by the API have a `Sent by` value of `API`.

#### Allowed For

* System users (flowstate)
* Agents

#### Single approval request

To create a single approval request, supply a top-level `assignee_user_id` or `assignee_group_id`. This is helpful when only one approval is required or approvals need to be received in a specific order.

The response returns the created request under the
`approval_request` key. See the **Example body** and **Example response(s)**
sections below for the single-request request and response shapes.

#### Parallel approval requests

To create multiple approval requests at once, for the approvers to review and respond to in parallel, supply an `approval_requests` array. The approval request's `subject` and `message` are set once at the top level and apply to every individual approval request in the array.

The approval requests are created atomically as an array under the `approval_requests` key, and all share the same `approval_workflow_instance_id`. If any of the approval request entries are invalid, none of the requests are created. To avoid invalid entries, do the following:

 * Specify exactly one `assignee_user_id` or `assignee_group_id` for each entry in the `approval_requests` array.
 * Make sure you don't combine a top-level `assignee_user_id` or `assignee_group_id` with the
  `approval_requests` array. Doing so returns a `422`.

Example request:

```bash
curl https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/approval_requests \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST \
  -d '{"ticket_id": 123, "subject": "Budget Approval", "message": "Please approve the Q1 budget", "approval_requests": [{"assignee_user_id": 101}, {"assignee_group_id": 202}]}' \
  -v -u {email_address}/token:{api_token}
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "approval_requests": [
    {
      "id": "01KFP3S9EVXF9CKAYY080NV98C",
      "approval_workflow_instance_id": "01KFP3S9EVXF9CKAYY080NV98D",
      "subject": "Budget Approval",
      "message": "Please approve the Q1 budget",
      "status": "active",
      "created_at": "2026-01-23T19:02:36Z",
      "created_by_id": 789,
      "assignee_user_id": 101,
      "assignee_group_id": null,
      "ticket_id": 123,
      "origination_type": "API_ORIGINATION"
    },
    {
      "id": "01KFP3S9EVXF9CKAYY080NV98E",
      "approval_workflow_instance_id": "01KFP3S9EVXF9CKAYY080NV98D",
      "subject": "Budget Approval",
      "message": "Please approve the Q1 budget",
      "status": "active",
      "created_at": "2026-01-23T19:02:36Z",
      "created_by_id": 789,
      "assignee_user_id": null,
      "assignee_group_id": 202,
      "ticket_id": 123,
      "origination_type": "API_ORIGINATION"
    }
  ]
}
```


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "assignee_group_id": 789,
  "message": "Please approve this request for new office equipment for the support team",
  "subject": "Office Equipment Approval",
  "ticket_id": 123
}
```

<h3 id="create-approval-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ApprovalRequestCreateRequest](#schemaapprovalrequestcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» approval_requests|body|[object]|false|Parallel approval requests only. One entry per approval request to create, up to five. Each entry must<br>specify exactly one of `assignee_user_id` or `assignee_group_id`.  Can't be used with a top-level `assignee_user_id` or `assignee_group_id`.<br>|
|» » assignee_group_id|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|The id of the group assigned to review and approve the request|
|» » assignee_user_id|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|The id of the user assigned to review and approve the request|
|» assignee_group_id|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|Single approval request only. The id of the group assigned to review and approve the request. Can't be used with an `approval_requests` array.|
|» assignee_user_id|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|Single approval request only. The id of the user assigned to review and approve the request. Can't be used with an `approval_requests` array.|
|» message|body|string|true|Details and context for the approval request. Shared by all approval requests created in the call.|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Optional metadata used to determine the origination of the approval request|
|» » callback_info|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» » » token|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » workflow_id|body|string \| null|false|The id of the workflow that triggered the request, if any|
|» subject|body|string|true|Subject line for the approval request. Shared by all approval requests created in the call.|
|» ticket_id|body|integer(int64)|true|The id of the ticket the approval request was added to|

```json
}
```

## Decide Approval Request

<a id="opIdDecideApprovalRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/approval_workflow_instances/01KFP3S9EVXF9CKAYY080NV98D/approval_requests/01KFP3S9EVXF9CKAYY080NV98C/decision \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "notes": "Looks good, approved",
    "status": "approved"
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/approval_workflow_instances/{workflow_instance_id}/approval_requests/{id}/decision`

Records a decision (approve, reject, or withdraw) on an approval request, with optional notes.

#### Allowed For

* The user or a member of the group assigned to review the approval request

The ticket requester, the ticket assignee, and the user who created the approval request are not
allowed to decide on it, even when they are also the assignee.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "notes": "Looks good, approved",
  "status": "approved"
}
```

<h3 id="decide-approval-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workflow_instance_id|path|string|true|The id of the approval workflow instance|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the approval request to decide on|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» notes|body|string|false|Optional notes to record with the decision|
|» status|body|string|true|The decision to record|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|pending|
|» status|active|
|» status|approved|
|» status|rejected|
|» status|withdrawn|

## Withdraw Approval Workflow Instance

<a id="opIdWithdrawApprovalWorkflowInstance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/approval_workflow_instances/01KFP3S9EVXF9CKAYY080NV98D/withdraw \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -d '{
    "withdrawn_reason": "No longer needed"
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/approval_workflow_instances/{workflow_instance_id}/withdraw`

Withdraws every non-withdrawn approval request in the given workflow instance and marks
the workflow instance as withdrawn. Works for both parallel and non-parallel workflow
instances.

#### Allowed For

* Agents who can manage approval requests and edit the associated ticket, and who are
  either the approval request's requester or the ticket's assignee


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "withdrawn_reason": "No longer needed"
}
```

|workflow_instance_id|path|string|true|The id of the approval workflow instance|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» withdrawn_reason|body|string|true|Reason provided for withdrawing the approval request(s)|

`GET /api/v2/it_asset_management/assets`

Lists all assets for all asset types.

#### Filtering

Use the `filter[ids]` or `filter[external_ids]` query parameters to filter results by asset IDs or external IDs. Both parameters accept comma-separated values.

#### Pagination

* [Cursor pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#cursor-pagination) only.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

<h3 id="list-assets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|object|false|Cursor-based pagination parameters (JSON:API style).<br><br>Supports nested parameters:<br>- `page[size]` - Number of records per page (default varies by endpoint, typically 100)<br>- `page[after]` - Cursor token to fetch records after this position<br>- `page[before]` - Cursor token to fetch records before this position<br><br>Example: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=eyJvIjoiaWQiLCJ2IjoiYVFFPSJ9`<br>|
|filter[ids]|query|string|false|Optional comma-separated list of ids to filter assets by. If one or more ids are specified, only matching assets are returned. The ids must be unique and are case sensitive.|
|filter[external_ids]|query|string|false|Optional comma-separated list of external ids to filter assets by. If one or more external ids are specified, only matching assets are returned. The external ids must be unique and are case sensitive.|

## Update Asset

<a id="opIdUpdateItamAsset"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/it_asset_management/assets/01K9AMAPSER316NHTJ2R36YAQ1 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "asset": {
      "custom_field_values": {
        "ip_address": "1.2.3.4",
        "managed": "no"
      },
      "notes": "Updating an asset"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/it_asset_management/assets/{asset_id}`

Updates an individual asset. This request takes an `asset` object that specifies the properties to update, with custom field values nested within a `custom_field_values` object. Values are updated only for the properties specified in the request. Any asset properties that aren't specified in the request are unaffected, and their values are preserved for the asset.

#### Allowed For

* Admins

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "asset": {
    "custom_field_values": {
      "ip_address": "1.2.3.4",
      "managed": "no"
    },
    "notes": "Updating an asset"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-asset-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|asset_id|path|string|true|The id of the asset|
|body|body|[ItamAssetUpdateRequest](#schemaitamassetupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» asset|body|object|true|Only the supplied properties are updated. Properties omitted from the request keep their current values|
|» » asset_tag|body|string \| null|false|The tag for the asset|
|» » asset_type_id|body|string|false|Id of the asset type|
|» » custom_field_values|body|object \| null|false|Custom asset field keys and values. Only the supplied keys are updated. The keys must be custom fields applicable to the asset's asset type. A `null` for the object itself is accepted and leaves every custom field value untouched, as is `{}`. A `null` against an individual key is the opposite - it clears that field's value, unless the field is required, in which case the update is rejected|
|» » external_id|body|string \| null|false|An id you can use to link an asset to external data|
|» » location_id|body|string \| null|false|Id of the asset location|
|» » manufacturer|body|string \| null|false|The asset's manufacturer name|
|» » model|body|string \| null|false|The asset's model name|
|» » name|body|string|false|Display name for the asset. Cannot be set to an empty value|
|» » notes|body|string \| null|false|The asset's notes|
|» » organization_id|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|Id of the organization the asset is associated with|
|» » purchase_cost|body|number(float) \| null|false|The asset's purchase cost|
|» » purchase_date|body|string(date) \| null|false|The asset's purchase date|
|» » serial_number|body|string \| null|false|The asset's serial number|
|» » status_id|body|string|false|Id of current status of the asset|
|» » user_id|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|Id of the user the asset is assigned to|
|» » vendor|body|string \| null|false|The asset's vendor name|
|» » warranty_expiration|body|string(date) \| null|false|The asset's warranty expiration date|

> Example responses

```json
    "asset_tag": "loaner-ABC123XYZ",
```

## Asset Bulk Jobs

<a id="opIdItamAssetBulkJobs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/it_asset_management/assets/jobs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "job": {
      "action": "create",
      "items": [
        {
          "asset_type_id": "01K9BW852KHGF59W0TM02J2F6H",
          "custom_field_values": {
            "manufacturer": "Apple",
            "model": "MacBookPro18,1"
          },
          "name": "Laptop 1",
          "status_id": "01K9BW8DD6Z2N7TXM313N8BR69"
        },
        {
          "asset_type_id": "01K9BW852KHGF59W0TM02J2F6H",
          "custom_field_values": {
            "manufacturer": "Dell",
            "model": "XPS 15"
          },
          "name": "Laptop 2",
          "status_id": "01K9BW8DD6Z2N7TXM313N8BR69"
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/it_asset_management/assets/jobs`

Queues a background job to perform bulk actions on up to 100 asset records per request.
Takes a `job` object with two nested fields:
* `action`, one of:
    * `"create"`
    * `"update"`
    * `"delete"`
    * `"delete_by_external_id"`
* `items`
    * For a `"create"` action, an array of JSON objects representing the assets being created
    * For an `"update"` action, an array of JSON objects representing the assets being updated (must include `id` attribute)
    * For a `"delete"` action, an array of strings representing Zendesk asset ids
    * For a `"delete_by_external_id"` action, an array of strings representing external ids

Note: For create and update actions, the `asset_type_id`, `status_id`, and `location_id` fields can be specified using either the ID or the name of the resource. For example, you can use `"asset_type_id": "01K9BW852KHGF59W0TM02J2F6H"` or `"asset_type": "Laptop"`.

#### Allowed For
* Admins

#### Response
This endpoint returns a `job_status` [JSON object](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#json-format) and queues a background job to do the work. Use the [Show Job Status](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#show-job-status) endpoint to check for the job's completion. Only a certain number of jobs can be queued or running at the same time. See [Job limit](/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/#job-limit) for more information.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "job": {
    "action": "create",
    "items": [
      {
        "asset_type_id": "01K9BW852KHGF59W0TM02J2F6H",
        "custom_field_values": {
          "manufacturer": "Apple",
          "model": "MacBookPro18,1"
        },
        "name": "Laptop 1",
        "status_id": "01K9BW8DD6Z2N7TXM313N8BR69"
      },
      {
        "asset_type_id": "01K9BW852KHGF59W0TM02J2F6H",
        "custom_field_values": {
          "manufacturer": "Dell",
          "model": "XPS 15"
        },
        "name": "Laptop 2",
        "status_id": "01K9BW8DD6Z2N7TXM313N8BR69"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="asset-bulk-jobs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ItamAssetBulkJobRequest](#schemaitamassetbulkjobrequest)|false|none|
|» job|body|object|false|none|
|» » action|body|string|false|none|
|» » items|body|[[ItamAsset](#schemaitamasset) \| string]|false|An array of asset objects for job actions that create or update. An array of strings for job actions that delete.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[ItamAsset](#schemaitamasset)|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » action|create|
|» » action|update|
|» » action|delete|
|» » action|delete_by_external_id|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "job_status": {
    "id": "V3-291e720c98aef4d953563ab090486213",
    "message": null,
    "progress": null,
    "results": null,
    "status": "queued",
    "total": 2,
    "url": "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/job_statuses/V3-291e720c98aef4d953563ab090486213"
  }
}
```

## Search Assets

<a id="opIdSearchItamAssets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/it_asset_management/assets/search?query=laptop' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/v2/it_asset_management/assets/search`

Returns an array of assets with values in text-based fields that match the search query.

If the query includes multiple words or numbers, it's treated as a space-separated list of search terms and assets with values matching one or more of the terms are returned. For example, `query=laptop Apple 2024` is encoded as `query=laptop%20Apple%202024` and treated as three distinct search terms: `laptop`, `Apple`, and `2024`. Every asset record with a text field containing 'laptop', 'Apple', or '2024' is returned.

If you need to search by more complex logic, use the [Filtered Search API](/api-reference/it-asset-management/assets/#filtered-search-of-assets) endpoint.

#### Pagination

* [Cursor pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#cursor-pagination) only.
* Returns the assets sorted by relevancy with page limits. Without a `sort` parameter, only the first 10,000 assets are returned. If your request includes a `sort` parameter, all assets are returned.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

<h3 id="search-assets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|true|Lists the search terms, separated by a space, used to identify the asset records.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Orders the returned records by: `name`, `created_at`, or `updated_at`. Defaults to sorting by relevance. Prepending `-` (`-name`, `-created_at`, or `-updated_at`) sorts the results in descending order by that value.<br>|
|page[before]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.before_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.<br>|
|page[after]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.after_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.<br>|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Specifies how many assets should be returned in the response, up to 100 assets per page.<br>|

## Filtered Search of Assets

<a id="opIdFilteredSearchItamAssets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/it_asset_management/assets/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "filter": {
      "$and": [
        {
          "model": {
            "$eq": "MacBook Pro"
          }
        },
        {
          "status": {
            "$eq": "01K9BT5XE82QS5DG58F4J8WQWY"
          }
        }
      ],
      "$or": [
        {
          "custom_object_fields.ip_address": {
            "$eq": "192.168.1.1"
          }
        },
        {
          "custom_object_fields.ip_address": {
            "$eq": "10.0.0.5"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/it_asset_management/assets/search`

Returns an array of assets that meet the complex search and filter criteria. For simple searches limited to text fields, use the [Search Assets API](/api-reference/it-asset-management/assets/#search-assets) endpoint instead.

Filters can contain either an individual [comparison object](#comparison-object) or an array of [comparison objects](#comparison-object) within logical namespaces.

A filter is a JSON object that has the following properties:

| Name      | Type   | Required | Description
| --------- | ------ | -------- | -----------
| ATTRIBUTE | object | no       | A [comparison object](#comparison-object) specifying an attribute value condition to be met for assets to match.<br/><br/>Examples are marked below.
| $and      | array  | no       | Array of comparison objects combined using logical AND
| $or       | array  | no       | Array of comparison objects combined using logical OR

##### Examples

```js
{
  "filter": {
    "model": { "$eq": "MacBook Pro" } // ATTRIBUTE (standard field)
  }
}
```

```js
{
  "filter": {
    "custom_object_fields.ip_address": { "$eq": "192.168.1.1" } // ATTRIBUTE (custom field)
  }
}
```

```js
// $or
{
  "filter": {
    "$or": [
      { "model": { "$eq": "MacBook Pro" } }, // ATTRIBUTE
      { "model": { "$eq": "ThinkPad X1" } } // ATTRIBUTE
    ]
  }
}
```

#### Comparison Object

A comparison object is essentially an 'if' statement that returns all asset records that meet the specified condition. Conditions are based on attribute values.

A comparison object is a JSON object that has the following properties:

| Name      | Type          | Required | Description
| --------- | ------------- | -------- | -----------
| FIELD_KEY | string        | yes      | To filter on a custom asset field, you must prepend `custom_object_fields.` on the field key. For example: `custom_object_fields.ip_address`<br/><br/>The following standard asset fields can be used without needing to prepend a namespace: `asset_type`, `user`, `organization`, `location`, `model`, `purchase_date`, `status`
| OPERATOR  | string        | yes      | A comparison operator, such as `$eq`
| VALUE     | string, array | yes      | The value you're filtering for

* Date values should be in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.

#### Pagination

* [Cursor pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/#cursor-pagination) only.
* Returns the assets sorted by relevancy with page limits. Requests with a `sort` parameter return all assets; requests without a `sort` parameter return the first 10,000 assets only.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filter": {
    "$and": [
      {
        "model": {
          "$eq": "MacBook Pro"
        }
      },
      {
        "status": {
          "$eq": "01K9BT5XE82QS5DG58F4J8WQWY"
        }
      }
    ],
    "$or": [
      {
        "custom_object_fields.ip_address": {
          "$eq": "192.168.1.1"
        }
      },
      {
        "custom_object_fields.ip_address": {
          "$eq": "10.0.0.5"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="filtered-search-of-assets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|Lists the search terms, separated by a space, used to identify the asset records.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Orders the returned records by: `name`, `created_at`, or `updated_at`. Defaults to sorting by relevance. Prepending `-` (`-name`, `-created_at`, or `-updated_at`) sorts the results in descending order by that value.<br>|
|page[before]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.before_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request<br>|
|page[after]|query|string|false|A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.after_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request<br>|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Specifies how many assets should be returned in the response, up to 100 assets per page.<br>|
|body|body|[ItamAssetFilteredSearchRequestBasic](#schemaitamassetfilteredsearchrequestbasic) \| [ItamAssetFilteredSearchRequestComplex](#schemaitamassetfilteredsearchrequestcomplex)|true|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[ItamAssetFilteredSearchRequestBasic](#schemaitamassetfilteredsearchrequestbasic)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[ItamAssetFilteredSearchRequestComplex](#schemaitamassetfilteredsearchrequestcomplex)|false|none|

## Delete Asset Type

<a id="opIdDeleteItamAssetType"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/it_asset_management/asset_types/01K9AMAY0ST7VTVSG7SDAMR4P1 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/it_asset_management/asset_types/{asset_type_id}`

Deletes an asset type with the specified id. The deletion will fail if
the asset type is one of the predefined standard asset types, is a base asset
type, has child asset types, has asset records, or still
has custom field keys assigned to it.

#### Allowed For

* Admins

<h3 id="delete-asset-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|asset_type_id|path|string|true|The id of the asset type|

> Example responses

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "description": "Record validation errors",
  "details": {
    "base": [
      {
        "description": "Base Asset Type cannot be deleted."
      }
    ]
  },
  "error": "RecordInvalid"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-asset-type-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No content response|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Returned if the asset type cannot be deleted for one of the reasons described above.|[ItamRecordInvalidError](#schemaitamrecordinvaliderror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Update Asset Type

<a id="opIdUpdateItamAssetType"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/it_asset_management/asset_types/01K9AMAY0ST7VTVSG7SDAMR4P1 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "asset_type": {
      "name": "Tablet"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/it_asset_management/asset_types/{asset_type_id}`

Updates an existing asset type. All fields are optional. Your request should include only the
properties you want to change.

The update will fail if you attempt to change the asset type's `parent_id`, the asset type's `name` isn't unique, the hierarchy depth limit would be exceeded, the asset type is one of the predefined standard asset types.

To set an icon, send a `multipart/form-data` request
instead of JSON — see the "Adding a photo to an asset type" code sample.
To remove an existing icon, send `"photo": null` in a normal JSON
request.

#### Allowed For

* Admins

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "asset_type": {
    "name": "Tablet"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-asset-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|asset_type_id|path|string|true|The id of the asset type|
|body|body|[ItamAssetTypeUpdateRequest](#schemaitamassettypeupdaterequest)|false|none|
|» asset_type|body|object|false|none|
|» » description|body|string \| null|false|A description of the asset type|
|» » external_id|body|string \| null|false|An id you can use to link asset types to external data|
|» » name|body|string|false|A unique display name for the asset type|
|» » photo|body|object \| null|false|Sets or removes the asset type's icon. Setting an icon requires a `multipart/form-data` request with a file field named `asset_type[photo][uploaded_data]` — see the "Adding a photo" code sample. Pass `null` to remove the existing icon via a normal JSON request.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "asset_type": {
    "created_by_user_id": 19837362232,
    "description": null,
    "display_icon_url": "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/system/record_photos/9812637451/large_1.png",
    "external_id": null,
    "field_keys": [
      "imei",
      "phone_number"
    ],
    "hierarchy_depth": 2,
    "icon_url": "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/system/record_photos/9812637451/large_1.png",
    "id": "01K9BT5X539BKC8SEF430HAJHJ",
    "is_standard": false,
    "name": "Mobile",
    "parent_id": "01K9BT5SXPR60963HJVPWTZQHD",
    "updated_by_user_id": 19837362232,
    "url": "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/it_asset_management/asset_types/01K9BT5X539BKC8SEF430HAJHJ"
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "description": "Record validation errors",
  "details": {
    "base": [
      {
        "description": "Parent ITAM AssetType may not be updated after creation."
      }
    ]
  },
  "error": "RecordInvalid"
}
```

<h3 id="update-asset-type-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success response|[ItamAssetTypeResponse](#schemaitamassettyperesponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Returned if the asset type update is rejected for one of the reasons described above.|[ItamRecordInvalidError](#schemaitamrecordinvaliderror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<a id="opIdCreateTaskListTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -X POST \
```

`PUT /api/v2/task_list_templates/{task_list_template_id}`

Creates, modifies, or deletes tasks in a task list template. Only the tasks included in the `task_list_template` object in the request are updated. Tasks that aren't specified in the request are unchanged.

#### Allowed For

* Admins

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "task_list_template": {
    "name": "Updating a task list template",
    "tasks": [
      {
        "description": "Updating a task's description",
        "id": "01K3KVF20JE2QNA47FY6HJWQKB"
      },
      {
        "_destroy": true,
        "id": "01K3KVF23JWZ5M98BJBQHENYZ9"
      },
      {
        "description": "A new task",
        "name": "New task"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

|» » name|body|string|false|The new name of the task list template|
|» » tasks|body|[object]|false|Tasks to create, update, or delete for the template|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|Delete an existing task|
|» » » _destroy|body|boolean|true|If true, deletes the task|
|» » » id|body|string|true|The id of the task to delete from a task list template|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|Update an existing task|
|» » » description|body|string|false|The new description of the task|
|» » » id|body|string|true|The id of the task to update|
|» » » name|body|string|false|The new name of the task|
|» » » position|body|integer|false|The new position of the task within the task list template|
|» » » required|body|boolean|false|Whether the task is required when an agent adds the task list to a ticket|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|Create a new task|
|» » » description|body|string|false|The description of the task|

## Update Task Item

<a id="opIdUpdateTaskItem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/task_lists/01KFGZJGMQ3NA9DNX34Y5YGGYM/task_items/01KH2TPNQR5WB7MV9XEJD0FZHS \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "task_item": {
      "completed": true,
      "description": "Updated description",
      "name": "Updated task name"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/task_lists/{task_list_id}/task_items/{task_item_id}`

Updates a task item. Available fields depend on the item type:

**Any task item:** Use `completed` to mark the item complete (`true`) or incomplete (`false`). This is reflected as `is_completed` in the response. Completing all task items in a task list automatically marks the task list as completed.

**Custom task items only:** Also supports updating `name` and `description`. Template-based task items cannot be renamed.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

> Body parameter

```json
{
```

## Create Subticket

<a id="opIdCreateSubticket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/123456/task_items/01KH2TPNQR5WB7MV9XEJD0FZHS/subticket \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "subticket": {
      "comment": {
        "body": "Please provision a laptop for the new hire."
      },
      "requester_id": 123,
      "subject": "Need a laptop"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/task_items/{task_item_id}/subticket`

Creates a ticket and links it to the specified task item as a subticket. The parent ticket must not already be a subticket.

`subject` and `comment.body` are required. `comment.body` can contain up to 1,000 characters.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "subticket": {
    "comment": {
      "body": "Please provision a laptop for the new hire."
    },
    "requester_id": 123,
    "subject": "Need a laptop"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-subticket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|
|task_item_id|path|string|true|The id of the task item|
|body|body|[SubticketCreateRequest](#schemasubticketcreaterequest)|false|none|
|» subticket|body|object|true|none|
|» » assignee_id|body|integer(int64)|false|The id of the assignee|
|» » comment|body|object|true|none|
|» » » body|body|string|true|The first comment body|
|» » » public|body|boolean|false|Whether the first comment is public. Defaults to false.|
|» » requester_id|body|integer(int64)|false|The id of the requester. Defaults to the current user when omitted.|
|» » status|body|string|false|The initial status of the subticket. Supported values are new, open, pending, and hold.|
|» » subject|body|string|true|The subject of the subticket|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » status|new|
|» » status|open|
|» » status|pending|
|» » status|hold|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "subticket": {
    "id": 456
  },
  "task_object_link": {
    "created_at": "2025-08-06T17:10:00Z",
    "created_by": {
      "id": 123,
      "name": "Ada Lovelace"
    },
    "id": "01KH2Y95EFXWNA0BVXD4R2JH22",
    "linked_object_status": "New",
    "nice_id": 456,
    "object_type": "Ticket",
    "private": false,
    "task_item_instance_id": "01KH2TPNQR5WB7MV9XEJD0FZHS",
    "updated_at": "2025-08-06T17:10:00Z",
    "updated_by": {
      "id": 123,
      "name": "Ada Lovelace"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-subticket-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created response|[SubticketCreateResponse](#schemasubticketcreateresponse)|

basicAuth

## Create Task List

<a id="opIdCreateTaskList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/123456/task_lists \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "task_list": {
      "description": "Custom task list for this ticket",
      "name": "Custom follow-up checklist"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/task_lists`

Adds a task list to the specified ticket. There are two ways to create a task list:

**Create from a template:** Include `task_list_template_id` in the request body. The new task list will inherit the template's name, description, and task items.

**Create a custom task list:** Include `name` (and optionally `description`) instead of `task_list_template_id`. Custom task lists have no template and allow you to add, update, and delete task items individually.

A ticket can hold more than one task list, up to the account's task list limit. Requests beyond that limit return a 422 error.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "task_list": {
    "description": "Custom task list for this ticket",
    "name": "Custom follow-up checklist"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-task-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the ticket|
|body|body|[TaskListCreateRequest](#schematasklistcreaterequest)|false|none|
|» task_list|body|object|false|To create a task list from a template, provide `task_list_template_id`.<br>To create a custom task list without a template, provide `name` (and optionally `description`).<br>|
|» » description|body|string|false|The description of the custom task list.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the custom task list. Required if `task_list_template_id` is not provided.|
|» » task_list_template_id|body|string|false|The id of the task list template to attach to the ticket. Required if not creating a custom task list.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "task_list": {
    "created_at": "2025-08-06T17:08:40Z",
    "description": "Complete HR, IT, and payroll setup for new employees.",
    "id": "01K3KVF23JWZ5M98BJBQHENYZ9",
    "is_required": false,
    "name": "Onboarding checklist",
    "task_count": 2,
    "task_list_template_id": "01K205PG0J2ET0B8AFHA106C1E",
    "ticket_id": "1",
    "updated_at": "2025-08-06T17:08:40Z"
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "description": "Record validation errors",
  "details": {
    "base": [
      {
        "description": "Maximum of 5 task list(s) per ticket has been reached."
      }
    ]
  },
  "error": "RecordInvalid"
}
```

<h3 id="create-task-list-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created response|[TaskListCreateResponse](#schematasklistcreateresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The task list couldn't be created. For example, the ticket already has the maximum number of task lists allowed.|[TaskListValidationErrorResponse](#schematasklistvalidationerrorresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

The Explore plan of the account. An empty object when the account has no recognised Explore plan type.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|active|boolean|false|none|Whether the Explore subscription is active (subscribed, free, or in an unexpired trial)|
|boost_expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the boost expires, or null when the plan is not boosted|
|boosted_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the boosted plan, or null when the plan is not boosted|
|boosted_plan_type|integer \| null|false|none|The plan type id of the active boost, or null when the plan is not boosted|
|boosted_weight|integer \| null|false|none|The weight of the boosted plan, or null when the plan is not boosted|
|days_left_in_trial|integer|false|none|Days left in the Explore trial. -1 when there is no trial or it has expired|
|onboarded_status|object|false|none|The account's Explore onboarding status, as returned by Explore.<br>An empty object if Explore is unavailable.<br>|
|plan_name|string|false|none|The Explore plan name, for example "Professional"|
|plan_type|integer|false|none|The Explore plan type id|
|plan_weight|integer|false|none|The relative weight of the plan, used to order plans|
|precanned_dashboards|[object]|false|none|The precanned dashboards available to the requesting user, as returned by Explore.<br>An empty array if Explore is unavailable.<br>|
|state|string|false|none|The state of the Explore subscription|
|trial|boolean|false|none|Whether the Explore subscription is a trial|
|trial_expires_on|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the Explore trial expires|

```json
  "focus_mode": true,
  "idle_timeout_enabled": true,
  "show_user_profile_page_toggle": true,
  "spell_checker_enabled": true,
  "split_view_enabled": true,
  "split_view_tos_accepted": true,

  "suggested_assignees_eap_enabled": true,

    1
  ],

  "unified_navigation_enabled": true,
  "unified_navigation_terms_and_conditions_accepted": true
}
```

Agent workspace/UI settings. See `settings_controller_support.rb`
(`args_transformation_map['agents']`).

A non-admin agent may update this category alone or alongside `tickets`, but
only when every key is one of `spell_checker_enabled`,
`ai_async_comment_translations_eap_enabled` or
`ai_translation_disclosure_enabled` — any other key in the same request falls
back to requiring full admin (`tickets_settings_payload?`,
`settings_controller.rb`).

`additionalProperties: true`: the controller also dynamically permits two
boolean keys per active, non-excluded EAP feature — `<feature>_tos_accepted`
and `<feature>_enabled` for each `Zendesk::Eap::Catalog.writable_account_settings`
entry (`eap_feature_parameters`/`writable_account_setting_binding`,
merged into both the outer gate and this category's write map). That set is not
enumerable statically — it depends on which EAP features exist and are not
excluded at request time — so it is intentionally left open here rather than
listed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_dashboard_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|agent_home|boolean|false|none|none|
|agent_workspace|boolean|false|none|May be silently dropped without effect in either direction<br>(`validate_agent_workspace_update`, `settings_controller_support.rb`):<br>turning it on is dropped unless the account is `agent_workspace_compatible?`<br>and has `aw_self_serve_migration_enabled`, and (if Groups & Departments<br>aren't migrated) dropped outright when the account has a Chat product,<br>otherwise `groups.check_group_name_uniqueness` is forced to `true` as a side<br>effect; turning it off is dropped if the account has native messaging or<br>`aw_prevent_opt_out` without the auto-activation override. Setting it to<br>`false` also forces `routing.enabled` to `false`<br>(`settings_controller_support.rb:481-483`).<br>|
|ai_async_comment_translations_eap_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|ai_translation_disclosure_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|dark_mode_agent_workspace|boolean|false|none|none|
|dark_mode_terms_and_conditions_accepted|boolean|false|none|none|
|explore_zra_monitoring_assistant_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|focus_mode|boolean|false|none|none|
|idle_timeout_enabled|boolean|false|none|Deprecated: silently dropped without effect for accounts with the<br>`deprecate_idle_timeout_from_settings_api` Arturo<br>(`has_deprecate_idle_timeout_from_settings_api?`,<br>`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|show_user_profile_page_toggle|boolean|false|none|Silently dropped without effect unless the account has<br>`has_ocp_customer_profile?` (`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|spell_checker_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|split_view_enabled|boolean|false|none|Writing this also writes the canonical EAP setting<br>`split_view_eap_enabled` to the same value unless<br>`split_view_eap_enabled` itself is explicitly set in the same request<br>(`synchronize_split_view_eap_settings`,<br>`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|split_view_tos_accepted|boolean|false|none|Writing this also writes the canonical EAP setting<br>`split_view_eap_tos_accepted` to the same value unless<br>`split_view_eap_tos_accepted` itself is explicitly set in the same request<br>(`synchronize_split_view_eap_settings`,<br>`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|suggested_assignees_all_groups|boolean|false|none|none|
|suggested_assignees_eap_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|suggested_assignees_group_ids|[integer]|false|none|Each id must be a positive integer (`Parameters.gt(0)`). Duplicates are<br>removed before persistence (`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|unified_agent_statuses|boolean|false|none|For accounts with `has_omnichannel_contact_centre_enabled?`, this is<br>overwritten to match `routing.enabled` whenever `routing.enabled` is<br>present in the same request — even if this request does not otherwise<br>touch `agents` (`sync_routing_and_unified_agent_statuses`,<br>`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|unified_navigation_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|unified_navigation_terms_and_conditions_accepted|boolean|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_AccountSettingsBrandingInput">AccountSettingsBrandingInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccountsettingsbrandinginput"></a>
<a id="schema_AccountSettingsBrandingInput"></a>
<a id="tocSaccountsettingsbrandinginput"></a>
<a id="tocsaccountsettingsbrandinginput"></a>

```json
{
  "header_color": "string",
  "page_background_color": "string",
  "tab_background_color": "string",
  "text_color": "string"
}
```

Branding colors. See `Branding.from_hash` (`lib/branding.rb`), invoked from
`settings_controller_support.rb` as
`current_account.branding = Branding.from_hash(setting_arguments['branding'])`.

**Destructive partial**: `Branding.from_hash` builds a brand-new `Branding`
instance seeded with hardcoded defaults (`03363D` / `7FA239` / `FFFFFF` /
`333333`), then overwrites only the keys present and valid in this payload — it
does not start from the account's current branding. Any property omitted from
this object, or supplied with an invalid value (must be a 6-character hex
string), is silently reset to that hardcoded default rather than left
unchanged. Sending only one color resets the other three.

**Two `Branding` attributes are not exposed here at all**: `tab_hover_color`
(default `ACC76B`) and `sidebox_color` (default `F6F6F6`) exist on the model
(`lib/branding.rb`) but have no corresponding key in this endpoint's parameter
gate (`settings_controller.rb`). Because `Branding.from_hash` always
constructs a fresh instance rather than seeding from the account's current
branding, **any request that includes a `branding` key at all unconditionally
resets both of these to their hardcoded defaults** — there is no way to
preserve the account's current `tab_hover_color`/`sidebox_color` through this
endpoint. This is pre-existing behavior, not introduced by this change; flagged
here so a caller reading this schema isn't surprised by it.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|header_color|string|false|none|6-character hex color, no leading `#` (`Branding.validate`). Omitted or<br>invalid ⇒ reset to the hardcoded default `03363D`, not left unchanged. See<br>the destructive-partial note on the parent object.<br>|
|page_background_color|string|false|none|6-character hex color, no leading `#`. Omitted or invalid ⇒ reset to the<br>hardcoded default `333333`, not left unchanged. See the destructive-partial<br>note on the parent object.<br>|
|tab_background_color|string|false|none|6-character hex color, no leading `#`. Omitted or invalid ⇒ reset to the<br>hardcoded default `7FA239`, not left unchanged. See the destructive-partial<br>note on the parent object.<br>|
|text_color|string|false|none|6-character hex color, no leading `#`. Omitted or invalid ⇒ reset to the<br>hardcoded default `FFFFFF`, not left unchanged. See the destructive-partial<br>note on the parent object.<br>|
