<h2 id="tocS_AccountSettingsBrandsObject">AccountSettingsBrandsObject</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccountsettingsbrandsobject"></a>
<a id="schema_AccountSettingsBrandsObject"></a>
<a id="tocSaccountsettingsbrandsobject"></a>
<a id="tocsaccountsettingsbrandsobject"></a>

```json
{
  "brand_user_separation_scope_query_default": "0",
  "default_brand_id": 0,
  "end_user_across_brand_requests": true,
  "end_user_upgrade_brand_association_behavior": "string",
  "new_agent_brand_association_behavior": "string",
  "require_brand_on_new_tickets": true
}
```

Brand settings. See [Brands](#brands)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brand_user_separation_scope_query_default|string|false|none|Controls which users the [List Users](/api-reference/ticketing/users/users/#list-users),<br>[Count Users](/api-reference/ticketing/users/users/#count-users),<br>[Search Users](/api-reference/ticketing/users/users/#search-users) and<br>[Autocomplete Users](/api-reference/ticketing/users/users/#autocomplete-users) endpoints<br>return when an external request omits `brand_id`.<br><br>* `"0"` — customers in non-separated brands and all team members (default). A string,<br>  matching the `brand_id=0` (account scope) value of the users endpoints.<br>* `"default_brand"` — customers in the default brand and all team members. Falls back to `"0"`<br>  if the default brand doesn't have user separation enabled.<br>* `"all"` — customers and team members across all brands, within the caller's permissions.<br>* `"error"` — reject the request with `400 Bad Request` and<br>  `{"error": "brand_id parameter is required"}`. Integrations that don't send<br>  `brand_id` stop working.<br><br>Only returned, and only writable, when brand separation is available on the account.<br>Only admins can update it. Any other stored value is treated as `"0"`.<br>|
|default_brand_id|integer(int64)|false|none|none|
|end_user_across_brand_requests|boolean|false|none|none|
|end_user_upgrade_brand_association_behavior|string|false|none|Controls how end users are associated with brands when upgraded to agents.|
|new_agent_brand_association_behavior|string|false|none|Controls how new agents are associated with brands. Determines the default brand assignment for newly created agents.|
|require_brand_on_new_tickets|boolean|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|brand_user_separation_scope_query_default|0|
|brand_user_separation_scope_query_default|default_brand|
|brand_user_separation_scope_query_default|all|
|brand_user_separation_scope_query_default|error|

<h2 id="tocS_AccountSettingsMessagingInactivityInput">AccountSettingsMessagingInactivityInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccountsettingsmessaginginactivityinput"></a>
<a id="schema_AccountSettingsMessagingInactivityInput"></a>
<a id="tocSaccountsettingsmessaginginactivityinput"></a>
<a id="tocsaccountsettingsmessaginginactivityinput"></a>

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "end_session": true,
  "reminders": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "tags": [
        "string"
      ],
      "ticket_status_id": 0,
      "timeout": 60
    }
  ],
  "ticket_status_id": 0,
  "timeout": 3
}
```

Messaging inactivity (capacity release) settings. See
`settings_controller_support.rb` (`args_transformation_map['messaging_inactivity']`),
`app/validators/messaging_inactivity_validator.rb`, and
`settings_controller.rb#update`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|end_session|boolean|false|none|none|
|reminders|[object]|false|none|At most 3 reminders. Tags on each reminder are lower-cased, split on commas<br>and whitespace, deduplicated and compacted before validation<br>(`sanitize_tags`, `settings_controller.rb`). Then validated positionally by<br>`MessagingInactivityValidator` — the array's index, not any field on the<br>item, decides which fields are required: the first reminder (index 0) must<br>omit both `timeout` and `ticket_status_id`; the second (index 1) must<br>supply `timeout`; the third (index 2) must supply both `timeout` and a<br>non-null `ticket_status_id`. A validation failure on any reminder renders a<br>400 for the whole request.<br>|
|ticket_status_id|integer|false|none|none|
|timeout|integer|false|none|Minutes. Enforced at the parameter gate as `3..15`.|

|messaging_end_session|boolean|false|none|Setting this to `false` also forces `routing.transform_to_email_enabled` to<br>`false` in the same request (`settings_controller_support.rb:485-487`), and<br>is itself required (this request's value, or the account's existing<br>setting) for `routing.transform_to_email_enabled` to be enabled<br>(`validate_assignment_setting_set`, `settings_controller.rb`).<br>|
|messaging_end_user_presence|boolean|false|none|none|
|messaging_ticket_subject_template|string|false|none|Silently dropped without effect unless the account has<br>`has_permissions_data_masking_adpp?` — the controller only registers this<br>key in its write map for accounts with that capability<br>(`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|messaging_trust_unverified_claim|boolean|false|none|none|
|messaging_use_unverified_email|boolean|false|none|none|

|Property|Value|

|messaging_ticket_subject_template|requester_id|

Omnichannel routing settings. See `settings_controller_support.rb`
(`args_transformation_map['routing']`) and
`validate_assignment_setting_set`/`settings_controller.rb`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assignment_method|string|false|none|none|
|auto_accept_messaging_enabled|boolean|false|none|Rejected with a 422 if this and `reassignment_messaging_enabled` would both<br>end up enabled together (`validate_assignment_setting_set`,<br>`settings_controller.rb`).<br>|
|auto_open_email_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|autorouting_tag|string|false|none|Lower-cased before being saved.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|For accounts with `has_omnichannel_contact_centre_enabled?`, sending this<br>also overwrites `agents.unified_agent_statuses` to the same value, even if<br>this request does not otherwise touch `agents`<br>(`sync_routing_and_unified_agent_statuses`, `settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|focus_mode_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|max_email_capacity|integer|false|none|none|
|max_messaging_capacity|integer|false|none|none|
|messaging_activity_routing_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|missed_messaging_assignments|object|false|none|Both this key and `missed_talk_assignments` are dropped from the request<br>before any validation or processing unless the account has the<br>`ocr_missed_assignments_limit` Arturo<br>(`has_ocr_missed_assignments_limit?`, `settings_controller.rb`). Unlike<br>every other property in this payload, only the keys supplied here are<br>written — they are merged into the account's existing stored<br>`routing_missed_messaging_assignments` hash, so omitted keys keep their<br>stored values (`merge_missed_assignments_settings`,<br>`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|missed_talk_assignments|object|false|none|Dropped from the request before any validation or processing unless the<br>account has the `ocr_missed_assignments_limit` Arturo<br>(`has_ocr_missed_assignments_limit?`, `settings_controller.rb`) — see<br>`missed_messaging_assignments` for the merge-into-stored-hash semantics.<br>|
|reassignment_agent_status_change_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|reassignment_agent_status_change_messaging_agent_statuses|[integer]|false|none|none|
|reassignment_agent_status_change_messaging_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|reassignment_agent_status_change_messaging_ticket_priorities|[integer]|false|none|none|
|reassignment_agent_status_change_support_agent_statuses|[integer]|false|none|none|
|reassignment_agent_status_change_support_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|reassignment_agent_status_change_support_ticket_priorities|[integer]|false|none|none|
|reassignment_messaging_enabled|boolean|false|none|Rejected with a 422 if this and `auto_accept_messaging_enabled` would both<br>end up enabled together (`validate_assignment_setting_set`,<br>`settings_controller.rb`).<br>|
|reassignment_messaging_timeout|integer|false|none|none|
|reassignment_reopened_tickets_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|reassignment_reopened_tickets_messaging_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|reassignment_reopened_tickets_messaging_statuses|[integer]|false|none|none|
|reassignment_reopened_tickets_support_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|reassignment_reopened_tickets_support_statuses|[integer]|false|none|none|
|reassignment_talk_timeout|integer|false|none|none|
|reassignment_through_queues_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|skills_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|skills_timeout_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|skills_timeout_messaging|integer|false|none|none|
|skills_timeout_support|integer|false|none|none|
|skills_timeout_talk|integer|false|none|none|
|throttle_cool_down_time|integer|false|none|Validated to 30-720; an out-of-range update fails the save<br>(`register_property :routing_throttle_cool_down_time`,<br>`app/models/account_setting.rb`).<br>|
|throttle_enabled_email|boolean|false|none|none|
|throttle_enabled_messaging|boolean|false|none|none|
|throttle_percentage_email|integer|false|none|Validated to 1-99; an out-of-range update fails the save<br>(`register_property :routing_throttle_percentage_email`,<br>`app/models/account_setting.rb`).<br>|
|throttle_percentage_messaging|integer|false|none|Validated to 1-99; an out-of-range update fails the save<br>(`register_property :routing_throttle_percentage_messaging`,<br>`app/models/account_setting.rb`).<br>|
|throttle_ramp_up_time_email|integer|false|none|Validated to 5-180; an out-of-range update fails the save<br>(`register_property :routing_throttle_ramp_up_time_email`,<br>`app/models/account_setting.rb`).<br>|
|throttle_ramp_up_time_messaging|integer|false|none|Validated to 5-180; an out-of-range update fails the save<br>(`register_property :routing_throttle_ramp_up_time_messaging`,<br>`app/models/account_setting.rb`).<br>|
|ticket_sorting_prioritize_sla|boolean|false|none|none|
|transform_to_email_enabled|boolean|false|none|Rejected with a 422 unless `messaging.messaging_end_session` (this<br>request's value, or the account's existing<br>`messaging_end_session_enabled` setting) is enabled<br>(`validate_assignment_setting_set`, `settings_controller.rb`). Also forced<br>to `false` as a side effect whenever `messaging.messaging_end_session` is<br>explicitly set to `false` in the same request<br>(`settings_controller_support.rb:485-487`).<br>|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|assignment_method|highest_spare_capacity|
|assignment_method|round_robin|
|assignment_method|highest_percentage_spare_capacity|

non-admin agent may update alone or alongside a restricted `agents` subset — see
`conditional_require_permission_or_admin!`/`tickets_settings_payload?`,
`settings_controller.rb`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accepted_new_collaboration_tos|boolean|false|none|none|
|agent_can_change_requester|boolean|false|none|none|
|agent_email_ccs_become_followers|boolean|false|none|Forced to `false` whenever `comment_email_ccs_allowed` is explicitly set to<br>`false` in the same request, overriding any other value sent for this<br>property in that request (`settings_controller_support.rb:383-386`).<br>|
|agent_invitation_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|agent_ticket_deletion|boolean|false|none|none|
|allow_group_reset|boolean|false|none|none|
|app_shortcuts_context_panel_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|assign_tickets_upon_solve|boolean|false|none|none|
|attachment_otp|boolean|false|none|Silently dropped without effect, together with `attachment_otp_duration`,<br>unless the account has the `attachment_otp_challenge` capability<br>(`has_attachment_otp_challenge?`, `settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|attachment_otp_duration|integer|false|none|Silently dropped without effect, together with `attachment_otp`, unless the<br>account has the `attachment_otp_challenge` capability<br>(`has_attachment_otp_challenge?`, `settings_controller_support.rb`). The<br>saved value is validated to 1-720 (`register_property<br>:attachment_otp_duration`, `app/models/account_setting.rb`); an out-of-range<br>update fails the save.<br>|
|attachment_public_duration|integer|false|none|none|
|attachment_public_expiration|boolean|false|none|none|
|audio_recorder_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|auto_translation_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|auto_updated_ccs_followers_rules|boolean|false|none|Sending `false` is a no-op: the key is dropped before persisting unless<br>truthy (`acct_settings.delete('auto_updated_ccs_followers_rules') unless<br>acct_settings['auto_updated_ccs_followers_rules']`,<br>`settings_controller_support.rb`), so this setting can be turned on via this<br>endpoint but not turned off.<br>|
|bcc_archive_address|string|false|none|none|
|cc_blacklist|string|false|none|none|
|cc_email_template|string|false|none|Only takes effect when `new_collaboration_disabled?` is true — see<br>`collaboration` above.<br>|
|cc_subject_template|string|false|none|Only takes effect when `new_collaboration_disabled?` is true — see<br>`collaboration` above.<br>|
|ccs_followers_no_rollback|boolean|false|none|none|
|ccs_requester_excluded_public_comments|boolean|false|none|none|
|chat_sla_enablement|boolean|false|none|none|
|collaboration|boolean|false|none|Only takes effect for accounts where new-collaboration is disabled, i.e.<br>`new_collaboration_disabled?` is true — the account has neither<br>`has_follower_and_email_cc_collaborations_enabled?` nor accepted the<br>new-collaboration EAP ToS (`settings_controller_support.rb`). Accepted at<br>the gate regardless of account state; silently has no effect otherwise.<br>|
|collaborators_addable_only_by_agents|boolean|false|none|Only takes effect when `new_collaboration_disabled?` is true — see<br>`collaboration` above.<br>|
|collaborators_settable_in_help_center|boolean|false|none|none|
|comment_email_ccs_allowed|boolean|false|none|Setting this to `false` also forces `agent_email_ccs_become_followers` and<br>`light_agent_email_ccs_allowed` to `false` in the same request, even if this<br>request explicitly supplies a different value for either of them<br>(`settings_controller_support.rb:383-386`).<br>|
|comments_public_by_default|boolean|false|none|none|
|copy_original_assignee_and_group_to_followup|boolean|false|none|none|
|custom_allowed_attachment_file_types_list|string|false|none|none|
|custom_statuses_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|default_solved_ticket_reassignment_strategy|string|false|none|none|
|default_to_draft_mode|boolean|false|none|none|
|edit_ticket_skills_permission|integer|false|none|Any integer is accepted at the gate, but only `0`-`3` are meaningful<br>(`EDITABLE_BY_ADMINS`/`VISIBLE_TO_AGENTS`/`HIDDEN_FOR_ALL`/`EDITABLE_BY_ALL`).<br>Any other value is silently coerced to `0` before being saved<br>(`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|email_attachments|boolean|false|none|none|
|email_ccs_addable_only_by_agents_via_email|boolean|false|none|none|
|email_comments_public|boolean|false|none|none|
|email_redact_attachments_when_placeholders_disallow|boolean|false|none|none|
|emoji_autocompletion|boolean|false|none|none|
|end_user_attachments|boolean|false|none|none|
|follower_and_email_cc_collaborations|boolean|false|none|none|
|follower_email_template|string|false|none|none|
|follower_subject_template|string|false|none|none|
|has_color_text|boolean|false|none|none|
|is_first_comment_private_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|light_agent_email_ccs_allowed|boolean|false|none|Forced to `false` whenever `comment_email_ccs_allowed` is explicitly set to<br>`false` in the same request, overriding any other value sent for this<br>property in that request (`settings_controller_support.rb:383-386`).<br>|
|list_empty_views|boolean|false|none|none|
|list_newest_comments_first|boolean|false|none|none|
|markdown_ticket_comments|boolean|false|none|none|
|messaging_transcript_public|boolean|false|none|none|
|modern_ticket_reassignment|boolean|false|none|none|
|modify_closed_tickets_customer_setting|boolean|false|none|none|
|only_allowed_attachment_file_types|string \| boolean|false|none|When set to the string `custom`, `custom_allowed_attachment_file_types_list`<br>(this request's value, or the account's existing one) must be non-blank or<br>the update raises (`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|only_allowed_attachment_file_types_agreement|string|false|none|none|
|private_attachments|boolean|false|none|none|
|private_end_user_attachments|boolean|false|none|none|
|push_solved_ticket_reassignment_strategy_now|boolean|false|none|Not stored as a setting: a truthy value enqueues a one-off<br>`GroupDefaultReassignmentStrategyJob`, throttled per-account<br>(`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|reengagement|boolean|false|none|none|
|render_custom_uri_hyperlinks|string|false|none|none|
|rich_text_comments|boolean|false|none|none|
|show_modern_ticket_reassignment|boolean|false|none|none|

|ticket_auto_tagging|boolean|false|none|none|
|ticket_email_ccs_suspension_threshold|integer|false|none|none|
|ticket_followers_allowed|boolean|false|none|none|
|ticket_id_sequence|string|false|none|Only takes effect when it parses to an integer greater than the account's<br>current ticket-id sequence position; otherwise silently ignored<br>(`update_ticket_id_sequence`, `settings_controller_support.rb`). Cannot lower<br>the sequence.<br>|


The account settings to update. Every category and property is optional — a
request only needs to include the settings it wants to change; omitted
categories and properties are left unchanged. See
`allow_parameters :update`, `app/controllers/api/v2/account/settings_controller.rb`,
and `Zendesk::Accounts::SettingsControllerSupport.normalize_and_update_settings`,
`lib/zendesk/accounts/settings_controller_support.rb`, for the full trace.

A non-admin agent may only update this object when it is either `{"tickets": ...}`
alone, or `{"agents": ...}` (or both `agents` and `tickets`) where every `agents`
key is one of `spell_checker_enabled`, `ai_async_comment_translations_eap_enabled`
or `ai_translation_disclosure_enabled` — any other combination of top-level keys
requires full admin (`conditional_require_permission_or_admin!`/
`tickets_settings_payload?`, `settings_controller.rb`). This authorization rule
ranges over the whole request body, not any single property, and cannot be
expressed as a schema constraint here — see the property descriptions on
`agents`/`tickets` instead.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active_features|object|false|none|none|
|agents|object|false|none|See the authorization note on the parent object: a non-admin agent may<br>only send this key when every property in it is one of<br>`spell_checker_enabled`, `ai_async_comment_translations_eap_enabled` or<br>`ai_translation_disclosure_enabled`.<br>|
|ai|object|false|none|none|
|api|object|false|none|none|
|approvals|object|false|none|none|
|automatic_answers|object|false|none|none|
|branding|object|false|none|none|
|brands|object|false|none|none|
|cross_sell|object|false|none|none|
|device_metadata|object|false|none|none|
|email|object|false|none|none|
|google_apps|object|false|none|none|
|groups|object|false|none|none|
|it_asset_management|object|false|none|none|
|knowledge|object|false|none|none|
|localization|object|false|none|none|
|messaging|object|false|none|none|
|messaging_inactivity|object|false|none|none|
|messaging_routing|object|false|none|The whole key is deleted from the request without effect unless the<br>account has `messaging_routing_enabled` (`has_messaging_routing_enabled?`,<br>`settings_controller.rb`).<br>|
|notifications|object|false|none|The whole object is dropped without effect unless the account has the<br>`admin_center_framework_api_notifications_setting` Arturo — see<br>`AccountSettingsNotificationsInput.yaml`.<br>|
|onboarding|object|false|none|none|
|qa|object|false|none|none|
|realtime_insights|object|false|none|none|
|routing|object|false|none|none|
|rule|object|false|none|none|
|saas_management_enabled|boolean|false|none|Top-level setting, not nested under a category<br>(`settings_controller_support.rb`).<br>|
|sandbox|object|false|none|none|
|side_conversations|object|false|none|none|
|surveys|object|false|none|none|
|ticket_form|object|false|none|none|
|tickets|object|false|none|See the authorization note on the parent object: a non-admin agent may<br>send this key alone (or with a restricted `agents` subset).<br>|
|user|object|false|none|none|

The current subscription configuration of the account

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_type|string|false|none|The account type, for example "trial", "spoke", "customer", "sandbox", "sponsored" or "unknown"|
|active|boolean|false|none|The account's active status|
|add_agents_available|boolean|false|none|Whether agents can be added to the subscription|
|base_agents|integer|false|none|The number of Zendesk agents without any secondary agents included|
|billing_backend|string|false|none|The account's billing backend|
|collect_vat|boolean|false|none|Whether VAT is collected for the subscription|
|created_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the subscription was created|
|days_left_in_trial|integer|false|none|Days left in the trial period. 0 if the account is not in a trial|
|dunning|string|false|none|The account's dunning status, for example "OK", "WARNING", "SECONDCHANCE", "LASTCHANCE" or "SUSPENDED"|
|file_upload_cap|integer|false|none|The maximum attachment size in megabytes|
|future_subscription_exists|boolean|false|none|Whether a future-dated subscription exists in Zuora|
|help_desk_size|string|false|none|The account's help desk size, for example "Small team"|
|is_elite|boolean|false|none|The account's elite status|
|max_agents|integer|false|none|The total number of Zendesk agents|
|plan_name|string|false|none|The plan name, for example "Starter", "Regular", "Plus" or "Enterprise" (depends on the pricing model)|
|plan_type|string|false|none|The plan type, for example "Small", "Medium", "Large" or "ExtraLarge"|
|plans|object|false|none|Per-product plan details. The `zendesk`, `zopim`, `voice`, `guide`, `tpe`, `explore`,<br>`answer_bot` and `outbound` keys are present. `guide`, `explore`, `answer_bot` and `outbound`<br>are empty objects unless the `pricing` side-load is requested.<br>|
|pricing_model_revision|integer|false|none|The id of the pricing model used for this subscription|
|sales_model|string|false|none|The account's sales model|
|source|string \| null|false|none|The lead source through which the account was created|
|suite_active|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the account has a suite trial or paid suite|
|suite_allowed|boolean|false|none|Whether the account is allowed to use the Suite|
|support_experience_type|string|false|none|The support experience type, for example "CX" or "ES"|
|suspended|boolean|false|none|The account's suspension status|
|term_end_date|string \| null|false|none|The end date of the current subscription term|
|trial|boolean|false|none|The account's trial status|
|trial_expires_on|string \| null|false|none|The end date of the trial|
|updated_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the subscription was last updated|
|voice_customer|boolean|false|none|Whether the account is a voice customer|
|zuora_payment_method_type|string \| null|false|none|The payment method type in Zuora, for example "manual invoice", "paypal", "credit card" or "none"|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|actor|object|false|read-only|The full user record of the user responsible for the ticket activity. See [Users](/api-reference/ticketing/users/users/)|
|actor_id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The id of the user responsible for the ticket activity. An `actor_id` of "-1" is a Zendesk system user, such as an automations action.|
|created_at|string|false|read-only|When the record was created|
|id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Automatically assigned on creation|
|object|object|false|read-only|The content of the activity. Can be a ticket, comment, or change.|
|target|object|false|read-only|The target of the activity, a ticket.|
|title|string|false|read-only|Description of the activity|
|updated_at|string|false|read-only|When the record was last updated|
|url|string|false|read-only|The API url of the activity|
|user|object|false|read-only|The full user record of the agent making the request. See [Users](/api-reference/ticketing/users/users/)|
|user_id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The id of the agent making the request|
|verb|string|false|read-only|The type of activity. Can be "tickets.assignment", "tickets.comment", or "tickets.priority_increase"|


### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|false|none|If false, the token is inactive and cannot be used to authenticate API requests|
|assigned_user_id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The id of the agent or admin the token is assigned to. Only present when the token<br>was created with a `user_id`.<br>|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The time the token was created|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The description of the token that displays in Admin Center|
|id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Automatically assigned upon creation|
|last_used|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|The time the token was last used to authenticate a request. Null if the token has never been used|
|token|string|false|read-only|The full, unencrypted token value. For security reasons, this is only ever returned once,<br>in the response to the request that created the token. Store this value securely — it<br>cannot be retrieved again. On all other requests, `visible_token` is returned instead.<br>|
|updated_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|The time of the last update of the token. Null for legacy tokens that have never been updated|
|user_email|string|false|read-only|The email address of the agent who created the token. Only included when<br>`include_users=true` is passed as a query parameter.<br>|
|user_id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The id of the agent who created the token. Only included when `include_users=true` is<br>passed as a query parameter.<br>|
|user_name|string|false|read-only|The name of the agent who created the token. Only included when `include_users=true` is<br>passed as a query parameter.<br>|
|visible_token|string|false|read-only|The first 8 characters of the token, truncated for display purposes. Returned instead of<br>`token` on every request except the one that created the token.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_ApprovalRequestCreateRequest">ApprovalRequestCreateRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaapprovalrequestcreaterequest"></a>
<a id="schema_ApprovalRequestCreateRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSapprovalrequestcreaterequest"></a>
<a id="tocsapprovalrequestcreaterequest"></a>

```json
{
  "approval_requests": [
    {
      "assignee_user_id": 101
    },
    {
      "assignee_group_id": 202
    }
  ],
  "assignee_group_id": 789,
  "assignee_user_id": 456,
  "message": "Please approve this request for a new laptop for the engineering team",
  "metadata": {
    "callback_info": {
      "token": "string"
    },
    "workflow_id": "string"
  },
  "subject": "Laptop Purchase Approval",
  "ticket_id": 123
}
```

Request body for approval requests. Two mutually exclusive shapes are supported:

* **Single**: Specify a top-level `assignee_user_id` or `assignee_group_id` to create one approval request with a specified `subject` and `message`. 
* **Parallel**: Specify an `approval_requests` array instead of a top-level assignee value. This creates multiple approval requests under a single workflow instance. All approval requests in the array share the same `subject` and `message`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|approval_requests|[object]|false|none|Parallel approval requests only. One entry per approval request to create, up to five. Each entry must<br>specify exactly one of `assignee_user_id` or `assignee_group_id`.  Can't be used with a top-level `assignee_user_id` or `assignee_group_id`.<br>|
|assignee_group_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|Single approval request only. The id of the group assigned to review and approve the request. Can't be used with an `approval_requests` array.|
|assignee_user_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|Single approval request only. The id of the user assigned to review and approve the request. Can't be used with an `approval_requests` array.|
|message|string|true|none|Details and context for the approval request. Shared by all approval requests created in the call.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Optional metadata used to determine the origination of the approval request|
|subject|string|true|none|Subject line for the approval request. Shared by all approval requests created in the call.|
|ticket_id|integer(int64)|true|none|The id of the ticket the approval request was added to|

<h2 id="tocS_ApprovalRequestCreateResponse">ApprovalRequestCreateResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaapprovalrequestcreateresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_ApprovalRequestCreateResponse"></a>
<a id="tocSapprovalrequestcreateresponse"></a>
<a id="tocsapprovalrequestcreateresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "approval_request": {
    "approval_workflow_instance_id": "01KFP3S9EVXF9CKAYY080NV98D",
    "assignee_group_id": 0,
    "assignee_user_id": 456,
    "created_at": "2026-01-23T19:02:36Z",
    "created_by_id": 789,
    "id": "01KFP3S9EVXF9CKAYY080NV98C",
    "message": "Please approve this request for a new laptop",
    "origination_type": "API_ORIGINATION",
    "status": "active",
    "subject": "Laptop Purchase Approval",
    "ticket_id": 123
  },
  "approval_requests": [
    {
      "approval_workflow_instance_id": "01KFP3S9EVXF9CKAYY080NV98D",
      "assignee_group_id": 0,
      "assignee_user_id": 456,
      "created_at": "2026-01-23T19:02:36Z",
      "created_by_id": 789,
      "id": "01KFP3S9EVXF9CKAYY080NV98C",
      "message": "Please approve this request for a new laptop",
      "origination_type": "API_ORIGINATION",
      "status": "active",
      "subject": "Laptop Purchase Approval",
      "ticket_id": 123
    }
  ]
}
```

Response returned when creating approval requests. A single request returns
the created approval request under the `approval_request` key. A parallel
request returns an array of the created approval requests under the
`approval_requests` key. Exactly one of these keys is present. Every approval request in a parallel approvals array shares the same
`approval_workflow_instance_id`.

```json
{
```

```json
  "assignee_group_id": 0,
  "assignee_user_id": 456,
  "created_at": "2026-01-23T19:02:36Z",
  "created_by_id": 789,
  "id": "01KFP3S9EVXF9CKAYY080NV98C",
  "message": "Please approve this request for a new laptop",

  "status": "active",
  "subject": "Laptop Purchase Approval",
  "ticket_id": 123
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|approval_workflow_instance_id|string|false|read-only|Unique identifier (ULID) of the parent workflow instance. Approval requests created together as a parallel group share the same value.|
|assignee_group_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The id of the group assigned to review the request|
|assignee_user_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The id of the user assigned to respond to the request. Also referred to as the `approver`|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The ISO 8601 formatted date-time when the approval request was created|
|created_by_id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The id of the user who created the approval request|
|id|string|false|read-only|Unique identifier for the approval request (ULID format)|
|message|string|false|none|Details and context for the approval request|
|origination_type|string \| null|false|read-only|How the approval request was created|
|status|string|false|read-only|Current status of the approval request|
|subject|string|false|none|Subject line for the approval request|
|ticket_id|integer(int64)|false|none|The id of the ticket this approval request is attached to|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|origination_type|API_ORIGINATION|
|origination_type|UI_ORIGINATION|
|origination_type|TRIGGER_ORIGINATION|
|origination_type|DATA_IMPORTER_ORIGINATION|
|origination_type|TEMPLATE_ORIGINATION|
|origination_type|ACTION_FLOW_ORIGINATION|
|origination_type|UNKNOWN_ORIGINATION|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
{
  "content_type": "string",
  "content_url": "string",
  "deleted": true,
  "file_name": "string",
  "height": 0,
  "id": 0,
  "inline": true,
  "malware_access_override": true,
  "malware_scan_result": "string",
  "mapped_content_url": "string",
  "size": 0,
  "url": "string",
  "width": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|content_type|string|false|read-only|The content type of the image. Example value: "image/png"|
|content_url|string|false|read-only|A full URL where the attachment image file can be downloaded. The file may be hosted externally so take care not to inadvertently send Zendesk authentication credentials. See [Working with url properties](/documentation/api-basics/best-practices/working-with-url-properties/)|
|deleted|boolean|false|read-only|If true, the attachment has been deleted|
|file_name|string|false|read-only|The name of the image file|
|height|integer \| null|false|read-only|The height of the image file in pixels. If height is unknown, returns null|
|id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Automatically assigned when created|
|inline|boolean|false|read-only|If true, the attachment is excluded from the attachment list and the attachment's URL<br>can be referenced within the comment of a ticket. Default is false<br>|
|malware_access_override|boolean|false|read-only|If true, you can download an attachment flagged as malware. If false, you can't download such an attachment.|
|malware_scan_result|string|false|read-only|The result of the malware scan. There is a delay between the time the attachment is uploaded and when the malware scan is completed. Usually the scan is done within a few seconds, but high load conditions can delay the scan results. Possible values: "malware_found", "malware_not_found", "failed_to_scan", "not_scanned"|
|mapped_content_url|string|false|read-only|The URL the attachment image file has been mapped to|
|size|integer|false|read-only|The size of the image file in bytes|
|url|string|false|read-only|A URL to access the attachment details|
|width|integer \| null|false|read-only|The width of the image file in pixels. If width is unknown, returns null|

The writable attributes accepted when creating an automation

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actions|[[AutomationActionInput](#schemaautomationactioninput)]|false|none|An object describing what the automation will do. See [Actions reference](/documentation/ticketing/reference-guides/actions-reference).<br>`null` is accepted and treated as omitted<br>|
|active|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the automation is active. Defaults to `true`. `null` is accepted and treated as omitted|
|all|[[ConditionObject](#schemaconditionobject)]|false|none|Logical AND conditions. Accepted as a top-level alternative to `conditions.all`.<br>The automation must have at least one time-based condition and at least one condition<br>that checks `status`, `type`, `group_id`, `assignee_id`, or `requester_id`.<br>`null` is accepted and treated as omitted<br>|
|any|[[ConditionObject](#schemaconditionobject)]|false|none|Logical OR conditions. Accepted as a top-level alternative to `conditions.any`.<br>`null` is accepted and treated as omitted<br>|
|conditions|[ConditionsObject](#schemaconditionsobject) \| object \| null|false|none|`null` is accepted and treated as omitted. A `null` *inside* the object is not the same thing:<br>`conditions.all` and `conditions.any` are folded into the top-level fields as<br>`rule_params[:all] \|\|= conditions[:all] \|\| []`, so a nested `null` becomes an empty condition<br>set rather than being discarded<br>|
|position|integer \| null|false|none|The position of the automation, which specifies the order it will be executed in.<br>`null` is accepted and treated as omitted, placing the automation last<br>|
|restriction|object \| null|false|none|Who owns this automation. Set to `null` for the whole account. Not returned when reading an automation|
|title|string|true|none|The title of the automation|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|actions|[[AutomationActionInput](#schemaautomationactioninput)]|false|none|An object describing what the automation will do. See [Actions reference](/documentation/ticketing/reference-guides/actions-reference).<br>`null` leaves the stored actions unchanged. An empty array `[]` is not the same thing: it<br>builds an empty definition, which is rejected with a 422<br>|
|active|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the automation is active. `null` is accepted and leaves the stored value unchanged|
|all|[[ConditionObject](#schemaconditionobject)]|false|none|Logical AND conditions. Accepted as a top-level alternative to `conditions.all`.<br>The automation must have at least one time-based condition and at least one condition<br>that checks `status`, `type`, `group_id`, `assignee_id`, or `requester_id`.<br>`null` leaves the stored conditions unchanged. An empty array `[]` is not the same thing: it<br>builds an empty definition, which is rejected with a 422<br>|
|any|[[ConditionObject](#schemaconditionobject)]|false|none|Logical OR conditions. Accepted as a top-level alternative to `conditions.any`.<br>`null` leaves the stored conditions unchanged. An empty array `[]` is not the same thing: it<br>builds an empty definition, which is rejected with a 422<br>|
|conditions|[ConditionsObject](#schemaconditionsobject) \| object \| null|false|none|`null` leaves the stored conditions unchanged. An empty object `{}` is not the same thing: it<br>builds an empty definition, which is rejected with a 422. Neither is a `null` *inside* the<br>object: `conditions.all` and `conditions.any` are folded into the top-level fields as<br>`rule_params[:all] \|\|= conditions[:all] \|\| []`, so a nested `null` becomes an empty condition<br>set instead of being discarded, and an automation whose conditions are all cleared this way is<br>rejected with the same 422<br>|
|position|integer|false|none|The position of the automation, which specifies the order it will be executed in|
|restriction|object \| null|false|none|Who owns this automation. Set to `null` for the whole account. Not returned when reading an automation|

<h2 id="tocS_CustomObjectFieldPropertiesObject">CustomObjectFieldPropertiesObject</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomobjectfieldpropertiesobject"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomObjectFieldPropertiesObject"></a>
<a id="tocScustomobjectfieldpropertiesobject"></a>
<a id="tocscustomobjectfieldpropertiesobject"></a>

```json
{
  "autoincrement_enabled": true,
  "autoincrement_next_sequence": 1,
  "autoincrement_padding": 5,
  "autoincrement_prefix": "Order # ",
  "is_unique": false
}
```

A set of field-specific properties. For the standard::name field, this includes autonumbering and uniqueness settings (which can't be used together). For text, integer, regexp, and lookup fields, this includes the uniqueness setting. For currency fields, this includes the allowed currency code. For parent fields, includes the `cascade_permissions_enabled` setting. For roll-up summary fields, includes the aggregation configuration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allowed_currencies|[string]|false|none|An array containing exactly one [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) currency code (for example, ["USD"]). The currency code can't be changed after the field is created.|
|autoincrement_enabled|boolean|false|none|Turns autonumbering on or off|
|autoincrement_next_sequence|integer|false|none|The next number in the autonumbering sequence. It can't be negative or less than the current autonumbering value|
|autoincrement_padding|integer|false|none|Sets the number of digits for autogenerated numbers. Valid values are 0-9|
|autoincrement_prefix|string|false|none|A prefix to autogenerated numbers that can't exceed 30 characters|
|cascade_permissions_enabled|boolean|false|none|Parent fields only. If true, permissions for the child object's records cascade from the parent record. When enabled, agents must provide a parent record context to list or search child records. Only one parent field per child object can have this setting enabled. Default: false.|
|is_unique|boolean|false|none|Turns uniqueness on or off. Supported on the standard::name field and on text, integer, regexp, and lookup fields|
|rollup_aggregated_field|string \| null|false|none|Roll-up fields only. The key of the field on the child object to aggregate. Not required for COUNT|
|rollup_aggregated_field_title|string|false|read-only|Roll-up fields only. Read-only. The display title of the aggregated child field|
|rollup_aggregation_type|string|false|none|Roll-up fields only. The aggregation operation to apply to child records. One of: "COUNT", "SUM", "MIN", "MAX"|
|rollup_child_object|string|false|none|Roll-up fields only. The Zendesk resource name (ZRN) of the child object whose records are aggregated. Example: "zen:custom_object:order_item". The child object must have a parent-child relationship with this field's object|
|rollup_filter_criteria|object \| null|false|none|Roll-up fields only. Optional filter conditions (using `all`/`any` arrays) to restrict which child records are included in the aggregation. Uses the same DSL as lookup relationship filters|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|rollup_aggregation_type|COUNT|
|rollup_aggregation_type|SUM|
|rollup_aggregation_type|MIN|
|rollup_aggregation_type|MAX|

<h2 id="tocS_CustomObjectFieldUpdateInput">CustomObjectFieldUpdateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomobjectfieldupdateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomObjectFieldUpdateInput"></a>
<a id="tocScustomobjectfieldupdateinput"></a>
<a id="tocscustomobjectfieldupdateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "custom_field_options": [
    {
      "id": "4398096843007",
      "name": "Apple Pie",
      "value": "apple"
    }
  ],
  "description": "string",
  "position": 0,
  "properties": {
    "autoincrement_enabled": true,
    "autoincrement_next_sequence": 1,
    "autoincrement_padding": 5,
    "autoincrement_prefix": "Order # ",
    "is_unique": false
  },
  "raw_description": "string",
  "raw_title": "string",
  "regexp_for_validation": "string",
  "relationship_filter": {
    "all": [
      {
        "field": "status",
        "operator": "is",
        "value": "open"
      }
    ],
    "any": [
      {
        "field": "status",
        "operator": "is",
        "value": "open"
      }
    ]
  },
  "required": true,
  "tag": "string",
  "title": "string"
}
```

The writable attributes accepted when updating a custom object field. Every property is optional and an omitted property is left unchanged,
with one exception: see the deletion warning on `custom_field_options`. `key` and `type` cannot be changed — `type` is filtered out of the
request and a changed `key` is rejected with a validation error. On a standard field (`standard::name`, `standard::external_id`) only
the title, description and properties may change (`raw_title` and `raw_description` are alternate routes to the title and description);
anything else fails validation

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|false|none|Whether the field is available for use|
|custom_field_options|[[CustomObjectFieldOptionInput](#schemacustomobjectfieldoptioninput)]|false|none|For `dropdown` and `multiselect` fields only; sending it for any other field type is rejected. **The array replaces the whole option<br>set: every option you omit is removed, and records referencing a removed option no longer resolve a value. An empty array removes every<br>option.** So list all the options you want to keep, not just the ones you are changing. `null` and `[]` do opposite things here: `null`<br>is ignored and leaves the option set exactly as it is, while `[]` deletes every option — both return a 200<br>|
|description|string|false|none|A description of the field|
|position|integer|false|none|The relative position of the field. Note that the [Reorder Custom Fields of an Object endpoint](#reorder-custom-fields-of-an-object) reassigns positions across every active field|
|properties|[CustomObjectFieldPropertiesObject](#schemacustomobjectfieldpropertiesobject) \| object \| null|false|none|Field-specific properties, merged into the field's current properties: a property you omit keeps its current value, and omitting the<br>whole object changes nothing. Only the properties that apply to this field's type are kept and the rest are **silently discarded** — the<br>autonumbering and `is_unique` properties apply to the standard name field, `allowed_currencies` to `currency` fields,<br>`cascade_permissions_enabled` to `parent` fields, and the roll-up properties to roll-up fields. Three of these are also account-gated and<br>are only accepted when the feature is enabled on the account: the roll-up properties, `allowed_currencies` and<br>`cascade_permissions_enabled`. Sending `allowed_currencies` without the currency feature is rejected outright. The autonumbering and<br>`is_unique` properties cannot be changed once the object has any records. Use the top-level `required` property rather than `properties`<br>to change whether a field is required. `null` in place of the whole object is accepted and changes nothing<br>|
|raw_description|string|false|none|The dynamic content placeholder for the description, if the description is dynamic content. Takes precedence over `description`|
|raw_title|string|false|none|The dynamic content placeholder for the title, if the title is dynamic content. Takes precedence over `title`|
|regexp_for_validation|string|false|none|A pattern a field value must match to be valid. Honoured by `regexp` and `integer` fields|
|relationship_filter|[CustomObjectFieldRelationshipFilterInput](#schemacustomobjectfieldrelationshipfilterinput) \| object \| null|false|none|Narrows down the records the field can be set to. `null` is accepted and leaves the current filter in place|
|required|boolean|false|none|Whether the field must have a value when a record is created or updated. Stored as the `is_required` field property. Not editable on<br>the standard name field, which is always required<br>|
|tag|string|false|none|For `checkbox` fields only; sending it for any other field type is rejected. It has no tagging effect on a custom object field — custom<br>object records are not tagged. Downcased before it is saved<br>|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the field|

```json

  "custom_object_field_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

A new ordering for the object's active custom fields. The array is treated as the complete order: any active field whose id is absent from
it is pushed to the end of the list rather than left in place, so send every field id you want ordered. The standard fields
(`standard::name`, `standard::external_id`) are ordered alongside the rest and are repositioned like any other field. Positions are written
directly without running field validations

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_field_ids|[string]|true|none|The ids of the object's custom fields, in the desired order. Required|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomobjectrecordupdateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomObjectRecordUpdateInput"></a>
<a id="tocScustomobjectrecordupdateinput"></a>
<a id="tocscustomobjectrecordupdateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "custom_object_fields": {},
  "external_id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "photo": {
    "uploaded_data": "string"
  }
}
```

The writable attributes accepted when updating a custom object record. Every property is optional and an omitted property is left
unchanged. `name` and `external_id` fall back to the record's current value, so they cannot be cleared by sending null — send a new
value instead

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_object_fields|object \| null|false|none|A map of the object's custom field keys to their new values. Merged into the record: only the keys present in the map are written and<br>any field key omitted from the map keeps its current value. A field key the object does not define is ignored, and a key sent with a<br>blank value (null or an empty string) clears that field's value. Two exceptions: a read-only field such as a roll-up field is validated<br>rather than cleared, and the standard field keys are recognised here, so sending one with a value returns a validation error instead of being<br>ignored. `null` in place of the whole map is accepted and writes nothing, whereas a field key *inside* the map whose value is `null`<br>clears that field<br>|
|external_id|string \| null|false|none|An id you can use to link the record to your own record keeping. Omitting it, or sending `null`, leaves the current value in place —<br>`null` is accepted but is a no-op, so it cannot be used to clear the external id<br>|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the record. Omitting it, or sending `null`, leaves the current name in place — `null` is accepted but is a no-op, so it<br>cannot be used to clear the name. Rejected if the object's name field has `autoincrement_enabled`, and must be unique if it has<br>`is_unique`<br>|
|photo|object \| null|false|none|A photo to attach to the record. Requires `allows_photos` on the custom object. Sending an explicit null removes the current photo,<br>whereas omitting the property leaves it in place. Uploading actual image data requires a `multipart/form-data` request — see the<br>cURL sample<br>|

```json
  "allows_photos": true,
  "description": "string",
  "include_in_list_view": true,
  "title": "string",
  "title_pluralized": "string"
}
```

The writable attributes accepted when updating a custom object. Every property is optional: the request hash is mass-assigned to the
object, so an omitted property is left unchanged. `key` is accepted by the parameter filter on create only and cannot be updated

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allows_attachments|boolean|false|none|Whether this object allows file attachments|
|allows_photos|boolean|false|none|Whether this object allows photo uploads|
|description|string|false|none|A description of the custom object|
|include_in_list_view|boolean|false|none|Whether to include this object in list views|
|title|string|false|none|Display name for the object|
|title_pluralized|string|false|none|Pluralized version of the object's title|

|raw_description|string|false|read-only|The dynamic content placeholder. If the dynamic content placeholder is not available, this is the "description" value. [Dynamic Content Items](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/)|
|raw_end_user_description|string|false|read-only|The dynamic content placeholder. If the dynamic content placeholder is not available, this is the "end_user_description" value. See [Dynamic Content Items](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/)|
|raw_end_user_label|string|false|read-only|The dynamic content placeholder. If the dynamic content placeholder is not available, this is the "end_user_label" value. See [Dynamic Content Items](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/)|
|status_category|string|true|none|The status category the custom ticket status belongs to|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The date and time the custom ticket status was last updated|
|url|string|false|read-only|The URL for this resource|

|---|---|

<h2 id="tocS_DynamicContentInput">DynamicContentInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadynamiccontentinput"></a>
<a id="schema_DynamicContentInput"></a>
<a id="tocSdynamiccontentinput"></a>
<a id="tocsdynamiccontentinput"></a>

```json
{
  "content": "string",
  "default_locale_id": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "variants": [
    {
      "content": "string",
      "default": true,
      "locale_id": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

A new dynamic content item. There are two ways to give it a default variant: supply `default_locale_id` and `content` to
create a single variant, or supply the `variants` array. `content` must not be combined with `variants`;
`default_locale_id` may be sent alongside `variants` but is ignored.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|content|string|false|none|The content of the item's default variant. Use this together with `default_locale_id` as a shorthand for creating<br>an item with a single variant. Required when `variants` is omitted — without it the default variant has no content<br>and the request is rejected. **Must not be sent together with `variants`** — the two forms are mutually<br>exclusive, and sending both returns a 400 `Invalid attribute` error whatever the value is.<br>|
|default_locale_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The default locale of the item, which becomes the locale of its default variant. Must be one of the locales the<br>account has active. Required unless `variants` is supplied, in which case this value is **ignored** and the default<br>locale is taken from the variant whose `default` is `true`. A `null` is therefore only accepted alongside<br>`variants`; without `variants` it is rejected.<br>|
|name|string|true|none|The unique name of the item. Must be unique within the account, must not contain non-ASCII characters and must not<br>end in a hyphen. The item's `placeholder` is derived from it, and a name whose derived placeholder is already in<br>use is also rejected.<br>|
|variants|[[DynamicContentItemVariantInput](#schemadynamiccontentitemvariantinput)]|false|none|The variants to create for the item. Exactly one of them must have `default` set to `true`; if none does, the<br>request is rejected because the item would have no default variant. Supplying this array makes `default_locale_id`<br>inert, and `content` must not be sent alongside it. A `null` is treated as if the array were omitted, so the item is<br>created from `default_locale_id` and `content` instead; an empty array is **not** equivalent and is rejected.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_DynamicContentItemVariantInput">DynamicContentItemVariantInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadynamiccontentitemvariantinput"></a>
<a id="schema_DynamicContentItemVariantInput"></a>
<a id="tocSdynamiccontentitemvariantinput"></a>
<a id="tocsdynamiccontentitemvariantinput"></a>

```json
{
  "content": "string",
  "default": true,
  "locale_id": 0
}
```

A variant supplied in the `variants` array of a Create Item request. Create Item accepts a narrower set of attributes
than the Item Variants API does, so this schema is not interchangeable with a standalone variant request body.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|content|string|true|none|The content of the variant. Evaluated as Liquid in the `dc` namespace, so it must be valid Liquid and must not<br>reference the item's own placeholder. Cannot be blank.<br>|
|default|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether this variant is the item's default variant. Exactly one variant in the array must set it to `true`, and the<br>request is rejected if none does. Only the literal `true` counts — `null` and any other value are treated as<br>`false`. If more than one variant sets it to `true`, only the last of them is stored as the default and the earlier<br>ones are silently discarded.<br>|
|locale_id|integer(int64)|true|none|The locale of the variant. Must be an existing locale id, and each locale may appear at most once per item.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_DynamicContentVariantBulkUpdateItem">DynamicContentVariantBulkUpdateItem</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadynamiccontentvariantbulkupdateitem"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "content": "string",
  "default": true,
  "id": 0
}
```

A single variant to update. The update is partial — any omitted attribute is left unchanged. `locale_id` is not accepted: a variant's locale
is fixed at creation, and sending it has no effect

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the variant is used when a user's locale matches it. Forced to `true` while the variant is the item's default, so `false` is<br>silently ignored for that variant. `null` is accepted and stores no value, which reads the same as `false`<br>|
|content|string|false|none|The content of the variant. Cannot be blank, and is parsed as a Liquid template: invalid Liquid is rejected, as is content that<br>references its own item's `{{dc.<identifier>}}` placeholder<br>|
|default|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the variant is the item's default, used as the fallback when no variant matches the user's locale. Setting it to `true` demotes<br>the item's previous default, and while a variant is the default it is always active and cannot be deleted. `null` is accepted and behaves<br>the same as `false`<br>|
|id|integer(int64)|true|none|The id of the variant to update. An item without it, or with an id that is not a variant of this item, fails that item alone rather than the request|

Setting it to `true` demotes<br>the item's previous default, and while a variant is the default it is always active and cannot be deleted. `null` is accepted and behaves<br>the same as `false`<br>|

The request is rejected with a 400 if the array is missing or empty, or if it holds more than 100 variants —<br>the shared bulk-job cap, `BulkJobData::ITEM_COUNT_LIMIT`. Variants are created by a background job, so each one succeeds or fails<br>independently: a variant with a missing or invalid attribute fails on its own rather than failing the request. Check the returned job<br>status for the per-variant result<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_EndUserIdentityCreateInput">EndUserIdentityCreateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaenduseridentitycreateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_EndUserIdentityCreateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSenduseridentitycreateinput"></a>
<a id="tocsenduseridentitycreateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "auto_ownership": true,
  "ownership": "owned",
  "primary": true,
  "type": "email",
  "value": "string",
  "verification_method": "none",
  "verified": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auto_ownership|boolean \| null|false|none|Write-only ownership control for the Shared Email EAP. When true, `owned` is attempted first and falls back to `shared` on an ownership conflict. The fallback is subject to the same restrictions as `ownership: shared`: it requires the `shared_email_creation_enabled` account setting, respects the per-brand shared-identity cap, and never applies to `google` identities - an ownership conflict for a Google-backed email identity is returned as an error instead of falling back. null is accepted and treated exactly like `false`. Only applies to `email` and `google` identities, and ignored unless the account has the Shared Email EAP enabled. Mutually exclusive with `ownership`; requests that supply both keys are rejected.|
|ownership|string \| null|false|none|Write-only ownership control for the Shared Email EAP. Only applies to `email` and `google` identities, and ignored unless the account has the Shared Email EAP enabled. null is accepted and falls back to `owned`. `shared` additionally requires the `shared_email_creation_enabled` account setting, is rejected outright for `google` identities (a Google-backed email identity can only be owned), and is subject to a per-brand cap on shared identities per address (100 by default; past the cap the request fails with `LimitExceeded`). A create that will send a verification email for a shared address is rate-limited and can be rejected with `429 Too Many Requests`. Mutually exclusive with `auto_ownership`; requests that supply both keys are rejected.|
|primary|boolean \| null|false|none|Makes the new identity the primary one. null is accepted and ignored. Only takes effect for `email` identities. For a verified<br>email identity (`verified: true` or `verification_method: low`) the identity becomes primary<br>immediately; for an unverified one the promotion is deferred - the verification email link carries<br>`make_primary=true`, so the identity becomes primary (and the former primary is removed) when the<br>recipient verifies. Ignored for non-email identity types, including `google`.<br><br>To promote an identity that already exists, use the<br>[Make Identity Primary](#make-identity-primary) endpoint instead.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|The type of identity to create.<br><br>Only the types listed here can be created through this endpoint. The remaining identity types<br>(`any_channel`, `foreign`, `sdk`, `microsoft`) are created by internal systems only, and a request<br>for one of them is rejected with a `400`.<br><br>`messaging` and `slack` back internal channel integrations. `slack` additionally requires the<br>Slack identity feature to be enabled on the account.<br>|
|value|string|true|none|The identifier for this identity. An email address for `email` and `google`, the screen name for<br>`twitter`, the Facebook user id for `facebook`, and an E.164 phone number for `phone_number` and<br>`agent_forwarding`. Phone numbers are validated unless the account has phone number validation<br>turned off.<br>|
|verification_method|string \| null|false|none|The verification state to create the identity with. `low` creates a verified identity and<br>suppresses the verification email. Only `none` and `low` are accepted here; the higher methods<br>(`sso`, `embed`, `full`) are set by the corresponding authentication flows.<br><br>Has no effect for `phone_number` and `agent_forwarding` identities, which are always verified, nor<br>for `slack`. Also ignored when creating an email identity (including `google`) for the account owner: that identity is<br>always created unverified and a verification email is sent.<br><br>null is accepted and treated exactly like `none`. Because this property wins over `verified`,<br>sending `verified: true` alongside `verification_method: null` creates an unverified identity.<br>|
|verified|boolean \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** Creates the identity already verified, equivalent to `verification_method: low`. Deprecated - use<br>`verification_method` instead. Ignored when `verification_method` is also sent - that property<br>wins. null is accepted and treated exactly like `false`.<br><br>Has no effect for `phone_number` and `agent_forwarding` identities, which are always verified, nor<br>for `slack`. Also ignored when creating an email identity (including `google`) for the account owner: that identity is<br>always created unverified and a verification email is sent.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|ownership|owned|
|ownership|shared|
|ownership|null|
|type|email|
|type|twitter|
|type|facebook|
|type|google|
|type|agent_forwarding|
|type|phone_number|
|type|messaging|
|type|slack|
|verification_method|none|
|verification_method|low|
|verification_method|null|

The writable attributes accepted when creating a group SLA policy. The whole resource is only available to
accounts with the operational level agreements feature, which requires both a Service Level Agreements
subscription and the group SLAs subscription feature; other accounts get a 403. `filter` must be a
non-empty object — an empty one is rejected as a missing parameter

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|filter|[GroupSLAPolicyFilterInput](#schemagroupslapolicyfilterinput)|true|none|The conditions a ticket must match for the group SLA policy to be applied to it. See [Filter](#filter). Keys other than `all` and `any` are accepted but ignored|
|policy_metrics|[[GroupSLAPolicyMetricInput](#schemagroupslapolicymetricinput)]|false|none|The targets for the policy. See [Policy Metric](#policy-metric)|
|position|integer \| null|false|none|Position of the group SLA policy, which determines the order policies are matched in. If not specified, the policy is added at the last position. A null value behaves the same as omitting the property|
|title|string|true|none|The title of the group SLA policy|

<h2 id="tocS_GroupSLAPolicyMetricInput">GroupSLAPolicyMetricInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemagroupslapolicymetricinput"></a>

```json
{
  "business_hours": true,
  "metric": "group_ownership_time",
  "priority": "normal",
  "target": 1800,
  "target_in_seconds": 108000
}
```

A target for one combination of ticket priority and metric. Each priority and metric pair may only appear once in a policy

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|business_hours|boolean|true|none|Whether the target is measured in business hours rather than calendar hours. Required — the value is assigned unconditionally and then validated for inclusion in `true`/`false`, so omitting it fails validation|
|metric|string|true|none|The time being measured. `group_ownership_time` is the only metric supported by group SLA policies — the account-level SLA metrics are not accepted here|
|priority|string|true|none|The ticket priority the target applies to. Allowed values are `low`, `normal`, `high`, or `urgent`|
|target|integer \| null|false|none|The target for the metric, in minutes. Ignored when `target_in_seconds` is supplied. Either `target` or `target_in_seconds` must be given. The allowed-range limits described on `target_in_seconds` apply here too, since seconds are derived from minutes. A null value is accepted only when `target_in_seconds` is supplied, because it is then not assigned at all; a null with neither target given fails the numericality validation|
|target_in_seconds|integer \| null|false|none|The target for the metric, in seconds. Takes precedence over `target`. On accounts with the SLA metrics allowed range feature, values below 15 seconds and above 31536000 seconds (8760 hours) are rejected. A null value is ignored, so the target falls back to `target`|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|

<h2 id="tocS_GroupSLAPolicyUpdateInput">GroupSLAPolicyUpdateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemagroupslapolicyupdateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_GroupSLAPolicyUpdateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSgroupslapolicyupdateinput"></a>
<a id="tocsgroupslapolicyupdateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "description": "Tier 1 Group SLA",
  "filter": {
    "all": [
      {
        "field": "group_id",
        "operator": "includes",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ],
    "any": [
      {
        "field": "group_id",
        "operator": "includes",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ]
  },
  "policy_metrics": [
    {
      "business_hours": true,
      "metric": "group_ownership_time",
      "priority": "normal",
      "target": 1800,
      "target_in_seconds": 108000
    }
  ],
  "position": 3,
  "title": "Tier 1 Group SLA"
}
```

Only the supplied properties are updated. Each property is applied only when its value is present, so a
blank or null value leaves the current value in place rather than clearing it, and an empty object is
rejected. `filter` and `policy_metrics` are the exceptions: when either is supplied it **replaces** what
the policy already has, so a partial value destroys the conditions or targets it leaves out

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The description of the group SLA policy. A blank or null value is ignored, so the description cannot be cleared through this endpoint|
|filter|[GroupSLAPolicyFilterInput](#schemagroupslapolicyfilterinput) \| object \| null|false|none|The conditions a ticket must match. Supplying this **replaces the policy's conditions in full** — sending only `any` deletes the existing `all` conditions and vice versa, so a partial value destroys the conditions it omits. Omitting the property, or sending an empty object or a null value, leaves the existing conditions untouched|
|policy_metrics|[[GroupSLAPolicyMetricInput](#schemagroupslapolicymetricinput)]|false|none|The targets for the policy. See [Policy Metric](#policy-metric). Supplying this **replaces the policy's targets in full** — the existing targets are deleted and only the ones listed here survive, so a partial list destroys the targets it omits. Omitting the property, or sending an empty array or a null value, leaves the existing targets untouched|
|position|integer \| null|false|none|Position of the group SLA policy, which determines the order policies are matched in. A null value is ignored|
|title|string \| null|false|none|The title of the group SLA policy. A blank or null value is ignored|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|created_by_user_id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The id of the user who created the asset type|

|id|string|false|read-only|Automatically assigned upon creation|
|is_standard|boolean|false|read-only|Whether this asset type is a standard asset type. Standard asset types cannot be modified.|
|name|string|true|none|A unique display name for the asset type|
|parent_id|string \| null|false|none|The id of the parent asset type within the hierarchy tree. If omitted on create, defaults to the base asset type. Cannot be changed after the asset type is created.|
|photo|object \| null|false|write-only|Sets or removes the asset type's icon. Setting an icon requires a `multipart/form-data` request with a file field named `asset_type[photo][uploaded_data]` — see the "Adding a photo" code sample. Pass `null` to remove the existing icon via a normal JSON request.|
|updated_by_user_id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The id of the user who last updated the asset type|
|url|string|false|read-only|Direct link to the specific asset type|

|html_body|string|false|read-only|The comment formatted as HTML|
|id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Automatically assigned when the comment is created|
|plain_body|string|false|read-only|The comment formatted as plain text|
|public|boolean|false|read-only|If true, the comment is public|
|request_id|string|false|read-only|The request token if available, the nice id of the request otherwise|
|type|string|false|read-only|The type of the comment, "Comment" or "VoiceComment"|

|url|string|false|read-only|The API url of this comment|

|can_be_solved_by_me|boolean|false|read-only|If true, the end user can mark the request as solved|
|can_comment|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the requester can comment on the request. Only present on accounts with the AI agent request comment persona enabled|
|can_update_ccs|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the requester can update collaborators. Only present on accounts with the AI agent request comment persona enabled|
|collaborator_ids|[integer(int64)]|false|none|Who is currently CC'ed on the ticket|
|comment_count|integer|false|read-only|The count of public comments associated to the request|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this record was created|
|csat|object \| null|false|read-only|The satisfaction rating for the request. Null when no rating exists or CSAT is not enabled for the SDK app|
|custom_fields|[object]|false|none|The fields and entries for this request|
|custom_status_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The custom ticket status id of the ticket. Only present on accounts with custom statuses enabled|
|description|string|false|read-only|The first comment on the request|
|due_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the task is due (only applies if the request is of type "task")|
|email_cc_ids|[integer(int64)]|false|read-only|The ids of users who are currently email CCs on the ticket|
|fields|[object]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated alias of `custom_fields`|
|first_comment|[MobileCommentObject](#schemamobilecommentobject)|false|none|A comment on a request as returned by the private mobile API.<br>Unlike the public v2 Request Comments API, `request_id` is the request token (or nice id) as a string.<br>|
|followup_source_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|read-only|The id of the original ticket if this request is a follow-up ticket|
|group_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|read-only|The id of the assigned group if the field is visible to end users|
|id|string|false|read-only|The request token if available, the nice id otherwise|
|is_public|boolean|false|read-only|Is true if any comments are public, false otherwise|
|last_comment|[MobileCommentObject](#schemamobilecommentobject)|false|none|A comment on a request as returned by the private mobile API.<br>Unlike the public v2 Request Comments API, `request_id` is the request token (or nice id) as a string.<br>|
|last_commenting_agents_ids|[integer(int64)]|false|read-only|The ids of the agents who made the most recent public comments on the request, most recent first|
|organization_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|read-only|The organization of the requester|
|priority|string \| null|false|none|The priority of the request|
|public_updated_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|When a public event last occurred on the request. Only present when sideloaded with `include=public_updated_at`|
|recipient|string \| null|false|none|The original recipient e-mail address of the request|
|requester_id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The id of the requester|
|solved|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the request is solved (an end user can set this if `can_be_solved_by_me` is true for that user)|
|status|string|false|none|The state of the request|
|subject|string|true|none|The value of the subject field for this request if the subject field is visible to end users; a truncated version of the description otherwise|
|ticket_form_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The numeric id of the ticket form associated with this request if the form is visible to end users - only applicable for enterprise accounts|
|type|string \| null|false|none|The type of the request|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this record last got updated|
|url|string|false|read-only|The API url of this request|
|via|[TicketAuditViaObject](#schematicketauditviaobject)|false|none|Describes how the object was created. See the [Via object reference](/documentation/ticketing/reference-guides/via-object-reference)|

|description|string|false|none|A short description of your client that is displayed to users when they are considering approving access to your application|
|global|boolean|false|read-only|Whether this client is globally accessible. See [Set up a global OAuth client](/documentation/apps/publish-your-app-or-theme/global_oauth_intro/)|

|identifier|string|true|none|The unique identifier for this client|
|kind|string|false|none|Either "public" or "confidential". Specifies whether the OAuth client operates in a public environment where credentials cannot be securely stored, or on secure servers that can safely store credentials. See [Client types](/documentation/ticketing/working-with-oauth/oauth-pkce/#client-types)|
|logo_url|string|false|read-only|The API logo url of this record|
|name|string|true|none|The name of this client|
|redirect_uri|[string]|false|none|An array of the valid redirect URIs for this client|
|scope|string|false|none|A space-separated list of allowed scopes for this client. Defines the maximum set of scopes the client is permitted to request during the OAuth authorization flow. When set, the client can only request scopes included in this list. If a client requests a scope not included in its allowed scopes, the request fails with a `400 Bad Request` response and an `invalid_scope` error. If not set, no scope restrictions are applied. For the full list of valid scope values, see [Scopes](/api-reference/ticketing/oauth/grant_type_tokens/#scope).<br>|
|secret|string|false|read-only|The client secret. Generated automatically on creation and returned in full only at that time|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The time of the last update of the client|
|url|string|false|read-only|The API url of this record|
|user_id|integer(int64)|true|none|The id of the admin who created the client|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_token|string|false|read-only|The access token|
|expires_in|integer|false|none|Number of seconds the access token is valid. Must be greater than or equal to 300 seconds (5 minutes) and less than or equal to 172,800 seconds (2 days), or less than refresh_token_expires_in, whichever is smallest. Defaults to null for clients created before April 30, 2026. Clients created on or after that date have a default value of 1,800 seconds (30 minutes).|
|refresh_token|string|false|read-only|The refresh token|
|refresh_token_expires_in|integer|false|none|Number of seconds the refresh token is valid. Must be greater than or equal to 604,800 seconds (7 days) or `expires_in` (if given), and less than or equal to 7,776,000 seconds (90 days). Defaults to 2,592,000 seconds (30 days)|
|scope|string|false|read-only|The valid scopes for this token. See [Scope](#scope) below|
|token_type|string|false|read-only|Type of the access token, for example "bearer"|
