<h2 id="tocS_OrganizationBatchUpdateItemInput">OrganizationBatchUpdateItemInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaorganizationbatchupdateiteminput"></a>
<a id="schema_OrganizationBatchUpdateItemInput"></a>
<a id="tocSorganizationbatchupdateiteminput"></a>
<a id="tocsorganizationbatchupdateiteminput"></a>

```json
{
  "details": "string",
  "domain_names": [
    "string"
  ],
  "external_id": "string",
  "group_id": 0,
  "id": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "notes": "string",
  "organization_fields": {},
  "shared_comments": true,
  "shared_tickets": true,
  "tags": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ticket_restriction": "restricted"
}
```

One organization to update, with the attributes to apply to it. The organization is matched by `id` first, then by `external_id`; `id` wins when both are supplied. An item that names neither, or that names an organization outside the account, is not rejected at the door — it is recorded as an `OrganizationNotFound` failure against that item in the job results. Every attribute is optional on a matched organization, and omitting one leaves the stored value unchanged — but see the per-property notes, as several properties replace the stored value wholesale rather than merging into it.
An agent without edit permission on organizations can only change `notes`; for such an agent every other attribute here is silently ignored and the item still counts as updated. `organization_fields` is the exception — it is applied for a restricted agent too, with no permission gate on this route.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|details|string \| null|false|none|Any details about the organization, such as the address. `null` clears the stored value.|
|domain_names|[string] \| string|false|none|Domain names and email addresses to associate with this organization. Accepts either an array of values or a single string of values separated by commas, semicolons or spaces. **Destructive:** the supplied list replaces the stored list wholesale, so every omitted domain and email is deleted; `null`, an empty array and an empty string all clear them all. Omit the property entirely to leave the stored list untouched.|
|external_id|string \| null \| integer|false|none|A unique external id to associate the organization to an external record. Plays two roles in this mode: when `id` is omitted or `null`, the `external_id` string selects the organization to update, and an item that names neither, or names an organization outside the account, is recorded as an `OrganizationNotFound` failure, not an HTTP error; and on a matched organization the value is written back as its external id — a no-op when the value is what matched, a change when `id` did the matching. `null` or an empty string clears the stored value when `id` selected the organization; a value already used by another organization is recorded as an update failure for this item.|
|group_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|New tickets from users in this organization are automatically put in this group. `null` unassigns the group.|
|id|integer(int64) \| string \| null|false|none|The id of the organization to update. Accepts an integer or its decimal string form. An unknown id is recorded as an `OrganizationNotFound` failure for this item, not an HTTP error. Omit it, or send `null`, to match on `external_id` alone.|
|name|string|false|none|A unique name for the organization. Cannot contain the `\|` character and must be unique within the account; a duplicate is recorded as an update failure for this item. Cannot be cleared — an empty string or `null` fails the presence validation the same way.|
|notes|string \| null|false|none|Any notes you have about the organization. `null` clears the stored value for an agent with edit permission; for an agent restricted to `edit_notes`, `null` is ignored and the item still reports success with the old notes — send an empty string to clear. This is the only attribute an agent restricted to `edit_notes` can change; for such an agent every other attribute here is silently ignored and the item still counts as updated. `organization_fields` is the exception — it is applied for a restricted agent too, with no permission gate on this route.|
|organization_fields|object|false|none|Custom organization field values, keyed by field key, applied to the matched organization. See [Custom organization fields](/api-reference/ticketing/organizations/organizations/#custom-organization-fields). Only keys matching an existing organization field take effect; unknown keys are silently ignored. Supplied keys are merged into the stored values, so omitted keys keep their value, and a `null` or blank value for a key deletes that field's stored value. Do not send `null` for the whole map — the batch job cannot handle it and the item fails; omit the property or send an empty object instead. Applied with no permission gate on this route — even for an agent restricted to `edit_notes`, and with no `up_restrict_organization_field_updates` check, unlike the single-organization update. Requires the `user_and_organization_fields` account feature; without it the whole map is silently ignored.|
|shared_comments|boolean|false|none|End users in this organization are able to comment on each other's tickets. An explicit `null` is rejected with 400. Only takes effect when `shared_tickets` is `true` — the model resets it to `false` whenever the organization is not sharing tickets.|

|tags|[string] \| string|false|none|The tags of the organization. Accepts either an array of tags or a single string of space-separated tags. <h2 id="tocS_OrganizationBulkUpdateInput">OrganizationBulkUpdateInput</h2>

```json
{
  "details": "string",
  "domain_names": [
    "string"
  ],
  "external_id": "string",
  "group_id": 0,
  "name": "string",

  "organization_fields": {},
  "shared_comments": true,
  "shared_tickets": true,

    "string"
  ],
```

The organization attributes to apply to every organization matched by the `ids` or `external_ids` query parameter. Every property is optional and omitting one leaves the stored values unchanged on every matched organization, but see the per-property notes: several properties replace the stored value wholesale rather than merging into it. An empty object is accepted and changes nothing.
An organization named by the query parameter that does not exist in the account is not rejected at the door — it is recorded as an `OrganizationNotFound` failure for that organization in the job results.
An agent without edit permission on organizations can only change `notes`; for such an agent every other attribute here is silently ignored and the organization still counts as updated. `organization_fields` is the exception — it is applied for a restricted agent too, with no permission gate on this route.

Accepts either an array of values or a single string of values separated by commas, semicolons or spaces. **Destructive:** the supplied list replaces the stored list wholesale on every matched organization, so every omitted domain and email is deleted; `null`, an empty array and an empty string all clear them all. Omit the property entirely to leave the stored lists untouched.|
|external_id|string \| null \| integer|false|none|A unique external id to associate the organizations to an external record. **In bulk mode this rewrites the external id of every matched organization**, which is rarely what a bulk update means to do. |group_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|New tickets from users in these organizations are automatically put in this group. `null` unassigns the group.|
|name|string|false|none|A unique name for the organization. Cannot contain the `\|` character and must be unique within the account; a duplicate is recorded as an update failure for every organization it was applied to. Cannot be cleared — an empty string or `null` fails the presence validation the same way.|
|notes|string \| null|false|none|Any notes about the organizations. `null` clears the stored value. This is the only attribute an agent restricted to `edit_notes` can change; for such an agent every other attribute here is silently ignored and the matched organizations still count as updated. `organization_fields` is the exception — it is applied for a restricted agent too, with no permission gate on this route.|
|organization_fields|object \| null|false|none|Custom organization field values, keyed by field key, applied to every matched organization. See [Custom organization fields](/api-reference/ticketing/organizations/organizations/#custom-organization-fields). Only keys matching an existing organization field take effect; unknown keys are silently ignored. Supplied keys are merged into the stored values, so omitted keys keep their value, and a `null` or blank value for a key deletes that field's stored value. `null` for the whole map is accepted and changes nothing. Applied with no permission gate on this route — even for an agent restricted to `edit_notes`, and with no `up_restrict_organization_field_updates` check, unlike the single-organization update. Requires the `user_and_organization_fields` account feature; without it the whole map is silently ignored.|
|shared_comments|boolean|false|none|End users in these organizations are able to comment on each other's tickets. An explicit `null` is rejected with 400. Only takes effect when `shared_tickets` is `true` — the model resets it to `false` whenever an organization is not sharing tickets.|
|shared_tickets|boolean|false|none|End users in these organizations are able to see each other's tickets. An explicit `null` is rejected with 400. Setting this to `false` also forces `shared_comments` to `false`. If both this and `ticket_restriction` are supplied and they disagree, either may win — this route does not run the single-update precedence resolver — so do not send conflicting values; the stored restriction and sharing state depend on which value actually changed.|
|tags|[string] \| string|false|none|The tags of the organizations. Accepts either an array of tags or a single string of space-separated tags. Requires the `user_and_organization_tags` account feature; without it the value is accepted and silently ignored. **Destructive:** the supplied list replaces the stored list wholesale on every matched organization, so every omitted tag is deleted; `null`, an empty array and an empty string all remove every tag. Omit the property entirely to leave the stored tags untouched.|
|ticket_restriction|string \| null|false|none|Who can see the tickets of end users in these organizations: `restricted` hides them from each other, `organization` shares them within the organization, and `organization_and_descendants` shares them within the organization and its descendants — the last requires the organization hierarchy feature, and is recorded as an update failure without it. An unknown value is likewise recorded as an update failure rather than rejected at the door.<br>Interacts with `shared_tickets`: if both this and `shared_tickets` are supplied and they disagree, either may win — this route does not run the single-update precedence resolver — so do not send conflicting values; the stored restriction and sharing state depend on which value actually changed.<br>An explicit `null` is accepted and clears the stored restriction value; when ticket-restriction sync is enabled the shared-tickets flag is then re-derived from it, so the organization is treated as sharing (the restriction reads back as `organization`).|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|ticket_restriction|organization|

```json
{
```

Bulk-update mode: the attributes in `organization` are applied to **every** organization named by the `ids` or `external_ids` query parameter. One of those two query parameters is required in this mode — the request returns 400 without one. At most 100 organizations can be updated in one request.

<h2 id="tocS_OrganizationCreateOrUpdateInput">OrganizationCreateOrUpdateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaorganizationcreateorupdateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_OrganizationCreateOrUpdateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSorganizationcreateorupdateinput"></a>
<a id="tocsorganizationcreateorupdateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "details": "string",
  "domain_names": [
    "string"
  ],
  "external_id": "string",
  "group_id": 0,
  "id": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "notes": "string",
  "organization_fields": {},
  "shared_comments": true,
  "shared_tickets": true,
  "tags": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ticket_restriction": "restricted"
}
```

Organization attributes to create with, or to apply to the matched organization. Matching is by `id` first and then by `external_id`; when neither matches, a new organization is created from these attributes and `name` becomes mandatory. When an organization is matched, every property is optional and omitting one leaves the stored value unchanged — but see the per-property notes, as several properties replace the stored value wholesale rather than merging into it.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|details|string \| null|false|none|Any details about the organization, such as the address. `null` clears the stored value.|
|domain_names|[string] \| string|false|none|Domain names and email addresses to associate with this organization. Accepts either an array of values or a single string of values separated by commas, semicolons or spaces. **Destructive on a matched organization:** the supplied list replaces the stored list wholesale, so every omitted domain and email is deleted; `null`, an empty array and an empty string all clear them all. Omit the property entirely to leave the stored list untouched.|
|external_id|string \| null \| integer|false|none|A unique external id to associate the organization to an external record. Used as the second matching criterion: when `id` matches nothing, a case-insensitive match on `external_id` selects the organization to update, so "company1" and "Company1" are considered the same. `null` or an empty string skips the match and clears the stored value; a value already used by another organization returns 422.|
|group_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|New tickets from users in this organization are automatically put in this group. `null` unassigns the group.|
|id|integer(int64) \| string \| null|false|none|The id of an existing organization to update. Accepts an integer or its decimal string form. If no organization has this id, matching falls back to `external_id`; only when neither matches is a new organization created. Omit it, or send `null`, to match on `external_id` alone.|
|name|string|false|none|A unique name for the organization. **Mandatory when creating** — if neither `id` nor `external_id` matches an existing organization, omitting it fails with 422. Optional when an existing organization is matched. Cannot contain the `\|` character and must be unique within the account; a duplicate returns 422. Cannot be cleared — an empty string or `null` fails the presence validation with 422.|
|notes|string \| null|false|none|Any notes you have about the organization. `null` clears the stored value. This is the only attribute applied for an agent restricted to `edit_notes` on a matched organization; for such an agent every other attribute here is silently ignored and the request still returns 200. `organization_fields` is the exception — it is applied for a restricted agent too. **Destructive exception:** for a caller without `edit` permission on organizations this is the only attribute applied, and it is assigned unconditionally — omitting `notes` on a matched organization clears the stored value (when `ocp_org_create_or_update_require_edit` is disabled; with it enabled such callers get 403 before matching).|
|organization_fields|object \| null|false|none|Custom organization field values, keyed by field key. See [Custom organization fields](/api-reference/ticketing/organizations/organizations/#custom-organization-fields). Only keys matching an existing organization field take effect; unknown keys are silently ignored. Supplied keys are merged into the stored values, so omitted keys keep their value, and a `null` or blank value for a key deletes that field's stored value. `null` for the whole map is accepted and changes nothing. Requires the `user_and_organization_fields` account feature; without it the whole map is silently ignored.|
|shared_comments|boolean|false|none|End users in this organization are able to comment on each other's tickets. An explicit `null` is rejected with 400. Only takes effect when `shared_tickets` is `true` — the model resets it to `false` whenever the organization is not sharing tickets.|
|shared_tickets|boolean|false|none|End users in this organization are able to see each other's tickets. An explicit `null` is rejected with 400. Setting this to `false` also forces `shared_comments` to `false`. Deprecated in favor of `ticket_restriction`, which takes precedence when both are sent in the same request: `shared_tickets` is then silently dropped from the request and, when the two contradict, the response carries a top-level `warnings` array saying so (this precedence behavior requires the `enable_sync_ticket_restriction` account feature). Sent on its own, it still applies: when the `enable_sync_ticket_restriction` account feature is enabled, the stored `ticket_restriction` is synchronized to `organization` for `true` or `restricted` for `false`; with the feature disabled a non-null stored `ticket_restriction` is left unchanged (a stored `null` always reads as derived from `shared_tickets`).|
|tags|[string] \| string|false|none|The tags of the organization. Accepts either an array of tags or a single string of space-separated tags. Requires the `user_and_organization_tags` account feature; without it the value is accepted and silently ignored. **Destructive on a matched organization:** the supplied list replaces the stored list wholesale, so every omitted tag is deleted; `null`, an empty array and an empty string all remove every tag. Omit the property entirely to leave the stored tags untouched.|
|ticket_restriction|string \| null|false|none|Which tickets end users in this organization can see. `restricted` hides each end user's tickets from the other end users in the organization; `organization` lets them see each other's tickets; `organization_and_descendants` extends that to end users in descendant organizations and requires the organization hierarchy to be enabled on the account, otherwise it is rejected with 422. Any other value is rejected with 422. `null` clears the stored restriction, which then derives from `shared_tickets`. Takes precedence over `shared_tickets` — see that property for what happens when both are sent.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|ticket_restriction|restricted|
|ticket_restriction|organization|
|ticket_restriction|organization_and_descendants|

Options are "zen:user", "zen:organization", "zen:ticket",<br>"zen:attachment", or "zen:custom_object:{key}" where key is a custom object key. Cannot be changed after creation<br>|

When the id is null and the `value` matches a previously deleted option of this field, that option is<br>restored instead of a new one being created<br>|

|value|string|false|none|The tag value stored on the organization when the option is selected. Omit to leave an existing option's value<br>unchanged. Must be a valid tag, must be unique within the field, and cannot be blank or `null`. Required when `id`<br>is null<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_OrganizationFieldUpdateInput">OrganizationFieldUpdateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaorganizationfieldupdateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_OrganizationFieldUpdateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSorganizationfieldupdateinput"></a>
<a id="tocsorganizationfieldupdateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "custom_field_options": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "name": "string",
      "raw_name": "string",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "description": "string",
  "position": 0,
  "raw_description": "string",
  "raw_title": "string",
  "regexp_for_validation": "string",
  "relationship_filter": {
    "all": [
      {
        "field": "string",
        "operator": "string",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ],
    "any": [
      {
        "field": "string",
        "operator": "string",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tag": "string",
  "title": "string"
}
```

The writable attributes accepted when updating an organization field. Every attribute is optional and only the
attributes sent are changed, with the exception of `custom_field_options`, which replaces the whole option list.
The `type`, `key` and `relationship_target_type` attributes cannot be changed after creation. On a field flagged as
a system field (`is_system` is true in the response) only `active` and `position` are applied and every other
attribute is silently discarded.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether this field is available. A `null` value does not leave the field as it is: it reverts the field to the<br>default and reactivates a deactivated field<br>|
|custom_field_options|[[OrganizationFieldOptionUpdateInput](#schemaorganizationfieldoptionupdateinput)]|false|none|For `dropdown`, `tagger` and `multiselect` fields only; any other field type rejects the request. The list<br>replaces the stored options in full, so every option that is to be kept must be sent with its `id`. Options<br>omitted from the list are deleted, and sending an empty list deletes every option, removing those values from<br>any organization that had them. A `null` value leaves the stored options unchanged<br>|
|description|string \| null|false|none|User-defined description of this field's purpose. A `null` value does not clear the description: the value of<br>`title` is written into it instead<br>|
|position|integer|false|none|The relative position of the organization field on a ticket. Unlike on create, the position is written directly to<br>this field and the other organization fields are not reordered<br>|
|raw_description|string \| null|false|none|The dynamic content placeholder for `description`. When a non-null value is sent it takes precedence over<br>`description`. A `null` value is ignored and `description` is used instead. See [Dynamic Content](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/)<br>|
|raw_title|string \| null|false|none|The dynamic content placeholder for `title`. When a non-null value is sent it takes precedence over `title`. A `null`<br>value is ignored and `title` is used instead. See [Dynamic Content](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/)<br>|
|regexp_for_validation|string \| null|false|none|For `regexp` fields only. The validation pattern for a field value to be deemed valid. A blank or `null` value is<br>rejected for a `regexp` field. Accepted and ignored for every other type, including as `null`<br>|
|relationship_filter|object \| null|false|none|For `lookup` fields only. A filter definition that limits the results offered by the field's autocomplete. The<br>supplied filter replaces the stored one in full, so sending only `any` removes the stored `all` conditions, and<br>sending an empty object removes the filter altogether. Ignored for every other field type. A `null` value leaves<br>the stored filter unchanged<br>|
|tag|string \| null|false|none|For `checkbox` fields only. A tag added to the organization when the checkbox field is selected. The value is<br>downcased before it is saved. A `null` value clears the stored tag. Any other field type rejects a non-null `tag`<br>|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the organization field|

<h2 id="tocS_OrganizationMembershipCreateManyItemInput">OrganizationMembershipCreateManyItemInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaorganizationmembershipcreatemanyiteminput"></a>
<a id="schema_OrganizationMembershipCreateManyItemInput"></a>
<a id="tocSorganizationmembershipcreatemanyiteminput"></a>
<a id="tocsorganizationmembershipcreatemanyiteminput"></a>

```json
{
  "organization_id": 0,
  "user_id": 0
}
```

One membership to create: a user and an organization to assign them to. Neither property is required, and neither is checked at the door — an item that omits or nulls either one, or that names a user or an organization outside the account, is accepted with a 200 and recorded as a `UserNotFound` or `OrganizationNotFound` failure against that item in the job results. An item whose user already belongs to the named organization is not a failure: the existing membership is returned unchanged, so the item is idempotent.
Creating a membership has effects beyond the new row. On accounts **without** the multiple organizations setting, the same user may appear in at most one item in the whole request — the same user in two items, even two identical items, is rejected with 400 before the job starts — and creating a membership **deletes** the user's other organization memberships. On accounts with the `ocp_tighten_agent_org_access` feature, an item whose user the caller cannot manage organization memberships for is recorded as a `PermissionDenied` failure.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The ID of the organization to assign the user to. An explicit `null` behaves exactly like an unknown ID: the item is recorded as an `OrganizationNotFound` failure in the job results.<br>Creating a membership has effects beyond the new row:<br>* If this is the user's first organization membership, it is created as the default, which<br>  also sets the user's `organization_id`, and every unclosed ticket requested by the user is<br>  reassigned to this organization.<br>* On accounts **without** the multiple organizations setting, all of the user's other<br>  organization memberships are **deleted**, and the user's unclosed requested tickets that<br>  belonged to those removed organizations move to the user's new default organization — or<br>  have their organization cleared, if the account has the<br>  `unset_ticket_org_when_removing_default_user_org` feature. Tickets the user has in other<br>  organizations are left alone.<br>* An item is recorded as a failure if the user is already at the account's<br>  `max_organization_memberships_per_user` limit (300 by default).|
|user_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The ID of the user to assign to the organization. The user must belong to the same account as the organization. An explicit `null` behaves exactly like an unknown ID: the item is recorded as a `UserNotFound` failure in the job results.|

Tickets<br>  the user has in other organizations are left alone.<br>* Returns a 422 if the user is already at the account's `max_organization_memberships_per_user` limit<br>  (300 by default).<br>|

The user must belong to the same account as the<br>organization.<br><br>Required **unless** a `user_id` is supplied at the root of the request or as a query parameter, in<br>which case that value selects the user and this one is ignored.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_OrganizationMembershipRequest">OrganizationMembershipRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaorganizationmembershiprequest"></a>
<a id="schema_OrganizationMembershipRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSorganizationmembershiprequest"></a>
<a id="tocsorganizationmembershiprequest"></a>

```json
{
  "organization_id": 0,
  "organization_membership": {
    "organization_id": 0,
    "user_id": 0
  },
  "user_id": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|integer(int64)|false|none|The ID of the organization to assign the user to, supplied at the root of the request instead of<br>inside `organization_membership`. It is only consulted when no `user_id` is given at the root or in<br>the query string; when it is consulted, `organization_membership.organization_id` is ignored.<br><br>This may equivalently be sent as an `organization_id` **query parameter**, which takes precedence<br>over the root of the body.<br><br>An organization must likewise be identified in **at least one of** three places — this property, the<br>`organization_id` query parameter, or `organization_membership.organization_id` — and a request that<br>names none of them is a 422. As with `user_id`, that rule is stated rather than encoded, because the<br>query location is not visible to a request-body schema.<br>|
|organization_membership|[OrganizationMembershipInput](#schemaorganizationmembershipinput)|true|none|none|
|user_id|integer(int64)|false|none|The ID of the user to assign to the organization, supplied at the root of the request instead of<br>inside `organization_membership`. When present it selects the user the membership is created for,<br>and `organization_membership.user_id` is ignored.<br><br>This may equivalently be sent as a `user_id` **query parameter**, which takes precedence over the<br>root of the body.<br><br>A user must be identified in **at least one of** three places — this property, the `user_id` query<br>parameter, or `organization_membership.user_id` — and a request that names none of them is a 422.<br><br>That rule is stated here rather than encoded as a schema constraint, deliberately: one of the three<br>legal locations is the **query string**, which lies outside the request body a body schema can see.<br>Any structural encoding of "at least one of" would therefore have to reject a body that names the<br>user nowhere — even though such a body is a legal `201` whenever the `user_id` query parameter<br>supplies it. Being unenforced is the lesser fault: over-strictness here would forbid calls the API<br>accepts.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_OrganizationUpdateInput">OrganizationUpdateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaorganizationupdateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_OrganizationUpdateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSorganizationupdateinput"></a>
<a id="tocsorganizationupdateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "details": "string",
  "domain_names": [
    "string"
  ],
  "external_id": "string",
  "group_id": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "notes": "string",
  "organization_fields": {},
  "shared_comments": true,
  "shared_tickets": true,
  "tags": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ticket_restriction": "restricted"
}
```

Organization attributes to update. Every property is optional and omitting one leaves the stored value unchanged, but see the per-property notes: several properties replace the stored value wholesale rather than merging into it. An empty object is accepted and changes nothing.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|details|string \| null|false|none|Any details about the organization, such as the address. `null` clears the stored value.|
|domain_names|[string] \| string|false|none|Domain names and email addresses to associate with this organization. Accepts either an array of values or a single string of values separated by commas, semicolons or spaces. **Destructive:** the supplied list replaces the stored list wholesale, so every omitted domain and email is deleted; `null`, an empty array and an empty string all clear them all. Omit the property entirely to leave the stored list untouched.|
|external_id|string \| null \| integer|false|none|A unique external id to associate the organization to an external record. The id is case-insensitive, so "company1" and "Company1" are considered the same. `null` or an empty string clears it; a value already used by another organization returns 422.|
|group_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|New tickets from users in this organization are automatically put in this group. `null` unassigns the group.|
|name|string|false|none|A unique name for the organization. Cannot contain the `\|` character and must be unique within the account; a duplicate returns 422. Cannot be cleared — an empty string or `null` fails the presence validation with 422.|
|notes|string \| null|false|none|Any notes you have about the organization. `null` clears the stored value for a caller with `edit` permission; for an agent restricted to `edit_notes`, `null` is ignored and the stored notes are left untouched — only a non-empty value (including an empty string) is assigned. This is the only attribute an agent restricted to `edit_notes` can change; for such an agent every other attribute here is silently ignored and the request still returns 200. `organization_fields` is the exception — it is applied for a restricted agent too, unless the account has `up_restrict_organization_field_updates` enabled.|
|organization_fields|object \| null|false|none|Custom organization field values, keyed by field key. See [Custom organization fields](/api-reference/ticketing/organizations/organizations/#custom-organization-fields). Only keys matching an existing organization field take effect; unknown keys are silently ignored. Supplied keys are merged into the stored values, so omitted keys keep their value, and a `null` or blank value for a key deletes that field's stored value. `null` for the whole map is accepted and changes nothing. Requires the `user_and_organization_fields` account feature; without it the whole map is silently ignored, as it also is for agents without `edit` permission on organizations when the account has `up_restrict_organization_field_updates` enabled.|
|shared_comments|boolean|false|none|End users in this organization are able to comment on each other's tickets. An explicit `null` is rejected with 400. Only takes effect when `shared_tickets` is `true` — the model resets it to `false` whenever the organization is not sharing tickets.|
|shared_tickets|boolean|false|none|End users in this organization are able to see each other's tickets. An explicit `null` is rejected with 400. Setting this to `false` also forces `shared_comments` to `false`. Deprecated in favor of `ticket_restriction`, which takes precedence when both are sent in the same request: `shared_tickets` is then silently dropped from the request and, when the two contradict, the response carries a top-level `warnings` array saying so (this precedence behavior requires the `enable_sync_ticket_restriction` account feature). Sent on its own, it still applies: when the `enable_sync_ticket_restriction` account feature is enabled, the stored `ticket_restriction` is synchronized to `organization` for `true` or `restricted` for `false`; with the feature disabled a non-null stored `ticket_restriction` is left unchanged (a stored `null` always reads as derived from `shared_tickets`).|
|tags|[string] \| string|false|none|The tags of the organization. Accepts either an array of tags or a single string of space-separated tags. Requires the `user_and_organization_tags` account feature; without it the value is accepted and silently ignored. **Destructive:** the supplied list replaces the stored list wholesale, so every omitted tag is deleted; `null`, an empty array and an empty string all remove every tag. Omit the property entirely to leave the stored tags untouched.|
|ticket_restriction|string \| null|false|none|Which tickets end users in this organization can see. `restricted` hides each end user's tickets from the other end users in the organization; `organization` lets them see each other's tickets; `organization_and_descendants` extends that to end users in descendant organizations and requires the organization hierarchy to be enabled on the account, otherwise it is rejected with 422. Any other value is rejected with 422. `null` clears the stored restriction, which then derives from `shared_tickets`. Takes precedence over `shared_tickets` — see that property for what happens when both are sent.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|ticket_restriction|restricted|
|ticket_restriction|organization|
|ticket_restriction|organization_and_descendants|

<h2 id="tocS_QueueInput">QueueInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaqueueinput"></a>

```json
{
  "definition": {
    "all": [
      {
        "field": "priority",
        "operator": "is",
        "value": "urgent"
      }
    ],
    "any": [
      {
        "field": "priority",
        "operator": "is",
        "value": "urgent"
      }
    ]
  },
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "predictive_routing": true,
  "primary_groups_id": [
    0
  ],
  "priority": 1,
  "secondary_groups_id": [
    0
  ],
  "subqueues": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "percentage": 0,
      "predictive_routing": true,
      "primary_groups_id": [
        0
      ],
      "priority": 1,
      "secondary_groups_id": [
        0
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The writable attributes accepted when creating a queue. A queue routes either to groups or to subqueues, never both: pass `priority` and
`primary_groups_id` for a group queue, or `subqueues` for a subqueue queue, in which case `priority` and the group ids must be omitted

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|definition|[QueueDefinitionInput](#schemaqueuedefinitioninput)|true|none|The conditions under which the queue applies. `all` and `any` must contain at least one and at most 100 conditions combined|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The description of the queue|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the queue. Must be unique within the account, including against subqueue names|
|predictive_routing|boolean|false|none|Whether predictive routing is applied to the queue. Forced to `false` when the queue has subqueues|
|primary_groups_id|[integer(int64)]|false|none|The ids of the groups the queue routes to first. At least one is required for a group queue, and the field must be omitted when<br>`subqueues` is set. `null` is accepted and behaves as omitted: the group assignment is skipped entirely rather than applied as empty<br>|
|priority|integer \| null|false|none|The priority applied to tickets that enter the queue. Required for a group queue, and must be omitted when `subqueues` is set.<br>`null` is accepted and behaves as omitted<br>|
|secondary_groups_id|[integer(int64)]|false|none|The ids of the groups the queue falls back to. Ignored unless `primary_groups_id` is also set, and ignored when `subqueues` is set.<br>Ids also present in `primary_groups_id` are ignored. `null` is accepted and behaves as omitted<br>|
|subqueues|[[QueueSubqueueInput](#schemaqueuesubqueueinput)]|false|none|The subqueues that tickets are distributed across, instead of routing to groups directly. Requires the account to have a minimum<br>Enterprise level plan for whichever of Support, Chat, Talk products it has — without that the whole `subqueues` array is dropped<br>before it reaches the model. The array is the complete set: any existing subqueue whose id is absent from it is deleted, and<br>passing an empty array deletes them all. `null` is accepted and behaves as omitted, creating a queue with no subqueues<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_QueueSubqueueInput">QueueSubqueueInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaqueuesubqueueinput"></a>
<a id="schema_QueueSubqueueInput"></a>
<a id="tocSqueuesubqueueinput"></a>
<a id="tocsqueuesubqueueinput"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "percentage": 0,
  "predictive_routing": true,
  "primary_groups_id": [
    0
  ],
  "priority": 1,
  "secondary_groups_id": [
    0
  ]
}
```

A subqueue of the parent queue. Requires the account to have a minimum Enterprise level plan for whichever of Support, Chat, Talk
products it has — without that the whole `subqueues` array is dropped before it reaches the model. Omit `id` to create a subqueue, or
pass the id of an existing one to update it. An unknown id is rejected. `name`, `priority` and `percentage` are required for a new
subqueue (one without `id`); when updating an existing subqueue (one with `id`) they may be omitted and the stored values are preserved.
`primary_groups_id` is always required

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string \| null|false|none|The id of an existing subqueue to update. Omit it to create a new subqueue. `null` means the same thing as omitting it — the writer<br>branches on `id.nil?` — so it is the explicit way to say "create"<br>|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the subqueue. Must be unique within the account, including against queue names|
|percentage|integer|false|none|The share of matching tickets routed to this subqueue. The percentages across all subqueues of a queue must total exactly 100|
|predictive_routing|boolean|false|none|Whether predictive routing is applied to this subqueue|
|primary_groups_id|[integer(int64)]|false|none|The ids of the groups this subqueue routes to first. At least one is required|
|priority|integer|false|none|The priority applied to tickets that enter this subqueue|
|secondary_groups_id|[integer(int64)]|false|none|The ids of the groups this subqueue falls back to. Ids also present in `primary_groups_id` are ignored. `null`, an empty array and<br>omitting the property all remove every secondary group from the subqueue, and nothing validates secondary groups, so the request<br>succeeds<br>|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_QueueUpdateInput">QueueUpdateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaqueueupdateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_QueueUpdateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSqueueupdateinput"></a>
<a id="tocsqueueupdateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "definition": {
    "all": [
      {
        "field": "priority",

        "value": "urgent"
      }
    ],

      }
    ]
  },

  "name": "string",
  "predictive_routing": true,
  "primary_groups_id": [
    0
  ],
  "priority": 1,
  "secondary_groups_id": [
    0
  ],
  "subqueues": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "percentage": 0,
      "predictive_routing": true,
      "primary_groups_id": [
        0
      ],
      "priority": 1,
      "secondary_groups_id": [
        0
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The writable attributes accepted when updating a queue. `name`, `description` and `definition` are left unchanged when omitted, but
`priority` and the group assignments are always rewritten from the request, so a group queue must send `priority` and `primary_groups_id`
on every update. A subqueue queue omits both instead, and sends `subqueues`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|definition|[QueueDefinitionInput](#schemaqueuedefinitioninput) \| object \| null|false|none|`null` is accepted and leaves the stored definition unchanged|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The description of the queue. `null` clears the stored description; on create it creates a queue with no description<br>|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the queue. Must be unique within the account, including against subqueue names|
|predictive_routing|boolean|false|none|Whether predictive routing is applied to the queue. Forced to `false` when the queue has subqueues|
|primary_groups_id|[integer(int64)]|false|none|The ids of the groups the queue routes to first. Replaces the current primary groups, so a group queue must send the full list and it<br>cannot be empty. Must be omitted when the queue has subqueues. `null`, an empty array and omitting the property are all the same<br>request: each clears the primary groups, which a group queue then rejects with a 422 that rolls the whole update back, and which is the<br>required state for a subqueue queue<br>|
|priority|integer \| null|false|none|The priority applied to tickets that enter the queue. Rewritten on every update, so omitting it on a group queue clears the priority<br>and fails validation. Must be omitted when the queue has subqueues. `null` is indistinguishable from omitting the property — the<br>controller rewrites `priority` from the request either way — so it fails validation on a group queue and is the required value on a<br>subqueue queue<br>|
|secondary_groups_id|[integer(int64)]|false|none|The ids of the groups the queue falls back to. Replaces the current secondary groups, and clears them when omitted. Must be omitted<br>when the queue has subqueues. Ids also present in `primary_groups_id` are ignored. **`null` is destructive and silent**: like an empty<br>array and like omitting the property, it removes every secondary group, and because nothing validates secondary groups the request still<br>returns a 200<br>|
|subqueues|[[QueueSubqueueInput](#schemaqueuesubqueueinput)]|false|none|The subqueues that tickets are distributed across, instead of routing to groups directly. Applied only when the account has a<br>minimum Enterprise level plan for whichever of Support, Chat, Talk products it has, and ignored without it. On such an account<br>this field is rewritten on every update rather than left<br>alone: the array is the complete set, so any existing subqueue whose id is absent from it is deleted, an empty array deletes them all,<br>and **omitting the field entirely also deletes them all** — which converts the queue to a group queue and so requires `priority` and<br>`primary_groups_id` in the same request. **`null` is destructive in exactly the same way**: the writer tests<br>`sub_queues.nil? \|\| sub_queues.empty?` and takes the delete-everything branch for both, so `null`, `[]` and omission are one request,<br>not three. Pass each subqueue's `id` to keep it, or omit `id` to add a new one<br>|

Requests from IP addresses outside these ranges will be routed to the normal sign-in form.<br>When this is blank, all requests are routed through remote authentication.<br>An IP range is in the format n.n.n.n, where n is a number or an asterisk (*) wild card.<br>Multiple IP ranges are separated with spaces<br>|

|issuer_url|string|false|none|For the "oidc" auth mode only.<br>This is the URL that is used as the logical identifier for your provider's connection<br>|

|masked_client_secret|string|false|none|For the "oidc" auth mode only.<br>|
|masked_secret|string|false|none|For the "jwt" auth mode only.<br>The token is a shared secret between you and Zendesk. It must never be publicized<br>|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the remote configuration. It's good to use something recognizable like the identity provider's name|
|priority|integer|false|none|none|
|remote_login_url|string|true|none|The URL that Zendesk invokes to redirect users to the identity provider<br>|
|remote_logout_url|string|true|none|The URL that Zendesk uses to redirect users after they sign out. Supported authentication types: SAML, JWT. Not supported for OIDC<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_RequestCommentInput">RequestCommentInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarequestcommentinput"></a>
<a id="schema_RequestCommentInput"></a>
<a id="tocSrequestcommentinput"></a>
<a id="tocsrequestcommentinput"></a>

```json
{
  "body": "string",
  "html_body": "string",
  "uploads": [
    "string"
  ],
  "value": "string"
}
```

The comment to add to the request. On Create Request the comment is mandatory and supplies the request's read-only
`description`. A comment carrying `uploads` but no text is rejected on both operations. Comments added through this
endpoint always take the publicity the account computes for the caller; an end user cannot choose it here.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|string \| null|false|none|The comment text, as Zendesk markdown. Takes precedence over `value`, but is overridden by `html_body` when both are sent. On create this becomes the request's `description`|
|html_body|string \| null|false|none|The comment text as HTML. Takes precedence over both `body` and `value` whenever it is sent, and stores the comment in rich-text format|
|uploads|[string] \| string|false|none|One or more attachment upload tokens to attach to the comment. Blank tokens are discarded, and both a null and an<br>empty array are discarded entirely, leaving the comment with no new attachments. On an anonymous create the number<br>of attachments is capped by the account's anonymous attachment limit<br>|
|value|string \| null|false|none|A legacy alias for `body`, applied only when `body` is absent, and likewise overridden by `html_body`|

The properties an end user may set when creating a request. A request is the end-user view of a ticket, and the set of
properties accepted here is much narrower than the one accepted by the Tickets API. Properties an end user is not
allowed to set for the account's configuration are discarded rather than rejected.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|collaborators|[integer(int64) \| string \| object \| [string]] \| string \| integer(int64) \| object \| null|false|none|The collaborators (CCs) to set on the request, as user ids, email addresses, or objects carrying a name and an<br>email. Only applied when the account allows collaborators, and rejected when the request is submitted from the<br>help center by an account that does not allow help center collaborators. At most 48 collaborators may be sent in<br>one call on accounts with CCs and followers enabled, and null is ignored<br>|
|comment|object|true|none|none|
|custom_fields|[object \| string \| integer \| boolean] \| object \| string \| integer \| boolean|false|none|Custom field values, either as an array of objects carrying an `id` and a `value`, or as an object mapping ticket<br>field id to value. Values for fields the end user cannot see are discarded. Takes precedence over `fields` when<br>both are sent. A bare string, integer or boolean is tolerated and ignored, as is null<br>|
|due_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When a request of type "task" is due. Only applied when the Type field is editable by end users. Send null or an empty string to leave the request without a due date|
|email_ccs|[[RequestEmailCCInput](#schemarequestemailccinput)]|false|none|The email CCs to add to the request, up to 48 entries with `action: "put"` per call. On an account without CCs and<br>followers enabled the `put` entries are still applied, as plain collaborators; only `delete` entries need the<br>feature. Rejected when the request is submitted from the help center by an account that does not allow help center<br>collaborators. Null and an empty array both add no CCs<br>|
|fields|[object \| string \| integer \| boolean] \| object \| string \| integer \| boolean|false|none|An alias for `custom_fields`, accepting the same shapes with the same tolerances. Ignored when `custom_fields` is also sent, and null is ignored|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|An arbitrary object stored as custom metadata on the request's first audit. A value that is not an object, including null, is ignored|
|organization_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The id of the organization to associate the request with. Must be one of the requester's organizations — any other value, and null, is silently replaced by the requester's default organization|
|priority|string \| null|false|none|The priority of the request. Only applied when the Priority field is editable by end users. An unrecognised value, and null, leave the request without a priority|
|recipient|string|false|none|The original recipient email address to record on the request|
|requester|object \| null|false|none|The requester of an anonymous request. Only applied when the request is created by an unauthenticated caller — for any authenticated caller the requester is the caller. Null is ignored|
|safe_update|boolean \| null|false|none|Has no effect on its own on create, but see `updated_stamp`: sending both fails the create with a 422|
|solved|boolean \| null|false|none|Accepted for symmetry with Update Request but has no effect on create — a request has no assignee at creation, so it cannot be solved|
|subject|string|false|none|The subject of the request. Required when the account requires a subject on end-user requests|
|system_metadata|object \| null|false|none|Client and IP information to store as system metadata on the request's first audit. Accepted from any caller but only applied for internal Zendesk services, and a null is ignored|
|tags|[string] \| string|false|none|The tags to set on the request. Null is ignored and leaves the request with no tags of its own|
|ticket_form_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The id of the ticket form to apply. Only applied when the account has ticket forms. Sending null behaves exactly like omitting the property — the brand's default form is used|
|type|string \| null|false|none|The type of the request. Only applied when the Type field is editable by end users. An unrecognised value, and null, leave the request without a type|
|updated_stamp|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Has no effect on its own — there is no earlier `updated_at` to compare against — but sending it together with<br>`safe_update: true` **fails the create** with a 422, because the safe-update check runs on a record that has no<br>stored timestamp yet. Send neither on create<br>|
|via|[RequestViaInput](#schemarequestviainput) \| object \| null|false|none|The channel the request came through|
|via_followup_source_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The id of a closed ticket that this request follows up on. Only closed tickets are accepted; any other value, and null, is ignored|
|via_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The channel to record the request against. Only a small set of channels may be chosen by an API caller — any other<br>value, and null, records the request as created through the API. Ignored when `via_followup_source_id` is sent,<br>which records the request as a follow-up instead<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|priority|low|
|priority|normal|
|priority|high|
|priority|urgent|
|priority|null|
|type|question|
|type|incident|
|type|problem|
|type|task|
|type|null|

<h2 id="tocS_RequestUpdateInput">RequestUpdateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarequestupdateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_RequestUpdateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSrequestupdateinput"></a>
<a id="tocsrequestupdateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "additional_collaborators": [
    0
  ],
  "comment": {
    "body": "string",
    "html_body": "string",
    "uploads": [
      "string"
    ],
    "value": "string"
  },
  "email_ccs": [
    {
      "action": "string",
      "user_email": "string",
      "user_id": 0,
      "user_name": "string"
    }
  ],
  "organization_id": 0,
  "safe_update": true,
  "solved": true,
  "system_metadata": {
    "client": "string",
    "ip_address": "string"
  },
  "updated_stamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "via": {
    "channel": "string",
    "source": 0
  }
}
```

The properties an end user may change on an existing request: a comment, the solved flag, collaborators and the
organization. Every other request attribute is read-only once the request exists, and the properties accepted only on
create are not accepted here.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|additional_collaborators|[integer(int64) \| string \| object \| [string]] \| string \| integer(int64) \| object \| null|false|none|Collaborators (CCs) to add to the request, as user ids, email addresses, or objects carrying a name and an email.<br>Existing collaborators are kept. Only applied when the account allows collaborators. At most 48 collaborators may<br>be sent in one call on accounts with CCs and followers enabled, and null is ignored<br>|
|comment|[RequestCommentInput](#schemarequestcommentinput) \| object \| null|false|none|The comment to add. Null and an empty object are both accepted and add no comment|
|email_ccs|[[RequestEmailCCInput](#schemarequestemailccinput)]|false|none|Email CCs to add to or remove from the request, up to 48 entries with `action: "put"` per call. Each entry is<br>applied on its own and CCs that are not listed are left untouched, so null and an empty array both leave the CC<br>list unchanged. On an account without CCs and followers enabled the `put` entries are still applied, as plain<br>collaborators; only `delete` entries need the feature<br>|
|organization_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The id of the organization to associate the request with. Applied for the requester, who may always edit their own<br>request's properties. Unlike on create there is no silent substitution here: an organization the requester does not<br>belong to **fails the update** with a 422 and `organization_id is not a valid organization for the requester`.<br>Null is replaced by the requester's default organization, if they have one<br>|
|safe_update|boolean \| null|false|none|Set to true to make the update conditional on `updated_stamp` still matching the request's `updated_at`. Null is ignored|
|solved|boolean \| null|false|none|Set to true to solve the request. Only applied when the request is assigned to an agent, which the request's<br>read-only `can_be_solved_by_me` property reports. Null is ignored<br>|
|system_metadata|object \| null|false|none|Client and IP information to store as system metadata on the update's audit. Accepted from any caller but only applied for internal Zendesk services, and a null is ignored|
|updated_stamp|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The request's last known `updated_at`, used with `safe_update` to reject the update if the request has changed since. Null is ignored|
|via|[RequestViaInput](#schemarequestviainput) \| object \| null|false|none|The channel the update came through|

<h2 id="tocS_RequestViaInput">RequestViaInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarequestviainput"></a>
<a id="schema_RequestViaInput"></a>
<a id="tocSrequestviainput"></a>
<a id="tocsrequestviainput"></a>

```json
{
  "channel": "string",
  "source": 0
}
```

Describes the channel the request came through. The channel is only recorded on the request when the account has the
agent-as-end-user anonymous via feature enabled, or when an internal Zendesk service records an LLM via; `source` is
always inspected to detect a help center submission, which changes whether collaborators may be set.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|channel|string \| null \| integer|false|none|The channel to record, either as a `via_id` or as a channel name. An unrecognised name is ignored and the request keeps its default channel|
|source|integer(int64) \| null \| string \| object|false|none|The via reference recorded against the request, for example the id of the ticket a follow-up came from. Send the help center via id here to identify a help center submission|

|priority|string|false|none|The ticket priority the target applies to. Allowed values are `low`, `normal`, `high`, or `urgent`|
|target|integer|false|none|The target for the metric, in minutes. Ignored when `target_in_seconds` is supplied|
|target_in_seconds|integer|false|none|The target for the metric, in seconds. Takes precedence over `target`|

Only the supplied properties are updated. Supplying `policy_metrics` replaces the policy's targets in full. Every property here is also a no-op when sent as null, so no property can be cleared that way

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The description of the SLA policy. A blank or `null` value is ignored, so the description cannot be cleared through this endpoint|
|filter|[SLAPolicyFilterInput](#schemaslapolicyfilterinput) \| object \| null|false|none|The conditions a ticket must match for the SLA policy to be applied to it. A supplied filter **replaces the policy's conditions in full**, so omitting `all` or sending it as `null` or `[]` removes the policy's existing `all` conditions - and likewise for `any`. Sending `null` or `{}` for `filter` itself is a no-op that leaves the current filter in place|
|metric_settings|[SLAPolicyMetricSettingsInput](#schemaslapolicymetricsettingsinput) \| object \| null|false|none|Per-metric activation and fulfillment settings. `null` is ignored and leaves the current settings in place, whereas `{}` **clears every setting** on the policy|
|policy_metrics|[[SLAPolicyMetricInput](#schemaslapolicymetricinput)]|false|none|The targets for the policy. See [Policy Metric](#policy-metric). Supplying this replaces the policy's targets in full, so a partial list deletes the targets it omits. `null` and `[]` are both ignored and leave the current targets in place|
|policy_triggers|[[SLAPolicyTriggerInput](#schemaslapolicytriggerinput)]|false|none|Notifications attached to the policy. Only acted on when the account has the SLA policy triggers feature; without it the field is accepted and then silently dropped. When it is acted on, the supplied list replaces the policy's notifications in full. `null` and `[]` are both ignored and leave the current notifications in place|
|position|integer \| null|false|none|Position of the SLA policy, which determines the order policies are matched in. A `null` value is ignored and the current position is kept|
|title|string \| null|false|none|The title of the SLA policy. A blank or `null` value is ignored and the current title is kept|

<h2 id="tocS_SatisfactionRatingInput">SatisfactionRatingInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasatisfactionratinginput"></a>
<a id="schema_SatisfactionRatingInput"></a>
<a id="tocSsatisfactionratinginput"></a>
<a id="tocssatisfactionratinginput"></a>

```json
{
  "comment": "string",
  "reason_code": 0,
  "score": "good"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comment|string \| null|false|none|The comment left by the requester with this rating. Omitting the property, sending an empty string and sending `null` are equivalent — the rating is created with no comment. A non-empty comment upgrades the score stored on the ticket from "good" to "good_with_comment" or from "bad" to "bad_with_comment", although the `score` in the response still reads "good" or "bad"|
|reason_code|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The reason code for a negative rating. See [Reason codes](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/satisfaction_reasons/#reason-codes) in the Satisfaction Reasons API. **This property is only accepted on accounts that have satisfaction reasons enabled**; on any other account the property is silently dropped and the rating is created without it, with a success response and no error. It also only takes effect on a "bad" score — a "good" score resets the reason to the default 0 ("no reason"). An explicit `null` is accepted and ignored, preserving any reason code already recorded on the ticket|
|score|string|true|none|The rating. Only "good" and "bad" create a rating: the parameter filter accepts the full satisfaction-score vocabulary used by the List Satisfaction Ratings `score` filter ("offered", "unoffered", "received", "good_with_comment" and so on), but any value other than "good" or "bad" is mapped to no score and the request then fails validation with a 422 rather than a 400|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|score|good|
|score|bad|

Responses don't include this property|

To get a descriptive value for the id, use the [Show Reason for Satisfaction Rating](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/satisfaction_reasons/#show-reason-for-satisfaction-rating) endpoint|

Documented request payload for `POST /access/sdk/anonymous`, used to
identify or create the end user to authenticate as. The controller's
parameter allowlist also accepts other general `/access` login parameters
(e.g. `return_to`, `locale`); those are ignored by this authentication
strategy and omitted here.

```json
  "client_id": "string",
  "error": "string",
  "error_description": "string",

```

Request parameters accepted by `POST /access/sdk/jwt`. This endpoint verifies a
mobile SDK user via a server-side JWT exchange (`Zendesk::Auth::Warden::SdkJWTStrategy`) —
it is not a client-supplied bearer JWT. The strategy calls out to the account's
configured mobile SDK JWT endpoint (`sdk_auth_settings`) using a `user_token`
to obtain and verify a signed JWT before authenticating the user.

### Properties

|auth_origin|string|false|none|none|
|brand_id|string|false|none|none|

|client_id|string|false|none|Identifies the OAuth/mobile client whose SDK JWT auth settings should be used<br>to verify the token. Can alternatively be supplied via the `Client-Identifier`<br>request header, in which case this body parameter may be omitted.<br>|
|error|string|false|none|none|
|error_description|string|false|none|none|
|flash_digest|string|false|none|none|
|force_unaltered_return_to|string|false|none|none|
|form_origin|string|false|none|none|
|locale|string|false|none|none|
|notice|string|false|none|none|
|profile|string|false|none|none|
|return_to|string|false|none|Post-login redirect target. Not used by this strategy's response, kept for parity with other /access endpoints.|
|return_to_on_failure|string|false|none|none|
|role|string|false|none|none|
|theme|string|false|none|none|
|use_ui_redirect|boolean|false|none|none|

|utf8|string|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_SharingAgreementCreateInput">SharingAgreementCreateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasharingagreementcreateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_SharingAgreementCreateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSsharingagreementcreateinput"></a>
<a id="tocssharingagreementcreateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "allows_public_comments": true,
  "remote_subdomain": "string",
  "sync_custom_fields": true,
  "sync_tags": true
}
```

The writable attributes accepted when creating a sharing agreement.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allows_public_comments|boolean|false|none|Whether the remote account may add public comments to the shared ticket and keep its status in<br>sync. When `false`, public comments arriving from the remote account are **discarded** rather<br>than imported — they are not stored as private comments — and ticket status is neither sent to<br>nor accepted from the remote account. Even when `true`, an account setting can separately<br>suppress a remote request to close the ticket. Defaults to `false` when omitted. Like<br>`sync_tags`, this value is only communicated to the remote account with the initial invitation<br>and cannot be changed later through the API.<br>|
|remote_subdomain|string|true|none|The subdomain of the Zendesk account you want to share tickets with. The account must already<br>exist — an unrecognized or blank subdomain is rejected, as is your own subdomain. This is the<br>only way to identify the remote party through this endpoint, so agreements created here are<br>always Zendesk-to-Zendesk and always outbound; agreements with Jira or another third party can<br>only be created in the admin interface. The new agreement is created with `status` `pending`<br>and an invitation is sent to the remote account, which must accept it before tickets can be<br>shared.<br>|
|sync_custom_fields|boolean|false|none|Whether custom field values are copied between the local ticket and its shared copy on the<br>remote account. Fields are matched by title, so a value is only applied on either side if a<br>ticket field with the same title exists there. Defaults to `false` when omitted. Like<br>`sync_tags`, this value is only communicated to the remote account with the initial invitation<br>and cannot be changed later through the API.<br>|
|sync_tags|boolean|false|none|Whether tags are copied between the local ticket and its shared copy on the remote account.<br>Defaults to `false` when omitted. This value is only communicated to the remote account with<br>the initial invitation, so it cannot be changed later through the API — only `status` is<br>updatable.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_SharingAgreementUpdateInput">SharingAgreementUpdateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasharingagreementupdateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_SharingAgreementUpdateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSsharingagreementupdateinput"></a>
<a id="tocssharingagreementupdateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "status": "pending"
}
```

The writable attributes accepted when updating a sharing agreement. Only `status` can be changed;
the sharing options chosen when the agreement was created are fixed for its lifetime. Sending an
empty object is accepted and changes nothing, though the agreement is re-validated on every request,
so the rejections described under `status` can apply even to a request that changes nothing.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|string \| null|false|none|The state of the agreement. Use `accepted` to accept an invitation you have received, `declined`<br>to reject or cancel one, `inactive` to suspend an accepted agreement without deleting it, and<br>`accepted` again to resume a suspended one. A request that actually changes the status sends the<br>new state to the account on the other side of the agreement, unless the new status is<br>`ssl_error`; a request that leaves the status as it was sends nothing. Moving to `inactive`,<br>`failed`, `ssl_error` or `configuration_error` also emails every administrator on your account;<br>the other statuses do not.<br><br>Three transitions are rejected. Moving back to `accepted` is rejected unless Zendesk recorded<br>your own account as the one that suspended the agreement, which it does only for an `accepted`<br>to `inactive` change made on your side — so an agreement the *other* account suspended cannot be<br>resumed from here. Moving to `pending` or `accepted` is rejected while you hold another accepted<br>agreement with the same remote URL in the same direction. Moving to anything other than<br>`inactive` or `declined` is rejected when the agreement's remote URL has come to point back at<br>your own account, which can happen after a subdomain change.<br><br>`failed`, `ssl_error` and `configuration_error` describe communication problems and are normally<br>set by Zendesk rather than by a client, but they are accepted here.<br><br>Note that `declined` set through this endpoint marks the agreement declined without deleting it<br>or its shared tickets — use the delete endpoint for that.<br><br>A blank value is accepted and leaves the status unchanged. `null` and an empty string are both<br>listed in the enum for that reason; a whitespace-only string such as `" "` behaves the same way<br>but cannot be enumerated. Omitting the property has the same effect. An unrecognized status name<br>is rejected.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|
|status|accepted|
|status|declined|
|status|inactive|
|status|failed|
|status|ssl_error|
|status|configuration_error|
|status|""|
|status|null|

The actor that created or last updated the suspension. Present for both human agents and system actors (for example, the messaging trigger subsystem). Empty (`{}`) when the suspension has no recorded actor.

### Properties

|zrn_type|messaging_trigger|

<h2 id="tocS_TagsAddRequest">TagsAddRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematagsaddrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_TagsAddRequest"></a>
<a id="tocStagsaddrequest"></a>
<a id="tocstagsaddrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "safe_update": true,
  "tags": [
    "customer"
  ],
  "updated_stamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "via": {
    "author_zrn": "string",
    "channel": "string"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|safe_update|boolean \| null|false|write-only|Write only. When `true`, protects against ticket update collisions. Requires<br>`updated_stamp`; sending `safe_update` without it returns a `409` on every resource.<br>`false` has the same effect as omitting the property or sending `null`: no collision<br>check is performed. Only affects the outcome for tickets. See [Protecting against<br>ticket update collisions](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/tickets/#protecting-against-ticket-update-collisions)<br>|
|tags|[string] \| string|false|none|The tags to add to the ones already applied. An array of tag strings, or a single<br>string. In either form each value is split on whitespace and on `,` `;` `\|` `(` `)`,<br>then stripped of special characters, downcased and de-duplicated. `null`, an empty array,<br>an empty string and omitting the property are all accepted and leave the existing tags<br>unchanged. Unlike the Set Tags operation, nothing here can clear a tag<br>|
|updated_stamp|string(date-time) \| null|false|write-only|Write only. The resource's last known `updated_at`. The update is applied only if it<br>still matches, otherwise the request returns a `409`. `null` has the same effect as<br>omitting the property: it is ignored unless `safe_update` is set, in which case the<br>request returns a `409`. Only affects the outcome for tickets. See the `safe_update`<br>property<br>|
|via|object \| null|false|write-only|Write only. `null` is accepted and treated as omitted. Only affects the outcome for tickets|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|tags|[string] \| string|false|none|An array of tag strings, or a single string. In either form each value is split<br>on whitespace and on `,` `;` `\|` `(` `)`, then stripped of special characters,<br>downcased and de-duplicated. **`null` is destructive**: it replaces the stored tags with<br>nothing, clearing every tag. An empty array, an empty string and omitting the property<br>entirely all do the same. Clearing every tag is the only thing `null` can mean here<br>|

|editable_in_portal|boolean|false|none|Whether this field is editable by end users in the help center|
|position|integer|false|none|The relative position of the ticket field on a ticket. Note that for accounts with ticket forms, positions are controlled by the different forms|

|regexp_for_validation|string|false|none|For "regexp" fields only. The validation pattern for a field value to be deemed valid|
|relationship_filter|object|false|none|A filter definition that allows your autocomplete to filter results|
|relationship_target_type|string|false|none|Required for `lookup` and `multi_lookup` fields. A representation of what type of object the field references.<br>Options are "zen:user", "zen:organization", "zen:ticket", or "zen:custom_object:{key}" where key is a custom<br>object key. Can't be changed after the field is created.<br>|
|required|boolean|false|none|If true, agents must enter a value in the field to change the ticket status to solved|
|required_in_portal|boolean|false|none|If true, end users must enter a value in the field to create the request|
|sub_type_id|integer|false|none|For system ticket fields of type "priority" and "status". Defaults to 0. A "priority" sub type of 1 removes the "Low" and "Urgent" options. A "status" sub type of 1 adds the "On-Hold" option|

|title|string|true|none|The title of the ticket field|
|title_in_portal|string|false|none|The title of the ticket field for end users in the help center|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the ticket field. Determines which additional attributes are relevant (for example `custom_field_options`<br>is required for `tagger` and `multiselect`). Defaults to `text` when not specified. Editable only on creation.<br>|

A condition set that shows and optionally requires child fields in the agent interface when a parent field
holds a given value. Requires the account's native conditional fields feature; without it the `agent_conditions`
array is silently ignored.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|child_fields|[object]|true|none|The fields shown while the condition is active. Duplicate `id` entries are collapsed. An empty array is accepted rather than rejected — it creates no condition, and on an update it deletes every existing condition of this kind, because none are restated|
|parent_field_id|integer(int64)|true|none|The ID of the ticket field whose value activates the condition. Must be a field on this form, active, and of type `tagger`, `priority`, `tickettype`, `checkbox`, `textarea` or `text`|
|value|string \| null \| boolean|true|none|The parent field value that activates the condition. For a `checkbox` parent field, send a boolean — any<br>unrecognized value is coerced to false rather than rejected. For `priority` send a priority name, which is limited<br>to `normal` and `high` on an account using the basic priority set. For `tickettype` send one of `question`,<br>`incident`, `problem` or `task`. For `tagger` send the tag value of one of the parent field's options.<br><br>Null is only accepted for a `checkbox` parent field, where it is coerced to false like any other unrecognized<br>value. For every other parent field type a null is rejected<br>|

|parent_field_id|integer(int64)|true|none|The ID of the ticket field whose value activates the condition. Must be a field on this form, active, editable in the help center, and of type `tagger`, `priority`, `tickettype`, `checkbox`, `textarea` or `text`|

For a `checkbox` parent field, send a boolean — any<br>unrecognized value is coerced to false rather than rejected. For `tickettype` send one of `question`,<br>`incident`, `problem` or `task`. For `tagger` send the tag value of one of the parent field's options.<br><br>Null is only accepted for a `checkbox` parent field, where it is coerced to false like any other unrecognized<br>value.
