The writable attributes accepted when creating a ticket form. The form must be given a name, through either `name`
or `raw_name`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|false|none|Whether the form is available for use. A form cannot be both inactive and the default form|
|agent_conditions|[[TicketFormAgentConditionObject](#schematicketformagentconditionobject)]|false|none|Condition sets applied in the agent interface. Null and an empty array both create no conditions|
|default|boolean|false|none|Whether this is the account's default form. Setting it forces `end_user_visible` to true, demotes the previous<br>default form, and is rejected for a `service_catalog` form or an inactive form<br>|
|display_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the form shown to end users. Defaults to `name`, but only when `end_user_visible` is also being set to<br>true. Sending null is equivalent to omitting it and follows the same defaulting<br>|
|end_user_conditions|[[TicketFormEndUserConditionObject](#schematicketformenduserconditionobject)]|false|none|Condition sets applied in end-user products. Null and an empty array both create no conditions|
|end_user_visible|boolean|false|none|Whether the form is visible to end users. Always true for the default form|
|form_type|string \| null|false|none|The type of form to create. Only honored on accounts with the Service Catalog feature, where `service_catalog`<br>creates a service catalog form; other accounts always get a `standard` form. Defaults to `standard`, as does a<br>null value<br>|
|in_all_brands|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the form is available in every brand on this account. A null value is ignored rather than applied|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the form|
|position|integer \| null|false|none|The position of this form among the account's other forms. Defaults to the end of the list when omitted or null<br>|
|raw_display_name|string \| null|false|none|A dynamic content placeholder for the display name. Takes the place of `display_name` when both are given,<br>including when it is an empty string. See [Dynamic Content](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/).<br>Sending null is accepted and discarded: `display_name` is left as sent<br>|
|raw_name|string \| null|false|none|A dynamic content placeholder for the name. Takes the place of `name` when both are given, including when it is an<br>empty string. See [Dynamic Content](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/). Sending null is<br>accepted and discarded: `name` is left as sent<br>|
|restricted_brand_ids|[integer(int64)]|false|none|The IDs of the brands this form is restricted to, used when `in_all_brands` is false. IDs that do not name an<br>active brand on the account are silently dropped. Unlike an update, a create applies these on any account, even<br>one with a single active brand — but such an account then cannot change them again. Null and an empty array both<br>leave the form unrestricted, the same as omitting the attribute<br>|
|ticket_field_ids|[integer(int64)]|false|none|The IDs of the ticket fields on this form, in the order they are shown. The account's system-required fields are<br>prepended automatically whether or not they are listed. An empty array or null is treated as if the attribute were<br>omitted, leaving the form with only those system-required fields<br>|

|form_type|service_catalog|
|form_type|null|

The writable attributes accepted when updating a ticket form. Every attribute is optional and an omitted attribute is
left unchanged, but `ticket_field_ids`, `restricted_brand_ids`, `agent_conditions` and `end_user_conditions` are
replaced wholesale rather than merged — see each description. A form's `form_type` cannot be changed after creation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|false|none|Whether the form is available for use. The default form cannot be made inactive|
|agent_conditions|[[TicketFormAgentConditionObject](#schematicketformagentconditionobject)]|false|none|The complete set of condition sets for the agent interface. Any existing agent condition not restated in the array<br>is deleted, so send the full list. Passing an empty array or null deletes them all<br>|
|default|boolean|false|none|Whether this is the account's default form. Setting it forces `end_user_visible` to true, demotes the previous<br>default form, and is rejected for a `service_catalog` form or an inactive form. The current default form cannot<br>clear its own flag — promote another form instead<br>|
|display_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the form shown to end users. Sending null clears it, but only on a form that is not end-user visible —<br>on an end-user-visible form a null is rejected, and when the same request also sets `end_user_visible` the null is<br>replaced by `name`<br>|
|end_user_conditions|[[TicketFormEndUserConditionObject](#schematicketformenduserconditionobject)]|false|none|The complete set of condition sets for end-user products. Any existing end-user condition not restated in the<br>array is deleted, so send the full list. Passing an empty array or null deletes them all<br>|
|end_user_visible|boolean|false|none|Whether the form is visible to end users. Always true for the default form|
|in_all_brands|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the form is available in every brand on this account. A null value is ignored rather than applied|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the form|
|position|integer|false|none|The position of this form among the account's other forms. Unlike a create, an update will not default it: a null<br>is rejected because a live form must have a position<br>|
|raw_display_name|string \| null|false|none|A dynamic content placeholder for the display name. Takes the place of `display_name` when both are given,<br>including when it is an empty string. See [Dynamic Content](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/).<br>Sending null is accepted and discarded: `display_name` is left as sent<br>|
|raw_name|string \| null|false|none|A dynamic content placeholder for the name. Takes the place of `name` when both are given, including when it is an<br>empty string. See [Dynamic Content](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/). Sending null is<br>accepted and discarded: `name` is left as sent<br>|
|restricted_brand_ids|[integer(int64)]|false|none|The complete set of brands this form is restricted to. Any brand currently restricting the form whose ID is absent<br>from the array is removed, so send the full list rather than a partial one. Passing an empty array or null removes<br>every restriction. IDs that do not name an active brand on the account are silently dropped. Only applied on<br>accounts with more than one active brand<br>|
|ticket_field_ids|[integer(int64)]|false|none|The complete, ordered set of ticket fields on this form. Any field currently on the form whose ID is absent from<br>the array is REMOVED from the form, so a partial list silently drops fields — send the full list, or omit the<br>attribute entirely to leave the form's fields untouched. An empty array and null are also treated as omitted and<br>cannot be used to clear the form. The account's system-required fields are prepended automatically<br>|

|comment|object|false|none|none|

|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|The time the ticket was created (for historical imports)|
|custom_fields|[[TicketFieldValueInput](#schematicketfieldvalueinput)]|false|none|Custom field values to set on the ticket.<br>Each entry specifies a field ID and its value.<br>|
|custom_status_id|integer(int64)|false|none|The custom ticket status id of the ticket|
|description|string|false|none|Read-only first comment on the ticket. When [creating a ticket](#create-ticket), use `comment` to set the description. See [Description and first comment](#description-and-first-comment)|
|email_ccs|[[EmailCCObject](#schemaemailccobject)]|false|none|An array of objects that represent agent or end users email CCs to add or delete from the ticket. See [Setting email CCs](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/creating-and-updating-tickets#setting-email-ccs)|
|external_id|string|false|none|An id you can use to link Zendesk Support tickets to local records|
|followers|[[FollowerObject](#schemafollowerobject)]|false|none|An array of objects that represent agent followers to add or delete from the ticket. See [Setting followers](/documentation/ticketing/managing-tickets/creating-and-updating-tickets#setting-followers)|
|group_id|integer(int64)|false|none|The group this ticket is assigned to|
|priority|[TicketPriorityEnum](#schematicketpriorityenum)|false|none|The urgency with which the ticket should be addressed.|
|recipient|string|false|none|The original recipient e-mail address of the ticket|
|requester_id|integer(int64)|false|none|The user who requested this ticket|
|solved_at|string(date-time)|false|none|The time the ticket was solved (for historical imports)|
|status|string|false|none|The state of the ticket|
|subject|string|false|none|The value of the subject field for this ticket|
|submitter_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The user who submitted the ticket. The current API caller is used if not specified|
|tags|[string]|false|none|The array of tags applied to this ticket|
|type|string \| null|false|none|The type of the ticket. `null` maps to the account's default ticket type|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|The time the ticket was last updated (for historical imports)|
|via|object|false|none|An object explaining how the ticket was created. See the [Via object reference](/documentation/ticketing/reference-guides/via-object-reference)<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_TokenRequest">TokenRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematokenrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_TokenRequest"></a>
<a id="tocStokenrequest"></a>
<a id="tocstokenrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "auth_origin": "string",
  "brand_id": "string",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "return_to_on_failure": "string"
}
```

Request payload for `POST /access/token`, used to request a one-time password
access token via email. The controller accepts several optional parameters
that provide context for the authentication flow.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auth_origin|string|false|none|Optional identifier tracking where the authentication request originated,<br>used for analytics and logging.<br>|
|brand_id|string|false|none|Optional brand identifier for multi-brand accounts. When specified, the<br>lookup and token generation will be scoped to that brand if brand user<br>separation is enabled.<br>|
|email|string(email)|true|none|Email address to send the OTP token to. The endpoint will look up a user<br>with this email and send them a token if they are permitted to use SSO<br>bypass (typically account owners and/or admins).<br>|
|return_to_on_failure|string|false|none|Optional URL to redirect to if authentication fails. Currently accepted<br>by the controller's parameter allowlist but may not be actively used by<br>this endpoint.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_TokenResponse">TokenResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematokenresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_TokenResponse"></a>
<a id="tocStokenresponse"></a>
<a id="tocstokenresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "success": true
}
```

Response from `POST /access/token`. Always returns a success indicator
regardless of whether a token was actually sent, to prevent email
enumeration attacks.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|success|boolean|true|none|Always returns `true` to indicate the request was processed. This does<br>not confirm that an email was sent - the actual delivery depends on<br>SSO bypass configuration and user permissions.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_TrialAccountInput">TrialAccountInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematrialaccountinput"></a>
<a id="schema_TrialAccountInput"></a>
<a id="tocStrialaccountinput"></a>
<a id="tocstrialaccountinput"></a>

```json
{
  "_zd_choose_shard_udupi": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "employee_service_suite_trial": true,
  "google_apps_domain": "string",
  "help_desk_size": "string",
  "language": "string",
  "multiproduct": true,
  "name": "string",
  "remote_authentication": {
    "fingerprint": "string",
    "remote_login_url": "string",
    "remote_logout_url": "string",
    "type": "string"
  },
  "remote_login_url": "string",
  "source": "string",
  "subdomain": "string",
  "suite_trial": true,
  "utc_offset": 0,
  "zendesk_suite_trial": true
}
```

Attributes of the trial account to provision. Corresponds to `Api::V2::AccountsController::ACCOUNT_PARAMETER`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_zd_choose_shard_udupi|integer \| null|false|none|Preferred database shard for the new account. Formerly read by `Zendesk::Accounts::Initializer` on the Classic creation path, which PLATOPS-1372 removed; the value is now accepted and forwarded verbatim, and whether the account service honours it is outside this repository.|
|currency|string \| null|false|none|Currency code for the account.|
|employee_service_suite_trial|boolean \| null \| string \| integer|false|none|Provisions an Employee Service Suite trial (a professional-plan `employee_service_suite` SKU expiring in 14 days) with `account.account_type` set to `pre_spp`. Enabled by any value the parameter gate coerces to true (`1`, `"1"`, `true`, `"true"`, `"on"`). Takes effect only when `zendesk_suite_trial` is not set, which is evaluated first.|
|google_apps_domain|string \| null|false|none|Google Workspace domain to associate with the account. Must not already be routed to another account and must not be `gmail.com`; either returns `409 Conflict`.|
|help_desk_size|string \| null|false|none|Free-form description of the expected number of agents, for example `Small Team`, `1-9` or `Large group`. Surfaced verbatim as `company_size` in the signup tracking properties (`Account::Tracking`); any categorisation happens downstream of this repository. Not enforced by this controller's own gates; `Account` validates its presence on create, but the record is created by the account service, out of process. `null` and omission are indistinguishable here.|
|language|string \| null|false|none|Locale for the new account, for example `ja`. Copied to `account.locale` before the payload is forwarded.|
|multiproduct|boolean \| null \| string \| integer|false|none|Legacy switch for the account's product configuration. PLATOPS-1372 removed the multiproduct branch and the legacy Classic fallback from `create`, so this controller no longer reads the value and it has no effect on which service handles the request. It is still accepted by the parameter gate and forwarded verbatim to the account service like every other permitted property; whether it affects provisioning is decided by the account service, outside this repository. The value the account service returns is echoed back as `account.multiproduct` in the response body.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the account. Not enforced by this controller's own gates; accepted and forwarded to the account service, which decides whether it is required. `null` and omission are indistinguishable here.|
|remote_authentication|[TrialAccountRemoteAuthenticationInput](#schematrialaccountremoteauthenticationinput) \| object \| null|false|none|Single sign-on configuration for the new account. Accepted and forwarded to the account service verbatim; this controller does not read it.|
|remote_login_url|string \| null|false|none|Remote login URL for the account. Distinct from `remote_authentication.remote_login_url`; both are accepted and forwarded.|
|source|string \| null|false|none|Provisioning channel this signup came from. Also copied into `trial_extras.source` when present.|
|subdomain|string|true|none|The subdomain to provision, and the only place this controller looks for it. Must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,}[a-z0-9]$` (`SUBDOMAIN_PATTERN`, lib/vars.rb), must not start with `xn--`, and must be neither taken nor reserved; the value is trimmed of surrounding whitespace before those checks run. A missing, blank, invalid, reserved or taken subdomain returns `409 Conflict` with a `success: false` body rather than a validation error. Note that a successful request locks the subdomain in the shared cache for 60 seconds *before* the account is created, so retrying a request that failed with a `422` returns a `409` until the lock expires.|
|suite_trial|boolean \| null \| string \| integer|false|none|Provisions a `suite` trial SKU instead of the default `support` SKU. Also copied into `trial_extras.suite_trial` when present. Declared as a boolean in the parameter gate, which also accepts and coerces the string and integer spellings `"true"`, `"1"`, `"on"`, `1`, `"false"`, `"0"` and `0`.|
|utc_offset|integer \| null \| string|false|none|Time zone for the new account, given either as a UTC offset (for example `7` or `"7"`) or as an ActiveSupport time zone name. Resolved by `Account::Localization.utc_to_tz` into `account.time_zone`; an unrecognised, empty or `null` value falls back to `Eastern Time (US & Canada)`.|
|zendesk_suite_trial|boolean \| null \| string \| integer|false|none|Provisions a Zendesk Suite trial (a professional-plan `zendesk_suite` SKU expiring in 14 days) rather than the default SKU. Enabled by any value the parameter gate coerces to true (`1`, `"1"`, `true`, `"true"`, `"on"`); every other value is ignored. Evaluated before `employee_service_suite_trial`.|

<h2 id="tocS_TrialAccountRequest">TrialAccountRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematrialaccountrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_TrialAccountRequest"></a>
<a id="tocStrialaccountrequest"></a>
<a id="tocstrialaccountrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "account": {
    "_zd_choose_shard_udupi": 0,
    "currency": "string",
    "employee_service_suite_trial": true,
    "google_apps_domain": "string",
    "help_desk_size": "string",
    "language": "string",
    "multiproduct": true,
    "name": "string",
    "remote_authentication": {
      "fingerprint": "string",
      "remote_login_url": "string",
      "remote_logout_url": "string",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "remote_login_url": "string",
    "source": "string",
    "subdomain": "string",
    "suite_trial": true,
    "utc_offset": 0,
    "zendesk_suite_trial": true
  },
  "address": {
    "city": "string",
    "phone": "string",
    "province": "string",
    "street": "string",
    "zip": "string"
  },
  "agents": [
    {
      "email": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "role": "string"
    }
  ],
  "force_pod_id": "string",
  "owner": {
    "email": "string",
    "is_verified": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "password": "string"
  },
  "partner": {
    "name": "string",
    "url": "string"
  },
  "trial_extras": {}
}
```

Payload for provisioning a trial account through the reseller API. This controller does not filter the payload down before use: after the parameter gate it forwards the whole request body verbatim to the account creator, adding `skus`, `pod_id` and the derived `account.time_zone`, `account.locale`, `account.account_type` and `owner.is_verified`. Every request goes to `api/services/accounts` on the account service, with the SKU chosen by `account.zendesk_suite_trial` and `account.employee_service_suite_trial`; the multiproduct branch and the legacy Classic fallback that PLATOPS-1372 removed were the only alternatives. All requests merge a `trial_extras` bag into the payload. Unknown keys are stripped before the request is forwarded.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|object|true|none|Attributes of the account to provision.|
|address|object|true|none|Contact address of the account. Only `phone` is required.|
|agents|[[TrialAccountAgentInput](#schematrialaccountagentinput)]|false|none|Additional agents to invite into the new account. Forwarded to the account creator; this controller does not read the value.|
|force_pod_id|string \| null|false|none|Pins the new account to a specific pod. When present it is forwarded as `pod_id` to the account creator.|
|owner|object|true|none|Attributes of the account owner to create.|
|partner|[TrialAccountPartnerInput](#schematrialaccountpartnerinput) \| object \| null|false|none|Reseller/partner attribution for the account. Accepted and forwarded to the account service verbatim; this controller does not read it. The `partner_name`/`partner_url` account settings these historically became were written on the Classic creation path, removed by PLATOPS-1372.|
|trial_extras|object \| null|false|none|Free-form bag of trial metadata. Every value is coerced to a string, and the controller then injects `confirm_origin`, `creation_channel`, `original_remote_ip`, `region`, and copies `account.source` and `account.suite_trial` into it (`AccountsController#account_creation_params_trial_extras`). Declared as `Parameters.anything`, so a non-object value passes the parameter gate but then fails when the controller iterates it.|

<h2 id="tocS_TriggerReorderRequest">TriggerReorderRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematriggerreorderrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_TriggerReorderRequest"></a>
<a id="tocStriggerreorderrequest"></a>
<a id="tocstriggerreorderrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "trigger_ids": [
    0
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|trigger_ids|[integer(int64)]|true|none|The complete set of active ticket trigger ids in the account, in the firing order to apply. Each id's new position is its 1-based index in this array. The array must contain exactly the ids of every **active** ticket trigger in the account — no more, no fewer. A partial or padded list is rejected with a `400 Bad Request` ("Invalid attribute: all triggers are not provided") and nothing is reordered, so a generated call must first read the account's active ticket triggers and send all of them. Inactive triggers are not reordered and must not be included. An empty array is only accepted on an account that has no active ticket triggers; otherwise it is the same `400`. Omitting the property is not supported.|

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "custom_field_options": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "raw_name": "string",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],

  "key": "string",
  "permissions": {
    "restrict_access_by_role": true,

      {
        "role_id": 0,

          "read"
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "position": 0,
  "raw_description": "string",
  "raw_title": "string",
  "regexp_for_validation": "string",
  "relationship_filter": {
    "all": [
      {
        "field": "string",
        "operator": "string",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ],
    "any": [
      {
        "field": "string",
        "operator": "string",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ]
  },
  "relationship_target_type": "string",
  "tag": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "type": "checkbox"
}
```

The writable attributes accepted when creating a user field.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether this field is available. Defaults to `true`; sending null has the same effect|
|custom_field_options|[[UserFieldOptionInput](#schemauserfieldoptioninput)]|false|none|Required for `dropdown`, `tagger`, and `multiselect` fields; at least one option must be supplied. The array order<br>determines each option's position.<br><br>Do not send this for any other field type. It is not ignored: the options association is defined on every field<br>type, so the options are persisted against a field that can never present them, leaving unreachable rows behind.<br><br>Sending null is equivalent to omitting the key: no options are created. An empty array behaves the same way on<br>create.<br>|
|description|string \| null|false|none|User-defined description of this field's purpose. Defaults to the field's `title` when omitted; sending null has<br>the same effect and writes the `title` into `description`, rather than leaving it empty.<br>|
|key|string|true|none|A unique key that identifies this custom field. Used for updating the field and referencing in placeholders.<br>May contain only letters, digits, and underscores, must contain at least one letter or underscore, and is limited<br>to 255 characters. The values `count`, `reorder`, `check_permissions`, and `show_many` are reserved. Cannot be<br>changed after creation.<br>|
|permissions|[UserFieldPermissionsInput](#schemauserfieldpermissionsinput)|false|none|Restricts which agent roles can read and update this field's values. Only honored on accounts with the<br>`permissions_custom_user_fields` feature enabled; on all other accounts the key is accepted and silently ignored.<br>Sending null is equivalent to omitting the key and leaves any existing permissions untouched.<br>|
|position|integer \| null|false|none|Ordering of the field relative to other fields. The field is inserted at this index in the account's existing user<br>field order; when omitted or null, the field is appended last.<br>|
|raw_description|string \| null|false|none|The dynamic content placeholder for the description. See [Dynamic Content](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/).<br>When supplied, this value is written to `description` and any `description` sent alongside it is discarded. Sending<br>null is accepted and discarded: `description` is left as sent.<br>|
|raw_title|string \| null|false|none|The dynamic content placeholder for the title. See [Dynamic Content](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/).<br>When supplied, this value is written to `title` and any `title` sent alongside it is discarded. Sending null is<br>accepted and discarded: `title` is left as sent.<br>|
|regexp_for_validation|string|false|none|For `regexp` fields only. The validation pattern for a field value to be deemed valid|
|relationship_filter|object \| null|false|none|For `lookup` fields only. A filter definition that limits which records the field's autocomplete returns. Sending<br>null is equivalent to omitting it and leaves the field with no filter.<br>|
|relationship_target_type|string \| null|false|none|Required for `lookup` fields; omitting it returns a 400. A representation of what type of object the field<br>references. For user fields the options are `zen:user`, `zen:organization`, `zen:ticket`, `zen:attachment`, or<br>`zen:custom_object:{key}` where key is a custom object key. Values are downcased by the API. `zen:article`,<br>`zen:group`, and `zen:brand` are not valid on user fields and are rejected. Cannot be changed after creation.<br>Sending null is equivalent to omitting it, so a `lookup` field still returns a 400.<br>|
|tag|string \| null|false|none|For `checkbox` fields only. A tag added to the user when the checkbox field is selected. Supplying `tag` for any<br>other field type fails validation. Values are downcased by the API. Sending null is accepted and leaves the field<br>with no tag.<br>|
|title|string|true|none|The title of the user field|
|type|string \| null|false|none|The type of the user field. Determines which additional attributes are relevant (for example `custom_field_options`<br>is required for `dropdown`, `tagger`, and `multiselect`). Defaults to `text` when not specified. Cannot be changed<br>after creation. Sending null is equivalent to omitting it and creates a `text` field.<br>|

|type|date|
|type|decimal|
|type|integer|
|type|regexp|
|type|text|
|type|textarea|
|type|dropdown|
|type|tagger|
|type|multiselect|
|type|lookup|

<h2 id="tocS_UserFieldOptionCreateOrUpdateInput">UserFieldOptionCreateOrUpdateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemauserfieldoptioncreateorupdateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_UserFieldOptionCreateOrUpdateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSuserfieldoptioncreateorupdateinput"></a>
<a id="tocsuserfieldoptioncreateorupdateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "position": 0,
  "value": "string"
}
```

A single option for a `dropdown` user field, created or updated in place. Fields created with `type: tagger` are
dropdown fields and are also supported. `multiselect` fields are not: this endpoint returns 404 for them, and their
options must be managed through the `custom_field_options` array on Update User Field.

Supplying `id` updates that option. When `id` is omitted or null, the API looks up an option on the field with the
same `value`, whether that option is active or previously deleted. If one is found it is updated in place, restored if
it had been deleted, and the response is a 200 rather than a 201 — so reusing an existing `value` silently mutates
that option instead of creating a new one. Otherwise a new option is created.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The id of an existing, active option to update. A deleted option's id is not accepted and returns 404; a deleted<br>option can only be restored through the `value` match below. Omit `id` or send null to create a new option, or to<br>match an existing one by `value`.<br>|
|name|string|true|none|The presentation name of the option|
|position|integer|false|none|The relative position of the option in the field's option list. Defaults to the end of the list when creating a new option|
|value|string|false|none|The tag value applied to the user when the option is selected. Must be unique across the account's field options.<br>Required when creating an option; when updating an existing option by `id`, omitting it leaves the current value<br>unchanged.<br>|

Sending null is<br>accepted and discarded: `name` is left as sent.<br>|

An option for a `dropdown`, `tagger`, or `multiselect` custom user field, as supplied when updating the field. The
`id` key must always be present.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64) \| string \| null|true|none|The id of an existing option to update in place. To add a new option, send null or an empty string. The key<br>itself is mandatory on every entry: an option with no `id` key is rejected with a `BlankValue` error.<br>|

See [Dynamic Content](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/).<br>When supplied, this value is written to `name` and any `name` sent alongside it is discarded. Sending null is<br>accepted and discarded: `name` is left as sent.<br>|

Must be unique across the account's field options.<br>Required when adding a new option; when updating an existing option by `id`, omitting it leaves the current value<br>unchanged.<br><br>When adding an option whose `value` matches one that was previously deleted, the deleted option is restored<br>instead. Restricts which agent roles can read and update this field's values. Only honored on accounts with the

|roles|[[UserFieldPermissionsRoleInput](#schemauserfieldpermissionsroleinput)]|false|none|The custom agent roles granted access to this field, and the scopes each is granted. This list is a full<br>replacement, and null is treated the same as `[]`: sending either alongside `restrict_access_by_role: true` leaves<br>only the account's admin roles with access and drops every other role's grant.<br>|

|active|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether this field is available. Sending null does not leave the field unchanged: it reactivates the field, because<br>a nil `is_active` is defaulted back to `true`.<br>|
|custom_field_options|[[UserFieldOptionUpdateInput](#schemauserfieldoptionupdateinput)]|false|none|For `dropdown`, `tagger`, and `multiselect` fields only. Sending it for any other field type fails with an<br>`Invalid` error on the request.<br><br>**Destructive:** this array is a full replacement, not a patch. Every existing option you want to keep must be<br>present in every update request. Any option you omit is deleted, and those values are removed from the users that<br>held them. Passing an empty array deletes every option on the field. Omitting the `custom_field_options` key<br>entirely leaves the options untouched, so a partial update must omit the key rather than send a partial list.<br><br>Every entry must include an `id`: supply an existing option's `id` to update it in place, or a null or empty `id`<br>to add a new option. An entry with no `id` key at all is rejected. The array order determines each option's<br>position.<br><br>Null and `[]` are **not** interchangeable here. `custom_field_options: null` is accepted and ignored, leaving the<br>options untouched — it is the same as omitting the key. `custom_field_options: []` deletes every option on the<br>field and returns a 200. Send null, or omit the key, if you mean "leave the options alone".<br>|
|description|string \| null|false|none|User-defined description of this field's purpose. Sending null does not clear it: the field's current `title` is<br>written into `description` instead.<br>|
|permissions|[UserFieldPermissionsInput](#schemauserfieldpermissionsinput)|false|none|Restricts which agent roles can read and update this field's values. Only honored on accounts with the<br>`permissions_custom_user_fields` feature enabled; on all other accounts the key is accepted and silently ignored.<br>Sending null is equivalent to omitting the key and leaves any existing permissions untouched.<br>|
|position|integer|false|none|Ordering of the field relative to other fields. Unlike on create, this writes the field's position directly without<br>shifting its siblings, so it can leave two fields sharing a position. Use Reorder User Field to reposition a field<br>within the account's ordering.<br>|
|raw_description|string \| null|false|none|The dynamic content placeholder for the description. See [Dynamic Content](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/).<br>When supplied, this value is written to `description` and any `description` sent alongside it is discarded. Sending<br>null is accepted and discarded: `description` is left as sent, or unchanged if no `description` was sent.<br>|
|raw_title|string \| null|false|none|The dynamic content placeholder for the title. See [Dynamic Content](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/).<br>When supplied, this value is written to `title` and any `title` sent alongside it is discarded. Sending null is<br>accepted and discarded: `title` is left as sent, or unchanged if no `title` was sent.<br>|
|regexp_for_validation|string|false|none|For `regexp` fields only. The validation pattern for a field value to be deemed valid|
|relationship_filter|object \| null|false|none|For `lookup` fields only. A filter definition that limits which records the field's autocomplete returns. Sending<br>null is accepted and ignored, leaving the existing filter untouched; send `{}` to clear it.<br>|
|tag|string \| null|false|none|For `checkbox` fields only. A tag added to the user when the checkbox field is selected. Supplying `tag` for any<br>other field type fails validation. Values are downcased by the API. Sending null is accepted and clears the tag.<br>|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the user field|

<h2 id="tocS_UserIdentityCreateInput">UserIdentityCreateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemauseridentitycreateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_UserIdentityCreateInput"></a>

```json
{
  "auto_ownership": true,
  "ownership": "owned",
  "primary": true,
  "skip_verify_email": true,
  "type": "email",
  "value": "string",
  "verification_method": "none",
  "verified": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auto_ownership|boolean \| null|false|none|Write-only ownership control for the Shared Email EAP. When true, `owned` is attempted first and falls back to `shared` on an ownership conflict. The fallback is subject to the same restrictions as `ownership: shared`: it requires the `shared_email_creation_enabled` account setting, respects the per-brand shared-identity cap, and never applies to `google` identities - an ownership conflict for a Google-backed email identity is returned as an error instead of falling back. null is accepted and treated exactly like `false`. Only applies to `email` and `google` identities, and ignored unless the account has the Shared Email EAP enabled. Mutually exclusive with `ownership`; requests that supply both keys are rejected.|
|ownership|string \| null|false|none|Write-only ownership control for the Shared Email EAP. Only applies to `email` and `google` identities, and ignored unless the account has the Shared Email EAP enabled. null is accepted and falls back to `owned`. `shared` additionally requires the `shared_email_creation_enabled` account setting, is rejected outright for `google` identities (a Google-backed email identity can only be owned), and is subject to a per-brand cap on shared identities per address (100 by default; past the cap the request fails with `LimitExceeded`). A create that will send a verification email for a shared address is rate-limited and can be rejected with `429 Too Many Requests`. Mutually exclusive with `auto_ownership`; requests that supply both keys are rejected.|
|primary|boolean \| null|false|none|Makes the new identity the primary one. null is accepted and ignored. Only takes effect for `email` identities. For a verified<br>email identity (`verified: true` or `verification_method: low`) the identity becomes primary<br>immediately; for an unverified one the promotion is deferred - the verification email link carries<br>`make_primary=true`, so the identity becomes primary (and the former primary is removed) when the<br>recipient verifies. Ignored for non-email identity types, including `google`.<br><br>To promote an identity that already exists, use the<br>[Make Identity Primary](#make-identity-primary) endpoint instead.<br>|
|skip_verify_email|boolean \| null|false|none|Suppresses the verification or welcome email for the new identity. null is accepted and treated<br>exactly like `false`. Only effective when an agent<br>creates an identity for a different user - it is ignored when adding an identity to your own<br>profile.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|The type of identity to create.<br><br>Only the types listed here can be created through this endpoint. The remaining identity types<br>(`any_channel`, `foreign`, `sdk`, `microsoft`) are created by internal systems only, and a request<br>for one of them is rejected with a `400`. The deprecated `phone` alias is likewise rejected<br>here - use `phone_number`.<br><br>`messaging` and `slack` back internal channel integrations. `slack` additionally requires the<br>Slack identity feature to be enabled on the account.<br>|
|value|string|true|none|The identifier for this identity. An email address for `email` and `google`, the screen name for<br>`twitter`, the Facebook user id for `facebook`, and an E.164 phone number for `phone_number` and<br>`agent_forwarding`. Phone numbers are validated unless the account has phone number validation<br>turned off.<br>|
|verification_method|string \| null|false|none|The verification state to create the identity with. `low` creates a verified identity and<br>suppresses the verification email. Only `none` and `low` are accepted here; the higher methods<br>(`sso`, `embed`, `full`) are set by the corresponding authentication flows.<br><br>Has no effect for `phone_number` and `agent_forwarding` identities, which are always verified, nor<br>for `slack`. Also ignored when creating an email identity (including `google`) for the account owner: that identity is<br>always created unverified and a verification email is sent.<br><br>null is accepted and treated exactly like `none`. Because this property wins over `verified`,<br>sending `verified: true` alongside `verification_method: null` creates an unverified identity.<br>|
|verified|boolean \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** Creates the identity already verified, equivalent to `verification_method: low`. Deprecated - use<br>`verification_method` instead. Ignored when `verification_method` is also sent - that property<br>wins. null is accepted and treated exactly like `false`.<br><br>Has no effect for `phone_number` and `agent_forwarding` identities, which are always verified, nor<br>for `slack`. Also ignored when creating an email identity (including `google`) for the account owner: that identity is<br>always created unverified and a verification email is sent.<br>|

|---|---|

|ownership|shared|
|ownership|null|

|type|twitter|
|type|facebook|
|type|google|
|type|agent_forwarding|
|type|phone_number|
|type|messaging|
|type|slack|
|verification_method|none|
|verification_method|low|
|verification_method|null|

<h2 id="tocS_UserIdentityUpdateInput">UserIdentityUpdateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemauseridentityupdateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_UserIdentityUpdateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSuseridentityupdateinput"></a>
<a id="tocsuseridentityupdateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "auto_ownership": true,
  "deliverable_state": "deliverable",
  "ownership": "owned",
  "value": "string",
  "verification_method": "none",
  "verified": true
}
```

A partial update. Only the properties listed here can be changed on an existing identity - `type` and
`primary` cannot, and are ignored if sent. Omitting a property leaves it unchanged.

One exception to "leaves it unchanged": if the identity is a non-primary email identity of the account
owner, sending an `identity` object unverifies the identity and sends a verification email. The
trigger is the presence of the object - its contents make no difference, and `verified: true` or
`verification_method: low` does not prevent it. Sending `"identity": null` instead of an object is the
one way to avoid it, because the whole update branch is then skipped. The account owner's primary
email identity cannot be updated at all.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auto_ownership|boolean \| null|false|none|Write-only ownership control for the Shared Email EAP. When true, `owned` is attempted first and falls back to `shared` on an ownership conflict. The `shared` fallback is subject to the same restrictions as `ownership: shared`: it requires the `shared_email_creation_enabled` account setting, respects the per-brand shared-identity cap, and never applies to Google-backed identities - a conflict for one is returned as an error instead of falling back. null is accepted and treated exactly like `false`. Only applies to `email` and `google` identities, and ignored unless the account has the Shared Email EAP enabled. Mutually exclusive with `ownership`; requests that supply both keys are rejected.|
|deliverable_state|string \| null|false|none|Clears the undeliverable state of an email identity, so that Zendesk resumes sending to it. `deliverable` is the only value that has any effect, and only on an `email` identity that is currently undeliverable. Every other value, including null, is ignored.|
|ownership|string \| null|false|none|Write-only ownership control for the Shared Email EAP. Only applies to `email` and `google` identities, and ignored unless the account has the Shared Email EAP enabled. null is accepted and falls back to the identity's current ownership, so it changes nothing. Setting `owned` on a shared identity promotes it to owned and demotes the identity that currently owns the address to shared in the same transaction, instead of failing with an ownership conflict. Demoting an owned identity to `shared` additionally requires the `shared_email_creation_enabled` account setting, is rejected for Google-backed identities, and is subject to the per-brand cap on shared identities per address (100 by default, `LimitExceeded` past it) when the request also changes `value`. Mutually exclusive with `auto_ownership`; requests that supply both keys are rejected.|
|value|string \| null|false|none|The new identifier for this identity.<br><br>Changing the value resets `verification_method` to `none`, so the identity becomes unverified<br>unless the same request also sets `verified` or `verification_method`.<br><br>null is accepted and ignored - the current value is kept. It does not clear the value.<br>|
|verification_method|string \| null|false|none|Verifies (`low`) or unverifies (`none`) the identity. Only `none` and `low` are accepted here; the<br>higher methods (`sso`, `embed`, `full`) are set by the corresponding authentication flows.<br><br>Ignored for identities that belong to the account owner. `phone_number` and `agent_forwarding`<br>identities are re-verified on every save, so `none` has no effect on them.<br><br>null is **not** ignored here: it is treated like `none` and unverifies the identity. Because this<br>property wins over `verified`, sending `verified: true` alongside `verification_method: null`<br>unverifies it.<br>|
|verified|boolean \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** Verifies (`true`) or unverifies (`false`) the identity. null is **not** ignored here: it is<br>treated like `false` and unverifies the identity. Equivalent to setting<br>`verification_method` to `low` or `none`. Deprecated - use `verification_method` instead. Ignored<br>when `verification_method` is also sent - that property wins.<br><br>Ignored for identities that belong to the account owner. `phone_number` and `agent_forwarding`<br>identities are re-verified on every save, so they cannot be unverified through this endpoint.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|deliverable_state|deliverable|
|deliverable_state|null|
|ownership|owned|
|ownership|shared|
|ownership|null|
|verification_method|none|
|verification_method|low|
|verification_method|null|

The organization must belong to the same account as<br>the user.<br><br>Creating a membership has effects beyond the new row:<br><br>* If this is the user's first organization membership, it is created as the default, which also sets<br>  the user's `organization_id`, and every unclosed ticket requested by the user is reassigned to this<br>  organization.<br>* On accounts **without** the multiple organizations feature, all of the user's other organization<br>  memberships are **deleted**, and the user's unclosed requested tickets that belonged to those<br>  removed organizations move to the user's new default organization — or have their organization<br>  cleared, if the account has the `unset_ticket_org_when_removing_default_user_org` feature. Tickets<br>  the user has in other organizations are left alone.<br>* Returns a 422 if the user is already at the account's `max_organization_memberships_per_user` limit<br>  (300 by default).<br>|

Input schema for updating a user. All fields are optional - only include
the fields you want to update.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_brand_ids|[integer(int64)]|false|none|The IDs of the brands the agent is assigned to|
|alias|string \| null|false|none|An alias displayed to end users|
|auto_ownership|boolean|false|write-only|Write-only ownership control for the Shared Email EAP. When true, automatic ownership is applied only to the identity created from `email`. Ignored unless the account has the Shared Email EAP enabled.|
|custom_role_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|A custom role if the user is an agent on the Enterprise plan or above|
|default_group_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The id of the user's default group|
|details|string \| null|false|none|Any details you want to store about the user, such as an address|
|email|string|false|none|The user's primary email address|
|external_id|string \| null|false|none|A unique identifier from another system|
|group_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The id of the user's default group. Alias for default_group_id|
|identities|[[UserIdentityInput](#schemauseridentityinput)]|false|none|none|
|language|string \| null|false|none|The user's language preference. Alias for locale.|
|locale|string \| null|false|none|The user's locale. A BCP-47 compliant tag for the locale. If both "locale" and "locale_id" are present on create or update, "locale_id" is ignored and only "locale" is used.|
|locale_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The user's language identifier|
|moderator|boolean \| null|false|none|Designates whether the user has forum moderation capabilities|
|name|string|false|none|The user's name|
|notes|string \| null|false|none|Any notes you want to store about the user|
|only_private_comments|boolean \| null|false|none|true if the user can only create private comments|
|organization_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The id of the user's organization|
|organization_ids|[integer(int64)]|false|none|The ids of the user's organizations|
|phone|string \| null|false|none|The user's primary phone number|
|photo|object \| null|false|none|The user's profile picture|
|remote_photo_url|string \| null|false|none|A URL pointing to the user's profile picture|
|role|string|false|none|The user's role|
|shared_phone_number|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the phone number is shared or not|
|signature|string \| null|false|none|The user's signature. Only agents and admins can have signatures|
|skip_verify_email|boolean \| null|false|none|If true, the user won't receive a verification email|
|suspended|boolean \| null|false|none|If the user is suspended|
|tags|[string]|false|none|The user's tags|
|ticket_restriction|string \| null|false|none|Specifies which tickets the user has access to|
|time_zone|string \| null|false|none|The user's time zone|
|user_fields|object \| null|false|none|Values of custom fields in the user's profile|
|verified|boolean \| null|false|none|Any of the user's identities is verified|

<h2 id="tocS_ViewPreviewConditionInput">ViewPreviewConditionInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaviewpreviewconditioninput"></a>
<a id="schema_ViewPreviewConditionInput"></a>
<a id="tocSviewpreviewconditioninput"></a>
<a id="tocsviewpreviewconditioninput"></a>

```json
{
  "field": "string",
  "operator": "string",
  "value": "string"
}
```

A single condition of the previewed view definition. See the
[Conditions reference](/documentation/ticketing/reference-guides/conditions-reference).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|field|string|false|none|The ticket property the condition tests, such as "status", "priority", "group_id" or "current_tags".<br>Use "custom_fields_{id}" (or "ticket_fields_{id}") for a custom field. A condition object with no `field`<br>is silently discarded instead of returning an error.<br>|
|operator|string|false|none|The comparison operator, such as "is", "is_not", "less_than", "greater_than" or "includes". Defaults to "is" when omitted|
|value|string \| null \| integer(int64) \| [string \| integer(int64)]|false|none|The value the condition compares against. A scalar and a single-element array are equivalent - the value is<br>always wrapped in an array before it is used. null is normalized to an empty value, which is what<br>value-less conditions such as "group_is_set_with_no_assignee" expect<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_ViewPreviewInput">ViewPreviewInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaviewpreviewinput"></a>
<a id="schema_ViewPreviewInput"></a>
<a id="tocSviewpreviewinput"></a>
<a id="tocsviewpreviewinput"></a>

```json
{
  "all": [
    {
      "field": "string",
      "operator": "string",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "any": [
    {
      "field": "string",
      "operator": "string",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "conditions": {
    "all": [
      {
        "field": "string",
        "operator": "string",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ],
    "any": [
      {
        "field": "string",
        "operator": "string",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ]
  },
  "id": 0,
  "output": {
    "columns": [
      "string"
    ],
    "group_by": "string",
    "group_order": "string",
    "sort_by": "string",
    "sort_order": "string"
  }
}
```

The view definition to preview. Nothing is persisted. Unless `id` is given, at least one `all` condition must
be on "status", "type", "group_id", "assignee_id", "requester_id", "organization_id", "due_date",
"support_type", one of the status duration fields ("OPEN", "PENDING", "HOLD", "CLOSED") or, on accounts with
custom statuses, "custom_status_id". Otherwise the definition is rejected as invalid. With `id` the referenced
view's own conditions are merged in first and can satisfy the requirement on their own.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|all|[[ViewPreviewConditionInput](#schemaviewpreviewconditioninput)]|false|none|The conditions a ticket must all meet to appear in the preview. May also be supplied as `conditions.all`|
|any|[[ViewPreviewConditionInput](#schemaviewpreviewconditioninput)]|false|none|The conditions, at least one of which a ticket must meet to appear in the preview. May also be supplied as `conditions.any`|
|conditions|object|false|none|An alternative way of supplying `all` and `any`, mirroring the `conditions` object of the response. The<br>top-level `all` and `any` properties take precedence when both forms are sent<br>|
|id|integer(int64) \| string|false|none|An existing active view to base the preview on, or the string alias "incoming" for the built-in incoming<br>view. The conditions and output supplied here are then merged into that view's own definition rather than<br>replacing them. Inactive views cannot be previewed. A numeric string is accepted for the id and coerced<br>to an integer<br>|
|output|object|false|none|The columns, grouping and sorting of the previewed view. When `id` is given the supplied properties are<br>merged into that view's own output; otherwise anything left out falls back to its system default<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_ViewPreviewOutputInput">ViewPreviewOutputInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaviewpreviewoutputinput"></a>
<a id="schema_ViewPreviewOutputInput"></a>
<a id="tocSviewpreviewoutputinput"></a>
<a id="tocsviewpreviewoutputinput"></a>

```json
{
  "columns": [
    "string"
  ],
  "group_by": "string",
  "group_order": "string",
  "sort_by": "string",
  "sort_order": "string"
}
```

The columns, grouping and sorting used when the previewed view is rendered.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|columns|[string \| integer(int64)]|false|none|The ticket fields to display, in order. System columns are given by name (see [View columns](#view-columns)).<br>Custom fields are given by their numeric id or by their title. Unrecognized names and the "score" column are silently<br>dropped rather than rejected. A maximum of 15 columns is enforced after that filtering - more than that<br>fails validation.<br>|
|group_by|string|false|none|The column the tickets are grouped by. Unrecognized values are stored without error and simply do not group the view|
|group_order|string|false|none|The direction the groups are ordered in. May be "asc" or "desc"|
|sort_by|string|false|none|The column the tickets are sorted by. "id" is stored as "nice_id"|
|sort_order|string|false|none|The direction the tickets are sorted in. May be "asc" or "desc"|

Unless `id` is given, at least one `all` condition must<br>be on "status", "type", "group_id", "assignee_id", "requester_id", "organization_id", "due_date",<br>"support_type", one of the status duration fields ("OPEN", "PENDING", "HOLD", "CLOSED") or, on accounts with<br>custom statuses, "custom_status_id". Otherwise the definition is rejected as invalid. With `id` the referenced<br>view's own conditions are merged in first and can satisfy the requirement on their own.<br>|

```json
{
```

```json
  "components": [
    {
      "text": "Hi {{1}}, your order {{2}} has shipped.",

    }

  "id": "01JBQ8Z5K7N3M9P2R4T6V8X0YA",
  "integrations": [
    {
      "id": "5f3a1b2c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e",
      "name": "WhatsApp Support"
    }
  ],
  "is_active": true,
  "language": "en_US",
  "name": "order_confirmation",
  "status": "approved",
  "template_id": "1234567890",
  "updated_at": "2026-09-17T17:24:25Z"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|category|string \| null|false|read-only|Template category assigned by WhatsApp, for example `MARKETING`, `UTILITY`, or `AUTHENTICATION`|
|components|[object]|false|read-only|The template's WhatsApp components (header, body, footer, and buttons) as returned by WhatsApp|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The time the template was first synced|
|id|string|true|read-only|Automatically assigned ULID upon creation|
|integrations|[object]|true|read-only|The WhatsApp integrations this template is currently active on|
|is_active|boolean|true|none|Whether the template is enabled for use in this account|
|language|string|true|read-only|BCP 47 language tag the template is authored in, for example `en_US`|
|name|string|true|read-only|Name of the WhatsApp message template|
|status|string|true|read-only|Approval status of the template. Only approved templates are synced.|
|template_id|string|true|read-only|The template's identifier at WABA (WhatsApp)|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The time of the last update to the template|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|approved|

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|

|macro_ids|[integer(int64)]|false|none|The ids of the macros associated to this workspace|
|macros|[integer]|false|none|The ids of the macros associated to this workspace|
|position|integer|false|none|Ordering of the workspace relative to other workspaces|
|prefer_workspace_app_order|boolean|false|none|If true, the order of apps within the workspace will be preserved|
|selected_macros|[[MacroObject](#schemamacroobject)]|false|none|An array of the macro objects that will be used in this workspace. See [Macros](/api-reference/ticketing/business-rules/macros/)|
|ticket_form_id|integer(int64)|false|none|The id of the ticket web form associated to this workspace|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the workspace|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|The time of the last update of the workspace|
|url|string|false|none|The URL for this resource|
